controls.title: Governance Charter
controls.objective: Establish one approved charter that defines who directs, oversees and is accountable for assurance of each in-scope Capability Instance, which decision questions the programme serves, and the limits of reliance on AIDCF conclusions.
controls.requirement: The governing body shall approve an assurance governance charter that names the in-scope Capability Instances, the accountable executive, the assurance programme lead, the decision authority and the oversight committee; states the decision questions served and the intended users of conclusions; defines the programme model (self-assessment, co-sourced, second-party or independent provider); and states that AIDCF conclusions do not replace engineering, statutory or safety approval and are not certification. The accountable executive shall review the charter at no more than the governance charter review interval and after any change of ownership, organisation or programme model, and shall record the outcome of each review.
assessmentCriteria: The charter in use is the approved version, and the approval was given by the governing body or by a body holding a documented delegation from it.
The charter names, by role and current incumbent, the accountable executive, assurance programme lead, decision authority and oversight committee.
Every Capability Instance recorded as in scope in the capability register (MCF-CAP-001) falls within the charter scope; no in-scope instance is uncovered.

The charter states the decision questions served, the intended users, the programme model and the non-substitution limits (no replacement of engineering, statutory or safety approval; no certification).
The charter defines the independence safeguards required before a material gate result or Assurance Decision is relied upon.
The most recent charter review is within the review interval and post-dates every charter trigger event (ownership, reorganisation, programme-model change).

parameters.name: Governance charter review interval
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter set by the governing body; illustrative, shortened where the capability is changing rapidly

minimumEvidence: Approved governance charter with version identifier and effective date
Governing-body resolution or minute recording approval of that charter version
Delegation instrument where approval was given below the governing body
Reconciliation of charter scope to a dated extract of the capability register
Record of the most recent charter review and its outcome

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Charter version in force at the assessment date and the preceding review cycle
evidenceProfile.independence: Approval evidence shall originate from the governing-body secretariat or equivalent, not from the charter author
mandatoryItems: Approved governance charter with version identifier and effective date
Governing-body resolution or minute recording approval of that charter version
acceptableAlternatives: Terms of reference of a board-delegated committee containing equivalent content, supported by the delegation instrument
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: control result UNKNOWN; CG-13 gate-level evaluation records the gap; decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a named condition to evidence charter approval
reassessmentTriggers: Change of accountable executive or decision authority
Organisational restructuring affecting assurance reporting lines
Change of programme model or assurance provider
Addition of a Capability Instance to scope

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the charter in force and its approval record; confirm version identity and the authority of the approving body.
Reconcile the charter scope to a dated capability register extract and list any in-scope Capability Instance not covered.
Confirm the named roles against current appointment records.
Inspect the charter for decision questions, intended users, programme model, independence safeguards and non-substitution statements.
Interview the accountable executive to confirm their understanding of charter authority and the escalation route to the governing body.
Compare the last review date with the review interval and with trigger events since that review.
controls.applicability: Applies to every AIDCF assurance programme. For a single commissioned assessment, an engagement letter approved by the decision authority may satisfy the control if it contains the same content; full non-applicability is not permitted.
failureModes: No approved authority exists for issuing assurance conclusions
Charter scope omits a Capability Instance that is reported on
AIDCF conclusion is represented as engineering approval or certification
Charter remains in force after the accountable executive has left
controls.testingSafety: Non-intrusive document review and interview only; no site or system testing. Governing-body papers can be commercially sensitive and are accessed through the evidence lead under the classification rules of AIDCF-008.
controls.unknownRule: If the approval record cannot be produced, or the approving body's authority cannot be established, record a U1 or U6 UNKNOWN against the charter; approval shall not be inferred from the charter being in use.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 38500 (governance of IT for the organization)

controls.title: Decision Rights
controls.objective: Ensure that every consequential decision affecting the AI capability and its assurance (risk acceptance, gate disposition, Assurance Decision, emergency load action, test authorisation, exception approval) has a defined, delegated decision right that is used as designed, including in emergency states.
controls.requirement: The accountable executive shall maintain a decision-rights matrix that, for each decision class affecting an in-scope Capability Instance, names the role holding the decision right, its financial or risk limits, the escalation route, the delegation and sub-delegation rules, and the emergency decision rights that apply when the normal holder is unavailable. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that workflow and approval systems enforce the matrix, and that every decision in the sample population was taken by a role holding the right at the time it was taken.
assessmentCriteria: A decision-rights matrix exists, is approved by the accountable executive and covers at minimum: risk acceptance, gate disposition, Assurance Decision issue, exception approval, hazardous test authorisation, and emergency load curtailment or shutdown of AI workloads.
Each decision class names a single holding role, limits, escalation route and the emergency alternate.
Approval workflows (change, exception, risk and decision registers) are configured so that only roles holding the right can approve the corresponding record type.
In a sample of decisions taken during the assessment period, every approver held the decision right and was within limits on the date of the decision.
Emergency decision rights are defined for EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states and at least one exercised or rehearsed emergency decision shows the alternate route was usable.
No decision in the sample was taken by an assessor on behalf of management.

parameters.name: Decision sample size per decision class
parameters.illustrativeDefault: 10 or the full population if smaller
parameters.basis: Judgemental sample per AIDCF-008 sampling principles; illustrative, increased if exceptions are found

minimumEvidence: Approved decision-rights matrix with version and approval record
Delegation and sub-delegation instruments in force during the period
Export of approver role configuration from change, exception, risk and decision workflow tools
Sampled decision records with approver identity, role and date
Emergency decision-right definition and record of its exercise or rehearsal

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current matrix plus decisions taken in the twelve months preceding the assessment, or since the last assessment if shorter
evidenceProfile.independence: Workflow configuration shall be extracted by the assessor or under assessor observation, not supplied as a screenshot by the approver population
mandatoryItems: Approved decision-rights matrix with version and approval record
Export of approver role configuration from change, exception, risk and decision workflow tools
Sampled decision records with approver identity, role and date
acceptableAlternatives: Where approvals are paper-based, a complete approval log reconciled to signed records replaces the workflow configuration export
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED until the decision-rights evidence is produced
reassessmentTriggers: Reorganisation or change in delegation limits
Introduction or replacement of an approval workflow tool
A decision found to have been taken outside its decision right

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the decision-rights matrix and confirm it covers the minimum decision classes, including emergency classes.
Extract approver role configuration from each workflow tool and reconcile it to the matrix; list roles able to approve without holding the right.
Define the population of decisions per class for the period and select a sample using the stated sample size.
For each sampled decision, verify approver identity, role held on that date and limits, against appointment and delegation records.
Review the emergency decision-right record and interview the emergency alternate on how they would exercise it.
Expand the sample by the same size again for any class where a nonconforming decision is found, and record the result.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Capability Instance. Decision classes that do not occur (for example no hazardous testing is permitted) may be marked NOT_APPLICABLE individually with rationale; the matrix as a whole is always applicable.
failureModes: Unauthorised risk acceptance
Gate disposition or Assurance Decision issued by a role without authority
No one able to authorise emergency curtailment of AI load when the normal holder is unavailable
Workflow tool allows any user to approve
Assessor makes a management decision
controls.testingSafety: Read-only extraction of workflow configuration under the tool owner's supervision; no test approvals are submitted in production systems. Emergency decision rights are examined by walkthrough or tabletop, never by declaring a real emergency.
controls.unknownRule: If a workflow tool configuration cannot be extracted, or decisions cannot be tied to the approver's role on the date taken, record a U2 or U6 UNKNOWN; the decision class is treated as uncontrolled for CG-13 until resolved.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 38500 (governance of IT for the organization)

controls.title: Committee Oversight
controls.objective: Ensure that a standing oversight committee actually receives, challenges and acts on assurance information about the AI capability, including gate failures, critical UNKNOWN Records and overdue actions, at a frequency matched to the rate of change.
controls.requirement: The governing body shall constitute an assurance oversight committee with written terms of reference, quorum and membership that includes at least one member independent of the operating line. The committee chair shall ensure that the committee meets at no more than the oversight meeting interval, receives at every meeting the current gate register, UNKNOWN register (US3 and above), findings register and overdue action list for each in-scope Capability Instance, records challenge and decisions in minutes, and tracks its own actions to closure.
assessmentCriteria: Terms of reference define purpose, membership, quorum, frequency, independence of at least one member, and escalation to the governing body.
Meetings were held at intervals not exceeding the oversight meeting interval throughout the assessment period and each was quorate.
Every meeting pack in the sample contained the current gate register, UNKNOWN register (US3 and above), findings register and overdue action list.
Minutes record challenge or questions on at least each gate FAIL and each US4/US5 UNKNOWN Record presented, and the decision or action taken.
Committee actions are tracked and closed with evidence, and overdue committee actions are escalated to the governing body.
Any gate FAIL or US4/US5 UNKNOWN Record arising between meetings was notified to the chair within the out-of-cycle notification time.

parameters.name: Oversight meeting interval
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, shortened during build, major change or after a gate FAIL

parameters.name: Out-of-cycle notification time for gate FAIL or US4/US5 UNKNOWN

minimumEvidence: Meeting calendar and attendance records for the period
Sampled meeting packs with register extracts
Approved minutes and committee action log
Out-of-cycle notifications for gate FAIL or US4/US5 UNKNOWN events

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least four consecutive meeting cycles, or all meetings in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Minutes shall be the approved record held by the committee secretary; drafts or summaries prepared by management are not sufficient
mandatoryItems: Approved minutes and committee action log
Sampled meeting packs with register extracts
acceptableAlternatives: Recorded and transcribed meetings with approved action logs may replace minutes where the organisation's records policy permits
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: control result UNKNOWN; decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a condition that oversight operation is evidenced
reassessmentTriggers: Change of chair or loss of the independent member
Two consecutive missed or inquorate meetings
A gate FAIL not presented to the committee

assessmentProcedure: Obtain terms of reference and confirm membership, quorum, independence and escalation provisions.
List all meetings in the period from the calendar and attendance records; test interval and quorum for each.
Select meeting packs and confirm the four mandatory registers were included and were current at the meeting date.
Reconcile gate FAIL and US4/US5 UNKNOWN Records in the gate and UNKNOWN registers to the minutes; identify any not presented or not challenged.
Trace committee actions to closure evidence and confirm escalation of overdue items.
Interview the chair and the independent member on how challenge is exercised and recorded.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme where conclusions are relied upon beyond the immediate management team. For a single assessment with no continuing programme, review of the result by the decision authority may substitute, recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE with rationale.
failureModes: Gate FAIL or critical UNKNOWN never reaches oversight
Committee receives scores only and no gate or UNKNOWN information
Oversight meets too infrequently for the rate of capability change
Committee actions are not tracked
controls.testingSafety: Document and interview review only. Observation of a live committee meeting requires the chair's prior consent and is confined to the agenda items concerning the in-scope capability.
controls.unknownRule: If minutes for a meeting in the period are missing, record a U1 UNKNOWN for that meeting and do not count it as held; if more than one meeting in the period is affected, the criterion on meeting interval is not met.
informativeReferences: Institute of Internal Auditors Three Lines Model
AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard

controls.title: Methodology Ownership
controls.objective: Ensure that the assessment methodology actually applied (AIDCF artifact versions, capability profile, scoring version, any local tailoring) has a named owner, is version-controlled, and is identical to the version declared in reports.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall appoint a methodology owner who shall maintain a controlled methodology baseline listing the AIDCF artifact versions (including AIDCF-007A, AIDCF-008, AIDCF-009 and AIDCF-010), the capability profile, scoring version and every approved local tailoring, each with rationale and approval. The methodology owner shall ensure that assessment tools and templates are configured to that baseline and that every report declares the baseline version actually used.
assessmentCriteria: A methodology owner is appointed in writing and holds competence in AIDCF and assurance methods.
A controlled methodology baseline exists listing artifact versions, capability profile version, scoring version and approved tailorings with rationale and approver.
No tailoring weakens a critical-gate rule, an evidence floor or the UNKNOWN treatment of AIDCF-008 and AIDCF-010.
The control registry, vocabularies and scoring logic configured in the assessment tool match the declared baseline version (hash or version comparison).
Every report in the sample declares a baseline version, and that version was the one in force on the assessment date.
minimumEvidence: Methodology baseline record with versions, tailorings, rationale and approvals
Tool configuration export showing registry, vocabulary and scoring versions
Sampled reports with declared methodology baseline

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Methodology baseline in force and reports issued in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Tool configuration comparison shall be performed by the assessor against published release manifests, not by the tool owner alone
mandatoryItems: Methodology baseline record with versions, tailorings, rationale and approvals
Tool configuration export showing registry, vocabulary and scoring versions
acceptableAlternatives: Where no tool is used, controlled template versions with checksums replace the tool configuration export
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected control and gate results UNKNOWN where the methodology version cannot be established; decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED
reassessmentTriggers: Approval of a new local tailoring
Report found to declare an incorrect baseline

assessmentProcedure: Confirm the methodology owner appointment and competence record.
Review the methodology baseline and each tailoring; test each tailoring against gate rules, evidence floors and UNKNOWN treatment.
Extract registry, vocabulary and scoring versions from the assessment tool and compare them with the release manifest of the declared baseline.
Sample issued reports and compare the declared baseline with the baseline in force on each assessment date.
Record any divergence as a Finding and identify affected results.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme that issues AIDCF control, gate or decision results.
failureModes: Results produced under an undeclared or superseded control registry
Local tailoring silently weakens a gate or evidence floor
Scoring version in tool differs from the version reported
No one accountable for methodology changes
controls.testingSafety: Read-only inspection of tool configuration in a non-production or export copy; no change to scoring logic is made during assessment.
controls.unknownRule: If the tool configuration cannot be compared with a release manifest, record a U8 (method uncertain) UNKNOWN against every result produced with that tool in the period.
informativeReferences: ISO 9001 (quality management systems) - control of documented information
AIDCF-014 End-to-End Traceability and Machine-Executable Data Standard

controls.title: RACI and Role Ownership
controls.objective: Ensure that every role named in the assurance programme and in operation of the AI capability has a current incumbent, a defined RACI position for each process, and no unresolved overlap or gap between owner, operator and providers.
controls.requirement: The accountable executive shall maintain a RACI that assigns, for each in-scope process (capability management, assurance, evidence, change, incident, recovery, provider management), exactly one Accountable role and the Responsible, Consulted and Informed roles across owner, operator, tenants and providers. The assurance programme lead shall reconcile the RACI to current appointments and to contractual responsibility clauses at least at the RACI reconciliation interval and after every organisational or contract change.
assessmentCriteria: The RACI covers every in-scope process and assigns exactly one Accountable role to each.
Every role in the RACI has a named current incumbent and a deputy.
RACI assignments for providers and tenants match the responsibility clauses of the corresponding contracts or service descriptions.
No process has a responsibility split between owner, operator and provider that leaves an activity with no Responsible role.
Reconciliation to appointments and contracts occurred within the reconciliation interval and after each trigger event.
Interviewed role holders describe their RACI position consistently with the document.
minimumEvidence: Current appointment or HR role extract for named roles
Responsibility clauses of operator, provider and tenant contracts
Interview notes from sampled role holders

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: RACI in force and appointments current at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Interview evidence shall be obtained by the assessor directly from role holders, separately from the RACI author
mandatoryItems: Responsibility clauses of operator, provider and tenant contracts
acceptableAlternatives: A responsibility matrix embedded in a service management system, exported with version metadata
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: New, changed or terminated provider or tenant contract
Departure of an Accountable role holder
Incident in which responsibility was disputed

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the RACI and confirm each in-scope process has exactly one Accountable role.
Reconcile named roles to current appointment records and identify vacancies or missing deputies.
Reconcile provider and tenant assignments to contractual responsibility clauses and list gaps or conflicts.
Analyse each process for activities with no Responsible role at owner/operator/provider interfaces.
Interview a sample of Accountable and Responsible role holders, including at least one provider role, and compare their description with the RACI.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Capability Instance. Where the owner and operator are the same organisation, the owner/operator interface criteria are evaluated within the organisation.
failureModes: Two parties each believe the other is responsible for an activity
Accountable role vacant
Provider contract assigns responsibility differently from the RACI
No deputy for an Accountable role during an emergency
controls.testingSafety: Interview and document review only. Provider contract extracts may be commercially restricted; where access is limited, only responsibility clauses are disclosed under the evidence lead's restriction record.
controls.unknownRule: If a provider or tenant contract cannot be accessed to confirm responsibility clauses, record a U2 UNKNOWN for that interface; it shall not be assumed that the provider is responsible.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures) - management and operational information

controls.title: Critical Function Accountability
controls.objective: Ensure that every Required Function and material Dependency supporting an in-scope Service Outcome (power, cooling, compute, storage, network, control plane, external providers) has one accountable owner with authority to act, recorded in the assurance graph.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall ensure that each Required Function and each material Dependency linked to an in-scope Service Outcome has exactly one accountable owner recorded in the assurance graph, that the owner holds the decision right to commit resources and to authorise degraded-state actions for that function, and that cross-organisational functions (for example utility supply, facility water, network carriers, cloud control planes) have both an internal accountable owner and a named counterparty contact. The assurance programme lead shall reconcile function ownership to the RACI and decision-rights matrix after every change to the Required Function or Dependency set.
assessmentCriteria: Every Required Function and material Dependency in the assurance graph linked to an in-scope Service Outcome has exactly one accountable owner.
Each owner holds, in the decision-rights matrix, the right to commit resources and to authorise degraded-state actions for that function.
Each external or cross-organisational Dependency has an internal accountable owner and a named counterparty contact with a verified contact route.
Function ownership in the graph reconciles to the RACI and decision-rights matrix with no conflicts.
Ownership was reconciled after each addition, removal or change of a Required Function or Dependency in the period.
minimumEvidence: Assurance graph extract of Required Functions and Dependencies with owner attributes
Counterparty contact register with last verification date
Reconciliation record after each function or dependency change

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Graph state at the assessment date and changes during the preceding twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: The graph extract shall be produced by query executed or witnessed by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Assurance graph extract of Required Functions and Dependencies with owner attributes
acceptableAlternatives: Where no graph exists, a function and dependency register maintained under document control, with an explicit limitation recorded against traceability
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN for each unowned critical function; decision capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: New Required Function or material Dependency identified
Change of provider for an external dependency

assessmentProcedure: Query the assurance graph for all Required Functions and material Dependencies linked to in-scope Service Outcomes and their owner attributes.
Identify functions or dependencies with zero or more than one accountable owner.
Reconcile each owner to the decision-rights matrix for authority to commit resources and authorise degraded-state actions.
Test the counterparty contact route for a sample of external dependencies by confirming the last successful verification.
Interview a sample of owners, prioritising shared or external dependencies, on their authority and escalation in a degraded state.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Required Function and material Dependency supporting an in-scope Service Outcome; dependencies assessed as non-material in the DEP domain are excluded with that rationale.
failureModes: Shared facility water loop has no single accountable owner across facility and IT teams
External carrier dependency has no internal owner
Owner lacks authority to authorise load shedding during a cooling degradation
Ownership not updated after a provider change
controls.testingSafety: Graph queries are executed read-only. Contact-route verification uses existing records or a pre-agreed non-operational test message; it shall not simulate an incident to a provider.
controls.unknownRule: Any Required Function or material Dependency whose owner cannot be established is recorded as a US4 UNKNOWN Record against CG-13; ownership shall not be presumed from organisational proximity.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-005 AIDCF-AI Trust Graph Integration Standard

controls.title: Risk Acceptance Authority
controls.objective: Ensure that residual risks, Findings left open and conditions attached to decisions are accepted only by a role holding risk-acceptance authority for that magnitude, with an expiry and review, and never by assessors.
controls.requirement: The accountable executive shall define risk-acceptance authority levels linked to the risk appetite (MCF-GOV-014) and impact tolerances (MCF-CAP-010). Each risk owner shall record every risk acceptance with the risk description, affected Service Outcomes and gates, residual consequence, compensating measures, acceptor, expiry date and review date. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that no acceptance of a risk that would cause a CRITICAL control or gate to be relied upon is recorded without the decision authority's approval, and that expired acceptances revert to open Findings.
assessmentCriteria: Risk-acceptance authority levels are defined and linked to risk appetite and impact tolerance.
Every risk acceptance in the sample was made by a role holding authority for its magnitude on the date of acceptance.
Every acceptance records affected Service Outcomes and gates, residual consequence, compensating measures, expiry and review date.
No acceptance has passed its expiry date without renewal by an authorised acceptor or reversion to an open Finding.
No acceptance in the population was made or recommended for acceptance by an assessor.
No acceptance is used to convert a gate FAIL or US4/US5 UNKNOWN into PASS; such risks appear only as decision-level conditions.

parameters.name: Maximum risk-acceptance validity
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, shorter for acceptances touching gate-critical controls

minimumEvidence: Risk register extract of acceptances in the period
Sampled acceptance records with acceptor role and date
Register of expired acceptances and their disposition

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: All acceptances active at any point in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor selects the sample from a full register extract; management selection of examples is not accepted
mandatoryItems: Risk register extract of acceptances in the period
Sampled acceptance records with acceptor role and date
acceptableAlternatives: Where risk acceptances are recorded in decision minutes rather than a register, a complete extraction from minutes reconciled to the action log
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: Change of risk appetite or authority levels
Expiry of acceptances touching gate-critical controls

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the authority schedule and confirm linkage to risk appetite and impact tolerance.
Extract the full population of acceptances active during the period and select a sample weighted to acceptances touching gate-critical controls.
For each sampled acceptance, verify acceptor authority on the date, completeness of required fields and expiry status.
Analyse the population for expired acceptances not renewed or reverted, and for acceptances used to clear a gate FAIL or US4/US5 UNKNOWN.
Confirm from engagement records that no assessor made or recommended an acceptance.
controls.applicability: Applies whenever any residual risk, open Finding or decision condition is accepted for an in-scope Capability Instance.
failureModes: Risk accepted by an operator below the authority threshold
Indefinite risk acceptance with no expiry
Gate FAIL hidden by a risk acceptance
Assessor accepts risk on management's behalf
controls.testingSafety: Document and register review only; no operational activity.
controls.unknownRule: If the acceptor's authority on the acceptance date cannot be established, record a U6 UNKNOWN and treat the acceptance as not made; the underlying Finding is reported as open.

controls.title: Evidence Custody
controls.objective: Assign accountable custody for assurance evidence so that every Evidence Object relied on by a decision has a custodian, an access policy and an unbroken custody record from collection to retention or destruction.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall appoint an evidence lead who shall assign a custodian role to each evidence repository and each Evidence Package, define who may read, add, alter, export, redact or destroy evidence, and ensure that every custody event defined in AIDCF-008 (transfer, access, export, alteration, redaction, retention action) is recorded. The evidence lead shall review custody records for Evidence Packages supporting gate results before each Assurance Decision is issued.
assessmentCriteria: An evidence lead is appointed and each repository and Evidence Package supporting a gate or decision has a named custodian.
Access policies define permitted actions per role and are configured in the repository so that alteration and destruction are restricted to authorised roles.
For a sample of Evidence Objects supporting gate results, the custody log is complete from collection to current state with no unexplained gap.
Custody review of gate-supporting Evidence Packages was performed before each Assurance Decision in the period.
Transfers of evidence to or from providers are recorded with sender, receiver, method, time and integrity value.
minimumEvidence: Evidence lead appointment and custodian register
Repository access policy and role configuration export
Custody logs for sampled Evidence Objects

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F3 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Custody events for Evidence Objects supporting decisions issued in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Custody logs shall be extracted from the repository system of record by the assessor, not compiled by the custodian
mandatoryItems: Repository access policy and role configuration export
Custody logs for sampled Evidence Objects
acceptableAlternatives: For paper or physical evidence, a sealed-bag custody register with signatures and seal numbers
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected gate evidence treated as integrity-uncertain (U7); dependent gate results may become UNKNOWN under CG-11

assessmentProcedure: Confirm evidence lead appointment and custodian assignment for each repository and gate-supporting package.
Extract role configuration and compare with the access policy; list roles able to alter or destroy evidence without authority.
Sample Evidence Objects supporting gate results and trace custody logs from collection to current state.
Verify pre-decision custody reviews for each decision in the period.
Trace a sample of provider evidence transfers and confirm integrity values were recorded and verified on receipt.
controls.applicability: Applies to all evidence relied on for control, gate or decision results. Operational records retained only in source systems are within scope when cited as evidence.
failureModes: Evidence altered after collection with no record
No custodian for provider-supplied test reports
Evidence destroyed before decision challenge period ends
Shared accounts used to upload evidence
controls.testingSafety: Read-only inspection of repository configuration and logs. Any test of access restrictions uses a dedicated test account and test object approved by the evidence lead; production evidence is never altered.
controls.unknownRule: If custody logs are absent for a period or object, record a U7 UNKNOWN against the affected Evidence Objects; they may not be used to support a gate result until integrity is re-established by re-collection or independent corroboration.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 27037 (identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence)

controls.title: Policy Hierarchy
controls.objective: Ensure that policies, technical standards, procedures and runbooks governing the AI capability form a coherent hierarchy in which each lower document traces to a higher one and contradictions are identified and resolved.
controls.requirement: The policy owner shall maintain a policy hierarchy register that identifies, for each in-scope document, its level (policy, standard, procedure, runbook), parent document, owner, scope (sites, halls, clusters, systems) and approval status. The policy owner shall ensure that no procedure or runbook relies on a superseded or absent parent, and that identified contradictions between documents are recorded and resolved by the owner of the higher document.
assessmentCriteria: A register exists listing each in-scope policy, standard, procedure and runbook with level, parent, owner, scope and approval status.
Every document below policy level traces to an approved, current parent.
Policy-level documents cover at minimum assurance, risk, change, incident, safety of work, information security, evidence and provider management for the in-scope capability.
Contradictions identified in the period (including those found by the assessor in a sample comparison) are recorded and resolved by the higher-document owner.
Scopes declared in documents cover all in-scope sites, halls and clusters without gaps.
minimumEvidence: Sample of standards, procedures and runbooks with parent references

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Documents in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Contradiction comparison on a sample of document pairs shall be performed by the assessor
acceptableAlternatives: Document management system metadata export with parent-child links in place of a separate register
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: control result UNKNOWN; reliance on procedures for affected controls is limited and recorded as a condition
reassessmentTriggers: New site, hall or cluster added to scope

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the register and confirm completeness against the document management system.
Check that minimum policy topics are covered for the in-scope capability.
Trace a sample of procedures and runbooks, prioritising emergency and recovery runbooks, to approved current parents.
Compare a sample of document pairs at adjacent levels for contradictions in requirements, roles or limits.
Reconcile declared document scopes to the capability register and identify uncovered sites, halls or clusters.
controls.applicability: Applies to every organisation operating or assuring an in-scope Capability Instance; for providers, applies to documents the provider makes available under contract.
failureModes: Runbook traces to a superseded standard
Contradictory limits in procedure and standard
No policy covering evidence or provider management
New cluster not covered by any operating procedure
controls.testingSafety: Document review only; no runbook is exercised. Emergency runbooks are read in the document system, not at operational consoles.
controls.unknownRule: If a document cited as parent cannot be produced, record a U1 UNKNOWN against the child document and treat the child as untraced.

controls.title: Technical Standard Baselines
controls.objective: Ensure that the engineering and technical standards baseline the capability is designed, built and operated against (electrical, mechanical, fire, OT security, accelerator platform, network and storage standards and vendor envelopes) is declared, versioned and actually applied to the as-built and as-configured state.
controls.requirement: The chief engineer for the capability shall declare a technical standards baseline listing each external standard family, internal engineering standard and OEM specification applied to in-scope infrastructure, with edition or version, scope of application and any declared deviation. The chief engineer shall ensure that design, commissioning and change records cite the baseline edition applied, and that adoption of a new edition is controlled through change control with impact assessment.
assessmentCriteria: A technical standards baseline lists the standards, internal engineering standards and OEM specifications applied, with edition, scope and deviations.
The baseline covers each infrastructure domain in scope (power, thermal, physical, compute, storage, network, OT and control-plane security).
Design and commissioning records in a sample cite the baseline edition applied.
Each declared deviation has a rationale, a compensating measure and approval through exception governance (MCF-GOV-011).
Adoption of new editions or OEM specification revisions in the period was processed through change control with impact assessment.
minimumEvidence: Technical standards baseline with editions and scope
Sampled design and commissioning records citing the baseline

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Baseline in force and records produced since the last major design or commissioning event
evidenceProfile.independence: Domain specialists for each infrastructure domain shall confirm applicability of the listed standard families
mandatoryItems: Technical standards baseline with editions and scope
acceptableAlternatives: Design basis documents per domain that each list applied standards, consolidated by the assessor
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected DESIGN claims in infrastructure domains may become UNKNOWN; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: New edition of an applied standard adopted
OEM specification revision for accelerators, CDUs or power equipment
New infrastructure domain or technology introduced (for example immersion cooling)

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the baseline and confirm coverage of each in-scope infrastructure domain.
Ask each domain specialist to confirm that listed standard families are applicable and complete for their domain.
Sample design and commissioning records and verify citation of the baseline edition.
Trace deviations to approved exceptions and confirm compensating measures.
Trace edition adoptions in the period to change records with impact assessment.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope infrastructure. Where a colocation provider owns the facility baseline, the provider's baseline is assessed through MCF-SUP controls and referenced here.
failureModes: Design built against an undeclared standard edition
OEM thermal or power envelope revision not reflected in design
Undocumented deviation from an applied standard
New technology deployed with no applicable standard declared
controls.testingSafety: Document review only; no inspection of energised equipment is required for this control.
controls.unknownRule: If the edition applied to a design cannot be determined, record a U8 UNKNOWN against the affected DESIGN claims in the relevant infrastructure domain.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures)
EN 50600 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures)
ASHRAE TC 9.9 thermal guidelines for data processing environments
IEC 62443 series (industrial automation and control systems security)

controls.title: Exception Governance
controls.objective: Ensure that every deviation from policy, technical baseline or control requirement is recorded, risk-assessed, approved by an authorised role, time-bound and visible in assurance reporting, so that exceptions do not silently accumulate into an unassessed configuration.
controls.requirement: The policy owner shall operate an exception process in which each exception records the requirement deviated from, affected Capability Instances, Service Outcomes, controls and gates, the risk assessment, compensating measures, approver, expiry and closure criteria. Exceptions affecting a gate-critical control shall be approved by the decision authority. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that the exception register is an input to every assessment and that expired exceptions are escalated to the oversight committee.
assessmentCriteria: Every exception in the sample records the deviated requirement, affected scope, controls and gates, risk assessment, compensating measures, approver, expiry and closure criteria.
Exceptions affecting gate-critical controls were approved by the decision authority.
No exception in the register is past expiry without renewal or closure; expired exceptions were escalated to the oversight committee.
The exception register was used as an input to each assessment in the period and affected controls reference the relevant exceptions.
Configuration or practice found by the assessor to deviate from a requirement has a corresponding exception or is raised as a Finding.

parameters.name: Maximum exception duration
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, renewable once by the approver

minimumEvidence: Exception register extract for the period
Oversight committee records of expired-exception escalation
Assessment planning records citing the exception register

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: All exceptions active during the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor compares observed configuration deviations with the register independently of the exception owner
mandatoryItems: Exception register extract for the period
acceptableAlternatives: Exception records held in a GRC tool, exported with full field history
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected control results UNKNOWN where undeclared deviation cannot be excluded; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Exception approved for a gate-critical control

assessmentProcedure: Extract the exception register for the period and analyse expiry status across the population.
Sample exceptions, weighting toward gate-critical controls, and test completeness and approver authority.
Confirm escalation of expired exceptions in oversight committee records.
Reconcile deviations observed in other domain assessments to the register and raise Findings for undeclared deviations.
Confirm that the assessment plan and affected control assessments reference active exceptions.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Capability Instance. If no exceptions exist, the control is still assessed by testing for undeclared deviations.
failureModes: Temporary bypass of a protection or interlock left in place indefinitely
Exceptions approved by the requester
Exception register not used in assessment, so results ignore known deviations
Accumulated exceptions create an unassessed configuration
controls.testingSafety: Register review only. Where the assessor verifies a deviation in a live system, it is by read-only inspection with the system owner present.
controls.unknownRule: If the existence of undeclared deviations cannot be tested for a domain (for example configuration not accessible), record a U5 coverage-gap UNKNOWN for that domain against this control.

controls.title: Document Lifecycle
controls.objective: Ensure that documents used to operate and assure the capability are controlled through creation, review, approval, publication, supersession and withdrawal, so that the version at the point of use is the approved current version.
controls.requirement: The policy owner shall define document lifecycle states, review intervals by document level and approval roles, and the document control administrator shall ensure that only approved current versions are published at points of use (control room, plant rooms, runbook systems, assessor workpaper templates), that superseded versions are withdrawn from points of use while retained in history, and that review dates are tracked.
assessmentCriteria: Lifecycle states, review intervals by document level and approval roles are defined.
At a sample of points of use (including control room and runbook system), the version available is the approved current version.
Superseded documents are withdrawn from points of use and retained in history with supersession metadata.
No document in the sample is past its review date without a recorded extension.
Emergency and recovery runbooks are available at the point of use in a form usable during loss of the primary document system.

parameters.name: Runbook review interval
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, shorter for emergency runbooks after change

minimumEvidence: Document management system version and status export
Offline or alternate runbook availability record

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Document versions current at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Point-of-use inspection shall be performed by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Document management system version and status export
acceptableAlternatives: Controlled print register with issue and withdrawal signatures where points of use rely on printed documents
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected OPERATION claims in operational domains may be qualified; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Incident where an outdated document was used

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the document control procedure and confirm lifecycle states, review intervals and approval roles.
Select points of use, including the control room and runbook system, and compare available versions with the document management system.
Check that superseded versions are absent at points of use and present in history.
Test review dates on a sample of documents.
Inspect alternate availability of emergency and recovery runbooks for loss of the primary document system.
controls.applicability: Applies to all controlled documents used to operate or assure in-scope infrastructure.
failureModes: Operator executes a superseded switching or cooling procedure
Emergency runbook unavailable when the document system is down
Assessor uses a superseded template
Review dates lapse unnoticed
controls.testingSafety: Point-of-use inspection in control rooms and plant rooms is escorted, follows site induction and access rules, and does not involve touching operational equipment.
controls.unknownRule: If the version at a point of use cannot be compared with the system of record, record a U6 UNKNOWN for that point of use.
informativeReferences: ISO 9001 (quality management systems) - control of documented information

controls.title: Assurance Plan
controls.objective: Ensure that a risk-based assurance plan determines which Capability Instances, Service Outcomes, claim types and gates are assessed, at what Assurance Level, by whom and when, so that assurance effort follows consequence and change rather than convenience.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall prepare, and the oversight committee shall approve, an assurance plan for each planning period that, for each in-scope Capability Instance, states the decision questions, target Assurance Level (AL0-AL6), claim types and gates to be evaluated, assessment type, provider model, resourcing and schedule, and the rationale linking depth to criticality (MCF-CAP-009) and planned change (MCF-CAP-023). The programme lead shall record and approve deviations from the plan.
assessmentCriteria: An approved assurance plan exists for the current period.
For each in-scope Capability Instance the plan states decision questions, target Assurance Level, claim types, gates, assessment type, provider model and schedule.

Planned depth is justified by criticality classification and planned material change; higher-criticality instances are not planned at a lower Assurance Level than lower-criticality instances without rationale.
Gates CG-01 to CG-15 are each planned for evaluation or recorded as APPROVED_NA with boundary rationale for each instance.
Deviations from the plan in the period are recorded and approved.
minimumEvidence: Planned change schedule used for planning

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current planning period
evidenceProfile.independence: Approval by the oversight committee, separate from the programme lead who prepared the plan
acceptableAlternatives: Engagement-level plan for a single assessment, approved by the decision authority
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED; condition requires an approved plan before reliance is extended

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the approved plan and approval record.
Reconcile plan coverage to the capability register and criticality classification.
Analyse planned depth against criticality and planned change; identify inversions.
Confirm each gate is planned or recorded as APPROVED_NA with rationale.
Review plan deviations and their approvals.
controls.applicability: Applies to continuing programmes. For a one-off assessment the engagement plan satisfies the control.
failureModes: Low-consequence systems assessed deeply while critical ones are not
Gates omitted from plan without rationale
Planned change not reflected in assurance schedule
Plan never approved
controls.testingSafety: Desk review of planning records only; draft plans for future periods are treated as confidential programme information.
controls.unknownRule: If criticality classification is unavailable, record a U1 UNKNOWN against this control and the depth-justification criterion is not met.
informativeReferences: ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information)

controls.title: Risk Appetite Linkage
controls.objective: Ensure that the organisation's stated risk appetite is translated into measurable limits for the AI capability (for example tolerated outcome interruption, tolerated loss of training progress, tolerated degraded-state duration) that drive impact tolerances, risk acceptance and decision conditions.
controls.requirement: The governing body shall approve a risk appetite statement covering service continuity, safety, data integrity and dependency concentration for the AI capability. The accountable executive shall translate it into measurable appetite limits per Service Outcome class and shall demonstrate that impact tolerances (MCF-CAP-010), risk-acceptance authority (MCF-GOV-007) and decision condition rules reference those limits.
assessmentCriteria: A risk appetite statement covering service continuity, safety, data integrity and concentration is approved by the governing body.
Appetite is expressed as measurable limits per Service Outcome class, with units.
Each impact tolerance in the capability profile is at or within the corresponding appetite limit, or the exceedance is approved by the governing body.
Risk-acceptance authority levels reference appetite limits.
Zero appetite for life-safety risk is stated and is not subject to risk acceptance below the governing body.
minimumEvidence: Appetite limits schedule per Service Outcome class
Reconciliation of impact tolerances to appetite limits

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Appetite statement and tolerances in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation performed by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Reconciliation of impact tolerances to appetite limits
acceptableAlternatives: Enterprise risk appetite with capability-specific annex
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: impact tolerances cannot be confirmed as governed; decision condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the approved risk appetite statement and confirm coverage of the four topics.
Confirm measurable limits with units per Service Outcome class.
Reconcile each impact tolerance to the appetite limit and identify unapproved exceedances.
Confirm risk-acceptance authority levels reference appetite limits and that life-safety risk is excluded from delegated acceptance.
Interview the accountable executive on how appetite is used in decision conditions.
controls.applicability: Applies to every organisation that owns an in-scope Capability Instance. Providers are not required to share their own appetite.
failureModes: Impact tolerances set without reference to governed appetite
Appetite expressed only qualitatively
Life-safety risk accepted operationally
Concentration risk absent from appetite
controls.testingSafety: Desk review only. Risk appetite statements are board-confidential and are viewed in a read-only data room where the organisation requires it.
controls.unknownRule: If appetite is stated only qualitatively, the measurable-limit criterion is not met (PARTIAL), not UNKNOWN; UNKNOWN is recorded only if the approved statement itself cannot be produced.

controls.title: Critical Gate Governance
controls.objective: Ensure that critical gates are evaluated, disposed and reported under governance that prevents them from being averaged away, re-scoped or overridden, and that every FAIL or UNKNOWN Gate Result reaches the decision authority with its controlling effect.
controls.requirement: The decision authority shall maintain a gate register for each in-scope Capability Instance recording, for every gate CG-01 to CG-15, applicability, CRITICAL control results, evidence sufficiency against the gate floor, Gate Result, controlling effect on the decision and closure criteria. The assurance programme lead shall ensure that Gate Results are computed by the roll-up rule of AIDCF-010, that no Gate Result is changed except by reassessment, and that APPROVED_NA is granted only by the decision authority with a boundary rationale.
assessmentCriteria: A gate register exists for each in-scope Capability Instance covering all fifteen gates.
In a sample of assessments, each recorded Gate Result reproduces when the AIDCF-010 roll-up rule is reapplied to the recorded CRITICAL control results and gate evidence.
Every APPROVED_NA was granted by the decision authority with a boundary rationale.
No Gate Result in the register history was changed without a corresponding reassessment record.
Every FAIL or UNKNOWN Gate Result appears with its controlling effect in the decision record and on the first page of the executive report.
No decision in the sample was issued at a state above the ceiling implied by its Gate Results.
minimumEvidence: Assessment records with CRITICAL control results and gate evidence
Decision records and executive reports for sampled assessments

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: All Assurance Decisions issued in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Roll-up reperformance by the assessor or independent reviewer, separate from the team that produced the Gate Results
mandatoryItems: Decision records and executive reports for sampled assessments
acceptableAlternatives: Machine-readable gate results exported from the assessment tool with full audit history
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decisions in the period may not be relied on above CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED until gate governance is evidenced
reassessmentTriggers: Change to AIDCF-010 roll-up rule or gate criteria

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the gate register and confirm all fifteen gates are recorded per Capability Instance.
Select assessments and reapply the AIDCF-010 roll-up rule to the recorded CRITICAL control results and evidence sufficiency.
Compare reperformed Gate Results with recorded results and investigate differences.
Review APPROVED_NA approvals and register history for changes without reassessment.
Trace FAIL and UNKNOWN Gate Results to decision records and executive reports; test decision state against the gate ceiling.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme issuing Assurance Decisions.
failureModes: Gate FAIL offset by a high domain score
Gate marked APPROVED_NA to avoid failure
Gate Result edited after review
Critical UNKNOWN omitted from executive report
controls.testingSafety: Reperformance uses exported records; no change is made to the system of record.
controls.unknownRule: If the CRITICAL control results underlying a Gate Result cannot be retrieved, record a U1 UNKNOWN against that Gate Result and treat the reperformance criterion as not met for that assessment.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard

controls.title: Independent Review
controls.objective: Ensure that a competent reviewer independent of the assessment team challenges method, evidence, gates, UNKNOWN treatment and decision wording before material conclusions are relied upon, and that the review demonstrably detects errors.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall ensure that every Assurance Decision supporting a material decision question is subject, before issue, to independent review by a reviewer who did not prepare or perform the assessment, has no conflict under MCF-GOV-021 and holds the competence defined in MCF-GOV-023. The independent reviewer shall record challenges, responses and dispositions, and shall have authority to withhold their concurrence. The programme lead shall periodically test review effectiveness by reperformance or by seeded-defect review.
assessmentCriteria: Every material Assurance Decision in the period has an independent review record dated before issue.
Each reviewer is independent of preparation and performance, conflict-free and competent for the domains reviewed.
Review records show challenge to method, evidence sufficiency, Gate Results, UNKNOWN treatment and decision wording, with dispositions.
No decision was issued over a withheld concurrence without escalation to the governing body or oversight committee.

Review effectiveness was tested in the period (reperformance of a completed review or seeded-defect exercise), and the test detected at least the defects the review was expected to detect, or the shortfall was addressed.
minimumEvidence: Independent review records for each material decision
Review effectiveness test record with seeded defects and detection outcome

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: All material decisions in the last twelve months and at least one effectiveness test
evidenceProfile.independence: Effectiveness test designed and scored by a party other than the reviewers tested
mandatoryItems: Independent review records for each material decision
Review effectiveness test record with seeded defects and detection outcome
acceptableAlternatives: External quality assessment of the review function by a second-party or independent provider, if it includes reperformance
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decisions are treated as self-reviewed; decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED for intended users beyond management

assessmentProcedure: List material decisions in the period and match each to a review record dated before issue.
Verify reviewer independence and competence declarations against engagement records and the competence register.
Examine review records for challenge across the five topics and for dispositions.
Check for decisions issued over withheld concurrence and their escalation.
Examine the review effectiveness test design, seeded defects and detection results; where no test exists, reperform one completed review and compare findings.
controls.applicability: Applies to Assurance Decisions relied on for material decision questions or by intended users beyond the management team. Internal-only diagnostic assessments at AL0-AL1 are excluded.
failureModes: Reviewer from the same team as the assessor
Review performed after issue
Review signs off without challenge
Reviewer lacks competence in the domain where the decisive gate sits
controls.testingSafety: Seeded-defect tests use copies of closed engagements with synthetic defects clearly labelled; they are never introduced into live engagements or live reports.
controls.unknownRule: If a review record exists but its date relative to issue cannot be established, record a U7 UNKNOWN and treat the decision as not independently reviewed for this control.
informativeReferences: ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information)
Institute of Internal Auditors Global Internal Audit Standards (quality assurance and improvement)

controls.title: Stakeholder Obligations
controls.objective: Ensure that obligations owed to stakeholders (customers, tenants, regulators, grid and water authorities, insurers, lenders, community) that constrain the AI capability are identified and translated into Service Outcomes, tolerances or constraints.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a stakeholder obligation register identifying each obligation that constrains an in-scope Capability Instance (for example contracted availability, data residency, grid connection conditions, water abstraction limits, noise and emission permits, insurance warranties), its source document, owner and the Service Outcome, tolerance or operating constraint into which it is translated.
assessmentCriteria: A stakeholder obligation register exists covering customers, tenants, regulators, utilities, insurers and financiers relevant to the instance.
Each obligation identifies its source document, owner and the Service Outcome, tolerance or constraint into which it is translated.
Grid connection and utility conditions that constrain load ramp rates, curtailment or on-site generation are captured.
A sample of source contracts and permits contains no constraining obligation absent from the register.
Obligations with conflicting requirements are identified and resolved by the capability owner.
minimumEvidence: Sampled source contracts, permits and connection agreements
Traceability from obligations to Service Outcomes and constraints

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Obligations in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample of source documents selected by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Traceability from obligations to Service Outcomes and constraints
acceptableAlternatives: Contract management system extract with obligation tagging
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected Service Outcome definitions qualified; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: New grid connection or permit condition

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the register and confirm stakeholder classes covered.
Sample source documents and identify constraining obligations absent from the register.
Trace each sampled obligation to a Service Outcome, tolerance or constraint.
Confirm grid and utility constraints on ramp rate, curtailment and generation are captured.
Review conflict identification and resolution.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Capability Instance.
failureModes: Grid connection ramp-rate limit unknown to operators of synchronous training workloads
Data residency obligation not reflected in recovery site selection
Insurance warranty breached by unrecorded configuration
Contracted availability exceeds designed capability
controls.testingSafety: Document review only; contract access governed by the evidence lead's restriction record.
controls.unknownRule: If a source contract or permit cannot be accessed, record a U2 UNKNOWN against the obligations it would contain.

controls.title: Regulatory Monitoring
controls.objective: Ensure that changes in law, regulation, permits and mandatory standards affecting the AI capability (energy, water, emissions, safety, data and critical-infrastructure regimes) are detected, assessed for impact and actioned in time.
controls.requirement: The compliance owner shall operate a regulatory monitoring process covering each jurisdiction in which in-scope infrastructure is located, record each relevant change with an impact assessment against Service Outcomes, controls and obligations, assign actions, and report material changes to the oversight committee. Changes affecting life safety, hazardous energy or reporting duties shall be escalated within the regulatory escalation time.
assessmentCriteria: Monitoring covers each jurisdiction and regulatory topic relevant to in-scope infrastructure.
Each relevant change in the period has an impact assessment and assigned actions.
Material changes were reported to the oversight committee.
Changes affecting life safety, hazardous energy or reporting duties were escalated within the escalation time.
Actions arising from regulatory changes are tracked to closure or have approved exceptions.

parameters.name: Regulatory escalation time for safety or reporting-duty changes

minimumEvidence: Regulatory monitoring scope by jurisdiction and topic
Change log with impact assessments for the period

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor or legal specialist checks a sample of known changes against the log
mandatoryItems: Regulatory monitoring scope by jurisdiction and topic
Change log with impact assessments for the period
acceptableAlternatives: Subscription legal-update service records combined with internal impact assessments
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: obligation completeness qualified; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Major regulatory change affecting energy, water or critical infrastructure

assessmentProcedure: Confirm monitoring scope by jurisdiction and topic.
Sample changes from the log and test impact assessments and actions.
Check escalation timing for safety and reporting-duty changes.
Confirm committee reporting of material changes.
Interview the compliance owner on sources and coverage limits.
controls.applicability: Applies to every organisation that owns or operates in-scope infrastructure. AIDCF does not determine legal compliance; this control assesses the monitoring process only.
failureModes: New energy-reporting duty missed
Permit condition change not reflected in operating envelope
Safety regulation change not escalated
Jurisdiction omitted from monitoring
controls.testingSafety: Desk review of the change log and impact assessments; no legal opinion is given or implied by the assessor.
controls.unknownRule: If the monitoring scope cannot be confirmed for a jurisdiction, record a U5 coverage-gap UNKNOWN for that jurisdiction.

controls.title: Customer Commitments
controls.objective: Ensure that what is promised to customers and tenants (SLAs, SLOs, credits, capacity reservations, recovery commitments) reconciles to the approved Service Outcomes and to the capability actually provided, so that commitments do not exceed assured capability.
controls.requirement: The commercial owner shall ensure that each customer or tenant commitment concerning availability, performance, integrity, capacity or recovery of an in-scope Capability Instance is recorded with its metric definition, measurement method and exclusions, and is reconciled by the capability owner to the approved Service Outcomes and tolerances before signature and after every change to either. Commitments exceeding approved Service Outcomes shall be approved by the accountable executive with a recorded risk acceptance.
assessmentCriteria: Each in-scope customer or tenant commitment is recorded with metric definition, measurement method and exclusions.
Each commitment is reconciled to an approved Service Outcome with the same metric definition and measurement window.
No commitment exceeds the approved Service Outcome tolerance without accountable-executive approval and risk acceptance.
Reconciliation was performed before signature for commitments made in the period.
Measurement of committed metrics uses the same data sources as Service Outcome measurement.
minimumEvidence: Approvals and risk acceptances for exceedances

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Commitments in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor selects contracts and reperforms reconciliation
acceptableAlternatives: Standard product terms plus a register of negotiated deviations
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decision condition recorded; Service Outcome adequacy for customer reliance qualified

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the commitment register and confirm completeness against the contract system.
Sample contracts and reperform reconciliation of metric definitions, windows and exclusions to Service Outcomes.
Identify exceedances and verify approvals and risk acceptances.
Confirm reconciliation dates precede signature.
Compare data sources for commitment reporting with those for Service Outcome measurement.
controls.applicability: Applies where in-scope capability is provided to external customers or internal tenants under defined commitments. Not applicable to purely internal research capability without commitments, with rationale.
failureModes: SLA promises accelerator availability beyond designed redundancy
SLA measured with different exclusions from Service Outcome
Recovery commitment shorter than tested recovery time
Capacity reservation exceeds power or cooling envelope
controls.testingSafety: Document review only; commercial terms are disclosed only to the extent needed and under restriction.
controls.unknownRule: If a contract cannot be accessed, record a U2 UNKNOWN for that commitment; it shall not be assumed to match the Service Outcome.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 19086 series (cloud computing service level agreement framework)

controls.title: External Reporting
controls.objective: Ensure that assurance conclusions communicated externally (customer statements, regulatory submissions, investor or public disclosures) are no stronger than the approved Assurance Decision, carry its limitations, and are approved before release.
controls.requirement: The decision authority shall approve every external communication that conveys an AIDCF assurance conclusion before release. The communications owner shall ensure that each such communication uses the controlled decision language of AIDCF-012, identifies the Capability Instance, scope, period and limitations, includes every gate FAIL and US4/US5 UNKNOWN relevant to the audience, contains no prohibited claim (certification, accreditation, universal safety or resilience), and is withdrawn or corrected when the underlying decision is suspended, withdrawn or superseded.
assessmentCriteria: Every external communication in the period conveying an AIDCF conclusion was approved by the decision authority before release.
Each communication uses controlled decision language and states Capability Instance, scope, period and limitations.
No communication contains a prohibited claim.
No communication omits a gate FAIL or US4/US5 UNKNOWN material to its audience.
Communications based on decisions later suspended, withdrawn or superseded were corrected or withdrawn within the correction time.

parameters.name: External correction time after decision suspension

minimumEvidence: Register of external communications conveying conclusions

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor compares each communication with the underlying decision record
mandatoryItems: Register of external communications conveying conclusions
acceptableAlternatives: Communications archive search by assessor where no register exists, with a coverage limitation recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decision condition recorded; continued external reliance is qualified

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the communications register and test completeness by searching published and submitted material.
Compare each communication with the underlying decision record for state, scope, period and limitations.
Screen for prohibited claims.
Check inclusion of material gate FAIL and US4/US5 UNKNOWN items.
Trace suspended or superseded decisions to correction or withdrawal of communications.
controls.applicability: Applies whenever an AIDCF conclusion is communicated outside the organisation issuing it.
failureModes: Marketing states the facility is 'AIDCF certified'
Customer statement omits a critical UNKNOWN
Communication remains published after decision suspension
Scope broadened in the summary beyond the assessed boundary
controls.testingSafety: Desk review of published and submitted material only; the assessor does not contact external recipients of the communications.
controls.unknownRule: If the completeness of the communications register cannot be tested, record a U5 coverage-gap UNKNOWN and limit the conclusion to communications identified.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard
ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information)
ISO/IEC 17000 (conformity assessment vocabulary and general principles)

controls.title: Conflict Management
controls.objective: Ensure that conflicts of interest affecting assessors, reviewers, specialists and decision authorities (financial, self-review, familiarity, advocacy, intimidation) are declared, evaluated and safeguarded before work begins and throughout the engagement.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall require every assessor, reviewer, specialist and decision authority to declare interests before assignment and on any change, shall evaluate each declared or identified threat (self-review, self-interest, familiarity, advocacy, intimidation), and shall apply and record a safeguard or exclusion. The programme lead shall prohibit outcome-contingent fees for assurance conclusions and shall exclude from assessment any person who designed, built, operates or advised on the control under assessment within the cooling-off period.
assessmentCriteria: Every person assigned to engagements in the period has a declaration dated before assignment.
Each declared or identified threat has a recorded evaluation and safeguard or exclusion.
No assessor assessed a control they designed, built, operated or advised on within the cooling-off period.
No engagement in the period used an outcome-contingent fee.
Changes in interests during engagements were declared and re-evaluated.
minimumEvidence: Declarations of interest for engagement personnel

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Engagements active in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor cross-checks declarations against design, change and advisory records independently of the declarant
mandatoryItems: Declarations of interest for engagement personnel
acceptableAlternatives: Provider's own conflict register, if the provider grants access to records for the engagement personnel
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results treated as not independently assessed; decision capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED for external reliance
reassessmentTriggers: Assessor previously involved in design or operation

assessmentProcedure: List engagement personnel and match each to a dated declaration.
Review threat evaluations and safeguards.
Cross-check assessors against design, change, operation and advisory records for the controls they assessed.
Inspect fee arrangements for outcome contingency.
Interview a sample of assessors on declaration practice.
controls.applicability: Applies to all engagements producing Control Assessments, Gate Results or Assurance Decisions.
failureModes: Assessor reviews a design they produced
Provider paid more for a favourable conclusion
Familiarity threat from long-standing operator relationship unaddressed
Decision authority holds a commercial interest in the outcome
