controls.testingSafety: Document review and interview only; personal declarations are handled as restricted personal data.
controls.unknownRule: If a declaration is missing for a person who assessed a control, record a U1 UNKNOWN and treat that person's results as not independently assessed until a retrospective declaration is evaluated.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 17020 (requirements for bodies performing inspection) - impartiality
ISO/IEC 17021-1 (requirements for bodies providing audit and certification) - impartiality

controls.title: Assessor Independence
controls.objective: Ensure that the organisational and reporting independence of the assessment function matches the reliance placed on its conclusions, so that preparation, performance, review and decision remain separable.
controls.requirement: The governing body shall define the independence level required for each class of intended reliance (management use, customer reliance, regulatory or financing reliance). The assurance programme lead shall ensure that for each engagement the assessment team's reporting line, provider model and separation of preparation, performance, review and decision meet the required level, and that the actual independence level is stated in the Assurance Statement.
assessmentCriteria: Required independence levels are defined per reliance class.
For each engagement, the provider model and reporting line meet the required level for the stated intended users.
Preparation, performance, independent review and decision are assigned to separate persons or roles as required by the level.
The Assurance Statement states the actual independence level and provider model.
Assessors did not operate controls or accept risks for management during the engagement.
minimumEvidence: Independence policy with levels per reliance class
Engagement records with team composition, provider model and reporting line

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Engagements completed in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessment of this control shall not be performed by the assessment function it concerns
mandatoryItems: Independence policy with levels per reliance class
Engagement records with team composition, provider model and reporting line
acceptableAlternatives: Engagement letters stating provider model and intended users
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: intended use of affected decisions restricted to management; condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Change of assessment function reporting line

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the independence policy and levels.
For each engagement, compare provider model, reporting line and role separation with the required level.
Compare stated independence level in Assurance Statements with engagement records.
Interview management and assessors on any operation of controls or risk acceptance by assessors.
controls.applicability: Applies to all engagements; the required level may be management-only for AL0-AL1 diagnostic work.
failureModes: Internal team reporting to the operations head issues customer-facing assurance
One person prepares, reviews and decides
Statement overstates independence
Assessor runs a failover test as operator
controls.testingSafety: Document review and interview only.
controls.unknownRule: If the reporting line of an assessment team cannot be established, record a U6 UNKNOWN and restrict intended use to management.
informativeReferences: Institute of Internal Auditors Three Lines Model
ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information)

controls.title: Competence Management
controls.objective: Ensure that assessors, specialists and reviewers are competent for the domains, technologies and test methods they apply (for example high-density liquid cooling, accelerator fabrics, protection studies, OT security), and that competence is current.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall maintain a competence framework for each role and domain (aligned to AIDCF-011 Part IX), a register recording each person's evidenced competence and its currency, and an assignment check confirming that every engagement assignment matches recorded competence. Where competence is not available internally, the lead shall engage a specialist under recorded reliance with scope and responsibility.
assessmentCriteria: A competence framework defines required knowledge, experience and evidence per role and domain.
A register records each person's competence with evidence and currency date.
Every assignment in the period matches recorded, current competence for the domain and method.
Specialist reliance is recorded with scope, competence evidence and responsibility.
Competence gaps identified in the period have development actions or were filled by specialists.

parameters.name: Competence currency period
parameters.basis: Programme parameter; illustrative, shorter for rapidly changing technologies

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assignments in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor verifies a sample of competence evidence at source (certificates, prior work records)
acceptableAlternatives: Provider-held competence records made available for engagement personnel
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected domain results carry a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 and a decision condition

assessmentProcedure: Review the framework against AIDCF-011 competence expectations and the technologies in scope.
Sample register entries and verify evidence at source.
Reconcile assignments to recorded competence and currency.
Review specialist reliance records.
Interview a sample of assessors on their domain experience.
controls.applicability: Applies to all engagement roles. AIDCF does not accredit people; this control assesses the programme's own competence management.
failureModes: Mechanical assessor without liquid-cooling experience assesses CDU failover
Lapsed competence for protection-study review
Specialist used without recorded scope
Reviewer unfamiliar with accelerator fabric failure modes
controls.testingSafety: Document review and interview only; personal data handled under minimisation.
controls.unknownRule: If competence evidence for an assigned person cannot be verified, record a U6 UNKNOWN and apply a CONF-2 ceiling to results that person produced.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 17024 (requirements for bodies operating certification of persons)
ISO 19011 (guidelines for auditing management systems) - competence of auditors

controls.title: Appeal and Challenge
controls.objective: Ensure that capability owners, operators and affected stakeholders can challenge a Finding, Gate Result or Assurance Decision through a defined, impartial process with recorded outcomes, without suppressing the original record.
controls.requirement: The decision authority shall maintain an appeal and challenge procedure that defines who may challenge, grounds, time limits, the impartial reviewer, evidence required, and possible outcomes. The decision authority shall ensure that every challenge is logged, decided by a person not involved in the challenged result, and that the original result, the challenge and the outcome are all preserved, with any change made only by reassessment.
assessmentCriteria: A procedure defines eligible challengers, grounds, time limits, reviewer, evidence and outcomes.
Every challenge in the period is logged and was decided by a person not involved in the challenged result.
Original results, challenges and outcomes are preserved; no original record was deleted or overwritten.
Changed results arising from challenges were produced by reassessment with new or re-evaluated evidence.
Challenges were decided within the procedure time limits or the delay was recorded.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Challenges raised in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Record history extracted by the assessor from the system of record
acceptableAlternatives: Where no challenges occurred, a walkthrough of the procedure with the decision authority, recorded as limited operating evidence
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence in contested results limited to CONF-2
reassessmentTriggers: Repeated challenges on the same gate

assessmentProcedure: Review the procedure.
Sample challenges and verify reviewer non-involvement and timeliness.
Inspect record history for preservation of original results.
Trace changed results to reassessment records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme issuing Findings, Gate Results or Assurance Decisions.
failureModes: Finding deleted after management objection
Challenge decided by the original assessor
Result changed without new evidence
No route for operators to contest a Finding
controls.testingSafety: Document and record inspection only.
controls.unknownRule: If record history cannot demonstrate preservation of originals, record a U7 UNKNOWN against challenged results.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 17020 (requirements for bodies performing inspection) - complaints and appeals
ISO/IEC 17021-1 (requirements for bodies providing audit and certification) - appeals

controls.title: Capability Register
controls.objective: Maintain an authoritative register of AI Capability Instances (for example a named training cluster, an inference service pool, a sovereign AI hall) so that every assurance claim is anchored to an identified, bounded instance rather than to a site or product.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a capability register in which each Capability Instance has a unique identifier, a description of the AI work it delivers (training, fine-tuning, inference, data preparation), its physical and logical location (site, hall, pods, clusters), its tenancy model, its lifecycle status, its accountable owner, its Service Outcomes and its current ArchitectureSnapshot reference. The capability owner shall reconcile the register to the scheduler or orchestration inventory and to the facility asset register at no more than the register reconciliation interval and after every material change.
assessmentCriteria: Every Capability Instance has a unique, stable identifier and the required attributes (work type, location, tenancy model, lifecycle status, owner, Service Outcomes, ArchitectureSnapshot reference).
Every accelerator cluster, pod or service pool present in the scheduler or orchestration inventory is assigned to exactly one Capability Instance or recorded as out of scope with rationale.
Every Capability Instance in the register maps to physical locations present in the facility asset register.
The last reconciliation is within the reconciliation interval and after every material change in the period.
No assurance report in the period refers to a capability not present in the register at the report date.

parameters.name: Capability register reconciliation interval
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, aligned to the rate of cluster expansion

minimumEvidence: Capability register extract with all attributes
Scheduler or orchestration inventory export (cluster, pod, node counts) dated within the reconciliation interval
Facility asset register extract for the halls and pods concerned
Reconciliation record listing unmatched items and dispositions

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register state at the assessment date and reconciliations over the preceding two intervals
evidenceProfile.independence: Scheduler and asset exports shall be produced by query executed or witnessed by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Capability register extract with all attributes
Scheduler or orchestration inventory export (cluster, pod, node counts) dated within the reconciliation interval
Reconciliation record listing unmatched items and dispositions
acceptableAlternatives: Configuration management database extract with capability tagging, where the CMDB is itself reconciled to the scheduler
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: the Capability Instance definition is unresolved; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE
reassessmentTriggers: New cluster, pod or service pool brought into service
Hall or site added to or removed from an instance

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the register extract and check each instance for the required attributes.
Extract the scheduler or orchestration inventory and reconcile clusters, pods and node counts to Capability Instances.
Reconcile instance locations to the facility asset register.
Analyse unmatched items and their dispositions; treat unexplained differences as Findings.
Check reconciliation dates against the interval and change events.
Compare capabilities named in reports issued in the period with the register.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assurance programme; there is no assurance subject without it.
failureModes: Assurance claim made about 'the data centre' rather than a defined instance
New cluster in production but not in the register
Same accelerators counted in two instances
Register location does not match physical deployment
controls.testingSafety: Read-only queries against scheduler and asset systems, executed by the system owner under assessor observation; no job submission or node draining is performed.
controls.unknownRule: If the scheduler or orchestration inventory cannot be accessed, the instance boundary is unverified: record a US5 UNKNOWN Record against the Capability Instance and do not rely on the register alone.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures)

controls.title: Capability Ownership
controls.objective: Ensure that each Capability Instance has one accountable owner who owns its Service Outcomes, tolerances, risks and remediation, and who has authority over the facility and IT resources needed to sustain them.
controls.requirement: The accountable executive shall appoint, for each Capability Instance, one capability owner with documented authority over the Service Outcomes, impact tolerances, risk acceptance within delegated limits, and the commitment of facility, platform and provider resources needed to meet them. The capability owner shall be identified in the capability register, the RACI and the decision-rights matrix, and a deputy shall be named for EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states.
assessmentCriteria: Each Capability Instance has exactly one appointed capability owner with a dated appointment.
The owner's authority over Service Outcomes, tolerances, risk acceptance limits and resource commitment is documented.
The owner is consistently identified in the capability register, RACI and decision-rights matrix.
A deputy is named and authorised for EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states.
Where facility and AI platform are run by different organisations, the owner's authority over each is established by contract or internal agreement.
minimumEvidence: Capability register, RACI and decision-rights extracts
Facility and platform agreements establishing owner authority where organisations differ

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Appointments in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor interviews the owner and deputy separately from the appointing executive
mandatoryItems: Capability register, RACI and decision-rights extracts
acceptableAlternatives: Organisational role description with explicit capability ownership, plus appointment of the current holder
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-13 Gate Result UNKNOWN for the instance; decision capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: Change of facility operator or platform provider

assessmentProcedure: Obtain appointment and authority records for each instance.
Reconcile owner identity across register, RACI and decision-rights matrix.
Confirm deputy appointment and authority for EMERGENCY and RECOVERY.
Review agreements establishing authority across facility and platform organisations.
Interview the owner and deputy on authority to commit resources and accept risk.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance in the register.
failureModes: Instance owned jointly by facility and platform teams with no single accountable owner
Owner lacks authority over the colocation facility
No deputy during a cooling emergency
Owner identity differs between registers
controls.testingSafety: Interview and document review only.
controls.unknownRule: If no appointment record exists, record a US4 UNKNOWN Record against CG-13 for the instance; de facto ownership described in interview is not sufficient.

controls.title: Lifecycle Status
controls.objective: Ensure that each Capability Instance's lifecycle status (planned, in design, in build, commissioning, in service, degraded-service, in change, retiring, retired) is accurate at all times so that the claim type, evidence and gates applied match the instance's real stage.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall define lifecycle status values and transition criteria for Capability Instances, shall record each status transition with date, approver and the evidence that the transition criteria were met, and shall not transition an instance to in-service until commissioning acceptance (MCF-CAP-022) is recorded. The assurance programme lead shall use the recorded status to select claim types and Assurance Levels for each assessment.
assessmentCriteria: Lifecycle status values and transition criteria are defined.
Every status transition in the period has date, approver and evidence that transition criteria were met.
No instance entered in-service status before commissioning acceptance was recorded.
The recorded status of each instance matches observed reality (for example production workloads are not running on an instance recorded as commissioning).
Assessment plans in the period selected claim types consistent with the recorded status.
minimumEvidence: Lifecycle status definitions and transition criteria
Status transition log for the period
Scheduler evidence of production workload on each instance

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Status transitions over the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor obtains scheduler or tenancy evidence independently of the status log owner
mandatoryItems: Status transition log for the period
Scheduler evidence of production workload on each instance
acceptableAlternatives: Change records for go-live with linked acceptance evidence
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: claim-type selection for the instance may be wrong; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Production workload observed on a non-in-service instance

assessmentProcedure: Review status definitions and transition criteria.
Sample transitions and verify approver and criteria evidence.
Compare in-service dates with commissioning acceptance dates.
Compare recorded status with scheduler or tenancy evidence of production use.
Check claim types in assessment plans against recorded status.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance.
failureModes: Customer workloads placed on a partially commissioned pod
Instance reported in service after partial retirement
Operation claims assessed on a capability still in build
controls.testingSafety: Read-only scheduler queries; no workload is moved or paused.
controls.unknownRule: If actual production use cannot be determined, record a U5 UNKNOWN against the status criterion and do not assume the recorded status is correct.

controls.title: Architecture Linkage
controls.objective: Ensure that each Capability Instance is linked to a current ArchitectureSnapshot that identifies the InfrastructureSystems, AssetInstances and Interfaces implementing its Required Functions (power, cooling, compute, storage, network, control plane), so that the assessment boundary is grounded in the real architecture.
controls.requirement: The capability architect shall maintain, for each Capability Instance, a current ArchitectureSnapshot linked in the assurance graph that identifies the Required Functions of each Service Outcome and the InfrastructureSystems, AssetInstances and Interfaces implementing them, including shared and external elements. The capability architect shall version the snapshot after every material change and shall reconcile it to as-built and as-configured evidence at no more than the architecture reconciliation interval.
assessmentCriteria: Each Capability Instance has a current ArchitectureSnapshot reference in the graph.
Every Service Outcome is linked to Required Functions, and every Required Function is linked to the InfrastructureSystems that implement it.
Shared elements (for example a facility water loop serving several halls, a common spine layer, a shared parallel file system) and external elements are identified as such.
A sample of graph links reconciles to as-built drawings, single-line diagrams, P&IDs, topology exports and cluster manifests.
The snapshot was versioned after each material change and reconciled within the interval.
minimumEvidence: Assurance graph extract of Outcome-Function-System links
As-built drawings, single-line diagrams and P&IDs for sampled links
Network topology and cluster manifest exports

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Snapshot current at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Technical exports taken from source systems by or in front of the assessor; drawings verified by site inspection for a sample
mandatoryItems: Assurance graph extract of Outcome-Function-System links
As-built drawings, single-line diagrams and P&IDs for sampled links
Network topology and cluster manifest exports
acceptableAlternatives: Where no graph exists, a controlled architecture register with function-to-system tables, with a traceability limitation recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-02 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: Expansion or re-cabling of a fabric

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the snapshot and graph extract and check Outcome-Function-System completeness.
Identify shared and external elements and confirm they are marked.
Select a sample of links stratified by domain and reconcile to drawings, topology and manifests.
Verify a subset of the sample by site inspection or live read-only query.
Check versioning against the change log.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance assessed above AL1.
failureModes: Assessment boundary drawn from a design that no longer matches the as-built state
Shared facility water loop not identified, hiding common-mode exposure
Storage system serving checkpoints omitted from architecture
Graph links to decommissioned equipment
controls.testingSafety: Site verification follows induction and escort rules; no panels are opened and no equipment is operated. Network and cluster exports are read-only.
controls.unknownRule: Any Required Function with no linked implementing system, or any link that cannot be reconciled to evidence, is recorded as a US4 UNKNOWN Record against CG-02.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures)
AIDCF-013 AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture

controls.title: Availability Outcomes
controls.objective: Define availability Service Outcomes for each Capability Instance in units that reflect AI work actually delivered (for example usable accelerator capacity, job-serving availability), with measurement window, exclusions and tolerance, so that power, cooling and platform continuity can be assessed against a stated target.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall approve, for each Capability Instance, availability Service Outcomes that state the unit of availability (for example fraction of committed accelerators schedulable and healthy, or fraction of inference requests served), the target, the measurement window, the maximum single-interruption duration, permitted exclusions (for example planned maintenance) and the data source for measurement. The capability owner shall ensure the outcomes are consistent with customer commitments (MCF-GOV-019) and impact tolerances (MCF-CAP-010).
assessmentCriteria: Each Capability Instance has at least one approved availability Service Outcome.
Each outcome states unit, target, measurement window, maximum single-interruption duration, exclusions and measurement data source.
The unit measures delivered AI capability (schedulable healthy accelerators, served requests or equivalent) rather than facility uptime alone.
Targets and exclusions are consistent with customer commitments and impact tolerances.
The measurement data source exists and produces the metric for the current period.

parameters.name: Availability target
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter set by the capability owner; illustrative only

parameters.name: Maximum single-interruption duration
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, derived from impact tolerance

minimumEvidence: Approved Service Outcome records for availability
Metric definition and measurement data source description
Reconciliation to customer commitments and impact tolerances

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Outcome definitions in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Approval by the capability owner, separate from the author; assessor reperforms metric derivation from source for one window
mandatoryItems: Approved Service Outcome records for availability
Metric definition and measurement data source description
acceptableAlternatives: Service level objective specification in the platform's SLO system, approved by the capability owner
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: Service Outcome definition unresolved; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE
reassessmentTriggers: Change of availability target or exclusions

assessmentProcedure: Obtain approved availability outcomes for each instance and check required fields.
Assess whether the unit measures delivered AI capability.
Reconcile targets and exclusions to customer commitments and impact tolerances.
Obtain the current-period metric and reperform its derivation from the data source for one window.
Interview the capability owner on how the target was derived.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-service or planned Capability Instance with an availability expectation; research instances with no availability expectation shall record that expectation explicitly rather than omit the outcome.
failureModes: Availability defined as facility power uptime while accelerators are unschedulable
No measurement window, so outages are averaged away
Exclusions so broad that the outcome is untestable
Target exceeds designed redundancy
controls.testingSafety: Desk review and read-only metric extraction; no fault is induced to measure availability.
controls.unknownRule: If the measurement data source cannot produce the metric, the outcome is defined but unmeasurable: criterion 5 is not met and a U1 UNKNOWN is recorded; this is not treated as a missing definition.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures) - availability classes

controls.title: Performance Outcomes
controls.objective: Define performance Service Outcomes that capture whether the infrastructure lets AI work run at its required speed (for example training goodput, step-time stability, inference latency percentiles, collective bandwidth), so that throttling, fabric congestion or storage stalls are visible as outcome failures rather than hidden behind availability.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall approve, for each Capability Instance, performance Service Outcomes that state the metric (for example training goodput fraction, median and tail step time, inference latency at a stated percentile, sustained accelerator power without thermal or power throttling), target, measurement method, measurement window, workload or benchmark reference, and the infrastructure conditions under which the target applies. The AI platform owner shall ensure the measurement method is implemented and its data retained.
assessmentCriteria: Each Capability Instance has at least one approved performance Service Outcome appropriate to its work type.
Each outcome states metric, target, method, window, workload or benchmark reference and infrastructure conditions.
At least one outcome detects infrastructure-induced degradation (thermal or power throttling, fabric congestion, storage stall).
The measurement method is implemented and produces data for the current period.
Targets are consistent with the design basis for power per accelerator, cooling capacity and fabric bandwidth.

parameters.name: Training goodput floor
parameters.unit: % of wall-clock time doing useful training progress

minimumEvidence: Metric and method specifications with workload reference
Design basis extracts for power, cooling and fabric

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Outcome definitions in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor or compute specialist reviews metric adequacy independently of the platform team
mandatoryItems: Metric and method specifications with workload reference
acceptableAlternatives: SLO specifications in the platform observability system, approved by the capability owner
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: Service Outcome definition unresolved; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE
reassessmentTriggers: New accelerator generation or workload type
Change of benchmark or measurement method
Change of design power per accelerator

assessmentProcedure: Obtain approved performance outcomes and check required fields.
Evaluate with a compute specialist whether the metrics detect infrastructure-induced degradation.
Confirm current-period data exist and reperform one metric derivation.
Compare targets with design basis for power, cooling and fabric.
Interview the AI platform owner on measurement implementation and retention.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance whose value depends on delivered compute speed; that is all training and inference instances.
failureModes: Accelerators thermally throttle under high facility water temperature while availability shows 100%
Fabric congestion halves training throughput unnoticed
Storage stalls during checkpointing degrade goodput
Performance target set without reference to power or cooling design
controls.testingSafety: Desk review and read-only metric extraction. Benchmark runs, if requested for corroboration, are scheduled by the platform owner on non-production capacity.
controls.unknownRule: If throttling or congestion data are not collected, record a U1 UNKNOWN against criterion 3; the outcome cannot then support CG-08 evaluation.
informativeReferences: MLCommons MLPerf benchmark suites (training and inference)
ISO/IEC 25010 (systems and software quality models) - performance efficiency
ASHRAE TC 9.9 thermal guidelines for data processing environments

controls.title: Integrity Outcomes
controls.objective: Define integrity Service Outcomes for model weights, checkpoints, training data and inference results so that silent data corruption, partial writes and configuration drift are treated as outcome failures with stated tolerances and detection expectations.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall approve, for each Capability Instance, integrity Service Outcomes stating which data and states are protected (model weights, optimiser state, checkpoints, datasets, configuration), the integrity property required (no undetected corruption, verified completeness, version provenance), the detection mechanism expected (checksums, end-to-end verification, accelerator error reporting), the tolerated detection latency and the required response. The data platform owner shall confirm that each detection mechanism exists.
assessmentCriteria: Integrity outcomes identify protected data and states, including checkpoints and model weights.
Each outcome states the integrity property, detection mechanism, tolerated detection latency and required response.
Undetected corruption of model weights and checkpoints relied upon for recovery has a tolerance of zero.
Hardware-originated silent data corruption on accelerators is addressed by a stated detection expectation.
The data platform owner has confirmed each detection mechanism exists for the current architecture.

parameters.name: Tolerated detection latency for dataset corruption

minimumEvidence: Detection mechanism description per protected data class

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Outcome definitions in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Storage or compute specialist reviews adequacy of detection mechanisms
mandatoryItems: Detection mechanism description per protected data class
acceptableAlternatives: Data protection design specification approved by the capability owner and containing equivalent statements
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: Service Outcome definition unresolved; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE
reassessmentTriggers: Change of checkpoint format or storage system
Incident of detected or suspected silent data corruption

assessmentProcedure: Obtain integrity outcomes and check coverage of protected data classes.
Review each detection mechanism with a storage or compute specialist.
Confirm zero tolerance for undetected corruption of recovery-critical checkpoints and weights.
Inspect configuration evidence that detection mechanisms exist (for example checksum settings, error-reporting configuration).
Interview the data platform owner on response procedures.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance that stores model state or data whose corruption would affect outcomes; that is all training instances and inference instances serving stored weights.
failureModes: Corrupted checkpoint discovered only on restore after a power event
Silent data corruption on an accelerator propagates into a trained model
Partial checkpoint write accepted as complete
Model weights deployed without provenance verification
controls.testingSafety: Desk review and read-only configuration inspection; no fault injection into production data.
controls.unknownRule: If no detection mechanism can be shown for a protected data class, criterion 5 is NONCONFORMING (not UNKNOWN); UNKNOWN applies only where mechanism existence cannot be verified.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-209 (security guidelines for storage infrastructure)

controls.title: Recovery Outcomes
controls.objective: Define recovery Service Outcomes for each Capability Instance (time to restore stated capacity, tolerated loss of training progress, restoration order, recovered-state verification) so that power, cooling, compute, storage, network and control-plane recovery can be assessed against a stated target.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall approve, for each Capability Instance, recovery Service Outcomes that state the recovery time objective for restoring a stated fraction of capacity, the recovery point objective (for training expressed as maximum lost training time, driving checkpoint interval; for inference as maximum state or configuration loss), the restoration order of dependent services (facility power, cooling, control plane, storage, fabric, compute, scheduler), and the verification required before declaring recovery. The capability owner shall ensure these outcomes are consistent with impact tolerances and customer commitments.
assessmentCriteria: Each Capability Instance has approved recovery outcomes with RTO for a stated capacity fraction and RPO.
For training instances, RPO is expressed as maximum lost training time and is consistent with the configured checkpoint interval.
A restoration order of dependent services is defined from facility power through to scheduler.
Verification criteria for declaring recovery are defined (for example accelerator health checks, fabric validation, checkpoint integrity).
Recovery outcomes are consistent with impact tolerances and customer commitments.

parameters.name: Recovery point objective (training)
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, constrained by checkpoint write time

minimumEvidence: Reconciliation to impact tolerances and commitments

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Outcome definitions in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Resilience specialist reviews consistency of RTO/RPO with architecture
acceptableAlternatives: Business continuity plan section for the instance, approved by the capability owner, containing equivalent content
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: Service Outcome definition unresolved; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE
reassessmentTriggers: Change of checkpoint strategy or storage
New dependency in the restoration path

assessmentProcedure: Obtain recovery outcomes and check RTO, RPO, restoration order and verification criteria.
Extract checkpoint interval configuration and compare with RPO.
Analyse restoration order against the architecture snapshot for missing dependencies.
Reconcile to impact tolerances and customer commitments.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance in service or in design.
failureModes: Checkpoint interval longer than the tolerated lost training time
Restoration order omits the control plane or identity service
No criteria for declaring recovery, so degraded capacity is declared recovered
RTO shorter than the time to restart cooling and stabilise facility water
controls.testingSafety: Desk review and read-only configuration extraction; recovery is not exercised under this control.
controls.unknownRule: If the checkpoint interval cannot be extracted, record a U1 UNKNOWN against criterion 2; the RPO is then unsupported for CG-10 evaluation.

controls.title: Criticality Criteria
controls.objective: Establish approved criteria for classifying Capability Instances, Service Outcomes and Required Functions by criticality, so that assurance depth, evidence floors, gate applicability and remediation priority follow consequence consistently.
controls.requirement: The accountable executive shall approve criticality criteria that classify Capability Instances, Service Outcomes and Required Functions into defined classes using stated consequence dimensions (safety, customer and contractual, financial, regulatory, reputational, societal dependency) and thresholds. The capability owner shall apply the criteria to every in-scope item, record the class and rationale, and re-apply them after every material change.
assessmentCriteria: Criticality criteria are approved and define classes, consequence dimensions and thresholds.
Every in-scope Capability Instance, Service Outcome and Required Function has a recorded class and rationale.
Reperformance of the classification for a sample yields the same class.
Classifications were re-applied after each material change in the period.
Criticality class is used to set assurance depth in the assurance plan (MCF-GOV-013).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Classifications in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reperforms classification for a sample
acceptableAlternatives: Business impact analysis outputs applying approved criteria
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: assurance depth may be mis-set; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: New Capability Instance or Service Outcome

assessmentProcedure: Review the criteria for classes, dimensions and thresholds.
Check completeness of the classification register.
Reperform classification for a sample.
Check reclassification after material changes and use in the assurance plan.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme.
failureModes: Inconsistent classification across instances
Criticality not updated after a customer contract change
Assurance depth unrelated to consequence
controls.testingSafety: Desk review and reperformance on records only.
controls.unknownRule: If rationale is missing for a classification, reperform it; record a U9 UNKNOWN only if reviewers cannot agree on the class.
informativeReferences: ISO 22301 (business continuity management systems) - business impact analysis

controls.title: Impact Tolerance
controls.objective: Set approved, measurable impact tolerances for each Service Outcome (maximum tolerable interruption, capacity reduction, lost work and integrity loss) that define the limit beyond which harm is unacceptable, and against which gates and decisions are evaluated.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall set, and the accountable executive shall approve, for each Service Outcome of each Capability Instance, impact tolerances stating maximum tolerable interruption duration, maximum tolerable capacity reduction and its duration, maximum tolerable loss of work (for example training progress), and tolerated integrity loss, each with units and the operating states to which it applies. Tolerances shall lie within risk appetite limits (MCF-GOV-014) or have governing-body approval of the exceedance.
assessmentCriteria: Each Service Outcome has approved impact tolerances with units and applicable operating states.
Tolerances cover interruption duration, capacity reduction with duration, loss of work and integrity loss.
Tolerances lie within risk appetite limits or the exceedance is approved by the governing body.
Tolerances are at least as stringent as customer commitments for the same outcome.
Tolerances are expressed so that a test or observation can show whether they were breached.

parameters.name: Maximum tolerable capacity reduction
parameters.unit: % of committed capacity for stated duration

minimumEvidence: Approved impact tolerance records per Service Outcome
Approval record by the accountable executive
Reconciliation to risk appetite and customer commitments

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tolerances in force at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Approval by the accountable executive, separate from the capability owner who set them
mandatoryItems: Approved impact tolerance records per Service Outcome
Approval record by the accountable executive
acceptableAlternatives: Business impact analysis with approved maximum tolerable periods of disruption
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: tolerance T in the top claim is undefined; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE

assessmentProcedure: Obtain tolerance records and approvals for each Service Outcome.
Check coverage of the four tolerance dimensions and operating states.
Reconcile to risk appetite limits and customer commitments.
Assess each tolerance for testability.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Service Outcome of every in-scope Capability Instance.
failureModes: Tolerance stated qualitatively ('minimal disruption')
Tolerance looser than customer SLA
No tolerance for degraded capacity, only total outage
Tolerance not approved
controls.testingSafety: Desk review only; tolerances are not validated by inducing disruption under this control.
controls.unknownRule: A tolerance that exists but is not testable makes criterion 5 PARTIAL; UNKNOWN is recorded only if the approval cannot be evidenced.

controls.title: Stakeholder Consequence
controls.objective: Identify who is harmed, and how, when each Service Outcome is not met (internal research teams, external tenants, downstream services relying on inference, safety-relevant users), so that criticality and tolerances reflect real consequence chains.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall record, for each Service Outcome, the stakeholder groups affected by its failure, the consequence mechanism (for example lost training progress, failed inference for a dependent service, breach of a regulatory obligation), the consequence severity under each operating state and any downstream dependency outside the boundary. The capability owner shall review the analysis with representatives of affected stakeholder groups at least once per planning period.
assessmentCriteria: Each Service Outcome lists affected stakeholder groups and consequence mechanisms.
Consequence severity is stated per operating state.
Downstream services outside the boundary that depend on the outcome are identified.
Representatives of affected stakeholder groups reviewed the analysis in the current planning period.
The analysis is reflected in criticality classification and impact tolerances.
minimumEvidence: Stakeholder consequence analysis per Service Outcome

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Analysis current within the planning period
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor interviews at least one affected stakeholder representative directly
mandatoryItems: Stakeholder consequence analysis per Service Outcome
acceptableAlternatives: Business impact analysis containing stakeholder consequence content
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: criticality and tolerance rationale qualified; decision condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the consequence analysis and check coverage per outcome and state.
Interview at least one affected stakeholder representative.
Check identification of downstream dependent services.
Trace the analysis to criticality and tolerance records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Service Outcome; where the only stakeholder is the owner's own research function, the analysis may be brief but is still required.
failureModes: Inference outage affects a dependent safety-relevant service not considered
Tenants' contractual exposure unknown to the owner
Consequence in degraded state ignored
controls.testingSafety: Interview and desk review only; stakeholder interviews do not disclose other stakeholders' confidential information.
controls.unknownRule: If an affected stakeholder group cannot be consulted, record a U2 UNKNOWN against its consequence entry.

controls.title: Priority Classification
controls.objective: Ensure that the relative priority of workloads, tenants and Capability Instances is defined and implemented in the mechanisms that allocate scarce resources during degradation (power capping, load shedding, thermal curtailment, scheduler pre-emption), so that the most critical outcomes are protected first.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall define priority classes for workloads, tenants and Capability Instances derived from criticality, and the AI platform owner and facility operator shall implement those classes in scheduler pre-emption policies, power-capping and load-shedding sequences and thermal curtailment procedures. The capability owner shall confirm at the priority reconciliation interval that implemented sequences match the defined classes.
assessmentCriteria: Priority classes are defined and derived from criticality classification.
Scheduler pre-emption and quota configuration implement the priority classes.
Power-capping and load-shedding sequences (EPMS or rack power management) and thermal curtailment procedures implement the same priority order.
Reconciliation of implemented sequences to priority classes is within the interval.
No safety-related or control-plane load is placed in a shed group ahead of AI workload.
minimumEvidence: Scheduler pre-emption and quota configuration export

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Configuration current at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Configuration exports taken from source systems under assessor observation
mandatoryItems: Scheduler pre-emption and quota configuration export
acceptableAlternatives: Where load shedding is manual, the switching procedure with shed order and evidence of operator training
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: degraded-state protection of critical outcomes unverified; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Change of shed sequence or EPMS logic

assessmentProcedure: Review priority class definitions and their derivation from criticality.
Export scheduler pre-emption and quota configuration and map to classes.
Export load-shedding and power-capping sequences and review thermal curtailment procedures; map to classes.
Confirm that safety and control-plane loads are not shed before AI workloads.
Check the reconciliation record date.
controls.applicability: Applies to instances where any resource can become constrained in a degraded state; that is all instances with shared power or cooling.
failureModes: Load shedding drops the highest-priority tenant first
Power capping applied uniformly, degrading critical inference
Control-plane servers in the same shed group as training racks
Scheduler pre-emption contradicts facility priority
controls.testingSafety: Read-only configuration export; shed sequences are not exercised under this control. Any sequence test is performed under the POW or THM domain controls with their authorisation requirements.
controls.unknownRule: If EPMS shed-sequence configuration cannot be exported, record a U2 UNKNOWN against criterion 3.

controls.title: Current Demand Baseline
controls.objective: Establish a measured baseline of the current IT, cooling and network demand of each Capability Instance (electrical load per pod and hall, heat rejected to air and liquid, facility water flow, fabric utilisation, storage throughput) from telemetry over a representative period, so that capacity and headroom claims rest on measurement rather than nameplate.
controls.requirement: The capacity manager shall establish, for each Capability Instance, a demand baseline derived from telemetry over at least the baseline period, covering electrical demand at rack, row, pod and hall level, heat load to air and to liquid, facility water flow and temperatures, and fabric and storage utilisation. The capacity manager shall state telemetry sources, resolution, gaps and calibration status, and refresh the baseline at the baseline refresh interval and after material change.
assessmentCriteria: The baseline covers electrical, thermal (air and liquid), facility water, fabric and storage demand for each instance.
The baseline is derived from telemetry over at least the baseline period, with sources, resolution and gaps stated.
Metering used for electrical and thermal baselines has current calibration or accuracy verification.
Baseline values reconcile to an independent source for a sample (for example utility meter, UPS output, CDU heat-meter readings).
The baseline was refreshed within the interval and after each material change.

parameters.name: Baseline period
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, should include representative workload cycles

parameters.name: Baseline telemetry resolution
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, transient characterisation is addressed in MCF-CAP-014

minimumEvidence: Demand baseline report with methods and sources
Telemetry extracts for the baseline period

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least the baseline period ending within the refresh interval
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reperforms aggregation for one hall or pod from raw telemetry
mandatoryItems: Demand baseline report with methods and sources
Telemetry extracts for the baseline period
acceptableAlternatives: Commissioning load measurements for an instance in service for less than the baseline period, with limitation recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: capacity headroom claims in POW and THM rest on unverified demand; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: New accelerator generation or cluster expansion
Telemetry outage longer than 10% of the baseline period

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the baseline report and check coverage across domains.
Obtain raw telemetry and reperform aggregation for one hall or pod.
Review meter calibration and telemetry gap records.
Reconcile a sample of baseline values to independent sources.
Check refresh dates against the interval and change events.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-service Capability Instance. For instances in design, MCF-CAP-015 forecasts substitute until in service.
failureModes: Headroom claimed from nameplate ratings while actual load is far higher
Liquid heat load not metered, so cooling headroom is guessed
Telemetry gaps conceal peak periods
Uncalibrated meters bias the baseline
controls.testingSafety: Read-only telemetry extraction; no meter is disconnected or tested under this control.
controls.unknownRule: If telemetry gaps exceed 10% of the baseline period or calibration status is unknown for a primary meter, record a U5 or U6 UNKNOWN and limit the baseline to the covered portion.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 30134 series (data centre key performance indicators)
ASHRAE TC 9.9 thermal guidelines for data processing environments

controls.title: Peak and Transient Demand
controls.objective: Characterise the peak and fast-transient demand of AI workloads (synchronous training power swings at iteration and checkpoint boundaries, job start and stop steps, inrush on restart, rapid heat-load changes on liquid loops) so that UPS, generation, grid connection, protection and cooling control are sized and tuned for real dynamics.
controls.requirement: The capacity manager, with the electrical and mechanical leads, shall characterise for each Capability Instance the peak demand and the transient demand profile, stating the maximum step change, ramp rate and repetition frequency of electrical load and heat load, measured at a resolution sufficient to resolve the transients, under representative workloads including job start, synchronous training, checkpointing and job failure. The capacity manager shall provide the characterisation to the POW and THM design owners and to the grid connection owner, and refresh it after any change in accelerator generation, workload type or power-management configuration.
assessmentCriteria: Peak electrical and thermal demand per pod and hall is stated with its measurement basis.
The transient profile states maximum step change, ramp rate and repetition frequency for electrical and heat load.
Measurements were taken at a resolution sufficient to resolve the stated transients and under the representative workload set (job start, synchronous training, checkpoint, job failure).
The characterisation was provided to POW and THM design owners and the grid connection owner, with recorded acknowledgement.
The characterisation was refreshed after each change in accelerator generation, workload type or power-management configuration.

parameters.name: Transient measurement resolution
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, must resolve the fastest step of interest

parameters.name: Maximum load step change
parameters.basis: Measured characteristic, not a design default

parameters.name: Maximum ramp rate
parameters.basis: Measured characteristic, not a design default

minimumEvidence: High-resolution power-quality or meter captures for representative workloads
Heat-load and facility water temperature transient captures from CDUs or heat meters
Distribution records to POW, THM and grid connection owners
Workload schedule showing representative workloads during capture

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Captures covering each representative workload type, taken since the last change in accelerator generation or power-management configuration
evidenceProfile.independence: Electrical specialist independent of the capacity manager reviews capture method and resolution
mandatoryItems: High-resolution power-quality or meter captures for representative workloads
acceptableAlternatives: OEM-provided transient profiles for the accelerator platform, only for DESIGN-stage use and with the limitation recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: POW and THM capacity and control-stability claims lack a demand basis; affected CG-05 and CG-06 evaluation records the gap
reassessmentTriggers: Change in power-capping or power-smoothing configuration
New workload type (for example very large synchronous training)
Protection trip or UPS alarm correlated with workload steps

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the characterisation report and check peak and transient attributes.
Examine raw captures and confirm resolution and workload coverage against the workload schedule.
Have an electrical specialist review the capture method and a mechanical specialist review heat-load transients.
Confirm distribution to POW, THM and grid connection owners.
Check refresh against change events.
controls.applicability: Applies to every instance running synchronous distributed training or other workloads with coordinated load changes; for inference-only instances with smoothed load the characterisation may be limited to peak and start-up steps, with rationale.
failureModes: Synchronous training load steps cause UPS or generator instability
Grid connection ramp-rate condition breached
Upstream protection trips on restart inrush
CDU control loop hunts under rapid heat-load swings, causing temperature overshoot
controls.testingSafety: Connection of power-quality analysers to live switchgear is hazardous-energy work and shall be performed only by authorised electrical personnel under the site's safe system of work and permit, with arc-flash PPE appropriate to the incident-energy study. The assessor observes; the assessor does not connect instruments. Workload scheduling for captures is arranged by the platform owner on capacity they control.
controls.unknownRule: If no capture at sufficient resolution exists, record a U1 UNKNOWN; average-interval telemetry shall not be used to infer the absence of transients.

controls.title: Growth Forecast
controls.objective: Forecast demand growth for each Capability Instance (accelerator count, power per accelerator, rack density, liquid-cooled fraction, fabric scale, storage capacity and throughput) over the planning horizon so that power, cooling, space and supply-chain lead times are committed before demand arrives.
controls.requirement: The capacity manager shall maintain a growth forecast for each Capability Instance over the planning horizon stating expected accelerator deployments by generation, power per accelerator and rack, liquid-cooled fraction, fabric and storage scale, with the assumptions and their sources, an uncertainty range, and the date by which each infrastructure commitment must be made given supplier and utility lead times. The capability owner shall approve the forecast and review it against actuals at the forecast review interval.
assessmentCriteria: A forecast exists per instance covering accelerators, power per rack, liquid-cooled fraction, fabric and storage over the planning horizon.
Assumptions are stated with sources and an uncertainty range.
Commitment dates are derived from stated lead times for power (including grid connection), cooling plant, and long-lead equipment.
The forecast is approved by the capability owner and was compared with actuals at the review interval.
Forecast values at the upper end of the uncertainty range are compared with site power and cooling limits.
minimumEvidence: Approved growth forecast with assumptions and uncertainty
Lead-time register for utility and long-lead equipment

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Forecast current at the assessment date and the last review against actuals
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reperforms one commitment-date derivation
mandatoryItems: Approved growth forecast with assumptions and uncertainty
Lead-time register for utility and long-lead equipment
acceptableAlternatives: Capital plan with capacity assumptions, approved by the capability owner
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence in forward-looking capacity claims limited to CONF-2
reassessmentTriggers: Forecast error beyond the uncertainty range

assessmentProcedure: Review forecast coverage, assumptions and uncertainty.
Reperform a commitment-date derivation from lead times.
Compare upper-range values with site limits.
Review forecast-versus-actual records.
controls.applicability: Applies to instances expected to grow within the planning horizon; static instances record 'no growth' as an approved forecast.
failureModes: Accelerators delivered before liquid cooling capacity exists
Grid connection lead time exceeds forecast need
Rack density growth exceeds floor loading or busway rating
Forecast never compared with actuals
controls.testingSafety: Desk review only; forecasts are commercially sensitive and handled under restriction.
controls.unknownRule: If the source of a key assumption (for example power per accelerator for an unreleased generation) cannot be identified, record a U6 UNKNOWN and widen the uncertainty range.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 30134 series (data centre key performance indicators)

controls.title: Scenario Demand
controls.objective: Characterise demand under adverse and recovery scenarios (simultaneous restart after power loss, checkpoint-restore storage bursts, failover of load to surviving halls, cooling recovery with high residual heat) and validate it in exercise, so that recovery does not itself overload power, cooling, fabric or storage.
controls.requirement: The capacity manager, with the resilience lead, shall model for each Capability Instance the demand on power, cooling, fabric and storage during the declared recovery and failover scenarios (including restart inrush, checkpoint-restore read bursts, re-scheduling storms and transfer of load to surviving fault domains), shall define the staging that keeps demand within supply during recovery, and shall validate the model and staging in at least one recovery exercise per exercise interval.
assessmentCriteria: Recovery and failover scenarios are listed with modelled demand on power, cooling, fabric and storage.
Restart inrush, checkpoint-restore bursts and re-scheduling load are included where applicable.
A staging plan keeps modelled demand within available supply in each recovery step.
At least one recovery exercise in the interval measured actual demand against the model and staging.
Differences between measured and modelled demand were analysed and the model or staging updated.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Model current at the assessment date; exercise within the exercise interval
evidenceProfile.independence: Exercise observed by a party independent of the team that built the model
acceptableAlternatives: Measured demand from a genuine recovery event, analysed against the model, in place of an exercise
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: recovery staging unvalidated; CG-10 evaluation records the gap; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Change of recovery architecture or checkpoint strategy
Recovery event with demand exceeding model

assessmentProcedure: Review the scenario list and modelled demand by domain.
Check staging plan against available supply per step.
Examine the exercise record and measured demand; observe an exercise if one is scheduled.
Compare measured with modelled demand and review the resulting updates.
controls.applicability: Applies to instances whose recovery outcomes require restoration of more than one fault domain or of large accelerator populations; small single-rack instances may record NOT_APPLICABLE with rationale.
failureModes: Simultaneous restart of all racks trips upstream breakers
Checkpoint restore saturates the storage system and extends RTO
Failover of load to a surviving hall exceeds its cooling capacity
Scheduler re-queue storm overloads the control plane
controls.testingSafety: Recovery exercises that energise or de-energise equipment, restart cooling plant or perform restart of accelerator populations are hazardous-energy and service-affecting activities: they require written authorisation from the capability owner and facility operator, a method statement with abort criteria and initial-state verification, permits under the site safe system of work, and the safety authority's right to stop. Assessors observe and do not operate equipment.
controls.unknownRule: If no exercise has measured recovery demand, the RESILIENCE claim is UNKNOWN (U1); the model alone supports only a DESIGN-level statement.
informativeReferences: ISO 22301 (business continuity management systems) - exercising and testing

controls.title: Load Envelope
controls.objective: Define and enforce the electrical and thermal load envelope of each Capability Instance (maximum IT load per rack, row, pod and hall; maximum liquid heat load per CDU loop; power per accelerator) and ensure mechanisms prevent load from exceeding it.
controls.requirement: The capability architect shall define, for each Capability Instance, the load envelope: maximum IT power per rack, row, pod and hall, maximum heat load per CDU or liquid loop, and permitted power per accelerator, each derived from the lowest-rated element in the power and cooling path in the declared redundancy state. The AI platform owner and facility operator shall implement enforcement (power capping, admission control for new racks or jobs, alarm thresholds) and shall verify that configured limits equal the envelope.
assessmentCriteria: The envelope states rack, row, pod, hall and CDU loop limits and power per accelerator.
Each limit is derived from the lowest-rated element in its path in the declared redundancy state, with the derivation recorded.
Enforcement mechanisms (power capping, admission control, alarm thresholds) are configured at or below the envelope.
Configured limits reconcile to the envelope for a sample of racks, pods and loops.
Envelope exceedances in the period, if any, were alarmed and actioned.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Configuration current at the assessment date and exceedances in the preceding twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Configuration exports taken from source systems under assessor observation
acceptableAlternatives: Where enforcement is procedural, deployment approval records showing envelope checks before each rack installation
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: overload protection of power and cooling paths unverified; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Rating change of any path element

assessmentProcedure: Review envelope limits and derivations against path element ratings.
Export enforcement configurations and alarm thresholds.
Reconcile a sample of configured limits to the envelope.
Review exceedance alarms and actions in the period.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-service Capability Instance.
failureModes: Rack load exceeds busway or PDU rating
CDU loop heat load exceeds capacity in N state after a pump failure
Power capping disabled for a benchmark and not restored
New racks deployed without envelope check
controls.testingSafety: Read-only configuration export; capping and admission control are not tested by overloading equipment.
controls.unknownRule: If the rating of a path element cannot be established, record a U1 UNKNOWN against the derived limit and treat the envelope for that path as unverified.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures)

controls.title: Environmental Envelope
controls.objective: Define the environmental envelope the AI equipment requires (air inlet temperature and humidity, facility water and technology cooling system supply temperature, flow and pressure, coolant quality) by reference to OEM specifications and recognised thermal guidelines, and ensure setpoints and alarms enforce it.
controls.requirement: The capability architect shall define, for each Capability Instance, the environmental envelope covering air inlet temperature and humidity, technology cooling system and facility water supply temperature, minimum flow and differential pressure, and coolant quality, derived from accelerator and server OEM specifications and the applicable ASHRAE TC 9.9 classes. The facility operator shall configure BMS and CDU setpoints and alarm thresholds within the envelope and shall reconcile them to the envelope after every OEM specification revision.
assessmentCriteria: The envelope covers air temperature and humidity, liquid supply temperature, flow, differential pressure and coolant quality.
Each envelope value cites the OEM specification or ASHRAE TC 9.9 class from which it is derived.
BMS and CDU setpoints and alarm thresholds for a sample of zones and loops lie within the envelope.
Setpoints were reconciled after each OEM specification revision in the period.
Where OEM limits differ across equipment sharing a loop, the most restrictive limit is applied.

parameters.name: Air inlet temperature range
parameters.basis: ASHRAE TC 9.9 recommended envelope for air-cooled IT; OEM limits prevail where stricter

parameters.name: Technology cooling system supply temperature upper limit

minimumEvidence: BMS and CDU setpoint and alarm configuration export

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Configuration current at the assessment date
evidenceProfile.independence: Mechanical specialist verifies envelope derivation; configuration exported under assessor observation
mandatoryItems: BMS and CDU setpoint and alarm configuration export
acceptableAlternatives: Commissioning records of setpoints, where no change has occurred since commissioning and change records confirm this
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: thermal protection of equipment unverified; CG-06 evaluation records the gap
reassessmentTriggers: Change of BMS or CDU setpoints

assessmentProcedure: Review envelope values and their sources.
Export BMS and CDU setpoints and alarm thresholds.
Reconcile a sample of zones and loops to the envelope, applying the most restrictive OEM limit.
Check reconciliation after OEM revisions.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-service Capability Instance; liquid-cooling criteria apply where liquid cooling is used.
failureModes: Facility water supply temperature raised for efficiency beyond accelerator OEM limits
Flow alarm threshold below OEM minimum
Mixed-generation loop set to the less restrictive limit
Humidity outside envelope causing condensation risk on cold plates
controls.testingSafety: Read-only export of BMS and CDU configuration; no setpoint is changed during assessment.
controls.unknownRule: If an OEM specification is unavailable for installed equipment, record a U1 UNKNOWN against the affected envelope value; a generic guideline value shall not be substituted without approval.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 thermal guidelines for data processing environments
ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures) - environmental control

controls.title: Duration Limits
controls.objective: Establish and validate how long each Capability Instance can sustain its outcomes in each degraded condition (UPS autonomy at actual load, thermal ride-through of liquid loops and rooms on loss of cooling, fuel autonomy, time on reduced redundancy) so that response and recovery actions are timed within real limits.
controls.requirement: The capability architect shall state, for each Capability Instance, duration limits for each declared degraded condition: battery autonomy at measured load, thermal ride-through time before equipment limits are reached on loss of chilled or facility water, generator fuel autonomy, and maximum time on reduced redundancy. The facility operator shall validate each limit by test, measurement or validated model at the duration validation interval and after material change, and shall align alarms and runbooks to the validated limits.
assessmentCriteria: Duration limits are stated for each declared degraded condition, including UPS autonomy, thermal ride-through, fuel autonomy and reduced-redundancy time.
Each limit is validated by test, measured event or validated model at current load.
Thermal ride-through validation accounts for the actual liquid-cooled heat load and thermal mass of the loops.
Alarms and runbooks trigger actions with sufficient margin before each validated limit.
Validation is within the interval and after material change.

parameters.name: Thermal ride-through on loss of facility water
parameters.basis: Validated characteristic, not a design default

minimumEvidence: UPS autonomy test or discharge record at measured load
Thermal ride-through test, event record or validated model
Fuel autonomy calculation with measured consumption

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Validations within the duration validation interval at current load
evidenceProfile.independence: Test witnessed by a party independent of the facility operator or by an electrical/mechanical specialist assessor
mandatoryItems: UPS autonomy test or discharge record at measured load
Thermal ride-through test, event record or validated model
acceptableAlternatives: Validated computational model calibrated against a measured event, for thermal ride-through where a test is not safe
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: response timing unsupported; CG-05, CG-06 and CG-10 evaluations record the gap; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Load increase beyond the validated level
Event where a limit was approached or exceeded

assessmentProcedure: Review stated limits for completeness across degraded conditions.
Examine validation evidence for each limit and its load basis.
Have a mechanical specialist review thermal ride-through validation against liquid heat load and loop thermal mass.
Compare alarm and runbook timings with validated limits and margin.
Observe a scheduled validation test where one occurs in the assessment window.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-service instance; fuel autonomy is not applicable where no on-site generation exists, with rationale.
failureModes: UPS autonomy at today's AI load is a fraction of the design value
Liquid-cooled racks exceed thermal limits within seconds of facility water loss, faster than runbook response
Fuel autonomy calculated from nameplate consumption
Extended operation on N redundancy unnoticed
controls.testingSafety: UPS discharge and cooling-interruption tests are hazardous and service-affecting: they require written authorisation from the facility operator and capability owner, an engineered method statement with initial-state verification, abort criteria and restoration steps, load banks or protected test loads where possible, permits under the site safe system of work, and a safety authority able to stop the test. Thermal ride-through on production accelerators shall not be tested by deliberately stopping cooling; a calibrated model or measured event is used instead.
controls.unknownRule: If a limit has never been validated at current load, record a U3 (stale) or U1 UNKNOWN; design values shall not be presented as validated.
informativeReferences: IEEE 1188 (maintenance and testing of VRLA batteries)

controls.title: State-Specific Limits
controls.objective: Define and enforce limits that apply only in non-normal operating states (maintenance with reduced redundancy, degraded cooling, emergency, recovery, transition) so that permitted load, activities and changes are restricted when margins are smaller.
controls.requirement: The capability architect shall define for each Capability Instance the limits applying in each non-normal operating state, including maximum permitted IT load, prohibited activities (for example concurrent maintenance on both power paths, firmware rollouts, large job starts), required approvals and maximum duration. The facility operator and AI platform owner shall implement these limits in maintenance permits, change freezes, scheduler policies and power-capping profiles, and shall record state entry and exit.
assessmentCriteria: State-specific limits are defined for MAINTENANCE, DEGRADED, EMERGENCY, RECOVERY and TRANSITION states.
Limits include permitted load, prohibited activities, approvals and maximum duration.
Maintenance permits, change freezes, scheduler policies and capping profiles implement the limits.
State entry and exit events in the period are recorded.
For a sample of non-normal state periods, telemetry and change records show the limits were respected.

parameters.name: Maximum IT load in reduced-redundancy maintenance

minimumEvidence: Maintenance permits and change freeze records
Scheduler and capping profile configuration for non-normal states
Telemetry and change records for sampled state periods

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Non-normal state periods in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor samples state periods from the log and obtains telemetry independently
mandatoryItems: Telemetry and change records for sampled state periods
acceptableAlternatives: Maintenance window records with associated telemetry where no formal state log exists, with limitation recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: containment in non-normal states unverified; CG-09 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Review limit definitions for each non-normal state.
Inspect implementation in permits, freezes, scheduler policies and capping profiles.
Sample non-normal state periods from the log.
Analyse telemetry and change records for each sampled period against the limits.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-service instance.
failureModes: Full AI load run during maintenance on one power path, so a second fault drops the hall
Firmware rollout during degraded cooling
Large job start during recovery overloads restored supply
Maintenance state left open beyond its duration
controls.testingSafety: Record and telemetry review only; no state transition is induced.
controls.unknownRule: If state entry and exit cannot be reconstructed for a period, record a U5 UNKNOWN for that period.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures) - operational information

controls.title: Design-to-Operation Traceability
controls.objective: Ensure that design intent (Service Outcomes, envelopes, redundancy, fault domains) is traceable through build and commissioning into the operating configuration, so that differences between designed, installed, commissioned and operated states are visible.
controls.requirement: The capability architect shall maintain traceability from each Service Outcome and envelope to design requirements, to as-built records, to commissioning results and to the current operating configuration for each Capability Instance, recording deviations at each stage with disposition.
