The facility operator and AI platform owner shall provide current configuration evidence for reconciliation at the traceability reconciliation interval.
assessmentCriteria: Traceability links exist from Service Outcomes and envelopes to design requirements, as-built records, commissioning results and operating configuration.
Deviations at each stage are recorded with disposition.
A sample traced end to end shows no undisclosed deviation between design and operating configuration.
Reconciliation to current configuration is within the interval.
Designed, installed, commissioned and operated states are recorded distinctly, not overwritten.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current configuration and the most recent design and commissioning baseline
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor selects trace samples and obtains configuration independently
acceptableAlternatives: Per-system design basis and commissioning dossiers linked by system identifier
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: IMPLEMENTATION claims in infrastructure domains qualified; CG-02 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the traceability matrix or graph extract.
Select samples across domains and trace each from outcome to operating configuration.
Compare deviations found with the deviation register.
Confirm states are recorded distinctly and reconciliation is within interval.
controls.applicability: Applies to every instance assessed at AL3 or above.
failureModes: Redundancy designed as 2N but operated as N+1 after an undocumented change
As-built CDU configuration differs from design
Commissioning results overwritten by later configuration
Design envelope not carried into operating limits
controls.testingSafety: Read-only configuration exports; site inspection under escort without operating equipment.
controls.unknownRule: If any stage record (design, as-built, commissioning) is missing for a sampled trace, record a U1 UNKNOWN for that stage and do not infer it from the adjacent stage.

controls.title: Commissioning Acceptance
controls.objective: Ensure that a Capability Instance, or an expansion of it, is accepted into service only after integrated commissioning demonstrates that the combined power, cooling, control, compute, storage and network systems deliver the Service Outcomes under normal and declared degraded conditions.
controls.requirement: The commissioning manager shall plan and execute integrated systems testing for each new or expanded Capability Instance that exercises power, cooling, control systems, compute, storage and fabric together at representative load, including declared failure transfers (for example loss of a UPS module, CDU pump failover, loss of a fabric link) and their effect on Service Outcomes. The capability owner shall sign acceptance only when acceptance criteria tied to Service Outcomes are met or deviations are dispositioned, and shall record the accepted configuration baseline.
assessmentCriteria: An integrated test plan exists with acceptance criteria traced to Service Outcomes and envelopes.
Tests were executed at representative load, including heat load to liquid loops where liquid cooled.
Declared failure transfers were exercised and their effect on Service Outcomes measured.
Every failed or deferred test has a disposition approved by the capability owner before acceptance.
Acceptance was signed by the capability owner and the accepted configuration baseline recorded.
Commissioning results are retained as E4 evidence with test conditions and anomalies.

parameters.name: Commissioning test load
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; illustrative, using load banks or representative workloads

minimumEvidence: Integrated test plan with acceptance criteria
Executed test scripts with results, conditions and anomalies
Signed acceptance and accepted configuration baseline

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Commissioning of the current configuration or the latest expansion
evidenceProfile.independence: Commissioning witnessed by a commissioning authority independent of the installing contractor
mandatoryItems: Integrated test plan with acceptance criteria
Executed test scripts with results, conditions and anomalies
Signed acceptance and accepted configuration baseline
acceptableAlternatives: For an expansion of an accepted instance, a delta integrated test covering affected systems plus regression on shared systems
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: operating outcomes rest on unaccepted configuration; CG-02 and CG-08 evaluations record the gap
reassessmentTriggers: Failure in service of a function accepted at commissioning

assessmentProcedure: Review the test plan and trace acceptance criteria to Service Outcomes.
Examine executed scripts for load, conditions and anomalies.
Examine failure-transfer tests and measured outcome effects.
Review deviation dispositions and acceptance signature.
Reconcile accepted baseline to current configuration; observe commissioning if in progress.
controls.applicability: Applies to every new Capability Instance and every expansion or major reconfiguration; for capability in a colocation facility, facility-level commissioning by the provider is assessed through MCF-SUP controls and integrated testing remains required at the capability boundary.
failureModes: Systems commissioned individually but never together under heat load
CDU failover untested at full liquid load
Acceptance signed with open critical tests
Accepted baseline not recorded, so later drift is undetectable
controls.testingSafety: Integrated systems tests involve energised switching, load banks, pressurised liquid loops and induced failures: they require an approved commissioning method statement, initial-state verification, abort criteria, isolation and permits under the site safe system of work, competent operators, and a safety authority with stop authority. Assessors observe from a designated position and do not operate equipment.
controls.unknownRule: If test records lack conditions (load, state, configuration), record a U8 UNKNOWN against the affected test; the result shall not be used as effectiveness evidence.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE Standard 202 (commissioning process for buildings and systems)
ISO/IEC 22237 series (data centre facilities and infrastructures)

controls.title: Material Change Impact
controls.objective: Ensure that every proposed change that could affect a Capability Instance's Service Outcomes, envelopes, fault domains or dependencies (accelerator refresh, density increase, cooling conversion, fabric expansion, provider change) is assessed for capability impact, validated after implementation and used to trigger reassessment.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall ensure that every change classified as material for a Capability Instance has a capability impact assessment before approval that identifies affected Service Outcomes, envelopes, fault domains, dependencies, controls, gates and evidence; defines post-change validation; and identifies assurance claims to be suspended or reassessed. The change authority shall not approve a material change without the impact assessment, and the capability owner shall confirm post-change validation before the change is closed.
assessmentCriteria: Materiality criteria for capability changes are defined and applied to every change in the period.
Every material change in the sample had a capability impact assessment before approval identifying outcomes, envelopes, fault domains, dependencies, controls, gates and evidence.
Every material change in the sample had post-change validation confirmed by the capability owner before closure.
Assurance claims identified as affected were suspended or scheduled for reassessment.
A sample of changes classified non-material shows no misclassification.
minimumEvidence: Change log for the period with materiality classification
Capability impact assessments for sampled material changes

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: All changes in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor selects samples of both material and non-material changes from the full change log
mandatoryItems: Change log for the period with materiality classification
Capability impact assessments for sampled material changes
acceptableAlternatives: Programme-level impact assessment for a coordinated set of changes, if each change references it
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-14 Gate Result UNKNOWN; decision capped at LIMITED

assessmentProcedure: Review materiality criteria and their application across the change log.
Sample material changes and verify impact assessments preceded approval.
Verify post-change validation before closure.
Trace affected claims to suspension or reassessment records.
Sample non-material changes and test classification.
controls.applicability: Applies to every change affecting an in-scope Capability Instance, whether initiated by the owner, operator or a provider.
failureModes: Accelerator refresh raises rack power beyond the cooling envelope without assessment
Conversion from air to liquid cooling not treated as material
Provider changes a shared dependency without notification
Change closed without validation
Prior assurance relied on after material change
controls.testingSafety: Record review only; post-change validation tests are assessed under the relevant domain controls with their own safety requirements.
controls.unknownRule: If changes made by providers cannot be enumerated, record a U10 UNKNOWN (dependency unknown) against the provider's changes and treat CG-14 as UNKNOWN for affected dependencies.

controls.title: Retirement Control
controls.objective: Ensure that retiring all or part of a Capability Instance (decommissioning racks, draining liquid loops, removing storage, ending a provider service) is controlled so that remaining outcomes, data protection and safety are not compromised and records are updated.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall approve a retirement plan for each retirement of capability or infrastructure that identifies remaining Service Outcomes affected, dependencies to be removed or transferred, data sanitisation of storage media and accelerator memory, safe isolation and draining of liquid loops and disposal of batteries and coolant, and updates to the capability register, architecture snapshot and assurance graph. The facility operator shall confirm completion of each step with evidence.
assessmentCriteria: Each retirement in the period had an approved plan covering affected outcomes, dependencies, data sanitisation, safe isolation and disposal, and record updates.
Data sanitisation of retired storage media is evidenced to the required sanitisation level.
Liquid loops were isolated and drained, and batteries and coolant disposed of under safe-work and environmental requirements.
Capability register, architecture snapshot and assurance graph were updated within the record update time.
Remaining Service Outcomes were verified after retirement.
minimumEvidence: Register, snapshot and graph update records

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Retirements completed in the twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Sanitisation evidence from the performing party verified against asset serial numbers by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Register, snapshot and graph update records
acceptableAlternatives: Physical destruction certificates for media where sanitisation was by destruction
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: residual data exposure or stale architecture records; decision condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: List retirements in the period and obtain plans.
Reconcile sanitisation records to retired asset serial numbers.
Review isolation, draining and disposal records.
Verify record updates and post-retirement outcome verification.
controls.applicability: Applies whenever capability or infrastructure supporting an in-scope instance is retired; not applicable in a period with no retirements.
failureModes: Storage media containing model weights leave site unsanitised
Shared loop drained while still serving adjacent racks
Retired equipment remains in the architecture snapshot
Removal of a shared PDU drops a remaining rack
controls.testingSafety: Isolation and draining of liquid loops and removal of batteries are hazardous activities performed only by authorised personnel under permit and lock-out/tag-out; the assessor reviews records and, if observing, does so from a safe position without handling equipment or fluids.
controls.unknownRule: If sanitisation evidence cannot be matched to an asset serial number, record a U6 UNKNOWN for that asset and report it as a potential data exposure.

controls.title: Asset-to-Function Mapping
controls.objective: Every Required Function of the declared Capability Instance is traceable to the specific InfrastructureSystems and AssetInstances that implement it in each declared operating state, so that the consequence of losing, maintaining or changing any asset is known before it happens.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a versioned asset-to-function map that links each Required Function to the InfrastructureSystems and AssetInstances (including redundant and standby units) that implement it, stated separately for each declared operating state. The facility operator shall reconcile the map against the as-built asset register and current configuration at least at the interval set in the capability profile and after every material change, and shall record every asset that cannot be mapped, or every function with no identified implementing asset, as an UNKNOWN Record.
assessmentCriteria: Every Required Function in the assessment boundary has at least one IMPLEMENTED_BY relationship to an InfrastructureSystem, and every InfrastructureSystem resolves to identified AssetInstances.
Mappings are stated per operating state; at minimum NORMAL, MAINTENANCE (each planned maintenance configuration of a redundant path) and DEGRADED are distinguished where the implementing set differs.
A reconciliation sample of physical assets (by asset tag and location) and configuration items matches the map with no unexplained discrepancy above the profile tolerance.
Assets present in the as-built register but not mapped to any function are listed and dispositioned (mapped, excluded with rationale, or UNKNOWN).
The map is versioned, carries an effective date, and was re-validated after each material change recorded in the change log for the period.

parameters.name: Mapping completeness for critical Required Functions
parameters.basis: Illustrative; any unmapped critical function defeats dependency visibility, so the profile normally sets 100%.

parameters.name: Reconciliation sample size
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set by AIDCF-009 sampling rules and population size.

parameters.name: Reconciliation interval
parameters.basis: Illustrative; shorten for estates with high deployment churn such as accelerator cluster expansion.

minimumEvidence: Current versioned asset-to-function map (export from CMDB/DCIM or dependency graph) with effective date and owner.
As-built asset register extract for the boundary (asset tag, model, location, serial) at the same date.
Single-line diagrams, P&IDs and network topology exports used to derive the map.
Reconciliation record for the sample: asset-by-asset match/mismatch with resolution.
List of unmapped assets and unmapped functions with disposition.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Point-in-time reconciliation no older than the reconciliation interval; change log covering the 12 months preceding the assessment.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation sample shall be selected and checked by a person other than the map author; physical verification by walk-down or E2 export, not by the author's attestation.
acceptableAlternatives: Where no CMDB/DCIM exists, a controlled spreadsheet register is acceptable if versioned, owned and reconciled by walk-down with photographic or inspection evidence.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-02 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: Addition, removal or relocation of assets implementing a Required Function
Change to redundancy configuration or maintenance arrangement
New Capability Instance or Service Outcome definition

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the Required Function list for the Capability Instance and the current asset-to-function map with its version and effective date.
Check that every Required Function has implementing systems and assets per declared operating state; list gaps.
Select a reconciliation sample per InfrastructureSystem using AIDCF-009 sampling rules, weighted towards assets in recent changes.
Verify sampled assets by walk-down or authoritative E2 export (tag, location, serial, model) against the map and as-built register.
Extract assets in the register that are not mapped and confirm their disposition.
Confirm map re-validation after each material change in the period by cross-referencing the change log.
Record Findings for mismatches and UNKNOWN Records for unmappable functions or assets.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment where a Capability Instance is declared. Not applicable only for a pure DESIGN-stage assessment where no asset yet exists; in that case MCF-DEP-003 and the design-stage dependency model carry the obligation.
failureModes: Required Function silently implemented by an unregistered asset
Maintenance on an asset not known to support a function (scenario X04)
Map drift after cluster expansion or rack moves
Redundant unit recorded but not physically present or not connected
controls.testingSafety: Walk-downs in electrical rooms, plant spaces and liquid-cooled halls shall be escorted and follow site access and PPE rules; no covers, panels or enclosures shall be opened for verification without a permit issued under MCF-OPS-007.
controls.unknownRule: Record an UNKNOWN Record (U10 Dependency unknown, or U5 Coverage gap) for each Required Function with no verifiable implementing asset and for each sampled asset whose function cannot be established; any such UNKNOWN on a critical Required Function is US4.
informativeReferences: EN 50600-3-1 (data centre management and operational information)

controls.title: Upstream Dependency Mapping
controls.objective: Every material upstream dependency of each Required Function is traced to the point where it leaves the assessment boundary and, where knowable, to the first shared upstream node, so that external and shared reliance is visible rather than assumed.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain an upstream dependency graph for each Required Function that records, for every dependency, the provider, dependency type (electrical, thermal, hydraulic, network, control-system, timing/information, human/procedural, supplier/contractual, geographic, capacity), strength, applicable operating states and owner, following the AIDCF-003 dependency record schema. Tracing shall continue at least to the boundary exit point (for example the utility point of connection, carrier demarcation, facility-water flange, fuel delivery point, cloud or SaaS endpoint) and to the first known shared upstream node beyond it. The dependency owner shall record any trace that cannot be completed as an UNKNOWN Record.
assessmentCriteria: Each Required Function has an upstream graph covering all dependency classes in AIDCF-003 that apply; classes judged not applicable are stated with rationale.
Each dependency record has provider, type, strength, applicable states, owner and evidence populated, or the missing attribute is recorded as UNKNOWN.

External dependencies are traced to the boundary exit point and to the first known shared upstream node (for example grid substation or transmission circuit, carrier point of presence, cloud region, identity provider tenant).
Timing/information dependencies (DNS, NTP/PTP, DHCP/PXE, IPAM, certificate authorities, licence servers, identity providers) are included for compute, network, storage and control-system functions.
A sample of dependency records is corroborated by an independent source (contract, provider route record, configuration export or test).

parameters.name: Minimum trace depth beyond boundary
parameters.basis: Illustrative; deeper tracing is set in the profile where concentration risk is high.

parameters.name: Corroboration sample
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set per AIDCF-009 sampling rules.

minimumEvidence: Upstream dependency graph or register for each Required Function, with version and owner.
Utility connection agreement or point-of-connection diagram; carrier circuit and route records; facility-water and fuel supply records.
Configuration exports showing DNS, time, identity, licence and repository endpoints used by compute, network, storage and control systems.
UNKNOWN Records for traces that could not be completed.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current at assessment date; graph reviewed within the revalidation interval of MCF-DEP-024.
evidenceProfile.independence: Corroboration from a source independent of the graph author (provider document, configuration export or technical test).
mandatoryItems: Upstream dependency graph per Required Function
acceptableAlternatives: Provider attestations may substitute for route records only where the provider refuses disclosure; the dependency is then recorded with confidence no higher than CONF-2 and an UNKNOWN Record for the undisclosed attribute.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-15 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: New or changed provider, circuit, utility connection or cloud/SaaS service
Change to control-system or management-plane architecture
Provider notification of network or route change

assessmentProcedure: Select the Required Functions in scope and obtain their upstream graphs.
Check graph completeness against the AIDCF-003 dependency classes for each function; list omitted classes.
For external dependencies, confirm the boundary exit point and first shared upstream node from provider documents.
Extract configuration for timing, naming, identity, licensing and repository endpoints from a sample of compute, network, storage and BMS/EPMS systems and confirm each endpoint appears in the graph.
Corroborate the sampled records against independent evidence and record conflicts.
Record UNKNOWN Records for incomplete traces with US severity.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Required Function. Depth beyond the boundary may be limited by provider disclosure; that limitation is recorded, not treated as not applicable.
failureModes: Hidden dependency on a shared upstream node (substation, carrier POP, cloud region)
Unrecorded reliance on an external identity provider or licence server
Time-source dependency not recorded (scenario X13)
Dependency on a provider assumed to be diverse but sharing a parent
controls.testingSafety: Configuration extraction shall use read-only accounts and approved export methods; no live query against BMS/EPMS or PLCs shall be made without authorisation from the control-system owner.
controls.unknownRule: An incomplete upstream trace for a dependency of strength absolute or material is a U10 UNKNOWN Record of severity US4; an incomplete trace limited to supporting or recovery-only dependencies is US3 unless it affects a gate criterion.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-161r1 (cyber supply chain risk management)

controls.title: Downstream Consequence Mapping
controls.objective: For each material asset, system and dependency, the Service Outcomes it affects and the time from its loss to outcome impact are known, so that prioritisation, maintenance planning and response are driven by consequence rather than by asset type.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a downstream consequence analysis that states, for each material InfrastructureSystem and dependency, the Service Outcomes affected by its loss or degradation, the propagation path, and the time-to-impact under declared load (for example UPS autonomy, thermal ride-through of liquid-cooled racks, checkpoint interval loss for training, inference latency tolerance). A competent engineer independent of the author shall review the analysis before approval.
assessmentCriteria: Each material system and dependency has recorded affected Service Outcomes and a propagation path using PROPAGATES_TO relationships.
Time-to-impact is stated with unit, load assumption and source (calculation, test or OEM data) for power, thermal and control dependencies.
Time-to-impact for AI workloads accounts for workload behaviour (for example training job failure on single-node loss within a synchronous collective, and the work lost since last checkpoint).
The analysis has been independently reviewed and approved, and its assumptions are listed.
The analysis is used: consequence classes appear in maintenance planning, alarm prioritisation and change risk assessment for a sample of records.

parameters.name: Thermal ride-through at declared rack load
parameters.basis: Derived from THM analysis and test; liquid-cooled high-density racks can have very short ride-through, so it is never assumed.

parameters.name: Maximum training work lost per interruption
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set from the Service Outcome tolerance in CAP.

minimumEvidence: Approved consequence analysis (FMEA-style table or graph) with assumptions.
Source calculations or test reports for time-to-impact values.
Sample of maintenance plans, alarm priority records or change risk assessments showing use of consequence classes.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current approved version; reviewed within 12 months or after material change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Technical review by a competent engineer who did not author the analysis.
mandatoryItems: Approved consequence analysis with time-to-impact values and sources
acceptableAlternatives: A fault tree or reliability block model may substitute for a tabular FMEA if it states outcomes, paths and time-to-impact.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-09 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Change in rack power density or cooling method
Change in workload type (training vs inference) or checkpoint policy

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the consequence analysis, its assumptions and review record.
Check coverage against the material systems in the asset-to-function map (MCF-DEP-001).
Recompute or check a sample of time-to-impact values against their sources (UPS discharge data, thermal test, checkpoint configuration).
Trace a sample of maintenance, alarm and change records to confirm consequence classes are used.
Record Findings for unsupported time-to-impact values or uncovered systems.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope Capability Instances. Where the Capability Instance has a single Service Outcome, the analysis may be simplified to propagation paths and time-to-impact.
failureModes: Consequence of a loss underestimated because ride-through was assumed rather than measured
Low-priority alarm on an asset with seconds-scale time-to-impact
Maintenance scheduled during a training run without checkpoint coordination
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based analysis; where time-to-impact values require a test, the test is governed by the owning domain's control (POW/THM/RES) and not performed under this control.
controls.unknownRule: Missing time-to-impact for a power, thermal or control dependency of a critical Required Function is a US3 UNKNOWN Record; it escalates to US4 if a CG-05, CG-06 or CG-10 criterion relies on that value.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 thermal guidelines for data processing environments

controls.title: Recovery Dependency Mapping
controls.objective: Dependencies that are needed only, or mainly, during restoration are identified and available, and circular recovery dependencies are found and broken before an event rather than during it.
controls.requirement: The recovery owner shall maintain a recovery dependency map for each Required Function covering recovery-only and recovery-critical dependencies (for example generator start batteries and fuel delivery, black-start sequence, BMS/EPMS server and network availability, out-of-band management network, DHCP/PXE and golden images, licence and entitlement servers, identity provider and break-glass credentials, OEM remote support, spares and specialist labour). The recovery owner shall analyse the map for circular dependencies and for recovery dependencies that share a fault domain with the failure they recover from, and shall record each such case with a resolution or an UNKNOWN Record.
assessmentCriteria: A recovery dependency map exists for each Required Function and states, for each dependency, whether it is recovery-only, and the operating states (RECOVERY, EMERGENCY, SHUTDOWN) in which it is needed.

A circular-dependency analysis has been performed (for example cooling controls require network, network requires power, power restoration sequence requires cooling controls) and each cycle is broken by a documented manual or independent path.
Each recovery dependency is checked for shared fault domain with the failure scenarios it is intended to recover from (for example golden-image repository hosted in the hall it restores).
Recovery-only external dependencies (OEM remote support, licence servers, cloud identity) have a verified offline or alternative path, or are recorded as UNKNOWN.
The map is consistent with the recovery sequences in RES-04 and the restoration procedures in POW/THM/CMP/STO/NET.

parameters.name: Maximum acceptable unresolved circular dependencies on critical functions
parameters.basis: Illustrative; any unresolved cycle on a critical function defeats recovery planning.

minimumEvidence: Recovery dependency map per Required Function.
Configuration evidence of offline or alternative paths (for example local licence caches, cached credentials, local image mirrors, out-of-band network design).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current at assessment date; updated after each recovery test or real recovery event.
evidenceProfile.independence: Analysis reviewed by a person from a different discipline (for example a facilities engineer reviewing an IT recovery map and vice versa).
acceptableAlternatives: A documented recovery exercise (RES-05) that exercised the full restoration path may substitute for part of the circular analysis for the paths it covered.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-10 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Change to recovery sequence, golden-image location or licence model
Introduction of a cloud or SaaS dependency in a management path
Recovery test or real event revealing an unrecorded dependency

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the recovery dependency maps and the RES-04 recovery sequences for in-scope functions.
Construct or review the dependency graph for the RECOVERY state and search for cycles.
For each recovery dependency, test for shared fault domain with the initiating scenario using the AIDCF-003 fault-domain taxonomy.
Verify by configuration evidence that declared offline or alternative paths exist.
Interview recovery owners on any dependency not represented in procedures.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance with a declared Recovery Outcome. Where no Recovery Outcome is declared, this is recorded as a CG-01 matter rather than treated as not applicable.
failureModes: Circular recovery dependency (cooling controls need network that needs cooled equipment)
Golden image or configuration backup stored in the failed fault domain
Licence or entitlement server unreachable during recovery
Break-glass credentials depend on the failed identity provider
Recovery reintroduces corrupt configuration (scenario X15)
controls.testingSafety: Analysis is desk-based. Verification of offline paths shall not include disconnecting live services; any such test is performed under RES-05 with change approval.
controls.unknownRule: A recovery dependency whose availability in the RECOVERY state cannot be established is a U10 UNKNOWN Record; it is US4 where it lies on the restoration path of a critical Required Function and a CG-10 criterion depends on it, otherwise US3.

controls.title: Shared Source Analysis
controls.objective: Nominally redundant or diverse supplies are shown, on as-built evidence, not to share a source whose loss would defeat both, or the shared source is declared, owned and reflected in the resilience claim.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall analyse every redundant or diverse supply path that a resilience claim relies on (utility feeds, transformers, UPS paths, generator fuel, facility water, chilled-water plant, heat rejection, carrier circuits, cloud regions) for shared sources and record each pair as INDEPENDENT_OF only where as-built evidence supports independence for the stated hazard. Where a shared source exists, the facility owner shall record a SHARES_DEPENDENCY_WITH relationship, an owner and the residual exposure, and the capability owner shall reflect it in the resilience claim.
assessmentCriteria: Every redundancy claim used in CG-05, CG-06 or CG-08 evaluation has a corresponding shared-source analysis.

Independence claims are supported by as-built evidence (for example utility statement of separate grid supply points, separate fuel contracts and storage, separate water mains), not by design intent alone.

Shared sources found (for example both utility feeds from one grid substation, both fuel contracts with one distributor, both carriers using one upstream fibre) are recorded with owner and residual exposure.
The resilience claim for each affected Required Function is consistent with the recorded shared sources.

parameters.name: Upstream depth examined for shared source
parameters.illustrativeDefault: To grid supply point / carrier POP / fuel terminal
parameters.basis: Illustrative; profile sets depth based on the declared external hazard set.

minimumEvidence: Utility connection documentation identifying supply points; carrier route and POP documentation; fuel and water supply contracts.
Single-line and P&ID diagrams for internal sources.
Resilience claim records showing reflected shared sources.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; re-performed after any change to supply arrangements.
evidenceProfile.independence: Independence claims corroborated by a provider document or as-built record, not the designer's statement.
mandatoryItems: Provider evidence for each claimed external independence
acceptableAlternatives: Where a utility will not disclose supply topology, a utility-signed statement of the number of independent supply points is acceptable at confidence no higher than CONF-2.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-05, CG-06, CG-09 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: Change of fuel or water supplier
New carrier circuit or carrier merger

assessmentProcedure: List every redundancy or diversity claim relied on for the Capability Instance.
For each, obtain the shared-source analysis and the supporting provider and as-built evidence.
Trace each path upstream and identify the first common node, if any.
Compare findings with the resilience claim and record inconsistencies.
Inspect accessible internal points (for example generator fuel interconnection, chilled-water headers) where documents conflict.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever a resilience or availability claim relies on redundancy or diversity. Not applicable to a Capability Instance that declares no redundancy (in which case the single source is the dependency and DEP-02 still records it).
failureModes: Two utility feeds from the same grid substation lost together
A and B fuel supply from one distributor or terminal
Diverse carriers sharing one long-haul fibre
Redundant cooling plant sharing one water main or make-up water source
controls.testingSafety: Inspection of plant interconnections shall be non-intrusive; valves, breakers and isolators shall not be operated for verification.
controls.unknownRule: Where independence of a pair cannot be established, the pair shall be treated as sharing a source for gate evaluation and an UNKNOWN Record (U10) raised; severity US4 when the pair underpins a CG-05 or CG-06 resilience criterion.

controls.title: Common Controller Analysis
controls.objective: Redundant systems are not defeated together by a shared controller, management server, automation logic, firmware baseline or orchestration plane.
controls.requirement: The control-system owner shall identify, for each redundant infrastructure pair or group, every shared control element (PLCs, BMS/EPMS servers, CDU controllers and their master/lead-lag logic, sequence-of-operation software, cluster managers and schedulers, fabric controllers, storage controllers, firmware and configuration sources, automation and AI agents) and record whether loss, malfunction or unsafe command of that element can affect more than one member of the group. The control-system owner shall either demonstrate independence, implement a safeguard (local autonomous control, fail-safe default, staggered firmware) or record the common controller as a declared common mode with owner.
assessmentCriteria: Each redundant group in POW, THM, CMP, STO and NET has a recorded common-controller analysis.
Controller failure behaviour (fail-last, fail-safe, fail-to-local) is stated from configuration or OEM evidence for each shared element.
Shared firmware or configuration sources are identified, and rollout to redundant members is staged (cross-reference MCF-SUP-015).
Each common controller that can affect more than one member has a safeguard or a recorded acceptance by the accountable owner.
Automation or AI agents with authority over more than one redundant member are recorded with their authority scope (cross-reference SEC-06).
minimumEvidence: Control architecture drawings (BMS/EPMS network and controller layout, CDU control topology, cluster/fabric management architecture).
Controller configuration exports showing failure mode settings.
Common-controller analysis record and acceptance decisions.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; re-performed after control-system change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Review by an engineer not responsible for the control-system design.
mandatoryItems: Configuration evidence of controller failure behaviour
acceptableAlternatives: OEM documentation of default failure behaviour is acceptable where configuration export is not possible, with an UNKNOWN Record for the as-configured state.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-07, CG-09 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Introduction of new automation or agent authority
Firmware baseline change across a redundant group

assessmentProcedure: Identify redundant groups from the asset-to-function map.
For each group, obtain control architecture and identify shared elements.
Obtain configuration or OEM evidence of failure behaviour for each shared element.
Check the safeguard or acceptance record for each shared element affecting multiple members.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every redundant group of InfrastructureSystems controlled or managed by software or programmable controllers.
failureModes: Single BMS server failure stops both chilled-water plants
CDU lead-lag controller fault stops all CDUs on a loop
Firmware rollout common-mode failure (scenario X08)
Fabric controller fault isolates both rails
Automation acts on all redundant members at once
controls.testingSafety: No controller shall be failed, isolated or forced to verify behaviour under this control; failure-behaviour tests are performed only under THM/POW/SEC test controls with authorisation from the control-system owner and the facility operator.
controls.unknownRule: If controller failure behaviour cannot be established, record a U8 or U1 UNKNOWN Record; US4 where the redundant group supports a CG-05, CG-06 or CG-07 criterion.
informativeReferences: IEC 62443-3-2 (security risk assessment for system design)
ASHRAE Guideline 36 (sequences of operation for HVAC control)

controls.title: Shared Route Analysis
controls.objective: Physically diverse paths for power, fluid and telecommunications are verified on site and on provider route records not to converge in a shared trench, duct, riser, bridge, building entry, cable tray, pipe rack or fire zone.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain route records for every path relied on for diversity (MV/LV cables, busways, fuel lines, chilled and facility water pipes, fibre between buildings and to carrier POPs, inter-hall fabric trunks) and shall identify every point where diverse routes converge or come within the separation distance set in the capability profile. The facility owner shall obtain route evidence from carriers and utilities for external routes, verify internal routes by inspection at least at the profile interval, and record each convergence point as a shared fault domain with owner.
assessmentCriteria: Route records exist for each diverse path and identify building entries, risers, trenches, bridges and fire zones traversed.
Convergence points and sub-separation sections are listed with location and the hazards that could affect both routes (fire, flood, excavation, vehicle impact).
External carrier routes are supported by carrier route documentation (KMZ, route maps or signed statements of diversity) to at least the first POP or regeneration site.
A sample of internal routes has been physically inspected within the interval and matches records.
Each convergence point has an owner and is reflected in the fault-domain model (RES-02) and resilience claims.

parameters.name: Minimum physical separation for diverse routes
parameters.basis: Set in capability profile with reference to fire-zone design and the separation guidance in the cabling standard adopted (for example ANSI/TIA-942 or EN 50600-2-4).

parameters.name: Route inspection interval
parameters.basis: Illustrative; shorter where third-party works or construction occur nearby.

minimumEvidence: Route drawings for internal diverse paths with fire-zone overlay.
Carrier route documentation for each external circuit relied on for diversity.
Inspection record (dated, with photographs) for the sample.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Route evidence no older than the inspection interval; carrier documentation current within 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Inspection by a person other than the route record author; carrier statements are provider evidence (E5 where independently produced).
mandatoryItems: Carrier route documentation for diversity-relied circuits
acceptableAlternatives: Where a carrier will not disclose routes, a contractual diversity commitment plus independent fibre-path verification (for example latency fingerprinting by a third party) may be used, at confidence no higher than CONF-2.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-09 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: New cable or pipe installation in shared spaces

assessmentProcedure: Obtain diverse path list and route records.
Overlay routes on site plans and fire zones; identify convergence points.
Obtain carrier and utility route evidence and check diversity to the first POP or supply point.
Inspect a sample of internal routes, prioritising building entries and risers.
Confirm convergence points are in the RES-02 fault-domain model.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to all paths relied on for physical diversity. For colocation tenants, internal routes owned by the colocation provider are assessed through MCF-DEP-018 provider boundary evidence.
failureModes: Fire disables paired infrastructure routes (scenario X09)
Diverse carrier circuits in one duct cut by excavation
A and B busways in one riser
Supply and return water mains crossing in one trench
controls.testingSafety: Route inspection in risers, trenches and plant rooms shall follow confined-space and electrical safety rules; trench or manhole entry requires a permit under MCF-OPS-007 and confined-space controls.
controls.unknownRule: Unverified diversity on a path relied on by a resilience claim shall be treated as shared for gate evaluation and recorded as U10 UNKNOWN; US4 where the path supports a CG-05, CG-06 or CG-08 criterion.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)

controls.title: Shared Human Dependency Analysis
controls.objective: Redundant technical systems are not made dependent on the same individual, team, shift, contractor or authorisation holder in a way that defeats redundancy during response, maintenance or recovery.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall analyse human and organisational dependencies for each Required Function, including authorised persons for HV/LV switching, refrigerant and liquid-cooling work, on-call specialists, OEM field engineers and maintenance contractors, and shall record where the same person, team or contractor is required to restore or operate more than one redundant member, or where response depends on fewer people than the emergency task analysis requires. The operations manager shall implement deputies, cross-authorisation or contractual capacity for each case or record it as a declared concentration with owner.
assessmentCriteria: Human/procedural dependencies are recorded for each Required Function using the AIDCF-003 dependency classes.
For each emergency procedure, the number of competent and authorised people required is compared with those available on shift and on call within the response time.
Cases where one contractor maintains both redundant members (for example A and B UPS systems or all generators) are identified and assessed.
Each identified shared human dependency has a mitigation or accepted concentration with owner.

parameters.name: Minimum authorised persons per critical switching task available within response time
parameters.basis: Illustrative; reflects a two-person rule for HV switching common in safe systems of work; set from the site safety rules.

minimumEvidence: Human dependency analysis per Required Function.
Authorisation register for hazardous tasks (cross-reference MCF-OPS-004).
Roster and on-call schedules for a representative period.
Maintenance contracts showing scope per system.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Roster sample covering at least 3 months including holiday periods.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reviewed by a person outside the operations line management (for example HSE or assurance).
acceptableAlternatives: A tabletop exercise (RES-05) testing staffing for concurrent events may substitute for part of the roster analysis.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Departure of a key authorised person

assessmentProcedure: Obtain emergency task analysis and the human dependency analysis.
Sample rosters and on-call schedules and compare with required authorised persons per task.
Review maintenance contracts for single-contractor coverage of redundant members.
Interview shift leads on response capacity for concurrent events.
Record Findings and accepted concentrations.
controls.applicability: Applies to all staffed and contractor-supported operations in the boundary.
failureModes: Only one authorised HV switching person available at night
Same contractor fault affects maintenance of both UPS systems
Concurrent events exceed on-shift capacity
Key-person absence prevents recovery
controls.testingSafety: Analysis only; no staffing reduction or simulated absence shall be imposed on live operations to test this control.
controls.unknownRule: If rosters or authorisation records are unavailable for the sample period, record U1 UNKNOWN of severity US3; escalate to US4 if CG-04 safe-work criteria rely on two-person availability.
informativeReferences: HSE HSG48 (reducing error and influencing behaviour)
Uptime Institute Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability

controls.title: Utility Dependency
controls.objective: The utility services the Capability Instance relies on (grid electricity, water, fuel, and where applicable gas or district cooling) are contracted, sized and characterised for the declared demand, ramp schedule and operating states, including any curtailment, flexibility or interruptibility terms.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain, for each utility dependency, the contractual and technical basis of supply: for grid electricity the connection agreement, firm and non-firm capacity, capacity reservation and energisation schedule, curtailment or flexible-connection terms, demand-response obligations, supply-point power quality characteristics and protection interface; for water the supply and discharge permits, contracted volume and restriction triggers; for fuel the supply contracts, priority status and delivery commitments. The facility owner shall reconcile contracted firm capacity against declared demand (including growth commitments from CAP-04) for each operating state and record any shortfall, non-firm reliance or undisclosed term as a Finding or UNKNOWN Record.
assessmentCriteria: A current utility connection agreement exists for each grid supply, with firm and any non-firm capacity, energisation dates and curtailment terms identified.
Contracted firm capacity is equal to or greater than the declared demand in each operating state, or the gap is covered by an evidenced on-site measure and declared in the capability profile.
Capacity reservations and staged energisation milestones match the capability growth forecast; slippage is tracked.
Curtailment, flexible-connection and demand-response obligations are mapped to Service Outcome effects and to operating procedures.
Water and fuel supply contracts state volume, priority and delivery lead time, and are consistent with POW fuel autonomy and THM/ENV water continuity analyses.
Supply-point power quality data (for example voltage dips and interruptions) is available for the preceding period or recorded as UNKNOWN.

parameters.name: Firm capacity margin over declared peak demand
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set in the capability profile from load growth uncertainty and utility terms.

parameters.name: Minimum fuel resupply commitment under emergency
parameters.basis: Set from POW fuel autonomy (MCF-POW-007/008) so that autonomy exceeds the committed resupply time with margin.

parameters.name: Power quality history reviewed
parameters.basis: Illustrative; longer history improves estimate of event frequency.

minimumEvidence: Grid connection agreement and any variation, capacity reservation and energisation schedule.
Utility-provided supply characteristics (fault level, protection settings at interface, declared power quality).
Water supply and discharge permits; fuel supply contracts with emergency priority terms.
Power quality monitoring records at the point of connection (EPMS or utility).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Agreements current at assessment date; power quality records covering at least the preceding 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Contractual evidence from the utility (E5 provider evidence) corroborated by on-site metering (E3).
mandatoryItems: Grid connection agreement with firm capacity
acceptableAlternatives: Where a connection agreement is under negotiation, a utility offer letter with stated capacity and conditions supports DESIGN-stage assessment only, and the IMPLEMENTATION claim remains UNKNOWN.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-05 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: Change to connection agreement, capacity or curtailment terms
Utility network reinforcement or reconfiguration notice
New water restriction or fuel contract change

assessmentProcedure: Obtain connection agreements, permits and fuel/water contracts.
Extract firm/non-firm capacity, curtailment and demand-response terms.
Reconcile contracted capacity with declared demand for each operating state and the growth forecast.
Check consistency with POW fuel autonomy and THM/ENV water analyses.
Review power quality records at the point of connection for the period.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every site supplying the Capability Instance. In colocation, the colocation provider's utility evidence is obtained through MCF-DEP-018; a tenant that cannot obtain it records UNKNOWN.
failureModes: Capability expansion energised against non-firm capacity without declaration
Curtailment event not reflected in operating procedures
Energisation delay strands installed compute (scenario X17)
Fuel resupply slower than autonomy under regional emergency
Water restriction reduces heat rejection (scenario X10)
controls.testingSafety: Document and data review only; no switching, metering intervention or protection testing at the utility interface shall be performed under this control.
controls.unknownRule: Undisclosed firm capacity or curtailment terms for a grid supply relied on by the Capability Instance is a U2 or U10 UNKNOWN Record of severity US4 (affects CG-03 and a CG-05 criterion).
informativeReferences: EN 50160 (voltage characteristics of public distribution networks)
Applicable network operator connection agreement and grid code (jurisdiction-specific)

controls.title: Telecom Dependency
controls.objective: External connectivity (internet transit, data-centre interconnect, wavelength or dark-fibre services, carrier-neutral cross-connects, out-of-band and management circuits) is provided by identified carriers over verified diverse routes with known service levels, so that connectivity Service Outcomes and remote management do not rest on unrecorded single carriers or paths.
controls.requirement: The network owner shall maintain a register of every external telecommunications circuit in scope, recording carrier, service type, A/Z ends, building entry, meet-me room and cross-connect identifiers, route diversity evidence, upstream carrier (where a reseller is used), service levels and fault escalation. The network owner shall verify that the circuits relied on for each connectivity outcome and for out-of-band management satisfy the declared diversity (carrier, route, entry, POP) and shall record shared elements and reseller dependencies as Findings or UNKNOWN Records.
assessmentCriteria: Every external circuit relied on by a Service Outcome or management path is in the register with carrier, route and demarcation identifiers.
Declared carrier diversity accounts for resale and wholesale relationships (the underlying network operator is identified).
Building entries and meet-me rooms for diverse circuits are distinct, or the shared element is recorded (cross-reference MCF-DEP-007).
Out-of-band management connectivity does not depend on the same carrier and path as the production connectivity it is meant to back up.
Carrier service levels (availability, time to repair) are recorded and compared with the connectivity Service Outcome tolerance.

parameters.name: Minimum number of independent carriers for production connectivity
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set by the connectivity Service Outcome.

minimumEvidence: Carrier order forms and service descriptions; reseller disclosure of underlying carrier.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register current; carrier documents current within 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Register entries corroborated by carrier documents and, for a sample, by configuration evidence (router interface descriptions, BGP sessions).
mandatoryItems: Underlying carrier identification for each diversity-relied circuit
acceptableAlternatives: Independent path verification by a third party may substitute for undisclosed carrier routes, at confidence no higher than CONF-2.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-10 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: Carrier merger, acquisition or wholesale change

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the circuit register and connectivity Service Outcomes.
Reconcile register to router/switch configuration (interfaces, BGP neighbours) for a sample.
Identify underlying carriers and check claimed diversity.
Inspect meet-me room cross-connect records for diverse circuits.
Compare carrier service levels with outcome tolerance.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever a Service Outcome or management/recovery path depends on external connectivity. Fully air-gapped environments record the air-gap boundary instead.
failureModes: Two 'diverse' carriers reselling one underlying fibre
Out-of-band circuit on same carrier as production
Single meet-me room for all external circuits
Carrier repair time exceeds outcome tolerance
controls.testingSafety: No circuit shall be disconnected, shut or failed over to verify diversity under this control; failover testing is governed by NET and RES controls with change approval.
controls.unknownRule: Undisclosed underlying carrier or route for a diversity-relied circuit is a U10 UNKNOWN Record; US4 where it underpins a connectivity Service Outcome assessed under CG-03 or CG-08.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)

controls.title: OEM Dependency
controls.objective: Reliance on original equipment manufacturers and system integrators for the operation, support, repair and recovery of critical assets (accelerators and rack-scale systems, NICs/DPUs, switches and optics, storage, UPS, switchgear, generators, chillers, CDUs, BMS/EPMS) is identified per Required Function, including reliance that persists after installation such as entitlement, licensing, telemetry and remote diagnostics.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain an OEM dependency register that records, for each critical asset class, the OEM and integrator, support entitlement and its expiry, RMA and advance-replacement terms, licence or entitlement mechanisms required for operation (including licence servers and online activation), telemetry or phone-home requirements, field-engineer coverage for the site, proprietary tools or software needed for diagnosis or recovery, and the functions that would be lost or degraded if OEM support were unavailable. The capability owner shall record each operating dependency on OEM-hosted services as an external dependency in the upstream graph (MCF-DEP-002).
assessmentCriteria: Every critical asset class in the asset-to-function map has an OEM dependency entry with current support entitlement and expiry.
Operating dependencies on OEM services (licence activation, entitlement checks, cloud management portals, remote diagnostics) are recorded with the effect of their loss on each Required Function.
Proprietary diagnostic or recovery tools are held on site or in an accessible repository with licences valid for emergency use.
Field-engineer coverage (response time, local presence, clearance requirements) is recorded and compared with recovery tolerances.
Entries are reconciled to contracts and to OEM portals for a sample of assets.

parameters.name: Support entitlement expiry warning
parameters.basis: Illustrative; allows renewal or replacement before entitlement lapses.

minimumEvidence: Support contracts and entitlement records for sampled assets.
Licence and activation design for software-licensed functions.
Evidence of local copies of proprietary tools.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register current at assessment; entitlements checked against OEM records within 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Entitlement status verified from the OEM record or portal, not from internal register alone.
mandatoryItems: Entitlement verification for sampled critical assets
acceptableAlternatives: An integrator-managed support arrangement is acceptable if the integrator's back-to-back OEM entitlement is evidenced.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-10 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: OEM change to licensing or telemetry model

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the OEM dependency register and asset-to-function map.
Check coverage of critical asset classes.
Sample assets and verify entitlement against OEM records.
Review licence and telemetry dependencies for effect on operation if OEM services are unreachable.
Confirm local availability of proprietary tools.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to all critical asset classes. Supplier due diligence and contract terms are assessed under SUP; this control records the dependency itself.
failureModes: Accelerator or switch feature stops after licence server unreachable
Loss of remote OEM support (scenario X18)
Support entitlement lapsed unnoticed
Proprietary recovery tool unavailable during incident
controls.testingSafety: Register and document review only; no licence server shall be blocked to test behaviour outside an approved RES-05 exercise.
controls.unknownRule: An unknown entitlement status or an unrecorded OEM operating dependency for a critical asset class is a U10 UNKNOWN Record of severity US3, escalating to US4 if the dependency lies on a CG-10 restoration path.

controls.title: Cloud and Service Dependency
controls.objective: Dependencies on hyperscale cloud and SaaS control planes (identity providers, cloud-hosted DCIM/BMS analytics, cluster management and scheduling services, container and model registries, certificate authorities, DNS, ticketing and paging, OEM portals) are identified, their failure behaviour is known, and the infrastructure can continue to operate safely when they are unavailable.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain a register of every cloud or SaaS service on which an in-scope Required Function, management path or recovery path depends, recording the provider, region/zone, control-plane and data-plane dependencies, authentication path, the effect on each function if the service is unavailable or degraded, and the local fallback mode. The control-system owner shall ensure that no facility safety or continuity function (power, cooling, fire, leak detection and their alarming) requires a cloud or SaaS service to operate, and shall record any exception with accountable acceptance.
assessmentCriteria: Every cloud/SaaS service used by in-scope functions is registered with provider, region and authentication path.
Failure behaviour on service unavailability is stated per function and is supported by provider documentation, configuration or test.
No facility safety or continuity control loop or critical alarm path depends on a cloud or SaaS service; exceptions are accepted by the accountable owner.
Identity dependencies (federated sign-on for operators, service accounts) have a documented local or break-glass path (cross-reference SEC-01).
Concentration in a single cloud provider or region across multiple functions is identified (cross-reference MCF-DEP-013/014).

parameters.name: Maximum dependency of safety or continuity loops on cloud/SaaS services
parameters.basis: Illustrative; profile may allow exceptions only with accountable acceptance.

minimumEvidence: Architecture diagrams for management and control planes.
Configuration evidence of local fallback (local controller logic, cached credentials, on-premises DNS/NTP).
Provider service descriptions and status-page history for the period.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register current; provider incident history for the preceding 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Failure behaviour corroborated by configuration evidence or test, not provider marketing material.
mandatoryItems: Evidence that safety and continuity loops do not require cloud services
acceptableAlternatives: A completed RES-05 exercise simulating SaaS unavailability may substitute for configuration evidence for the functions exercised.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-15, CG-10 require gate-level evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: New cloud/SaaS service adopted for operations

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the register and management/control-plane architecture.
Reconcile register to egress firewall rules, DNS logs or configuration exports to find unregistered services.
For each service, obtain stated failure behaviour and check it against configuration evidence.
Confirm safety and continuity loops operate without cloud services.
Review provider incident history for events affecting operations.
Record Findings and UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to all Capability Instances. In hybrid cloud/on-premises patterns, cloud-hosted compute is a separate Capability Instance boundary matter (MCF-DEP-017).
failureModes: Operators locked out when cloud identity provider fails (scenario X19)
Cloud-hosted BMS analytics issuing setpoints with no local fallback
Cluster scheduler SaaS outage stops job admission
Container or model registry unavailable during recovery
controls.testingSafety: Reconciliation uses log and configuration review only; blocking egress to test fallback is permitted only within an approved exercise with the facility operator's authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Unknown failure behaviour of a cloud/SaaS service on a management or control path of a critical function is a U10 UNKNOWN Record of severity US4.

controls.title: Capacity Concentration
controls.objective: The share of AI capability concentrated in any single fault domain (site, building, hall, power train, UPS system, cooling loop or CDU group, scale-up domain, fabric pod, storage cluster) is quantified and kept within the impact tolerance of the Service Outcome.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall calculate, for each declared fault domain, the proportion of the Capability Instance's usable capacity (for example accelerators, storage throughput, network bandwidth) that would be lost on its failure, and shall compare it with the concentration limit derived from the Service Outcome impact tolerance (CAP-03). Where a fault domain exceeds the limit, the capability owner shall record it as a CONCENTRATES relationship and either reduce the concentration, provide alternative capacity (RES-03) or obtain risk acceptance from the accountable owner.
assessmentCriteria: Concentration is calculated for every fault domain in the RES-02 model, using current deployment data.
The concentration limit is derived from and traceable to the Service Outcome impact tolerance.
Fault domains exceeding the limit have an approved treatment or acceptance.
Calculations account for job topology: training jobs spanning several fault domains are counted as lost if any spanned domain fails, unless elastic recovery is evidenced.

parameters.name: Maximum share of usable capability in one fault domain
parameters.basis: Derived from the CAP-03 impact tolerance; there is no universal value.

minimumEvidence: Deployment inventory and job placement data.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current deployment; recalculated at each capacity change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Calculation checked by a second analyst.
mandatoryItems: Traceability of limit to impact tolerance
acceptableAlternatives: A scheduler-generated report of capacity per fault domain is acceptable if its fault-domain labels are reconciled to RES-02.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-09 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Change in job topology or placement policy

assessmentProcedure: Obtain fault-domain model and deployment data.
Recompute concentration for a sample of fault domains.
Compare with limits and check traceability to impact tolerance.
Review treatment or acceptance for exceedances.
controls.applicability: Applies to all Capability Instances with more than one fault domain; a single-fault-domain capability records 100% concentration and its acceptance.
failureModes: Majority of training capacity on one UPS system
All inference replicas in one hall
Large capability concentration exceeding tolerance
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based analysis of deployment and placement data; no workload shall be moved or drained to test concentration.
controls.unknownRule: If job placement or fault-domain labels are unavailable, record U1 UNKNOWN of severity US3 and treat the largest plausible concentration as the working value.
informativeReferences: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), ICT concentration risk provisions — informative for financial-sector users

controls.title: Supplier Concentration
controls.objective: Single-source and sole-source reliance for critical products and services, including concentration at sub-tier (shared factories, components or logistics routes) and concentration in one firmware or software lineage, is identified and treated.
controls.requirement: The procurement lead shall maintain a supplier concentration analysis covering critical asset classes and services (accelerators and rack-scale systems, high-speed optics, switch silicon, storage media, transformers, MV/LV switchgear, UPS, generators, CDUs and pumps, chillers, BMS/EPMS platforms, maintenance contractors, specialist labour). For each, the procurement lead shall record whether supply is single-source (one qualified supplier available) or sole-source (only one supplier exists), the qualification time for an alternative, and known sub-tier concentration, and shall agree a treatment with the capability owner.
assessmentCriteria: Each critical asset class and service has a recorded sourcing status (multi-, single-, sole-source).
Sub-tier concentration known from MCF-SUP-004 is incorporated (for example two transformer brands sharing one core-steel supplier).
Qualification time for an alternative supplier is estimated with basis.
Each single- or sole-source item has an agreed treatment (dual qualification, strategic stock, framework agreement, design change) or acceptance.

parameters.name: Maximum share of a critical asset class from one supplier
parameters.basis: Set in capability profile; standardisation benefits must be weighed against common-mode exposure.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; reviewed at least annually.
evidenceProfile.independence: Review by a person outside the procurement function (engineering or risk).
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Supplier exit, acquisition or allocation change

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the concentration analysis and approved supplier list.
Check coverage of critical asset classes and services.
Verify sourcing status for a sample against market information and supplier disclosures.
Review treatments and acceptances.
controls.applicability: Applies to all critical asset classes and services.
failureModes: Sole-source accelerator allocation cut
One transformer supplier for all units with multi-year lead time
Single firmware lineage across all switches
Single contractor holds all specialist knowledge
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based analysis; supplier enquiries shall not disclose site-sensitive architecture beyond what the supplier already holds under contract.
controls.unknownRule: Unknown sourcing status for a critical class is US3; escalate to US4 where the class lies on a CG-10 restoration path with no strategic spare.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-161r1 (cyber supply chain risk management)
ISO 28000 (security and resilience: supply chain security management)

controls.title: Knowledge Concentration
controls.objective: Knowledge essential to operate, maintain and recover critical systems (control logic, sequences of operation, protection philosophy, fabric configuration and tuning, storage recovery procedures, proprietary scripts) is not held by a single person or a single external party without a documented and tested transfer path.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall identify knowledge items essential to each Required Function and record their holders, documentation status and accessibility. For each item held by fewer people than the profile minimum or held only by an external party, the operations manager shall implement documentation, cross-training or contractual access (including escrow of control logic and configuration where proprietary) and shall verify transfer by a practical demonstration.
assessmentCriteria: Knowledge items essential to each Required Function are listed with holders.
Items below the minimum holder count have a documented treatment and target date.
Proprietary control logic and configuration for BMS/EPMS/CDU/PLC systems is held by the owner or in escrow, in a usable form.
At least one transfer per critical item has been demonstrated by a second holder performing the task or a walkthrough.

parameters.name: Minimum independent holders per critical knowledge item
parameters.basis: Illustrative; external parties count only where contractually available within response time.

minimumEvidence: Escrow or ownership evidence for control logic.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; reviewed annually and on staff change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Demonstration observed by someone other than the original holder.
mandatoryItems: Evidence of control-logic ownership or escrow
acceptableAlternatives: OEM contractual commitment to provide logic within a stated time is acceptable for non-safety logic.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-13, CG-10 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain register and documentation inventory.
Interview holders to test completeness.
Verify escrow or ownership of control logic.
Observe or review demonstration records.
controls.applicability: Applies to all critical systems; most material for proprietary control systems and bespoke automation.
failureModes: Only one engineer can modify CDU control logic
Integrator holds the only copy of PLC source
Fabric tuning undocumented
controls.testingSafety: Demonstrations shall use simulators, test benches or walkthroughs; no live control-logic change for demonstration purposes.
controls.unknownRule: Unknown holder count or inaccessible control logic for a critical system is US3; escalate to US4 where a CG-10 recovery step depends on it.
informativeReferences: IEC 62443-2-4 (security requirements for IACS service providers)

controls.title: Substitution Readiness
controls.objective: For each material concentration or single external dependency, a substitute (alternative carrier path, alternate fuel supplier, mobile generation, temporary chillers or heat rejection, alternate OEM or qualified refurbished stock, alternate cloud region or provider, alternate capacity) can be brought into service within the time the Service Outcome tolerance allows, and this has been demonstrated.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall define a substitution plan for each concentration or single dependency recorded under DEP-02 to DEP-04, stating the substitute, prerequisites (connection points, permits, contracts, qualification), activation authority and time-to-substitute. The capability owner shall validate each plan by test, exercise or documented precedent at the profile interval, and shall record the demonstrated time-to-substitute against tolerance.
assessmentCriteria: Each recorded concentration or single external dependency has a substitution plan or an accepted no-substitute position.
Physical prerequisites (for example generator and chiller connection points, temporary fuel connections, spare fibre) exist and have been inspected.
Contractual prerequisites (call-off agreements, standby contracts) are current.
Each plan has been validated within the interval and demonstrated time-to-substitute is within tolerance, or the gap is recorded.
Lessons from validation have been incorporated.

parameters.name: Substitution validation interval
parameters.basis: Illustrative; shorter for dependencies with high event frequency.

parameters.name: Time-to-substitute margin
parameters.illustrativeDefault: 75 (demonstrated time no more than 75% of tolerance)
parameters.basis: Illustrative; provides margin for real-event degradation.

minimumEvidence: Test, exercise or precedent records with timing.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
