evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Validation within the interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Validation observed by a person independent of the plan owner.
acceptableAlternatives: A documented real event in which the substitute was used is acceptable precedent if it occurred within the interval and conditions were comparable.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Change to the dependency or substitute

assessmentProcedure: Obtain concentration and single-dependency records and corresponding plans.
Inspect physical prerequisites for a sample.
Verify contracts are current.
Review validation records and compare demonstrated times to tolerance.
Where proportionate, witness a substitution exercise.
controls.applicability: Applies to every material concentration or single external dependency; not applicable where an accepted no-substitute position exists and is reflected in the decision.
failureModes: Temporary generator connection point missing or incompatible
Call-off contract expired
Substitute takes longer than tolerance
Alternate region lacks capacity at the time of need
controls.testingSafety: Substitution tests involving temporary generation, temporary chillers, fuel transfer or electrical connection are hazardous; they require a method statement (MCF-OPS-006), permit to work (MCF-OPS-007), change approval (MCF-OPS-018) and authorisation by the facility operator's authorised person.
controls.unknownRule: A plan never validated is UNKNOWN for the EFFECTIVENESS claim (U5 coverage gap, US3); where the dependency is on a CG-10 restoration path, US4.

controls.title: Assessment Boundary
controls.objective: The assessment boundary is drawn so that every material dependency of the Capability Instance is either inside it and assessed, or outside it and explicitly recorded as an external dependency with owner, evidence and decision effect; nothing material is excluded silently.
controls.requirement: The assurance lead shall define the assessment boundary for each Capability Instance by reference to the dependency graph (DEP-01), listing included systems, external dependencies crossing the boundary (with boundary interface, provider and evidence obtained), and exclusions with rationale and approver. The assurance lead shall reconcile the boundary with the asset-to-function map and upstream graph before fieldwork and after any material change, and shall treat any material dependency found outside the boundary and not recorded as a boundary defect.
assessmentCriteria: The boundary statement lists included systems, crossing dependencies and exclusions, each with identifier.
Every dependency in the DEP-01 graph with strength absolute or material is either inside the boundary or recorded as a crossing dependency.
Each exclusion has a rationale and an approver with authority (GOV-01), and its decision effect is stated.
Each crossing dependency has an evidence plan (what will be obtained from the provider and how it will be verified).
Boundary reconciliation was performed before fieldwork and after material changes in the period.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Approved for the current assessment; reconciled within 30 days of fieldwork start.
evidenceProfile.independence: Boundary approved by a person with authority who is not the assessor performing reconciliation.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-02, CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Where the undetermined item concerns the boundary itself, the UNKNOWN is US5 and the decision is capped at INCONCLUSIVE.
reassessmentTriggers: Change in Capability Instance or Service Outcome

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the boundary statement, dependency graph and asset-to-function map.
Reconcile each material dependency to boundary inclusion or crossing record.
Check exclusion rationale, approver and decision effect.
Check evidence plans for crossing dependencies.
Record boundary defects as Findings and unresolved items as UNKNOWN Records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment.
failureModes: Material dependency excluded without approval
Colocation provider infrastructure assumed in scope but not evidenced
Cloud control plane outside boundary but not recorded
Boundary drawn around compute only, ignoring facility dependencies
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based.
controls.unknownRule: A material dependency whose boundary status cannot be determined is a US5 Systemic UNKNOWN (it affects the boundary) and caps the decision at INCONCLUSIVE until resolved.

controls.title: Provider Boundary
controls.objective: At every interface with a provider (colocation operator, utility, carrier, water or fuel supplier, cloud provider, managed-service or maintenance provider) the physical and logical demarcation point and the allocation of responsibility for operation, maintenance, monitoring, change, incident response and evidence are explicit for each lifecycle stage and operating state.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall maintain, for each provider interface, a demarcation record identifying the physical or logical demarcation point (for example HV metering point, tenant breaker in provider switchboard, facility-water flange or CDU primary connection, meet-me room patch panel, cloud API boundary) and a shared-responsibility record conforming to AIDCF-003 (IOT-REQ-051) for each function across lifecycle stages and operating states, including who may operate, who responds to alarms, who approves changes and who holds evidence. The capability owner shall obtain the provider's acceptance of each record and shall treat any function without a responsible and an accountable party as a responsibility gap.
assessmentCriteria: Each provider interface has a demarcation record with an identifiable physical or logical point.

Each shared function has a shared-responsibility record covering operation, maintenance, monitoring, change approval, incident response and evidence custody for NORMAL, MAINTENANCE, EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states.
The provider has accepted the record (signed, contractual schedule or equivalent).
Emergency authority across the boundary (for example who may shed tenant load or isolate a cooling loop) is explicit.
Responsibility gaps are recorded and dispositioned; contractual responsibility is not treated as proof of capability (IOT-REQ-052).
minimumEvidence: Demarcation records with drawings or photographs of demarcation points.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; reviewed at contract renewal and annually.
evidenceProfile.independence: Records corroborated by the provider's own documentation (contract schedule, service description).
acceptableAlternatives: Contract schedules containing equivalent allocation are acceptable if mapped to functions and states.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-13 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-03 require gate-level evaluation.

assessmentProcedure: List provider interfaces from the boundary statement.
Obtain demarcation and shared-responsibility records.
Inspect a sample of physical demarcation points.
Check states coverage and emergency authority.
Interview provider and owner staff on a sample of scenarios to test common understanding.
Record responsibility gaps.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever any function in the boundary is performed or supported by a third party.
failureModes: Colocation responsibility gap (scenario X14)
Neither party responds to a CDU primary-side alarm
Provider changes upstream configuration without tenant approval
Evidence held by provider not available to assessor
controls.testingSafety: Inspection of demarcation points inside provider spaces requires provider escort and permission; no provider equipment shall be operated.
controls.unknownRule: A critical function with no identifiable responsible or accountable party across a provider boundary is US4 (CG-13 criterion); an unaccepted but otherwise complete record is US3.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 27036-3 (supplier relationships: ICT supply chain security)

controls.title: Tenant Boundary
controls.objective: In shared or multi-tenant facilities and platforms, one tenant's load, configuration, actions or failures cannot propagate to another beyond declared limits, and shared infrastructure capacity is allocated and enforced.
controls.requirement: The platform or facility operator shall define for each shared resource (power path and UPS capacity, cooling loop and CDU capacity, coolant chemistry, fabric and storage, management plane) the per-tenant allocation, the enforcement mechanism (for example breaker sizing, power capping, flow limiting, QoS, quota) and the tenant obligations (load-step limits, coolant compatibility, change notification). The operator shall monitor tenant consumption against allocation and record exceedances as incidents.
assessmentCriteria: Each shared resource has per-tenant allocations recorded.
Enforcement mechanisms are implemented and evidenced by configuration.
Tenant obligations are in agreements and are monitored.
Exceedances in the period are recorded and handled as incidents.
Tenant change that could affect shared infrastructure (for example new rack-scale systems with large load steps) requires operator approval.

parameters.name: Per-tenant load-step limit
parameters.basis: Derived from POW-05 load-step response analysis.

minimumEvidence: Consumption monitoring reports and exceedance incidents.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Monitoring data for at least 3 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Enforcement verified from configuration, not from tenant attestation.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-09, CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Tenant expansion or hardware generation change

assessmentProcedure: Obtain shared resource list and allocations.
Verify enforcement configuration for a sample.
Review monitoring and exceedances.
Review tenant change approvals.
controls.applicability: Applies only to multi-tenant or shared-platform patterns. Not applicable to single-tenant dedicated facilities, with that pattern recorded in the boundary statement.
failureModes: Tenant rack load step trips shared UPS
Incompatible coolant introduced by tenant contaminates shared loop
Tenant consumes reserved headroom
Tenant fabric misconfiguration affects shared spine
controls.testingSafety: No enforcement mechanism shall be tested by deliberate exceedance on live shared infrastructure.
controls.unknownRule: Unverifiable enforcement on a shared resource supporting more than one tenant is US3; US4 where it is a CG-09 containment boundary.

controls.title: Cross-Boundary Enforcement
controls.objective: The conditions agreed at each boundary interface (power drawn, coolant supply temperature and flow, water quality, network traffic and routes, access) are measured at the boundary and deviations are detected, escalated and resolved, so that interface contracts operate in practice rather than on paper.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall instrument each material boundary interface so that the agreed interface properties (per AIDCF-013 interface contracts) are measured at or near the demarcation point, shall set alarm thresholds for deviation, and shall route deviations to the responsible party under MCF-DEP-018 with escalation timelines. The capability owner shall review deviations and their resolution at the interval set in the capability profile.
assessmentCriteria: Each material boundary interface has measured properties defined with units and thresholds.
Measurement exists at or near the demarcation point and data is retained for the period.
Deviations in the period were alarmed, routed to the responsible party and resolved within escalation timelines.
Recurring deviations have been raised as problems (MCF-OPS-016).
minimumEvidence: Boundary metering and telemetry data for the period.
Deviation alarms and tickets with resolution times.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 6 months of operation (illustrative; profile-defined).
evidenceProfile.independence: Telemetry extracted by the assessor or from a system not controlled by the party being monitored where possible.
acceptableAlternatives: Provider-supplied measurements are acceptable if cross-checked against at least one owner-side measurement.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-09, CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: New interface or changed contract property

assessmentProcedure: Obtain interface property definitions.
Extract boundary telemetry for the period and identify deviations independently.
Reconcile independently identified deviations with alarms and tickets.
Check resolution times against escalation timelines.
Check problem records for recurrence.
controls.applicability: Applies to material boundary interfaces where measurement is technically possible; where it is not, the gap is recorded as an UNKNOWN Record rather than not applicable.
failureModes: Coolant supply temperature from provider above agreed limit undetected
Tenant draws above allocated power without alarm
Upstream route change unnoticed
controls.testingSafety: Read-only telemetry extraction.
controls.unknownRule: Missing boundary telemetry for a material interface is U1 UNKNOWN, US3; US4 where the interface is a CG-06 or CG-05 supply interface.

controls.title: Dependency Health Indicators
controls.objective: The health of each material external and shared dependency is observed continuously or periodically through defined indicators, so that deterioration is detected before it defeats a Service Outcome.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall define health indicators for each material dependency (for example utility voltage events and frequency deviations, fuel stock and delivery status, facility water pressure and quality, carrier circuit errors and availability, cloud/SaaS service status, OEM case backlog and RMA turnaround, spares stock against minimum) with thresholds and alarm routing into the NOC/BMS, and shall review indicator trends at the profile interval.
assessmentCriteria: Each material dependency has at least one defined health indicator with threshold.
Indicators are collected and visible to the NOC or BMS operators.
Threshold breaches in the period generated alarms or tickets and were acted on.
Trend reviews were held at the interval and recorded actions.
minimumEvidence: Dashboards or reports for the period.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 6 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Indicator data sampled by the assessor from source systems.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.
reassessmentTriggers: Incident not preceded by indicator warning

assessmentProcedure: Obtain indicator definitions and map to material dependencies.
Observe NOC/BMS visibility of indicators.
Sample threshold breaches and trace to action.
Review trend minutes.
controls.applicability: Applies to all material dependencies recorded under DEP-01 to DEP-03.
failureModes: Fuel stock below minimum unnoticed
Carrier error rate rising before outage
OEM RMA backlog growing
Cloud identity degradation not visible to operators
controls.testingSafety: Observation only.
controls.unknownRule: No indicator for a material dependency is US3 for OPERATION claims.

controls.title: Provider Performance
controls.objective: Actual performance of each material provider against service levels and against the needs of the Service Outcome is measured and reviewed, and persistent shortfall leads to action.
controls.requirement: The supplier manager shall measure each material provider's performance against contracted service levels (availability, response and restore times, RMA turnaround, notification timeliness, RCA quality) from owner-side records, review it with the provider at the profile interval, and escalate persistent or material shortfall to the capability owner for treatment.
assessmentCriteria: Measured performance from owner-side records exists for each material provider for the period.
Reviews were held at the interval with recorded actions.
Shortfall against service levels or Service Outcome needs was escalated and treated.
Provider RCAs for significant incidents were received and assessed.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Measurement from owner-side tickets and telemetry, not provider self-reporting only.
acceptableAlternatives: Provider reports are acceptable if reconciled to a sample of owner tickets.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain service levels and measurements.
Recompute a sample of measurements from tickets.
Review minutes and escalation records.
Assess RCAs.
controls.applicability: Applies to material providers.
failureModes: Provider restore times exceed tolerance without escalation
Self-reported provider metrics mask shortfall
RCAs not received
controls.testingSafety: Not applicable to physical testing; review only.
controls.unknownRule: Absence of owner-side measurement is U1, US3 for OPERATION claims.

controls.title: Change Detection
controls.objective: Changes that alter the dependency graph, whether made internally or by providers (carrier reroute, utility network reconfiguration, cloud region or API change, OEM licensing or end-of-life notice, contractor change, new tenant), are detected and the dependency records and affected assessments are updated.
controls.requirement: The dependency owner shall operate a change-detection process that combines internal change records (OPS-05), provider notifications, contract events and technical discovery (for example route and configuration diffs) to identify changes to material dependencies, and shall update the dependency graph and raise reassessment triggers within the time set in the capability profile.
assessmentCriteria: Sources of dependency change are defined (internal changes, provider notifications, contract events, discovery).
Changes in the period were reflected in the dependency graph within the profile time.
Each material dependency change raised a ReassessmentTrigger where required.
A sample of provider notifications reconciles to graph updates.

parameters.name: Maximum time to update dependency graph after detected change

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 6 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation by assessor of notifications to graph versions.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-14, CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain procedure and sources.
Sample provider notifications and internal changes.
Trace to graph updates and reassessment triggers.
Measure update latency.
controls.applicability: Applies to all assessments with OPERATION claims on dependency controls.
failureModes: Carrier reroute merges diverse paths unnoticed
OEM licensing change not reflected
Contractor change removes authorised staff
controls.testingSafety: Review only.
controls.unknownRule: Inability to show that provider notifications are received is U5, US3; escalate to US4 if a CG-03 critical dependency changed in the period without update.

controls.title: Periodic Revalidation
controls.objective: The dependency graph, route records, provider demarcations and concentration analyses are revalidated against fresh evidence at a defined interval, so that dependency visibility does not decay between change events.
controls.requirement: The dependency owner shall revalidate every material dependency record at the interval set in the capability profile by obtaining current evidence (walk-down, configuration export, provider statement or contract), shall mark records not revalidated within the interval as STALE, and shall treat stale records as UNKNOWN for assessment purposes.
assessmentCriteria: A revalidation schedule covering all material dependency records exists.
Records were revalidated within the interval, with evidence attached.
Stale records are flagged and treated as UNKNOWN.
Revalidation findings led to graph updates.

parameters.name: Revalidation interval for material dependencies
parameters.basis: Illustrative; shorter for high-churn dependencies (cloud services, carriers).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: One full revalidation cycle.
evidenceProfile.independence: Revalidation evidence from a source other than the record itself.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain schedule and record list.
Sample records and check revalidation date and evidence.
Confirm stale flagging and treatment.
Check resulting updates.
controls.applicability: Applies to all material dependency records.
failureModes: Dependency graph accurate at build but stale years later
Provider demarcation changed without update
controls.testingSafety: Walk-downs follow site safety rules as for MCF-DEP-001.
controls.unknownRule: Stale material dependency records are U3 UNKNOWN; severity follows the dependency's gate role (US4 for CG-03 critical dependencies).

controls.title: Site Hazard Assessment
controls.objective: Establish that the natural and man-made hazards to which the site is exposed are identified, quantified against declared design levels and reflected in the design of facilities that host AI capability, so that no credible site-wide event exceeds the protection assumed by the architecture.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain a site hazard assessment, prepared or reviewed by competent specialists, that quantifies flood (fluvial, pluvial, coastal and groundwater), seismic, wind, lightning, extreme-temperature, wildfire and subsidence hazards at the declared design exceedance levels. The facility owner shall record, for each hazard, the design level adopted, the protective measures relied on and the residual exposure, and shall reassess the hazards when hazard mapping, climate projections or the site layout change.
assessmentCriteria: A hazard assessment exists that covers every hazard family in AIDCF-004 Part V applicable to the site, with excluded hazards justified.
Each quantified hazard states the source data, return period or annual exceedance probability and the design level adopted for critical plant.
Critical plant (MV intake, transformers, switchgear, UPS, generators, fuel, heat rejection, CDUs) elevation and protection are shown to meet the adopted flood design level plus freeboard.
Seismic design category and non-structural component requirements derived from the local code are recorded and traced into PHY-02 anchorage requirements.
Residual exposures are recorded as risks with an owner and are reflected in the resilience scenarios.
The assessment is no older than the declared review interval and post-dates the last material change to hazard mapping or site layout.

parameters.name: Design flood annual exceedance probability for critical plant
parameters.basis: Capability profile; national flood-risk mapping commonly publishes 1% and 0.1% AEP extents

parameters.name: Freeboard above design flood level for critical plant

minimumEvidence: Site hazard assessment report with hazard-by-hazard design levels and data sources
Flood-risk assessment and topographic survey showing critical plant finished floor levels
Seismic hazard determination and design category from the structural engineer of record
Lightning risk assessment (e.g. IEC 62305-2 method) and protection design
Risk register entries for residual site exposures with owners

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current assessment within the review interval; hazard data at its latest published edition.
evidenceProfile.independence: Hazard quantification by a competent specialist; acceptance by a reviewer independent of the site-selection sponsor.
mandatoryItems: Flood-risk assessment with critical plant levels
acceptableAlternatives: Insurer-commissioned natural-hazard survey where it quantifies the same hazards at stated exceedance levels
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-02, CG-03, CG-04.
reassessmentTriggers: Revised flood, seismic or wildfire hazard maps
New climate projection adopted by the owner
Relocation or addition of critical plant
Hazard event at or near the site

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the hazard assessment and confirm its date, author competence and hazard coverage.
Compare adopted design levels to the capability-profile parameters and to current public hazard data.
Walk down critical plant locations and verify finished floor and equipment plinth levels against survey.
Trace seismic and wind design levels into structural and anchorage design documents.
Confirm residual exposures appear in the risk register and in at least one resilience scenario.
controls.applicability: Applies to every site in the assessment boundary, including colocation sites where the assessed party must obtain the provider's hazard assessment. Not applicable to purely logical capability with no physical site in the boundary.
failureModes: Critical plant located below credible flood level
Seismic design level understated for non-structural components
Hazard assessment based on superseded mapping
Residual exposure not carried into resilience scenarios
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If the hazard assessment is absent or predates a material revision of hazard mapping, record a U1 or U3 UNKNOWN against the site and treat flood and seismic protection of critical plant as unverified for CG-02 and CG-04 evaluation.
informativeReferences: ASCE/SEI 7 or EN 1998 (seismic actions, per jurisdiction)
FM Global Property Loss Prevention Data Sheets (natural hazards)

controls.title: External Exposure
controls.objective: Ensure that threats and hazards originating outside the site boundary, including adjacent industrial activity, transport corridors, airspace, hostile vehicles and airborne contaminants, are characterised and mitigated so that they cannot disable redundant infrastructure together.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall identify external exposures within a defined radius of the site, including major-accident-hazard installations, pipelines, rail and road corridors carrying hazardous goods, flight paths, high-voltage corridors and sources of smoke or corrosive emissions. The facility owner shall specify perimeter protection (stand-off, hostile vehicle mitigation, blast and intrusion resistance) proportionate to the assessed threat, and shall show that no single external event can impair both redundant utility intakes, both generator yards or all heat-rejection plant.
assessmentCriteria: An external exposure register exists covering the declared radius, with each exposure's consequence path to site infrastructure described.
Hostile vehicle mitigation at the perimeter is rated to the vehicle mass and speed set in the threat assessment and covers all vehicle-accessible approaches to critical plant.
Redundant utility intakes, generator yards and heat-rejection plant are separated so that a single external event in the register cannot reach both.
Air intakes for halls and plant are located and protected against smoke, exhaust re-entrainment (including from the site's own generators) and corrosive emissions identified in the register.
Exposure changes in the surrounding area are monitored and the register is reviewed at the declared interval.

parameters.name: Hostile vehicle mitigation rating
parameters.basis: Threat assessment; rating per IWA 14-1 or PAS 68 test classification

minimumEvidence: External exposure register with distances and consequence paths
Security threat assessment and perimeter protection specification
Test certificates for installed hostile vehicle mitigation products
Site plan showing separation of redundant intakes, generator yards and heat rejection
Air-intake and exhaust plume study for generator exhaust re-entrainment

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register current within the review interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Threat assessment by a security specialist not responsible for the perimeter budget.
acceptableAlternatives: Statutory land-use consultation-zone determinations in place of a bespoke industrial-hazard study, where they cover the declared radius
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-09, CG-03.
reassessmentTriggers: New hazardous installation, pipeline or transport route within the radius
Change in threat level from the security function
Generator relocation or new exhaust stacks

assessmentProcedure: Review the exposure register and test it against public land-use and hazardous-installation data.
Inspect perimeter protection and match installed products to rated test certificates.
Overlay single external events (explosion overpressure contour, vehicle impact, smoke plume) on the site plan and check whether any reaches both redundant elements.
Review the exhaust re-entrainment study against current generator and intake positions.
controls.applicability: Applies to owned and leased sites; for colocation the assessed party relies on the provider's register and perimeter evidence. Not applicable where the site is wholly within a host facility whose perimeter is assessed as a separate boundary element.
failureModes: Single external explosion or fire affecting both redundant intakes
Vehicle-borne attack reaching transformer or generator yard
Generator exhaust drawn into hall air intakes during utility outage
New adjacent hazard not detected
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If separation of redundant intakes or generator yards against a registered external event cannot be demonstrated from drawings, record a U5 coverage UNKNOWN and carry it into the CG-09 evaluation as an untested containment boundary.

controls.title: Access and Logistics
controls.objective: Ensure that the site can receive the deliveries, emergency services and replacement equipment on which continuity and recovery of AI capability depend, including heavy dense racks, transformers and fuel, under normal and emergency conditions.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a logistics and access plan that defines routes and constraints for fuel delivery, emergency services, rack-scale IT deliveries and replacement of the largest plant items (transformers, generators, chillers, CDUs). The facility operator shall verify that loading docks, lifts, corridors, ramps and doors along each route are rated for the mass and dimensions of the heaviest declared item, and shall maintain an alternative access route for fuel and emergency services when the primary route is obstructed.
assessmentCriteria: Each route in the plan states the governing constraint (door clear opening, lift rating, ramp gradient, slab or dock rating) and the heaviest item it is verified for.
The heaviest declared fully populated rack (including integrated liquid-cooling manifolds) can be moved from dock to its final position without exceeding any route rating.
A replacement path exists for each transformer, generator and chiller that does not require de-energising the redundant counterpart.
At least the declared number of independent access routes for fuel tankers and fire appliances exists and has been driven or walked within the review period.
Logistics constraints are communicated to IT deployment teams before procurement of new rack types.

parameters.name: Heaviest declared delivered item on IT route (crated rack)
parameters.basis: Capability profile; rack OEM shipping data

parameters.name: Independent access routes for fuel and emergency vehicles

minimumEvidence: Logistics and access plan with route constraints
Lift, dock leveller and slab rating certificates or structural statements
Plant replacement method statements for largest items
Records of route trials or delivery records for the heaviest rack type deployed

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of delivery and route records, including at least one heaviest-rack delivery.
evidenceProfile.independence: Route verification records produced by the logistics or facilities team, sampled by the assessor against physical measurements.
mandatoryItems: Route rating evidence for the heaviest declared rack
acceptableAlternatives: Structural engineer's statement for route slabs where load-test certificates are unavailable
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-10.
reassessmentTriggers: Introduction of a heavier rack type or integrated liquid-cooled rack
Change of fuel supplier vehicle type

assessmentProcedure: Review the plan and identify the governing constraint on each route.
Measure a sample of constraints (door openings, ramp gradients) and compare with the plan.
Compare the heaviest rack in the deployment pipeline with lift and route ratings.
Review plant replacement method statements for dependency on redundant counterparts.
Confirm the alternative fuel and emergency route is unobstructed on the day of inspection.
controls.applicability: Applies to all sites hosting rack-scale or liquid-cooled AI systems and to any site relying on fuel deliveries for autonomy. Reduced scope applies to colocation tenants, who verify only the IT delivery route and rely on provider evidence for plant and fuel routes.
failureModes: Rack cannot be delivered without exceeding lift or slab rating
Transformer replacement requires outage of the redundant unit
Fuel tanker cannot reach fill point during flood or obstruction
Emergency services access blocked by deliveries
controls.testingSafety: Inspection only. Route trials with loaded racks are conducted by trained movers under the equipment-movement procedure (MCF-PHY-018); assessors do not participate in heavy-item moves.
controls.unknownRule: If route ratings for the heaviest declared rack cannot be established, record a U1 UNKNOWN and treat deployment of that rack type as unverified for PHY-02 structural claims.

controls.title: Adjacent Risk
controls.objective: Ensure that risks arising from adjacent occupancies, shared structures and neighbouring tenants on the same campus or in the same building are identified and cannot propagate into the facility hosting the assessed capability.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall identify adjacent occupancies and shared building elements (party walls, roofs, risers, plant rooms, car parks and loading areas) and the hazards they present, including fire load, water, vibration, vehicle impact and uncontrolled access. The facility owner shall agree with neighbouring occupiers or the landlord the separation, notification and emergency-coordination arrangements for each adjacent risk, and shall record any adjacent risk that cannot be controlled as an accepted risk with an accountable owner.
assessmentCriteria: An adjacency register identifies every occupancy sharing a structural element, riser or plant space with the facility.
Each adjacent risk has a recorded separation measure (fire rating, physical barrier, drainage, vibration isolation) or an approved risk acceptance.
Notification arrangements exist for adjacent works (hot works, roof works, demolition) that could affect the facility.
Emergency coordination with adjacent occupiers is documented, including shared alarms and evacuation interfaces.
minimumEvidence: Adjacency register with shared elements and hazards
Landlord or neighbour agreements covering notification of works
Fire strategy extracts for party walls and shared risers
Risk acceptances for uncontrolled adjacent risks

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register current within the review interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Register reviewed by someone other than the author; agreements verified against signed copies.
acceptableAlternatives: Building fire strategy where it identifies all adjacent occupancies and separations
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-03.
reassessmentTriggers: New adjacent tenant or change of use
Construction or demolition adjacent to the facility

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the adjacency register and verify it against building plans and site walk-down.
Check each shared riser and plant space for third-party equipment or access.
Review agreements and evidence that notification of adjacent works has operated.
Confirm uncontrolled risks have approved acceptance by the accountable owner.
controls.applicability: Applies to multi-occupancy buildings, campuses and colocation facilities. A standalone single-occupier building with no shared structure records the determination and is otherwise not applicable.
failureModes: Fire in adjacent occupancy breaches party wall
Water from neighbour plant floods hall
Uncoordinated hot works in shared riser
Neighbour access through shared roof
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: Where adjacent occupancies cannot be determined (for example landlord refuses disclosure), record a U2 UNKNOWN and treat the shared element as an unverified fault domain.
informativeReferences: NFPA 101 (life safety code) or national building regulations

controls.title: Structural Capacity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that floor slabs, raised floors, roofs and supports can carry the loads imposed by dense AI racks, liquid-filled cooling systems, battery systems and rooftop heat-rejection plant, with margin, for the declared deployment.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall hold a structural capacity statement from the structural engineer of record that states the uniformly distributed and concentrated load capacity of each data hall, plant room, battery room and roof area. The facility owner shall ensure the statement accounts for operating (wet) mass of liquid-cooled racks, CDUs, manifolds, coolant distribution pipework and immersion tanks, and shall require a structural re-check before any deployment that raises planned load above the declared utilisation threshold.
assessmentCriteria: Structural capacity is stated for every area hosting IT, power, battery or cooling equipment, in kN/m² distributed and kN concentrated.
The load model uses operating mass including coolant, not dry shipping mass, for liquid-cooled equipment and pipework.
Roof and plant-deck capacity covers heat-rejection plant at operating weight, including any additions for AI expansion.
Raised-floor pedestals and panels, where used, are rated for rolling and concentrated loads of the heaviest rack during movement.
Planned load per area is below the utilisation threshold, or a structural re-check is on file.

parameters.name: Design uniformly distributed live load, data hall
parameters.basis: Structural engineer of record; capability profile for dense liquid-cooled racks

parameters.name: Planned-load utilisation threshold requiring structural re-check

minimumEvidence: Structural capacity statement or drawings with load capacities per area
Load schedule with operating mass of racks, CDUs, pipework and battery systems
Raised-floor system rating certificates (where raised floor used)
Structural re-check reports for deployments above threshold

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current statement reconciled to the latest load schedule.
evidenceProfile.independence: Capacity statement by a chartered or licensed structural engineer; load schedule reconciliation by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: Original design calculations plus a current letter of reliance from a structural engineer
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-02, CG-04.
reassessmentTriggers: New rack type with higher mass or density
Introduction of liquid or immersion cooling
Change of use of a room

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the structural statement and confirm author competence and date.
Rebuild the planned load per area from the rack and plant schedule using operating mass.
Compare planned load with capacity and with the utilisation threshold.
Verify re-check reports exist where thresholds are exceeded.
controls.applicability: Applies to all facilities and to colocation suites where the tenant's equipment imposes load; the tenant obtains the provider's rated capacity and supplies its own load schedule.
failureModes: Slab overstressed by wet mass of liquid-cooled racks
Roof overloaded by added dry coolers
Raised floor pedestal failure under rolling load
Load model based on dry mass
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If the load schedule cannot be reconciled to installed equipment, record a U5 UNKNOWN and treat structural adequacy for the affected area as unverified.
informativeReferences: EN 1991 (actions on structures) or ASCE/SEI 7 (minimum design loads)

controls.title: Rack Loading
controls.objective: Ensure that as-installed rack positions do not exceed the floor, raised-floor and rack-frame ratings for the actual mass of installed equipment, including liquid in manifolds and cold plates.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a rack-position load register recording the operating mass of every rack and the rated capacity of its position. The facility operator shall verify rack mass at installation for each new rack type, shall prevent installation where the position rating would be exceeded, and shall reconcile the register to installed equipment at the declared interval.
assessmentCriteria: The load register covers every occupied rack position in the assessed halls.
For each rack type, operating mass is evidenced by OEM data or weighing, including coolant.
No position exceeds its rated capacity; any exceedance has a structural engineer's acceptance.
A sample of positions reconciles to installed equipment during inspection.
Installation workflow blocks commissioning of a rack whose mass is not recorded.

parameters.name: Maximum operating mass per rack position

minimumEvidence: OEM mass data or weighing records for each rack type

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Register reconciled within the last 12 months and after each new rack type.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation sample selected and checked by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: DCIM asset records with mass fields where they are the controlled source
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-04, CG-14.
reassessmentTriggers: Retrofit of liquid cooling to existing racks

assessmentProcedure: Select a sample of positions across halls, weighted to the densest rows.
Compare installed equipment to the register and recompute mass.
Compare with position rating and identify exceedances.
Review the installation workflow for the mass check gate.
controls.applicability: Applies to all halls hosting AI racks. Not applicable to areas with only network or low-mass equipment where the register shows ample margin.
failureModes: Position overloaded after mid-life densification
Rack frame rating exceeded
Register not updated after rack swap
controls.testingSafety: Inspection only; assessors do not move or open racks. Weighing is performed by the operator's trained staff using rated equipment.
controls.unknownRule: If more than the sampled tolerance of positions cannot be reconciled, record a U5 UNKNOWN for the hall and limit the PHY-005 conclusion to reconciled areas.

controls.title: Anchorage and Vibration
controls.objective: Ensure that racks, CDUs, battery systems, tanks, switchgear and suspended services are restrained against seismic and operational loads, and that vibration from rotating plant does not degrade IT or storage equipment.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall specify and install anchorage and bracing for racks, CDUs, battery cabinets, fuel and water tanks, switchgear, busway and overhead cable and pipe supports to the seismic design level determined in MCF-PHY-001. The facility operator shall isolate generators, chillers and pumps so that vibration transmitted to IT spaces remains within the most restrictive OEM limit for installed equipment, and shall verify installed anchorage by inspection at commissioning and after changes.
assessmentCriteria: Anchorage design for each equipment class references the site seismic design level.
A sample inspection finds installed anchors and bracing matching the design for the sampled items.
Overhead busway, cable tray and liquid-cooling manifolds have bracing compatible with the design level.
Vibration isolation is installed on rotating plant and measured transmitted vibration in IT spaces is within the declared limit.
Seismic flexibility is provided at liquid pipework connections to racks and CDUs where the design level requires it.

parameters.name: Transmitted vibration limit at IT equipment

minimumEvidence: Anchorage and bracing design calculations or details
Vibration survey report for IT spaces with plant running

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Commissioning records and a vibration survey after the last plant change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample inspection by the assessor or an independent structural inspector.
acceptableAlternatives: Manufacturer seismic certification for pre-engineered racks where installed per instructions
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-09.

assessmentProcedure: Trace seismic design level into anchorage design per equipment class.
Inspect a sample of racks, CDUs, battery cabinets and tanks for anchors and bracing.
Review vibration survey conditions and results against limits.
Check flexible connections on liquid pipework at rack and CDU interfaces.
controls.applicability: Seismic elements apply where the local code assigns a seismic design category requiring non-structural restraint; vibration elements apply to all sites with rotating plant.
failureModes: Battery cabinet overturn in seismic event
Rigid pipe connection fracture releasing coolant
Storage throughput degradation from transmitted vibration
controls.testingSafety: Visual inspection only; no load testing of anchors by assessors. Inspection in energised rooms follows site electrical-safety rules and keeps outside arc-flash boundaries.
controls.unknownRule: If anchorage design is unavailable for battery or tank systems, record a U1 UNKNOWN and carry it into CG-09 as an unverified containment element.

controls.title: Building Envelope
controls.objective: Ensure the building envelope keeps water, wind-driven rain, dust and uncontrolled air out of IT and plant spaces and maintains the enclosure integrity on which gaseous suppression and air management depend.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall inspect roofs, roof penetrations, gutters, façades, louvres and doors at the declared interval and after severe weather, shall correct defects within a risk-based period, and shall prohibit water-bearing services and roof drainage from passing over IT and electrical rooms unless they are contained and monitored.
assessmentCriteria: Envelope inspection records exist at the declared interval and after each severe-weather warning.
No uncontained water-bearing pipe or roof drain passes over IT or electrical rooms.
Open envelope defects are tracked with risk-based target dates and none affecting IT spaces is overdue.
Water ingress events in the last 12 months have root cause and corrective action recorded.
minimumEvidence: Drawings showing services over IT and electrical rooms

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months including at least one wet season.
evidenceProfile.independence: Records sampled and roof inspected by the assessor where safe access exists.
acceptableAlternatives: Roofing contractor maintenance reports
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-06.

assessmentProcedure: Review inspection and defect records for completeness against the interval.
Inspect ceilings of IT and electrical rooms for water marks and uncontained services.
Review water ingress incidents and closure of actions.
controls.applicability: Applies to all enclosed facilities, including modular and containerised units; colocation tenants rely on provider evidence.
failureModes: Roof leak onto energised switchgear
Louvre failure admitting wind-driven rain
Envelope leakage defeating suppression hold time
controls.testingSafety: Roof access only under the site's work-at-height permit with edge protection; assessors do not access fragile roofs.
controls.unknownRule: If envelope inspection records are missing for more than one interval, record a U1 UNKNOWN; the control result is UNKNOWN for OPERATION claims.

controls.title: Security Zones
controls.objective: Ensure that the site is divided into layered security zones whose protection increases towards the most critical assets, including power and cooling plant as well as IT halls, so that access to any asset that can disable AI capability requires passing proportionate barriers.
controls.requirement: The security manager shall define a zoning model with at least perimeter, building, secure-corridor, critical-space and rack/cage levels, and shall assign every critical asset (MV intake, switchgear, UPS and battery rooms, generator yard, fuel, heat rejection, CDU and pump rooms, meet-me rooms, data halls, control rooms) to a zone. The security manager shall ensure each zone boundary has physical barriers, access control and detection appropriate to the zone and that critical plant zones are protected no less than the IT halls they serve.
assessmentCriteria: A zoning plan assigns every critical asset in the boundary to a zone with stated protection measures.
Power, cooling and fuel plant zones have access control and intrusion detection at least equivalent to the data halls they serve.
Zone boundaries are continuous (no bypass via ceiling voids, raised floors, risers or louvres) in the sampled areas.
Access to critical-space zones requires multi-factor authentication and anti-tailgating measures.
The zoning model is reconciled to the current floor plan and security system configuration.

parameters.name: Authentication factors at critical-space zone entry

minimumEvidence: Access-control system zone and reader configuration export
Barrier specifications and intrusion detection layout

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current configuration and plan at assessment date.
evidenceProfile.independence: Zone continuity inspection by the assessor or an independent security consultant.
acceptableAlternatives: Certified physical-security audit report covering zone continuity, if current
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-15, CG-09.

assessmentProcedure: Map each critical asset from the architecture to a zone in the plan.
Reconcile zone readers and doors in the access-control export to the plan.
Inspect a sample of zone boundaries for bypass routes through voids and risers.
Compare plant-zone protection with data-hall protection.
controls.applicability: Applies to all physical sites in the boundary. Colocation tenants assess the zones they control and rely on provider evidence for shared zones.
failureModes: Generator yard protected only by perimeter fence
Ceiling void bypasses hall boundary
Zoning plan out of date with hall extension
controls.testingSafety: Inspection only. Above-ceiling and below-floor checks are performed by facilities staff under permit; assessors do not lift floor tiles in live halls.
controls.unknownRule: If a critical plant area cannot be assigned to a zone or its boundary inspected, record a U5 UNKNOWN against that asset and treat its physical protection as unverified.

controls.title: Fire Zones
controls.objective: Ensure that fire compartmentation separates redundant power, cooling and network paths so that a single fire cannot disable both halves of a redundant system, and limits fire and smoke spread between IT, battery, electrical and plant spaces.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall define fire compartments in the fire strategy so that A and B power paths, redundant UPS and battery rooms, redundant cooling plant and diverse network routes are in separate compartments or are protected by fire-rated enclosures of the declared rating. The facility operator shall maintain fire-stopping of every penetration through compartment boundaries and shall inspect a sample of penetrations at the declared interval and after works.
assessmentCriteria: The fire strategy identifies compartments and their fire-resistance ratings.
An overlay of redundant paths on compartments shows no single compartment containing both redundant elements of any path, or a rated enclosure where they share one.
Lithium-ion battery rooms (UPS or BESS) are separate compartments of at least the declared rating.
A sample of penetrations inspected shows intact, certified fire-stopping matching the tested system.
Penetrations created by works in the last 12 months have fire-stopping completion records.

parameters.name: Fire resistance between compartments holding redundant paths
parameters.basis: Fire strategy; national building regulations; capability profile

minimumEvidence: Overlay of redundant paths on compartments
Fire-stopping register with certified product data
Works completion records for new penetrations

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Fire strategy current; penetration inspection within the last interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Penetration sample inspected by the assessor or a third-party fire-stopping inspector.
acceptableAlternatives: Third-party certified fire-stopping installer records, where the inspector is independent of the installer
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-09 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.
reassessmentTriggers: New cable or pipe routes through compartment boundaries
Introduction of lithium-ion batteries in a new location

assessmentProcedure: Overlay A/B power, redundant cooling and diverse network routes from the architecture onto the compartment drawings.
Identify any compartment hosting both redundant elements and check for rated enclosures.
Inspect a sample of penetrations against the fire-stopping register.
Review works records for penetrations created since the last inspection.
controls.applicability: Applies to all facilities. In modular or containerised deployments, compartments are the modules and the overlay shows separation between modules hosting redundant elements.
failureModes: Single fire disables both A and B paths in a shared riser (AIDCF-004 X09)
Unsealed penetration after cabling works
Battery fire spreads to adjacent UPS room
controls.testingSafety: Inspection only; no penetration is opened. Access to energised electrical rooms follows site electrical-safety rules.
controls.unknownRule: If the redundant-path overlay cannot be produced, record a U5 UNKNOWN; CG-09 becomes UNKNOWN for fire as a common-mode initiator.

controls.title: Water Zones
controls.objective: Ensure that liquid-bearing systems, which are pervasive in liquid-cooled AI halls, are spatially and physically separated from electrical distribution and that any leak is contained, detected and drained before it reaches energised equipment.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall define water zones identifying all spaces where water, glycol, dielectric fluid or refrigerant-bearing pipework is present. The facility owner shall locate or protect electrical switchgear, UPS, busway and PDUs so that a leak from any pipe, joint, CDU, manifold or quick-disconnect cannot reach them uncontained, using routing above or below with drip trays, bunding, falls to drains and zoned leak detection that alarms and, where declared, initiates isolation.
assessmentCriteria: A water-zone plan shows every liquid-bearing route and its relation to electrical equipment.
No liquid joint or valve is located directly above switchgear, UPS, busway tap-off or PDU without containment.
Leak detection covers each containment area and alarms to a monitored location; where isolation is automatic, valve closure has been tested.
Drainage capacity for each zone is sized for the declared maximum credible leak rate.
Raised-floor or slab areas with liquid distribution have falls or barriers preventing migration to electrical zones.

parameters.name: Leak alarm to isolation time (automatic isolation zones)
Maximum credible leak rate for drainage sizing
parameters.illustrativeDefault: per largest pipe and pump capacity in zone

minimumEvidence: Water-zone plan overlaid on electrical layout
Leak detection layout and alarm configuration
Inspection photographs of containment under joints

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current layout; isolation tests within the last 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Overlay and inspection sample by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: 3D coordination model where it is the controlled as-built source
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-09, CG-04.

assessmentProcedure: Overlay liquid routes on electrical layouts and list proximity conflicts.
Inspect each conflict for containment and leak detection.
Review alarm routing and isolation test records.
Check drainage falls and barriers in a sample of zones.
controls.applicability: Applies to all spaces with liquid-bearing systems, including chilled-water air cooling. Most demanding for direct-to-chip and immersion halls.
failureModes: Quick-disconnect leak onto rack PDU
Glycol leak migrating under raised floor to busway
Leak detection alarm not routed
Drain overwhelmed by pump discharge
controls.testingSafety: Assessors do not operate isolation valves. Functional tests of automatic isolation are performed by the operator under a method statement with the affected loop in a declared maintenance state.
controls.unknownRule: If the overlay cannot be produced for a liquid-cooled hall, record a U5 UNKNOWN and carry it into THM leak-management and CG-09 evaluation.

controls.title: Tenant Segregation
controls.objective: Ensure that, in shared or colocation facilities, each tenant's equipment and the shared infrastructure serving it are physically segregated and that responsibility for shared elements is explicit.
controls.requirement: The facility provider shall physically segregate tenant spaces using cages, suites or dedicated halls with access restricted to authorised tenant personnel, and shall disclose to each tenant the shared infrastructure (power paths, cooling loops, meet-me rooms, risers) serving its space. The tenant shall map its capability to those shared elements and record provider and tenant responsibilities for each.
assessmentCriteria: Each tenant space is enclosed with access limited to that tenant and authorised provider staff.
The provider's disclosure lists the shared power, cooling and connectivity elements serving the tenant space.
A responsibility matrix covers each shared element, including maintenance switching notification.
Inspection finds no tenant equipment or cabling outside its space or in another tenant's space.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current at assessment date.
evidenceProfile.independence: Disclosure verified by inspection by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: Colocation service description and SLA where they enumerate shared elements
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-13, CG-02.
reassessmentTriggers: New tenant adjacent to assessed space

assessmentProcedure: Obtain disclosure and map shared elements to the tenant's capability architecture.
Inspect tenant space boundaries and shared cable routes.
Review the responsibility matrix for maintenance switching and incident notification.
controls.applicability: Applies to colocation and multi-tenant facilities. Not applicable to single-tenant facilities, which record the determination.
failureModes: Undisclosed shared UPS serving multiple tenants
Neighbour tenant access to shared riser
Maintenance switching on shared path without tenant notification (AIDCF-004 X14)
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If the provider will not disclose shared elements, record a U2 UNKNOWN and a U10 dependency UNKNOWN for the affected power and cooling paths.

controls.title: Identity-Based Access
controls.objective: Ensure physical access to critical zones is granted to identified individuals on a need basis, is promptly revoked, and is recorded so that every entry to a critical space can be attributed.
controls.requirement: The security manager shall operate a physical access control system that grants access to critical-space zones only to named individuals with approved business need, enforces multi-factor authentication at those zones, revokes access within the declared latency when a person leaves or changes role, and reviews critical-zone access rights at the declared interval. The security manager shall integrate leaver events from the authoritative HR or contractor source.
assessmentCriteria: Access rights to critical zones are traceable to an approval for every sampled holder.
Leavers in the sample period had critical-zone access revoked within the declared latency.
Access reviews for critical zones were completed at the declared interval with removals actioned.
Shared or generic credentials do not grant critical-zone access.
Access events are retained and time-synchronised for the declared period.
minimumEvidence: Access-control system user and rights export
HR/contractor leaver list reconciled to revocation logs

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of access reviews and leaver events.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation performed by the assessor from system exports obtained under observation.
acceptableAlternatives: Independent audit sample of the same population and period
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-15.

assessmentProcedure: Export critical-zone rights under observation and sample holders.
Trace each sampled holder to an approval.
Reconcile leavers in the period to revocation timestamps.
Review access-review evidence and removal actions.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever the assessed party controls physical access; colocation tenants assess the provider's process for their space through provider evidence.
failureModes: Leaver retains access to switchgear room
Contractor credential shared
Access rights accumulate
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If the leaver population cannot be obtained, record a U2 UNKNOWN; the OPERATION claim is UNKNOWN.

controls.title: Visitor Control
controls.objective: Ensure that visitors, vendors and contractors, including OEM field engineers servicing accelerator systems, are identified, authorised, escorted and supervised in critical spaces.
controls.requirement: The security manager shall require pre-registration, identity verification and host approval for every visitor, shall issue time-limited credentials, and shall require escort in critical-space zones at no more than the declared visitor-to-escort ratio. The facility operator shall link contractor attendance in plant spaces to an approved work order or permit.
assessmentCriteria: Every sampled visitor entry has pre-registration, ID verification and host approval.
Visitor credentials expire at the end of the approved visit.
Escort ratio in critical zones did not exceed the declared value in sampled visits.
Contractor entries to plant spaces trace to an approved work order or permit.

parameters.name: Maximum visitors per escort in critical zones

minimumEvidence: Work orders linked to contractor entries

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: A sample from the last six months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample selected by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: Manual visitor log where electronic system not used, if sequential and complete
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

assessmentProcedure: Sample visitor entries to critical zones.
Trace each to pre-registration, ID check and approval.
Reconcile contractor entries to work orders.
Observe a visitor journey.
controls.applicability: Applies to all staffed sites. Unstaffed edge sites apply the work-order linkage element only.
failureModes: Unescorted vendor in data hall
Contractor working without permit
Credential reused after visit
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If visitor records are incomplete for the sample, record a U1 UNKNOWN and a Finding.

controls.title: Surveillance Coverage
controls.objective: Ensure video surveillance covers entries to critical zones, critical plant and high-value asset areas at an image quality sufficient for the declared purpose, with retention and integrity supporting investigation.
controls.requirement: The security manager shall define an operational requirement for each camera view stating its purpose (detect, observe, recognise or identify), shall install and maintain cameras to meet it, shall retain recordings for the declared period with integrity protection, and shall verify coverage after layout changes.
assessmentCriteria: An operational requirement lists each critical zone entry and plant area with its purpose category.
Sampled camera views meet the image quality for their declared purpose.
Recordings are retained for the declared period and the sample retrieves successfully.
Camera health monitoring alarms on loss of view and outages are corrected within the declared time.
Exported footage has integrity protection (hash or signed export).

parameters.name: Recording retention
parameters.basis: Capability profile; local privacy law limits

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current configuration; health logs for three months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Stills and retrieval performed under assessor observation.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

assessmentProcedure: Review the operational requirement against the zoning plan.
Sample views and assess image quality against purpose.
Retrieve a recording at the end of the retention window.
Review camera health alarms and outage closure.
controls.applicability: Applies where surveillance is a declared safeguard; privacy law may limit retention and is recorded as a constraint.
failureModes: Blind spot at generator yard gate
Recordings overwritten before investigation
Camera outage undetected
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If retrieval cannot be demonstrated, record a U8 method UNKNOWN for surveillance evidence.

controls.title: Alarm Response
controls.objective: Demonstrate that intrusion, forced-door, held-door and tamper alarms at critical zones are acknowledged and physically attended within declared times, including at night and when many alarms occur together.
controls.requirement: The security manager shall define acknowledgement and attendance times for each alarm class in critical zones, shall staff and equip the response to meet them, and shall test response by unannounced exercises at the declared interval, including an exercise during concurrent facility alarms.
assessmentCriteria: Alarm classes and target acknowledgement and attendance times are defined.
Alarm records for the period show the targets were met for the declared percentage of alarms.
At least the declared number of unannounced exercises were run and met attendance targets.
One exercise tested response while other facility alarms were active.
Missed targets have root cause and corrective action.
minimumEvidence: Alarm logs with acknowledgement and attendance times

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of alarms and exercises, including night shifts.
evidenceProfile.independence: At least one exercise designed and timed by the assessor or an independent party.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.
reassessmentTriggers: Change of guard force or staffing

assessmentProcedure: Analyse alarm logs for acknowledgement and attendance times by class.
Review exercises for design, unannounced status and results.
Conduct or witness an unannounced exercise at a plant-zone door.
Review corrective actions for missed targets.
controls.applicability: Applies to staffed or remotely monitored sites. Unstaffed sites declare remote-response times and use the same criteria.
failureModes: Forced-door alarm acknowledged but not attended
Alarm missed during facility alarm flood (AIDCF-004 X11)
controls.testingSafety: Exercises are coordinated with the control room supervisor so that the exercise is not mistaken for a real event requiring emergency services; no exercise triggers suppression or EPO circuits.
controls.unknownRule: If attendance times are not recorded, record a U1 UNKNOWN; the EFFECTIVENESS claim is UNKNOWN.
informativeReferences: EN 50131 series (intrusion and hold-up alarm systems)

controls.title: Delivery Controls
controls.objective: Ensure inbound deliveries of high-value AI hardware, storage media and critical spares are received against an expected manifest, inspected for tampering and held under custody until accepted.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall receive critical deliveries only against an advance notice and purchase reference, shall inspect seals and packaging for tampering, shall record serial numbers at receipt and shall hold received items in a controlled store until they are accepted into the asset register.
assessmentCriteria: Sampled deliveries trace to advance notice and purchase reference.
Seal and packaging inspection is recorded for every sampled critical delivery.
Serial numbers recorded at receipt match the shipping manifest and the asset register.
Received items are stored in a controlled zone until acceptance.

parameters.name: Inbound critical shipments with seal inspection

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Six months of receipts.
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample selected by the assessor.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

assessmentProcedure: Sample critical deliveries.
Trace to notice, inspection, serials and register.
Observe the controlled store.
controls.applicability: Applies to sites receiving accelerators, storage media, network optics or critical spares.
failureModes: Tampered accelerator module accepted
Serial mismatch undetected
Delivery left in unsecured dock
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If receipt records cannot be reconciled to serials, record a U5 UNKNOWN and refer to SUP provenance controls.
informativeReferences: ISO 28000 (security management for the supply chain)

controls.title: Equipment Movement
controls.objective: Ensure movement of dense racks and heavy plant within the facility is planned, authorised and executed without exceeding route ratings, damaging live infrastructure or creating tip-over and crush hazards.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall require a move plan, approved by the facilities engineer, for every movement of a rack or plant item above the declared mass threshold, stating route, route ratings, equipment (skates, tuggers, lifting), crew competence and proximity to live services. The facility operator shall drain or isolate liquid-cooled racks where the OEM requires it before movement.
assessmentCriteria: Every sampled move above threshold has an approved move plan.
Move plans reference route ratings from MCF-PHY-003 and floor ratings from MCF-PHY-005.
Crew competence for heavy moves is evidenced.
Liquid-cooled racks were moved in the OEM-required fluid state.
Move incidents (floor damage, near misses) are recorded and investigated.

parameters.name: Rack or plant mass requiring an approved move plan

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of moves.
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample selected by the assessor.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-04.

assessmentProcedure: Sample moves from work orders.
Check move plans for route and floor rating references.
Verify crew competence and fluid-state compliance.
Observe a move where scheduled.
controls.applicability: Applies to sites deploying racks or plant above the mass threshold.
failureModes: Rack tip-over on ramp
Raised floor collapse under rolling load
Coolant spill during move
controls.testingSafety: Assessors observe moves from outside the exclusion zone set by the move supervisor and never assist.
controls.unknownRule: If move plans are missing for the sample, record a U1 UNKNOWN and a Finding.
informativeReferences: Rack OEM installation and relocation guides

controls.title: Media Custody
controls.objective: Ensure storage media holding training data, checkpoints or model weights are inventoried and in unbroken custody whenever they are removed from service, in transit, under repair or awaiting destruction.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a serialised inventory of data-bearing media outside production service, shall record each custody transfer with time, person and location, shall store media in a controlled container or room, and shall reconcile the inventory at the declared interval. The data owner shall define which media classes require encryption verification before leaving the controlled store.
assessmentCriteria: Every data-bearing device removed from service in the sample appears in the custody inventory.
Custody transfers are recorded without gaps from removal to final disposition.
Inventory reconciliation at the declared interval shows no unexplained missing media.
Failed drives returned to OEMs under RMA follow the data owner's rule (retain, sanitise or encrypt).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation reperformed by the assessor for a sample.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

assessmentProcedure: Sample drive removals from storage health and ticket records.
Trace each to the custody inventory and transfers.
Reperform a reconciliation of the controlled store.
Review RMA disposition against the data owner's rule.
controls.applicability: Applies to all data-bearing media in the boundary, including accelerator node local NVMe.
failureModes: Drive with model weights shipped under RMA unencrypted
Media missing from store
Custody gap during transit
