controls.testingSafety: Desk-based assessment; no hazardous testing. Site walk-downs follow the host site induction and are escorted in plant areas.
controls.unknownRule: If any media cannot be accounted for, record a Finding; if the inventory cannot be reconciled, record a U5 UNKNOWN.

controls.title: Decommissioning Custody
controls.objective: Ensure that equipment leaving the facility at end of life, including accelerators, servers, storage and network devices, is sanitised or destroyed to the declared standard with verified certificates, and that decommissioning does not disturb live infrastructure.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall decommission equipment only under an approved decommissioning work order that identifies the asset, its data-bearing components, dependent power and cooling connections and the sanitisation or destruction method. The facility operator shall obtain a certificate per serial from any third-party disposal provider and shall reconcile certificates to the decommissioning list.
assessmentCriteria: Each sampled decommissioned asset has an approved work order.
Sanitisation or destruction method matches the data owner's classification.
Certificates exist per serial and reconcile to the decommissioning list.
Isolation of power and liquid connections followed the approved method statement.

parameters.name: Decommissioned data-bearing devices with per-serial certificate

minimumEvidence: Reconciliation of certificates to asset list

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of decommissioning.
evidenceProfile.independence: Certificate reconciliation by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: Witnessed on-site destruction records
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

assessmentProcedure: Sample decommissioned assets from the register.
Trace each to work order, method and certificate.
Review isolation evidence for liquid-cooled equipment.
controls.applicability: Applies to all decommissioning in the boundary.
failureModes: Unsanitised drive leaves site
Wrong rack isolated during decommissioning
Certificate missing
controls.testingSafety: Assessors do not witness isolations inside arc-flash boundaries; liquid disconnection is observed from outside the drip zone.
controls.unknownRule: If certificates cannot be reconciled, record a U1 UNKNOWN per unreconciled serial and a Finding.

controls.title: Fire Detection
controls.objective: Demonstrate that fire detection in IT, electrical, battery and plant spaces detects incipient fires early enough for safe evacuation and for controlled response before a fire disables redundant infrastructure, accounting for high airflow and liquid-cooled hall conditions.
controls.requirement: The fire safety manager shall provide detection designed for the airflow conditions of each space: very early warning aspirating smoke detection in high-airflow IT halls and electrical rooms, and off-gas or appropriate gas detection plus heat and smoke detection in lithium-ion battery rooms and enclosures. The fire safety manager shall test detection functionally at the declared interval, including smoke transport time for aspirating systems, and shall ensure alarms are received at a continuously staffed location.
assessmentCriteria: Detection design for each space states the detection type and how high airflow was accounted for.
Lithium-ion battery rooms and BESS enclosures have off-gas detection as specified by the battery safety assessment, in addition to smoke and heat detection.
Functional tests at the declared interval cover all detectors or sampling points, with aspirating transport times within the design value.
Detection alarms are received and acknowledged at a continuously staffed location, demonstrated in the period.
Impairments are recorded with compensating measures and closed within the declared time.
Acceptance or periodic inspection by the authority having jurisdiction or a certified inspector is current.

parameters.name: Aspirating detection maximum transport time
parameters.illustrativeDefault: per design; not greater than the EN 54-20 class limit

parameters.name: Detection functional test interval
parameters.basis: NFPA 72 or national fire code; capability profile

parameters.name: Maximum detection impairment duration without compensating measure

minimumEvidence: Functional test reports with transport times
Battery safety assessment specifying off-gas detection

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent full test cycle and twelve months of impairments.
evidenceProfile.independence: Functional test performed or witnessed by a certified fire-system contractor or inspector independent of the design author.
acceptableAlternatives: Insurer engineering survey including witnessed detection tests
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.
reassessmentTriggers: Change of airflow regime (containment, liquid-cooling retrofit)

assessmentProcedure: Review detection design for airflow and battery hazards.
Check test reports for coverage, transport times and defects.
Witness a smoke or transport-time test at a sampled point.
Verify alarm receipt and acknowledgement at the staffed location.
Review impairment records and compensating measures.
controls.applicability: Applies to all facilities. Colocation tenants rely on provider test evidence and witness where contractually permitted.
failureModes: Smoke diluted by high airflow below detector threshold
Battery off-gas undetected before thermal runaway
Aspirating pipe blocked
Alarm not received during control-room outage
controls.testingSafety: Detection tests use approved test aerosols or smoke sources; the fire safety manager isolates suppression release and notifies the alarm receiving centre before testing, and restores after. No test is performed in a battery room during a known battery fault.
controls.unknownRule: If functional test evidence for detection in a battery room or IT hall is missing or older than the interval, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-04; testing that depends on the room (for example load tests) is not authorised until resolved.
informativeReferences: EN 54 series (fire detection and fire alarm systems)
FM Global Property Loss Prevention Data Sheets (data centres; energy storage)

controls.title: Suppression Interfaces
controls.objective: Demonstrate that suppression systems and their interfaces with power, cooling, ventilation and control systems act as designed, so that suppression is effective without causing an avoidable loss of AI capability or an unsafe condition.
controls.requirement: The fire safety manager shall maintain a cause-and-effect matrix covering every interface between detection, suppression (sprinkler, pre-action, water mist, gaseous agent) and other systems, including HVAC shutdown, damper closure, CDU and pump behaviour, power isolation and door release. The fire safety manager shall test the matrix end to end at the declared interval, shall verify room integrity for gaseous systems by enclosure test, and shall confirm that fire-mode actions do not stop liquid cooling to unaffected areas unless the fire strategy requires it.
assessmentCriteria: A cause-and-effect matrix exists and matches the configured logic in the fire panel and BMS.
End-to-end interface tests at the declared interval demonstrate each output, with deviations closed.
Gaseous-agent rooms pass an enclosure integrity test demonstrating the design hold time.
Fire-mode effects on liquid cooling and CDUs are defined, and unaffected halls keep cooling in the test.
Suppression agent quantity and cylinder pressure are verified at the declared interval.
Water-based suppression in IT spaces is pre-action or otherwise protected against inadvertent discharge, where the fire strategy requires.

parameters.name: Gaseous agent design hold time
parameters.basis: NFPA 2001 or ISO 14520 design practice; fire engineer's design

minimumEvidence: Fire panel and BMS logic exports
Agent quantity and cylinder inspection records

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent full interface test and enclosure test within interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Interface tests witnessed by a party independent of the fire contractor (assessor, insurer or AHJ).
acceptableAlternatives: Integrated systems test (IST) report where it exercises the full matrix
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.
reassessmentTriggers: BMS or fire panel logic change

assessmentProcedure: Reconcile the matrix to fire panel and BMS logic exports.
Review end-to-end test reports for coverage and deviations.
Witness an interface test where scheduled, including CDU behaviour.
Review enclosure integrity results against design hold time.
Confirm agent inventory and cylinder inspections.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever suppression is installed; partial applicability where only sprinklers exist (enclosure test not applicable).
failureModes: Fire alarm stops all CDUs site-wide
Gaseous agent leaks out before hold time
Damper fails open
Inadvertent discharge damages storage (acoustic) or IT (water)
controls.testingSafety: End-to-end tests are performed with agent release physically disabled and verified disabled before testing; HVAC and CDU interlocks are tested under a method statement approved by the facility operator with thermal contingency in place. Gaseous rooms are cleared and posted before enclosure tests; no assessor is present during any live discharge.
controls.unknownRule: If the matrix cannot be reconciled to configured logic, or no end-to-end test is current, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-04 and refer the cooling interlock gap to CG-06.

controls.title: Egress and Emergency Access
controls.objective: Ensure occupants of data halls, plant rooms and battery rooms can escape safely and emergency responders can gain access, including in dense hot-aisle/cold-aisle containment, liquid-cooled halls with overhead manifolds and spaces protected by gaseous agents.
controls.requirement: The fire safety manager shall maintain egress routes from every occupied space within the travel distances of the fire strategy, shall ensure secured doors on escape routes release on fire alarm or by local override, shall provide pre-discharge warning and abort controls for gaseous systems, and shall provide emergency responders with plans, hazard information (batteries, refrigerants, coolants, arc-flash hazards) and access means.
assessmentCriteria: Travel distances and exit widths in sampled spaces meet the fire strategy, including inside containment.
Containment doors and escape-route doors release on fire alarm and by local override, demonstrated.
Gaseous-agent spaces have audible and visual pre-discharge warnings and abort controls at exits.
Emergency responder information packs exist and include battery, refrigerant and electrical hazards.
Egress routes are unobstructed during inspection.
Emergency lighting is tested at the declared interval.

parameters.name: Emergency lighting full-duration test interval
parameters.basis: National emergency lighting standard (e.g. EN 50172); capability profile

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of tests; inspection at assessment.
evidenceProfile.independence: Fire authority or certified inspector acceptance current; inspection by the assessor.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Walk egress routes from the furthest point in sampled halls and plant rooms.
Test a sample of containment and escape doors for release.
Review gaseous warning and abort tests.
Review the responder pack for current hazards.
controls.applicability: Applies to all occupied facilities. Unoccupied modular units declare responder access only.
failureModes: Escape blocked by containment doors that lock on power loss
Responders unaware of lithium-ion BESS
Abort control unreachable
controls.testingSafety: Door release tests are coordinated with security so that zone protection is maintained; tests that drop fire alarm outputs follow the fire safety manager's isolation procedure.
controls.unknownRule: If egress in containment or battery rooms cannot be verified, record a US4 UNKNOWN for CG-04.
informativeReferences: NFPA 101 (life safety code) or national building regulations

controls.title: Emergency Shutdown Governance
controls.objective: Ensure emergency power-off (EPO) and other emergency shutdown functions protect people and responders while being protected against inadvertent or malicious activation that would cause an uncontrolled shutdown of AI capability.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall define the scope of each emergency shutdown function (EPO, battery disconnect, fuel shut-off, CDU emergency stop) and the authority to activate it. The facility operator shall protect activation devices against inadvertent operation (covers, two-action operation, location), shall verify by test at the declared interval that each function isolates exactly its declared scope, and shall review any activation as a significant incident.
assessmentCriteria: Each emergency shutdown function has a documented scope, activation authority and legal basis (code requirement or fire strategy).
Activation devices have protection against inadvertent operation and are labelled with scope.
Functional tests at the declared interval show each function isolates exactly its declared scope (no more, no less).
Remote or software activation paths, where present, are identified and protected under SEC controls.
Activations in the period were investigated with lessons applied.
minimumEvidence: Control logic exports for remote paths

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent test cycle and twelve months of activations.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test witnessed by an independent electrical or fire engineer.
acceptableAlternatives: Test during integrated systems test with recorded scope verification
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.
reassessmentTriggers: Change in electrical distribution or CDU controls

assessmentProcedure: Review scope schedule and legal basis.
Inspect a sample of activation devices for protection and labelling.
Review functional test evidence for scope correctness.
Identify remote activation paths and confirm protection.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever EPO or emergency shutdown functions are installed; where codes do not require EPO and none is installed, battery and fuel shut-off elements still apply.
failureModes: Unprotected EPO button pressed in error
EPO scope wider than labelled
Remote EPO path reachable from IT network
Battery disconnect fails to isolate
controls.testingSafety: EPO and shutdown function tests are hazardous to capability: they are performed only during an approved shutdown window or with the load transferred, under a method statement approved by the facility owner's authorised engineer, with written authorisation and a rollback plan. Assessors witness and do not operate.
controls.unknownRule: If the actual scope of an EPO function has never been verified by test, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-04 and an associated UNKNOWN on CG-09 for unbounded shutdown scope.

controls.title: Utility Capacity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that contracted and physically available utility import capacity covers the declared peak site demand, including AI training clusters at full power, cooling at design ambient and battery recharge after an outage, with margin and with a forecast that precedes deployments.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall hold a connection agreement stating firm import capacity and any non-firm or curtailable portions, and shall maintain a site demand model that sums IT load at declared accelerator power limits, cooling and mechanical load at design ambient, losses, and UPS/BESS recharge load. The facility owner shall show firm capacity exceeds modelled peak demand by the declared margin, shall compare modelled with metered peak demand at least quarterly, and shall not commission additional AI capacity that would erode the margin without an approved capacity increase or load-limiting measure.
assessmentCriteria: The connection agreement states firm import capacity, non-firm portions and any curtailment terms.
The demand model includes IT load at declared power limits, mechanical load at design ambient, distribution and conversion losses, and UPS/BESS recharge.
Firm capacity exceeds modelled peak demand by at least the declared margin.
Metered 15-minute or finer peak demand over the period is within the modelled value, or the model has been corrected.
Planned AI deployments in the next forecast horizon are included and a capacity gap, if any, has an approved remediation before deployment.
Transformer and incomer ratings in the as-built single-line diagram are consistent with the firm capacity and the demand model.

parameters.name: Margin of firm import capacity over modelled peak demand
Metered demand integration interval
parameters.basis: Utility tariff metering practice; finer resolution needed to capture AI load dynamics

minimumEvidence: Connection agreement and any curtailment/flexible connection terms
Site demand model with assumptions (accelerator power limits, PUE at design ambient, recharge)
Metered demand data from the revenue or EPMS meters for the period
As-built single-line diagram with incomer and transformer ratings
Capacity forecast and approved remediation actions

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of metered demand including the seasonal cooling peak and peak AI utilisation.
evidenceProfile.independence: Demand model recomputed by the assessor from source data; metered data obtained from the revenue meter operator or EPMS export under observation.
acceptableAlternatives: Utility capacity statement letter where the agreement is confidential, if it states firm capacity and curtailment terms
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.
reassessmentTriggers: New AI cluster or accelerator generation with higher power limit
Utility network reinforcement or constraint notice

assessmentProcedure: Extract firm and non-firm capacity and curtailment terms from the agreement.
Rebuild the demand model from rack power limits, mechanical design data and recharge rates.
Compare with metered peaks at the finest available resolution.
Check margin and forecast deployments against firm capacity.
Reconcile incomer and transformer ratings on the single-line diagram.
controls.applicability: Applies to every site drawing utility power. For colocation tenants the provider's capacity allocation to the tenant's suite replaces the connection agreement.
failureModes: Peak demand exceeds firm capacity during seasonal cooling peak
Recharge load after outage trips incomers
Non-firm capacity relied on for critical load
Deployment commissioned before capacity upgrade
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based analysis and meter data export; no switching or measurement inside energised enclosures.
controls.unknownRule: If metered peak demand for the cooling peak season is unavailable, record a U5 UNKNOWN; CG-05 becomes UNKNOWN for the capacity criterion until data for that season exists.
informativeReferences: Distribution or transmission network connection codes of the jurisdiction (e.g. EU Network Code on Demand Connection)

controls.title: Grid Quality
controls.objective: Establish the actual quality of the utility supply at the point of common coupling (voltage variations, dips, swells, interruptions, unbalance, flicker and harmonics) and confirm that the facility's ride-through and conversion equipment is specified for it.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall measure supply quality at each utility point of common coupling using power quality instruments conforming to IEC 61000-4-30 Class A, shall retain events and statistics for the declared period, and shall compare measured characteristics with the voltage characteristics assumed in the design basis and with the utility's declared characteristics. The facility operator shall report events that exceeded design assumptions to the electrical engineer responsible for MCF-POW-019 for evaluation.
assessmentCriteria: Class A power quality monitoring is installed at each utility point of common coupling.
Statistics for voltage magnitude, unbalance, flicker and harmonics are available for the period.
All dips, swells and interruptions in the period are logged with magnitude and duration.
Measured characteristics are compared with the design basis and the utility's declared characteristics.
Events outside design assumptions have an engineering evaluation.

parameters.name: Supply voltage variation assumed in design
parameters.basis: EN 50160 voltage characteristics or utility declaration

minimumEvidence: Power quality instrument list and Class A certificates
Utility declared characteristics or connection terms

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of continuous monitoring.
evidenceProfile.independence: PQ data exported under observation; evaluation by an electrical engineer independent of operations where events exceeded design.
acceptableAlternatives: Utility-provided PQ data at the PCC, if Class A and covering the period
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-05.
reassessmentTriggers: New large load or generator nearby

assessmentProcedure: Confirm instrument class and location at each PCC.
Analyse event logs and statistics for the period.
Compare with design assumptions and utility declaration.
Review evaluations of exceeding events.
controls.applicability: Applies to sites with a direct utility connection. Colocation tenants obtain provider PQ data at the tenant's UPS input.
failureModes: Frequent dips cause UPS battery cycling and premature ageing
Unbalance overheats transformers
Grid harmonics excite filter resonance
controls.testingSafety: Instrument data is retrieved via EPMS; installation of portable PQ loggers inside energised panels is performed only by authorised persons under permit with appropriate PPE.
controls.unknownRule: If no Class A data exists at the PCC, record a U1 UNKNOWN; ride-through claims under MCF-POW-019 are limited to design evidence.

controls.title: Connection Reliability
controls.objective: Establish the real independence and reliability of the utility connection(s), including shared upstream substations, transmission circuits and protection schemes, so that claimed dual feeds are not a single upstream fault domain.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall obtain from the network operator the upstream topology of each utility feed to the first point of independent supply, and shall identify shared substations, busbars, circuits, rights-of-way and protection schemes. The facility owner shall record the historic interruption performance of each feed, and shall not describe feeds as independent in the design basis unless no shared upstream element is identified.
assessmentCriteria: Upstream topology to the first independent source point is documented for each feed.
Shared upstream elements (substation, bus, circuit, route, protection) are listed or explicitly none.
Interruption history for each feed over the declared period is recorded.
Design basis claims of feed independence are consistent with the shared-element list.
Residual common-mode exposures are reflected in generator and UPS autonomy sizing.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current topology; interruption history for the declared period.
evidenceProfile.independence: Topology from the network operator, not the facility's own assumption.
acceptableAlternatives: Independent grid study commissioned by the owner using network operator data
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-03, CG-05, CG-09.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain topology and trace each feed upstream.
Identify shared elements and compare with design basis claims.
Review interruption history and correlation between feeds.
controls.applicability: Applies to all utility-connected sites; most significant where the design basis claims dual independent feeds.
failureModes: Two feeds from the same grid substation bus
Shared overhead route damaged by storm
Common intertrip scheme
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based.
controls.unknownRule: If the network operator does not provide upstream topology, record a U10 dependency UNKNOWN and treat feeds as one fault domain for CG-05 sizing.

controls.title: Utility Contingency
controls.objective: Ensure the facility can sustain declared outcomes through prolonged utility interruption, grid emergency instructions, curtailment and demand-response events, and can meet its grid connection obligations as a large load.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain a utility contingency plan covering prolonged interruption, grid-operator curtailment or disconnection instructions, demand-response commitments and re-energisation constraints. The facility owner shall define, for each event type, which AI workloads are shed or throttled, how cooling and IT load are reduced in a controlled sequence, the decision authority, and the communications with the network operator, and shall exercise the plan at the declared interval.
assessmentCriteria: The plan covers prolonged outage, curtailment instruction, demand response and re-energisation.
Load-reduction steps identify workloads (by class or cluster), expected MW reduction and time to achieve it.
Workload throttling or checkpoint-and-pause is demonstrated in an exercise to achieve the declared reduction within the declared time.
Contractual obligations as a large load (notification, ride-through, ramp limits) are listed and mapped to procedures.
Decision authority and network-operator contacts are current.

parameters.name: Time to achieve declared load reduction on curtailment instruction

minimumEvidence: Exercise records with achieved MW reduction and time

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent exercise within interval; twelve months of curtailment events.
evidenceProfile.independence: Exercise observed by the assessor or a party independent of the operations team.
acceptableAlternatives: Record of a real curtailment event handled per plan
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-05, CG-10.
reassessmentTriggers: Change in connection agreement or flexibility contract
New AI cluster with different shed characteristics

assessmentProcedure: Review plan coverage against event types.
Trace load-reduction steps to scheduler or power-capping mechanisms.
Review or observe an exercise and compare achieved reduction with plan.
Check obligations mapping and contacts.
controls.applicability: Applies to sites with grid connection agreements that include curtailment, flexibility or large-load obligations, and to all sites for prolonged outage planning.
failureModes: Curtailment instruction cannot be met in time
Uncontrolled shedding loses training state
Re-energisation inrush violates connection limits
controls.testingSafety: Exercises use workload throttling or scheduler controls; no electrical switching is performed for the exercise unless separately authorised under MCF-POW-023.
controls.unknownRule: If the plan has never been exercised, record a U5 UNKNOWN; the RESILIENCE claim is UNKNOWN and supports design only.
informativeReferences: EU Network Code on Demand Connection (Regulation (EU) 2016/1388)
Network operator large-load connection requirements of the jurisdiction

controls.title: Generator Capacity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that standby or prime generation can carry the declared critical load, including mechanical load and AI load dynamics, with the declared redundancy, at site design ambient and altitude, for the declared duration.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall size generation using the ISO 8528-1 rating class appropriate to the duty (for example data-centre continuous power where unlimited running hours at variable load are required) with derating for design ambient temperature, altitude and fuel. The facility owner shall verify by load-bank or real-load testing at commissioning and at the declared interval that each generator, and the paralleled system, carries its rated load at the declared redundancy with one unit out of service.
assessmentCriteria: Generator rating class and kW rating per ISO 8528-1 are recorded and are appropriate to the declared duty and running hours.
Derated capacity at site design ambient and altitude covers critical IT plus mechanical load with the declared redundancy (for example N+1) available.
Commissioning and periodic load-bank or real-load tests reached the declared load and duration for each unit and the paralleled system.
Generator capacity is reconciled to the current demand model in MCF-POW-001.
Radiator and air-intake performance at design ambient (including recirculation in the yard) is accounted for in derating.

parameters.name: Site design ambient for generator derating
parameters.illustrativeDefault: site extreme design value (ASHRAE climatic data, n-year return; illustrative n=20)
parameters.basis: ASHRAE Handbook climatic design data; capability profile

parameters.name: Periodic load-bank test duration at rated load
parameters.basis: NFPA 110 or national emergency power practice; capability profile

minimumEvidence: Generator datasheets with ISO 8528 rating class
Derating calculation for ambient and altitude

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Commissioning test plus the most recent periodic load test within interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Load tests witnessed by a party independent of the generator maintenance contractor.

evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

Recompute derated capacity at design ambient and altitude.
Compare with demand model and redundancy with one unit out.
Review load test records for load, duration and anomalies.
Witness a load test where scheduled.
controls.applicability: Applies to sites with on-site generation for critical load. Not applicable where the declared outcome tolerance accepts loss on utility failure beyond UPS autonomy and this is approved.
failureModes: Generators derate below load during heatwave
Prime-rated units used beyond rating class
Paralleled system cannot carry load with one unit out
controls.testingSafety: Hazardous-energy activity. Tests and switching are performed only by authorised persons under the site electrical safety rules, an approved method statement and permit to work, with written authorisation from the facility owner's authorised engineer; assessors witness from outside the arc-flash boundary and never operate equipment. Load-bank connection points are engineered; temporary cabling is inspected before energising.
controls.unknownRule: If no load test at rated load exists within the interval, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-05.

controls.title: Start Reliability
controls.objective: Demonstrate that generators start, synchronise and accept load within the time the UPS or BESS autonomy allows, on every demand, including after long standby periods and in cold or hot ambient.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall test each generator by monthly start and run tests at the declared load and by periodic transfer tests through the automatic transfer or paralleling controls, shall record start time, time to ready-to-load and anomalies, shall maintain starting systems (batteries or air, jacket-water heating, fuel priming), and shall treat any failed or delayed start as an incident with root cause analysis.
assessmentCriteria: Monthly start/run tests at the declared load and duration are recorded for every unit.
Recorded start-to-ready-to-load time is within the declared limit and within the UPS/BESS autonomy with margin.
Starting batteries or air systems, jacket-water heaters and fuel priming are maintained and monitored.
Failed or delayed starts in the period have root cause and corrective action.
Paralleling or transfer control sequences have been tested end to end at the declared interval.

parameters.name: Start reliability threshold for incident review
parameters.unit: failed or delayed starts per year

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of monthly tests including winter and summer.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test logs reconciled to controller event logs extracted under observation.
acceptableAlternatives: Real utility-outage starts with controller logs, if timing is recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Analyse twelve months of tests for completeness, timing and load.
Reconcile manual logs to controller event logs.
Review starting system maintenance and alarms.
Review failed or delayed starts and RCA.
Witness a monthly test where scheduled.
controls.applicability: Applies to all critical-load generators.
failureModes: Starting battery failure (AIDCF-004 X01)
Fuel line air lock after maintenance
Paralleling controller fails to close breaker
Cold-start delay exceeds UPS autonomy
controls.testingSafety: Hazardous-energy activity. Tests and switching are performed only by authorised persons under the site electrical safety rules, an approved method statement and permit to work, with written authorisation from the facility owner's authorised engineer; assessors witness from outside the arc-flash boundary and never operate equipment. Transfer tests with live critical load require approval of the test window and confirmation that UPS/BESS autonomy and redundancy are healthy before starting.
controls.unknownRule: If monthly test records are missing for any unit for more than one month, or controller logs cannot corroborate timing, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-05.

controls.title: Fuel Autonomy
controls.objective: Demonstrate that on-site fuel stored, usable and of acceptable quality supports generation at the declared load for the declared autonomy, without relying on deliveries during that period.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain usable on-site fuel (excluding unusable tank bottoms and day-tank minimums) sufficient for the declared autonomy at the declared load, using measured consumption curves, and shall keep the minimum stock level as an alarmed threshold. The facility operator shall test fuel quality at the declared interval against the applicable fuel specification, shall polish or replace fuel that fails, and shall maintain fuel transfer pumps and controls in a redundant configuration matching the generator redundancy.
assessmentCriteria: Usable fuel volume is calculated excluding unusable volumes and is at or above the minimum level for the declared autonomy at the declared load.
Consumption is based on measured or OEM curves at the declared load, not nameplate maximum only.
Fuel level telemetry with a minimum-stock alarm exists and is reconciled to dip or delivery records.
Fuel quality tests at the declared interval meet the fuel specification, or remediation is recorded.
Fuel transfer pumps, controls and piping have no single point of failure that disables more than the generator redundancy allows.
For renewable diesel (HVO) or blends, OEM approval and storage stability are documented.

parameters.name: On-site fuel autonomy at declared load
parameters.basis: Capability profile; outcome tolerance and replenishment risk

parameters.name: Fuel quality test interval
parameters.basis: Capability profile; fuel specification (EN 590, ASTM D975 or EN 15940)

minimumEvidence: Autonomy calculation with usable volumes and consumption curve
Fuel level telemetry and alarm configuration
Fuel system schematic showing pump redundancy

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of levels and tests.
evidenceProfile.independence: Fuel test by an accredited laboratory; autonomy recalculated by the assessor.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Recompute usable volume and autonomy at declared load.
Reconcile telemetry to dips and deliveries.
Review fuel test certificates.
Trace fuel transfer system for single points of failure.
controls.applicability: Applies to sites with liquid-fuelled generation. Gas-fuelled sites substitute supply-pressure and pipeline-dependency evidence and are assessed under MCF-POW-008 for supply continuity.
failureModes: Autonomy overstated by counting unusable volume
Microbial contamination blocks filters
Single transfer pump failure starves day tanks
controls.testingSafety: Fuel sampling follows the site's fuel handling procedure (ignition-source control, spill kit); assessors do not take samples.
controls.unknownRule: If usable volume cannot be established, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-05 for autonomy.

controls.title: Fuel Replenishment
controls.objective: Ensure that fuel can be replenished before on-site autonomy is exhausted during a regional emergency, when road access, supplier capacity and competing priority customers are constrained.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall hold fuel supply contracts with at least the declared number of independent suppliers, specifying guaranteed delivery lead time during declared emergencies, priority status and delivery capacity. The facility operator shall maintain a refuelling procedure that includes delivery while generators run, and shall exercise a delivery under emergency conditions or verify supplier capability at the declared interval.
assessmentCriteria: Contracts with the declared number of independent suppliers (not sharing a terminal) exist.
Guaranteed emergency lead time is shorter than on-site autonomy by the declared margin.
Supplier delivery capacity covers consumption at declared load for the outage duration being planned.
A refuelling-while-running procedure exists and has been performed or exercised.
Supplier capability was verified within the interval (exercise or real delivery record).
minimumEvidence: Delivery exercise or real delivery records

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current contracts; exercise within twelve months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Contracts reviewed directly; supplier capability confirmed with the supplier.
acceptableAlternatives: Government or utility priority fuel scheme membership with documented terms
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-05, CG-03, CG-10.

assessmentProcedure: Review contracts for lead time, priority and capacity.
Check supplier independence (terminal, transport).
Compare lead time with autonomy.
Review or observe a delivery exercise.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever declared outage tolerance exceeds on-site fuel autonomy. Where autonomy alone covers the declared outage scenario, the control is assessed at DESIGN depth only.
failureModes: Both suppliers served from one terminal
Delivery blocked by flood
Supplier prioritises hospitals in regional emergency
controls.testingSafety: Refuelling-while-running exercises follow the fuel handling procedure with fire watch; assessors observe from outside the delivery hazard zone.
controls.unknownRule: If emergency lead time is not contractually defined, record a U10 dependency UNKNOWN and limit CG-05 conclusions to on-site autonomy.

controls.title: UPS Topology
controls.objective: Demonstrate that the as-built UPS and critical distribution topology (N, N+1, 2N, distributed or block redundant, or rack-level battery backup) delivers the declared Service Outcomes in every declared operating state, judged by failure analysis rather than by topology label.
controls.requirement: The electrical engineer of record shall document the UPS topology and IEC 62040-3 performance classification of each system, and shall perform a failure analysis that, for every single component failure and every planned maintenance state, identifies the critical load that remains supported and the resulting loading of surviving modules. The facility owner shall reconcile the as-built single-line diagram to the analysis and shall not claim a redundancy level the analysis does not support for the declared load.
assessmentCriteria: The as-built single-line diagram reconciles to the installed UPS, static switch and distribution configuration in a site inspection sample.
Each UPS system's IEC 62040-3 classification (e.g. VFI) and operating mode (double conversion, eco-mode) is recorded.
A failure analysis covers every single UPS module, battery string, static switch and distribution board failure and every planned maintenance state.
In each analysed state, surviving modules remain within rating at the declared load including AI load swings; for distributed redundant designs, load reallocation after a failure is shown.
The redundancy claim stated in reports matches the analysis outcome at the current load.
Rack-level battery backup units, where used, are included and their interaction with upstream UPS is analysed.

parameters.name: Maximum normal-state loading of each path in a 2N design

minimumEvidence: Load data per UPS and path

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current configuration and twelve months of path loading.
evidenceProfile.independence: Failure analysis reviewed by an electrical engineer independent of the designer or operator.
acceptableAlternatives: Independent engineer's topology review report covering the same states
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Reconcile single-line diagram to installed equipment in a sample.
Review failure analysis completeness against component and maintenance-state list.
Recompute surviving-module loading using current and peak AI load.
Compare redundancy claims in reports with analysis results.
controls.applicability: Applies to all UPS-backed critical load. For AI clusters deliberately designed without UPS on accelerator load (relying on checkpointing), the analysis records that decision and its approval and remains applicable to cooling and control loads.
failureModes: Distributed redundant reserve consumed by growth
Maintenance state leaves load on single module
Topology label 2N but shared output switchboard
Eco-mode transfer exposes load to grid transients
controls.testingSafety: Inspection only; panel covers are not removed. Load data is obtained from EPMS.
controls.unknownRule: If the as-built single-line diagram cannot be reconciled, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-05 and a U5 against CG-02 architecture integrity.

controls.title: Battery Condition
controls.objective: Ensure UPS, BESS and rack-level batteries retain the capacity assumed in runtime claims and that lithium-ion and lead-acid hazards (thermal runaway, off-gassing, hydrogen evolution) are detected and managed before they cause fire or loss of energy storage.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall monitor battery condition continuously (cell or block voltage, temperature, internal resistance or impedance, and for lithium-ion the battery management system state of health and alarms), shall perform capacity tests at the declared interval, and shall replace batteries at the end-of-life capacity threshold. The facility owner shall hold a battery safety assessment for each lithium-ion installation, using large-scale fire test data (for example UL 9540A) to set separation, ventilation, explosion control and detection, and shall maintain hydrogen ventilation for vented lead-acid rooms.
assessmentCriteria: Continuous battery monitoring covers every string or rack and alarms to a staffed location.
Capacity tests at the declared interval show every string above the end-of-life threshold, or replacement is scheduled before the next interval.
Lithium-ion BMS alarms (over-temperature, cell imbalance, communication loss) are configured, routed and acted on within the declared time.
A battery safety assessment exists for each lithium-ion installation and its required measures (separation, explosion control, off-gas detection, suppression) are installed.
Rack-level battery backup units are inventoried, monitored and included in the safety assessment.
Vented lead-acid rooms have ventilation sized for hydrogen evolution and it is interlocked or alarmed.

parameters.name: Battery end-of-life capacity threshold
parameters.basis: IEEE 450 / IEEE 1188 replacement criterion for lead-acid; OEM criterion for lithium-ion

minimumEvidence: Battery monitoring configuration and alarm routing
Battery safety assessment with UL 9540A or equivalent data
Ventilation design and tests for lead-acid rooms

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months of monitoring data and the latest capacity test cycle.
evidenceProfile.independence: Battery safety assessment by a fire or battery safety engineer independent of the supplier; capacity tests witnessed or reviewed independently.
acceptableAlternatives: Continuous impedance trending with OEM-validated correlation in place of discharge test for VRLA, if the OEM supports it
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Review monitoring coverage and alarm routing.
Analyse capacity test results against threshold.
Review BMS alarm handling in the period.
Review the battery safety assessment and inspect required measures.
Inventory rack BBUs and confirm monitoring.
controls.applicability: Applies to all battery energy storage supporting critical load, including UPS strings, BESS and rack-level BBUs. Supercapacitor-only systems apply monitoring and safety elements.
failureModes: Lithium-ion thermal runaway propagating between racks
Hydrogen accumulation in lead-acid room
String capacity below runtime assumption
BMS communication loss hides cell fault
controls.testingSafety: Discharge capacity tests are hazardous-energy activities and also reduce autonomy: they are performed by authorised persons under permit with the string isolated from critical load or with redundancy confirmed, written authorisation, and battery-hazard PPE. No test is performed on a lithium-ion string with an active BMS fault.
controls.unknownRule: If no battery safety assessment exists for a lithium-ion installation, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-04; hazardous testing in that room is not authorised until resolved.
informativeReferences: UL 9540 / UL 9540A (ESS safety and thermal runaway fire test method)

controls.title: Runtime and Derating
controls.objective: Demonstrate that UPS and BESS runtime at the declared load, at end-of-life battery capacity and worst-case room temperature, exceeds the time needed for generators to accept load (or for orderly workload preservation where no generation exists) with margin.
controls.requirement: The electrical engineer shall calculate runtime per UPS system at the declared load using end-of-life capacity and the battery temperature derating at the highest declared battery room temperature, and shall compare it with the generator start-to-load time and the time needed to checkpoint or gracefully pause AI workloads. The facility operator shall verify runtime by a discharge test at the declared interval and shall recalculate after load growth.
assessmentCriteria: Runtime calculations use end-of-life capacity, current declared load and worst-case battery temperature.
Calculated runtime exceeds generator start-to-load time plus the declared margin.
Where generation is absent or fails, runtime exceeds the time needed to complete declared workload preservation (checkpoint or pause) demonstrated by CMP/STO controls.
A discharge test at the declared interval confirmed runtime at or above calculation at a representative load.
Recalculation was performed after each load increase above the declared threshold.

parameters.name: Minimum UPS/BESS runtime at declared load, end of life
parameters.basis: Capability profile; generator start time and workload preservation time

parameters.name: Load growth threshold triggering runtime recalculation

minimumEvidence: Workload preservation timing evidence from CMP/STO

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Latest discharge test within interval; twelve months of loads and battery temperatures.
evidenceProfile.independence: Runtime recalculated by the assessor; test witnessed independently.
acceptableAlternatives: Recorded real-event discharge with EPMS data of sufficient duration and load
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-05 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Reperform runtime calculation from current load and battery data.
Compare with generator start time and workload preservation time.
Review discharge test conditions and results.
Confirm recalculation after load increases.
controls.applicability: Applies to all UPS and BESS supporting critical load.
failureModes: Runtime at end of life below generator start time
Battery room overheating reduces capacity
Load growth erodes runtime unnoticed (AIDCF-004 X01)
controls.testingSafety: Hazardous-energy activity. Tests and switching are performed only by authorised persons under the site electrical safety rules, an approved method statement and permit to work, with written authorisation from the facility owner's authorised engineer; assessors witness from outside the arc-flash boundary and never operate equipment. Discharge tests on live systems require confirmed redundancy and an abort criterion on minimum cell voltage.
controls.unknownRule: If no discharge test exists within the interval, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-05; runtime claims are limited to calculation (DESIGN depth).

controls.title: Bypass Exposure
controls.objective: Ensure that time spent with critical load on static or maintenance bypass, eco-mode or other unconditioned paths is known, minimised, authorised and accounted for in risk, because the load is then exposed directly to utility or generator disturbances.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall log every transfer of critical load to static bypass, maintenance bypass or eco-mode with start, end, cause and authorisation, shall alarm and escalate any unplanned bypass within the declared time, shall require approval for planned bypass and verify return to normal, and shall report cumulative bypass exposure per system at the declared interval.
assessmentCriteria: All bypass transfers in the period are logged with cause and authorisation, reconciled to UPS event logs.
Unplanned bypass alarms were escalated within the declared time.
Planned bypass had approval and a recorded return-to-normal verification.
Cumulative bypass exposure per system is reported and within the declared limit.
Eco-mode operation, if used, is evaluated against AI load dynamics and grid quality (MCF-POW-002).

parameters.name: Cumulative bypass exposure limit per UPS system

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation to UPS controller logs by the assessor.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material): the decision is capped at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition; the UNKNOWN is carried into the gate-level evaluation of CG-05, CG-09.

Eco-mode transfer fails during fast AI load swing

controls.title: Switchgear Integrity
controls.objective: Ensure MV and LV switchgear, transformers and switchboards are maintained in a safe and serviceable condition and that arc-flash hazards are quantified, labelled, minimised and controlled for all persons working on or near them.
controls.requirement: The electrical duty holder shall maintain a current arc-flash risk assessment (incident energy analysis) for all switchgear, switchboards, busway and PDUs, shall label equipment with incident energy or PPE category and boundaries, shall apply incident-energy reduction measures where assessed energy exceeds the declared threshold (for example maintenance switches, arc-flash relays, arc-resistant switchgear), and shall perform condition maintenance including infrared thermography, MV partial-discharge monitoring and breaker testing at the declared intervals.
assessmentCriteria: An arc-flash study exists for all equipment, reviewed within the declared interval and after changes to fault level or protection settings.
Equipment labels in a sample match the study.
Where incident energy exceeds the threshold, a reduction measure is installed and tested.
MV switchgear is arc-classified (IAC per IEC 62271-200) or has documented compensating controls.
Infrared thermography and MV partial-discharge results within the interval show no unresolved critical anomalies.
Breaker maintenance and trip testing are current per manufacturer and standard intervals.

parameters.name: Incident energy threshold requiring reduction measure

controls.title: Selective Coordination
controls.objective: Ensure that protective devices are selective so that a fault is cleared by the device nearest to it, limiting loss of supply to the smallest fault domain, across utility, generator and UPS (inverter-limited) fault-current sources.
controls.requirement: The electrical engineer of record shall maintain a short-circuit and protection coordination study covering every source configuration (utility, generator, UPS inverter, bypass) and the declared maintenance states, and shall demonstrate selectivity from the rack PDU branch up to the main incomers within the declared fault-current range. The facility operator shall ensure as-found protection settings match the study by periodic setting extraction and secondary injection testing.
assessmentCriteria: Short-circuit study covers all source configurations including inverter-limited fault current.
Coordination curves show selectivity between each upstream and downstream device pair for the declared range, or approved exceptions are listed.
Rack PDU and busway tap-off protection is selective with upstream devices for faults at the rack.
Extracted relay and trip-unit settings match the study for the sampled devices.
Secondary injection tests at the declared interval confirm trip characteristics.
Changes to settings since the last study are controlled under change management.

parameters.name: Protection setting extraction and comparison interval
Permitted deviation of as-found settings from study

acceptableAlternatives: Independent protection audit with setting verification
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 (Critical): an UNKNOWN result on this gate-critical control sets CG-09 to UNKNOWN and caps the decision at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until dispositioned.

Check coordination curves for each critical device pair.

Review secondary injection results.

Secondary injection requires isolation of trip outputs or an outage of the protected circuit.

controls.title: Busway and PDU Capacity
controls.objective: Ensure overhead busway, tap-off units, remote power panels and rack PDUs are rated for the continuous and peak load of dense AI racks, are balanced across phases, and keep capacity in failover states where one feed carries the full rack load.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a capacity register for every busway run, tap-off and rack PDU showing rating, continuous load limit, measured peak per phase and failover load (the load each feed must carry if its partner fails). The facility operator shall prevent provisioning that would cause failover load to exceed the continuous limit and shall correct phase imbalance above the declared threshold.
assessmentCriteria: The register covers every busway, tap-off and rack PDU serving AI racks.
Measured per-phase peak and calculated failover load are within the continuous load limit for every device.
Phase imbalance is below the declared threshold or a correction is scheduled.
Provisioning workflows check the register before new load is connected.
Busway joints are torque-checked or thermally surveyed at the declared interval.

controls.title: Earthing and Bonding
controls.objective: Ensure that earthing, equipotential bonding and lightning protection protect people against electric shock, provide fault-current return for protective devices and limit noise and transient damage to IT equipment, including metallic liquid-cooling pipework.
controls.requirement: The electrical engineer of record shall design the earthing system (system earthing type, earth electrodes, main earthing terminal, supplementary bonding) and the facility operator shall verify it by initial and periodic inspection and testing, including earth electrode resistance, protective conductor continuity, earth fault loop impedance and bonding of liquid-cooling pipework, manifolds, raised floors and cable containment.
assessmentCriteria: Earthing design documents the system earthing type and bonding scheme for each building.
Periodic inspection and test records within the interval show earth electrode resistance, continuity and fault loop impedance within design values.
Liquid-cooling pipework, manifolds and CDUs are bonded, verified in a sample.
Bonding between generator, transformer and building earthing is verified.
Defects are corrected before the circuit is returned to service or within the declared period.

controls.title: Voltage Quality
controls.objective: Ensure voltage delivered to critical IT and cooling loads stays within equipment tolerance in all source configurations, including on generator and during load swings from AI clusters.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall monitor voltage magnitude, unbalance and short-duration variations at UPS outputs, critical switchboards and a representative sample of rack PDUs, shall compare results with the tolerance of connected equipment (power supply unit specifications and the ITIC/CBEMA or SEMI F47 curves where adopted), and shall investigate excursions.
assessmentCriteria: Voltage monitoring exists at UPS outputs, critical switchboards and sampled rack PDUs.
Excursions outside the declared envelope are logged and investigated.
Voltage on generator operation was recorded during a test and within envelope.
Unbalance at critical boards is within the declared limit.

controls.title: Harmonics
controls.objective: Ensure harmonic distortion from rectifier-based IT loads, UPS, VFDs and BESS inverters is within limits at the point of common coupling and internally, does not overheat transformers, neutrals or generators, and does not cause resonance with filters or power-factor correction.
controls.requirement: The electrical engineer shall perform a harmonic study for the declared load mix covering utility and generator source configurations, and the facility operator shall measure voltage and current harmonics at the PCC and at critical boards. The facility owner shall keep harmonic emissions at the PCC within the limits of the connection agreement (for example IEEE 519 or the applicable IEC 61000-3 limits) and shall derate or specify transformers and generators for measured harmonic content.
assessmentCriteria: A harmonic study covers utility and generator configurations and capacitive or filter elements.
Measured voltage THD and current TDD at the PCC are within the applicable limits.
Transformer and generator ratings account for measured harmonic content (K-factor or derating).
Leading power factor from IT PSUs and filters at light load is evaluated against generator capability.
Neutral currents in 4-wire systems are measured and within conductor rating.

controls.title: Transient Ride-Through
controls.objective: Demonstrate that critical IT, cooling and control loads ride through grid voltage dips, transfers between sources and switching transients without loss of service, and that the facility meets any fault ride-through obligations of its grid connection.
controls.requirement: The electrical engineer shall define the ride-through envelope for each load class (IT, CDU and pump drives, chillers, controls), including source transfers (UPS to bypass, static transfer switch, ATS, generator synchronisation) and grid dips. The facility owner shall verify by commissioning and periodic transfer tests that loads remain online for transfers within the envelope, shall ensure mechanical loads not on UPS restart automatically within the thermal time constant, and shall document compliance with connection-agreement ride-through requirements.
assessmentCriteria: A ride-through envelope is documented for each load class, including STS and ATS transfer times.
Transfer tests demonstrate IT and UPS-backed cooling loads remained online.
Non-UPS cooling drives and chillers restart automatically within the thermal ride-through time established by THM controls, demonstrated in test.
Control systems (BMS, EPMS, CDU controllers) are UPS-backed and remain operational through transfers.
Grid-code ride-through obligations for the site as a large load are identified and evidence of compliance exists.
Real dip events in the period caused no unexpected load loss, or loss was investigated.

controls.title: Load-Step Response
controls.objective: Demonstrate that UPS, BESS, generators and the grid connection remain stable under the load steps and synchronous power oscillations produced by large accelerator clusters (collective compute/communication phases, job start and stop, checkpoint pauses and failure-driven drops), and that these dynamics are bounded within the capability of every source.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall characterise the power dynamics of each AI cluster (step magnitude, ramp rate, oscillation amplitude and frequency band), using measured data at sub-second resolution or the accelerator vendor's specified behaviour, and shall verify that UPS rectifier and inverter controls, BESS, generator governors and voltage regulators, and the grid connection tolerate them without instability, protective trips or breach of connection limits. Where they do not, the facility owner shall apply mitigation (accelerator power-smoothing or ramp-limit features, workload scheduling, energy-storage buffering) and shall verify it by test, including a load-step test on generator supply.
assessmentCriteria: Cluster power dynamics are characterised with step size, ramp rate and oscillation band, from measured data at sub-second resolution or vendor specification.
Generator load-acceptance capability (ISO 8528-5 performance class or test data) covers the characterised steps with frequency and voltage deviation within declared limits.
UPS and BESS behaviour under characterised oscillation is verified (no rectifier walk-in conflict, battery cycling within design, no transfer to bypass).
Grid-connection ramp and oscillation obligations are identified and measured behaviour at the PCC is within them.
A load-step or oscillation test on generator supply, using load banks programmed to the characterised profile or the cluster itself, shows stable operation.
Mitigations in use (power smoothing, ramp limits) are configured, under change control and monitored.

controls.title: EPMS Coverage
controls.objective: Ensure the electrical power monitoring system observes every critical node with accurate, time-synchronised data and alarms, functions independently of the systems it monitors, and is configured and protected as a critical control system.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall instrument every utility incomer, generator, UPS, STS, critical switchboard, busway and representative rack PDU with metering connected to the EPMS, shall synchronise device clocks to the declared accuracy for sequence-of-events analysis, shall configure alarms per an approved alarm philosophy, and shall power the EPMS and its network from protected supplies. The facility operator shall maintain the EPMS configuration under change control and its access under SEC controls.
assessmentCriteria: A point list reconciles EPMS devices to the as-built single-line diagram with no unmonitored critical node.
Clock synchronisation accuracy meets the declared value, demonstrated by sequence-of-events data.
Alarm configuration matches the alarm philosophy and critical alarms reach a staffed location.
EPMS servers, network and gateways are on UPS-backed supplies and remain available through transfers.
EPMS configuration and firmware are baselined and changes are controlled.
Data gaps in the period are below the declared threshold and are investigated.

controls.title: Preventive Maintenance
controls.objective: Ensure electrical assets are maintained at intervals and to scopes that keep their reliability and safety within the assumptions of the design and resilience analysis, without maintenance itself introducing unmanaged risk.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a maintenance programme for each electrical asset class (switchgear, transformers, UPS, batteries, generators, ATS/STS, busway, PDUs, protection relays) with scopes and intervals based on manufacturer requirements and recognised maintenance practice, shall complete maintenance on time, and shall record deferrals with risk assessment and approval.
assessmentCriteria: Every critical electrical asset is in the maintenance system with scope and interval.
On-time completion in the period meets the declared percentage.
No critical maintenance is overdue beyond the declared tolerance without an approved deferral.
Deferrals have risk assessment and approval by the accountable engineer.
Findings from maintenance are tracked to closure.

controls.title: Switching Procedures
controls.objective: Ensure that every planned and emergency switching operation on critical distribution is performed to an approved, verified procedure by authorised persons, with hazardous energy controlled, so that switching neither injures people nor drops critical load.
controls.requirement: The electrical duty holder shall require a method of procedure (MOP) for every planned switching operation on critical distribution, prepared from the current single-line diagram, checked by a second authorised person, and executed with step verification. The electrical duty holder shall maintain emergency operating procedures for foreseeable failures, shall apply lockout/tagout and permit-to-work for isolation, and shall authorise persons for switching by competence assessment.
assessmentCriteria: Every sampled planned switching operation has an approved MOP checked by a second authorised person.
MOP steps reference current single-line diagram revision and include hold points and rollback.
Emergency operating procedures exist for each failure in the UPS failure analysis (MCF-POW-009).
Isolations in the sample applied lockout/tagout with permit-to-work and test-before-touch.
Persons performing switching hold current authorisation for the voltage level and equipment.
Switching incidents in the period were investigated.

controls.title: Black-Start and Restoration
controls.objective: Demonstrate that after a total loss of power the site can be restored from a dead state, in a safe and dependency-correct sequence (controls, cooling, then IT), within the declared recovery time, and that AI workloads can resume.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall maintain a black-start and restoration plan that defines the restoration sequence, the dependencies of each step (control power, EPMS/BMS availability, cooling restart, battery recharge limits, inrush and staged load pick-up on generator), the authority to proceed, and the hand-over to IT for workload restart. The facility owner shall exercise the plan at the declared interval, either by a full integrated test or by staged tests that together cover every step, and shall measure time to each milestone.
assessmentCriteria: A restoration sequence exists covering control power, EPMS/BMS, cooling, battery recharge and IT pick-up with dependencies.
Generator staged load pick-up respects load-acceptance limits including cooling motor inrush and IT power-on surge.
Restoration was exercised within the interval and measured milestones met declared times.
Manual operation is possible if EPMS/BMS is unavailable, with procedures and trained staff.
Hand-over criteria to IT and workload restart dependencies (storage, network, scheduler) are defined.

parameters.name: Restoration time from dead site to full critical load

controls.title: Heat-Load Model
controls.objective: Establish an authoritative, versioned model of the heat that each fault domain must reject, split by heat-removal path (air, direct-to-chip liquid, rear-door, immersion), so that every downstream capacity, redundancy and recovery claim is tested against a defensible demand figure rather than nameplate or average IT power.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall maintain a versioned heat-load model for each Capability Instance that states, per hall, row, rack group and CDU or air-handling fault domain, the design and peak heat load in kW, the liquid-capture ratio by platform, residual heat to air, and the transient load profile of synchronous AI training. The facility owner shall approve the model and shall not accept capacity claims that are not traceable to the current model version.
assessmentCriteria: The model exists as a controlled, versioned document or dataset with a named owner and approval record dated within the review interval.
Heat load is apportioned to each fault domain (hall, row, rack group, CDU loop, CRAH zone) and the sum reconciles to the IT power model within the stated tolerance.
For each liquid-cooled platform, the liquid-capture ratio and residual air-side heat are taken from OEM thermal data or measurement and the source is cited.
The model includes a synchronous-load transient profile (step change and ramp rate) for training workloads, not only steady-state averages.
Non-IT heat (power conversion losses, lighting, envelope gain, CDU pump heat) is included or explicitly excluded with rationale.
Planned densification and the next approved deployment phase are represented as named scenarios.

controls.title: Design Capacity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that the installed and commissioned capacity of every stage of the heat-removal path (air, TCS, CDU, FWS, heat rejection) meets the current heat-load model at design conditions, so that the facility can actually remove the heat it is declared to support.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall demonstrate, for each heat-removal stage and fault domain, that commissioned capacity at design ambient and design supply temperatures is not less than the design heat load from MCF-THM-001 plus the approved margin. The facility operator shall hold the commissioning records and shall not admit IT load beyond the demonstrated capacity of the weakest stage in the path.
assessmentCriteria: A stage-by-stage capacity table exists (CRAH/fan wall, rear-door, CDU, TCS pumps, FWS pumps, chillers, dry coolers or towers) with rated and commissioned capacity at stated conditions.
The weakest stage in each path is identified and its commissioned capacity is ≥ design load plus margin.
Commissioning (functional and integrated systems tests) was performed at or extrapolated with documented method to design load using load banks or equivalent.
Capacity ratings are stated at the actual design supply temperature and ΔT, not catalogue nominal conditions.
Admitted IT load is reconciled to the demonstrated capacity and no fault domain exceeds it.

controls.title: Resilient Capacity
controls.objective: Ensure heat removal remains within the IT inlet and coolant envelopes when any single credible component, path or controller is lost, during maintenance, and through power-event transients (utility loss, UPS transfer, generator start, chiller restart).
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall define the declared redundancy (for example N+1, 2N) for each heat-removal stage and shall demonstrate that, with the largest single unit or path out of service, capacity meets design load. The facility owner shall demonstrate thermal ride-through: that pumps, CDUs and controls needed to keep coolant moving are on continuous power, and that thermal storage or ride-through margin keeps TCS supply and IT inlet temperatures within limits until chillers or heat rejection restart.
assessmentCriteria: Declared redundancy per stage is documented and the N−1 capacity analysis shows design load is met with the largest unit lost.
Common-mode elements that defeat redundancy (shared header, single controller, common power board, single make-up water feed) are identified with treatment.
TCS and CDU pumps and their controls are supplied from UPS or equivalent continuous power, verified on the single-line diagram.
A ride-through analysis or test shows TCS supply temperature and IT inlet temperature stay within declared limits from loss of mechanical cooling until restart to capacity.
An integrated test (utility loss / generator transfer) recorded coolant temperature, flow and IT throttling during the transient.
Redundancy is maintained, or a documented risk acceptance applies, during planned maintenance of each stage.
