parameters.name: Thermal ride-through required
parameters.basis: Derived: restart time plus margin; capability profile

parameters.name: Maximum TCS supply temperature rise during transient
parameters.basis: OEM coolant inlet limit minus normal setpoint

minimumEvidence: Single-line diagram extract showing pump/CDU/control power sources
Ride-through calculation including thermal-storage volume and pipework thermal mass
IST or black-building test record with time-stamped coolant temperature and flow traces

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent integrated transient test (≤ 24 months) plus 12 months of operating data
evidenceProfile.independence: Integrated test witnessed by an independent commissioning or engineering party
acceptableAlternatives: Validated dynamic thermal simulation calibrated against a partial transient test, reviewed independently
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for affected fault domains; decision ≤ LIMITED until ride-through is evidenced
reassessmentTriggers: Change to UPS coverage of mechanical loads
Any thermal excursion during a power event

assessmentProcedure: Review the redundancy declaration and N−1 analysis for each stage.
Trace pump, CDU and controller power to UPS on the single-line diagram.
Review the ride-through calculation inputs (volume, ΔT, load) against current heat load.
Examine transient test traces for TCS supply temperature, flow and IT throttling events.
Compare maintenance-state redundancy matrix with the maintenance schedule.
Record common-mode elements without treatment as Findings.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever a Service Outcome requires continuity of heat removal through component loss or power events. A reduced scope applies where the outcome tolerates controlled shutdown, provided that tolerance is approved under CG-01.
failureModes: Redundancy defeated by shared header or controller
CDU or TCS pumps not on UPS, stopping coolant flow on utility loss
Chiller restart longer than ride-through, causing thermal trip
Redundancy lost during maintenance without compensating measure
controls.testingSafety: Utility-loss and transfer tests are hazardous and capability-affecting. Requires a permit-to-work and method statement approved by the site authorising engineer, the IT operator's agreement on load at risk, and a rollback plan. Prefer analysis and records of previous tests over new disruptive tests.
controls.unknownRule: If no transient test or calibrated simulation exists for the current load, record a U5 coverage-gap UNKNOWN; CONFORMING requires transient evidence, not steady-state capacity alone.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments
ASHRAE TC 9.9 Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers

controls.title: Seasonal Derating
controls.objective: Ensure heat-rejection and economiser capacity is rated at the site's extreme design ambient conditions, including projected climate change, so that capacity claims hold through heatwaves and high wet-bulb periods.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall define design ambient dry-bulb and wet-bulb conditions from a stated climatic data source and return period, shall derate chillers, dry coolers and cooling towers to those conditions, and shall review the derating annually against observed extremes. The facility operator shall monitor available heat-rejection capacity against load during high-ambient periods and shall invoke load-management procedures before capacity is exceeded.
assessmentCriteria: Design ambient conditions are documented with source and return period (for example an extreme annual percentile from a named climatic dataset).
Heat-rejection equipment capacity is derated to design ambient with manufacturer data at those conditions.
Observed ambient extremes over the last 12 months (including any period above design ambient) are compared with the design basis.
Available capacity against load during the hottest observed period shows the declared margin was maintained.
A high-ambient procedure exists with trigger thresholds and load-management actions agreed with the AI platform operator.
A climate-projection allowance is defined for the asset life or its absence is recorded.

parameters.name: Design ambient dry-bulb
parameters.basis: ASHRAE climatic design conditions or national equivalent

minimumEvidence: Manufacturer capacity data at design ambient
12 months of ambient and heat-rejection load telemetry
High-ambient operating procedure and records of its use

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 12 months including the local peak-ambient season
evidenceProfile.independence: Ambient data cross-checked against an independent meteorological source
acceptableAlternatives: Where less than a year of operation exists, manufacturer derated performance plus a witnessed high-ambient test or validated simulation
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for high-ambient states; decision ceiling applied to EMERGENCY/peak-season claims
reassessmentTriggers: Fouling or performance decline of heat-rejection units
Change to economiser or setpoint strategy

assessmentProcedure: Confirm the climatic design basis and its source.
Check derated capacity calculations against manufacturer data at design ambient.
Analyse telemetry for the hottest days in the period: load, available capacity, supply temperatures.
Review high-ambient procedure use and outcomes.
Record any period where margin fell below threshold as a Finding.
controls.applicability: Applies to all sites with ambient-dependent heat rejection. Not applicable to heat rejection to a source independent of ambient (for example a stable ground-water or district system), where MCF-THM-016 covers the dependency.
failureModes: Capacity rated at nominal rather than extreme ambient
Recirculation of hot exhaust raising effective ambient at dry coolers
Fouled coils reducing capacity in summer
No load-management plan for heatwaves
controls.testingSafety: Analysis of records only. High-ambient tests are not induced; any witnessed test during natural peak conditions follows the site permit-to-work.
controls.unknownRule: If design ambient basis or peak-season data is unavailable, record UNKNOWN (U1/U5); do not infer peak-season adequacy from mild-season data.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE Standard 169 / ASHRAE Handbook Fundamentals (climatic design conditions)
ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments

controls.title: Airflow Management
controls.objective: Ensure cold supply air reaches IT inlets at the required temperature and volume without bypass or recirculation, including the residual air-side heat from liquid-cooled racks.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain an airflow management regime (blanking, brush grommets, cable cut-out sealing, floor-tile or supply-diffuser placement, fan-wall or CRAH control) and shall verify by periodic measurement that IT inlet temperatures at the top, middle and bottom of sampled racks remain within the declared envelope and that bypass and recirculation are within declared limits.
assessmentCriteria: IT inlet temperature measurements at multiple heights across sampled racks are within the declared envelope for the period.
Supply/return temperature differential at air handlers is consistent with low bypass (within declared range).
A sample inspection finds blanking panels, cable sealing and tile/diffuser placement consistent with the airflow standard.
Residual air heat from liquid-cooled racks is included in airflow planning and measured in at least one hall.
Exceptions (hot spots, missing blanking) are ticketed and closed within the declared time.

parameters.name: IT inlet temperature envelope
parameters.basis: ASHRAE TC 9.9 recommended envelope (classes A1–A4); site may adopt narrower OEM limits

minimumEvidence: IT inlet temperature telemetry at multiple rack heights

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent 6 months
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample inspection by a party other than the hall operations team
acceptableAlternatives: Handheld survey grid at defined points where rack sensors are not deployed
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: air-side adequacy uncertain; condition recorded against CG-06 supporting evaluation

assessmentProcedure: Select sample rows covering highest-density racks.
Analyse inlet telemetry by height for the period.
Walk the sampled rows and inspect blanking, sealing and containment interfaces.
Review hot-spot tickets for closure time.
Compare air-handler ΔT with the bypass indicator.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever any IT heat is removed by air, including residual heat from liquid-cooled racks. Not applicable to fully immersion-cooled halls with no air-cooled IT.
failureModes: Recirculation of exhaust air to inlets
Bypass air reducing effective capacity
Missing blanking after maintenance
Residual heat from liquid racks unplanned
controls.testingSafety: Non-intrusive: inspection without opening live electrical enclosures; follow hall access rules and hot-aisle heat-stress limits.
controls.unknownRule: If inlet measurement is absent for high-density racks, record U5 UNKNOWN for those racks; do not rely on room-average temperatures.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments
ANSI/TIA-942 (telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)

controls.title: Containment
controls.objective: Ensure hot-aisle or cold-aisle containment, chimney cabinets or rear-door heat exchangers are installed and maintained as designed so that supply and exhaust air streams remain separated, and that containment does not compromise fire detection, suppression or egress.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall install and maintain containment in accordance with the approved design, shall reconcile the as-built containment (doors, roof panels, end-of-row doors, rear-door heat exchangers) with the design, and shall demonstrate that fire detection and suppression coverage inside containment and the release of drop-away or fusible panels have been accepted by the fire-safety authority.
assessmentCriteria: As-built containment reconciles to the approved design for sampled rows.
Doors, roof panels and seals are present and closed in sampled rows.
Fire detection and suppression design covers the contained volume and has fire-safety authority acceptance.
Where rear-door heat exchangers are used, their water connections, leak detection and fan power are documented and their capacity matches rack heat.
Egress from contained aisles meets the site safety rules.
minimumEvidence: Fire-safety authority acceptance for contained aisles
Rear-door heat exchanger schedule and connection details (if used)

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Inspection within 6 months
evidenceProfile.independence: Fire-safety acceptance from the competent fire authority or fire engineer
acceptableAlternatives: Thermal imaging survey demonstrating separation where physical inspection is restricted
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: air separation unverified; CG-06 supporting; any fire-safety acceptance gap escalated to CG-04 evaluation

assessmentProcedure: Obtain containment design and fire acceptance.
Inspect sampled rows for completeness and condition.
Reconcile rear-door heat exchanger connections and leak detection where present.
Record deviations.
controls.applicability: Applies where containment or rear-door heat exchangers are part of the air-side design. Not applicable to open-room designs that declare no containment, if MCF-THM-005 demonstrates inlet compliance.
failureModes: Open containment doors causing mixing
Containment obstructing suppression agent distribution
Rear-door heat exchanger fan or water failure unmonitored
controls.testingSafety: Inspection only. Do not open containment roof panels or trigger drop-away mechanisms.
controls.unknownRule: If fire-safety acceptance cannot be produced, record UNKNOWN and refer to the CG-04 evaluation; the control cannot be CONFORMING.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments
NFPA 75 (fire protection of information technology equipment)

controls.title: CRAH and In-Row Capacity
controls.objective: Ensure computer-room air handlers, fan walls and in-row coolers deliver the air-side capacity required by the heat-load model, with declared redundancy, at the actual chilled-water or facility-water supply temperature.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a unit schedule for air handlers and in-row coolers stating sensible capacity at the actual entering-water and return-air conditions, and shall demonstrate that each air-cooling zone meets residual air heat with the declared redundancy. The thermal engineering authority shall re-rate capacity when supply water temperature or return-air setpoints change.
assessmentCriteria: Unit schedule states sensible capacity at site entering-water and return-air conditions.
Each zone's capacity with the largest unit out of service meets zone air-side heat load.
Fan, valve and controller configuration matches commissioning records for sampled units.
Zone heat load used is the residual air heat from MCF-THM-001, including liquid-rack residual heat.
Units are maintained per schedule with no overdue critical maintenance in the sample.
minimumEvidence: Unit schedule with rated sensible capacity at site conditions
Unit configuration export or BMS point list
Air-handler and in-row cooler planned-maintenance completion records

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current configuration plus 6 months maintenance history
evidenceProfile.independence: Configuration export obtained directly from BMS rather than operator summary
acceptableAlternatives: Commissioning functional performance test results at site conditions
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: zone air-side capacity uncertain; CG-06 supporting evaluation required

assessmentProcedure: Obtain unit schedule and zone analysis.
Recalculate one zone's N−1 capacity at site conditions.
Reconcile configuration export with commissioning settings.
Check maintenance records for sampled units.
controls.applicability: Applies where air handlers or in-row coolers remove in-scope heat.
failureModes: Capacity overstated at elevated water temperature
Zone redundancy lost due to unit placement
Fan speed limits misconfigured
controls.testingSafety: Records and configuration review. Any unit isolation to verify redundancy follows site permit-to-work.
controls.unknownRule: If unit capacity at site water temperature is not documented, record UNKNOWN (U1) for the zone.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments

controls.title: Air-Side Monitoring
controls.objective: Ensure air temperature, humidity and differential pressure are measured at points that represent IT inlet conditions, with alarm thresholds that give operators time to act before IT thermal limits or throttling are reached.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall deploy and maintain air-side sensors at IT inlet positions (not only at return air), with calibrated accuracy, defined alarm thresholds tiered below the IT envelope limits, and alarm routing to a staffed function. The facility operator shall review alarm performance, sensor coverage and nuisance alarms at least quarterly.
assessmentCriteria: Sensor coverage includes IT inlet positions in every row of high-density racks.
Sensors have calibration records within the calibration interval.
Warning and critical thresholds are defined below the declared envelope limits and documented.
Alarm routing reaches a staffed function and response times are recorded.
Data gaps and sensor failures are detected and tracked.
minimumEvidence: Sensor layout drawing or point list
Calibration certificates for air-side temperature and humidity sensors

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent 3 months of telemetry and alarm logs
evidenceProfile.independence: Spot check with a calibrated reference instrument by the assessor
acceptableAlternatives: Portable logger survey for halls with incomplete fixed sensors
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2 Moderate: confidence ceiling CONF-2 for air-side operating claims

assessmentProcedure: Compare point list with rack layout.
Sample calibration records.
Review alarm thresholds against the envelope.
Analyse alarm log for response time and gaps.
Spot-check sensor reading against reference instrument.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever air-side cooling serves in-scope IT.
failureModes: Sensors at return air only, masking inlet hot spots
Uncalibrated sensors reading low
Alarms routed to unstaffed queue
Data gaps unnoticed
controls.testingSafety: Reference-instrument spot checks are non-intrusive; do not disconnect live sensors.
controls.unknownRule: If sensor calibration or data completeness cannot be shown, treat telemetry as R2 and record UNKNOWN for operating claims relying on it.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments

controls.title: Direct-to-Chip Architecture
controls.objective: Ensure the direct-to-chip liquid-cooling architecture (cold plates, manifolds, technology cooling system, CDUs and facility water interface) is designed to the accelerator OEM's coolant, temperature, flow, pressure and wetted-material requirements and to an explicit facility water class.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall document a direct-to-chip design basis stating: the TCS fluid, supply temperature range, minimum flow per rack and per cold plate, maximum pressure and differential pressure, filtration, wetted materials, and the ASHRAE liquid-cooling W-class of the facility water system at the CDU interface. The facility owner shall obtain written OEM confirmation that the design basis meets the platform requirements and shall maintain a TCS/FWS P&ID.
assessmentCriteria: The design basis states TCS fluid, supply temperature, flow, pressure, filtration and wetted materials, each with OEM source.
The FWS-to-TCS interface is classified by W-class with the facility water supply temperature range stated.
The approach temperature across the CDU heat exchanger is stated and the TCS supply temperature is achievable at worst-case FWS supply temperature.
A current P&ID shows TCS and FWS loops, CDUs, isolation valves, filters, expansion and fill points, and sensors.
OEM confirmation of compatibility with the design basis exists for each deployed platform.
The architecture identifies whether CDUs are liquid-to-liquid or liquid-to-air and the consequences for heat-rejection dependency.

parameters.name: Facility water class at CDU interface
parameters.basis: ASHRAE TC 9.9 liquid-cooling classes W17–W45 and W+

parameters.name: TCS supply temperature to cold plates
TCS filtration rating
parameters.basis: Platform OEM specification; OCP cold-plate guidance

minimumEvidence: OEM coolant and facility requirements documents
CDU selection data at design FWS temperature

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current design-basis version
evidenceProfile.independence: Design review by an engineer independent of the cooling vendor
acceptableAlternatives: OEM-supplied reference design adopted without modification, with deviations listed
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: liquid-cooling design adequacy uncertain; CG-06 supporting; downstream CDU and loop controls conditioned

assessmentProcedure: Obtain design basis, P&ID and OEM requirements.
Compare each design parameter with the OEM requirement.
Check approach temperature: worst-case FWS supply + approach ≤ maximum TCS supply.
Confirm OEM compatibility statements.
Record mismatches as Findings.
controls.applicability: Applies where any in-scope IT is cooled by direct-to-chip cold plates. Immersion systems are covered by MCF-THM-017 and MCF-THM-010 for their coolant and heat-exchange stages.
failureModes: TCS supply temperature unattainable at peak FWS temperature
Wetted-material incompatibility causing corrosion
Flow per cold plate below OEM minimum
Undocumented loop topology
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based review; no intrusive action.
controls.unknownRule: If OEM requirements for a platform are unavailable, record U1 UNKNOWN and treat dependent CDU capacity claims as unverified.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers
Open Compute Project Advanced Cooling Solutions guidance (cold plate, CDU, immersion)
ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: CDU Capacity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that coolant distribution units deliver the required heat transfer, flow and supply temperature to every served rack under design load, with declared redundancy of pumps, heat exchangers and power supplies.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall demonstrate, by commissioning or periodic test, that each CDU group delivers design heat transfer at design FWS temperature with the declared pump and heat-exchanger redundancy, and that pump failover maintains flow without TCS supply temperature leaving the OEM limit. The facility operator shall not connect racks to a CDU group beyond its demonstrated capacity.
assessmentCriteria: Each CDU group has a test record at design load (or load bank) showing heat transfer, TCS supply temperature and flow.
Pump redundancy (for example duty/standby or N+1) is tested by failing a duty pump; flow recovers within the declared time without exceeding TCS temperature limits.
CDU power supplies are dual-fed or the single-feed risk is treated under MCF-THM-003.
Racks connected per CDU group are within the demonstrated capacity.
For liquid-to-air CDUs, capacity is rated at the hall air temperature actually available.
Strainers and filters are monitored for differential pressure and the impact of fouling on flow is bounded.

parameters.name: CDU pump failover recovery time
parameters.basis: CDU manufacturer data; verify by test

minimumEvidence: CDU test records at design load
Pump failover test traces (flow, pressure, TCS supply temperature)
CDU configuration export (pump control mode, setpoints)

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within 12 months plus 3 months of telemetry
evidenceProfile.independence: Failover test witnessed by a party independent of the CDU vendor
acceptableAlternatives: Operational evidence of an unplanned pump failure with full telemetry, analysed against criteria
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for racks served by untested CDU groups

assessmentProcedure: Select CDU groups serving the highest-load racks.
Review design-load and failover test records against criteria.
Reconcile rack connection register with demonstrated capacity.
Review CDU configuration and filter ΔP trends.
Record untested groups as UNKNOWN.
controls.applicability: Applies to all CDUs serving in-scope IT, including in-rack, in-row and facility-scale CDUs and immersion-tank heat exchangers.
failureModes: Duty pump failure without successful standby start
CDU overloaded by rack additions
Strainer fouling reducing flow
Liquid-to-air CDU starved by high hall temperature
controls.testingSafety: Pump failover tests on live loops risk thermal trips of production IT. Requires a permit-to-work and method statement approved by the site authorising engineer, AI platform operator agreement and an abort criterion based on TCS supply temperature.
controls.unknownRule: If no failover test exists for a CDU group, record U1 UNKNOWN; design data alone cannot support the EFFECTIVENESS claim.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers
Open Compute Project Advanced Cooling Solutions guidance (cold plate, CDU, immersion)

controls.title: Secondary Loop Integrity
controls.objective: Ensure the technology cooling system (secondary loop) maintains pressure, flow, temperature and fluid inventory within limits, is pressure-tested, and has no unmanaged single points of failure between CDU and cold plate.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall monitor TCS supply and return temperature, differential pressure, flow, system pressure and make-up/fill volume continuously, shall pressure-test new and modified TCS pipework before fill, and shall investigate any unexplained make-up volume. The thermal engineering authority shall maintain a single-point-of-failure analysis of the TCS from CDU to manifold to cold plate.
assessmentCriteria: TCS pressure, differential pressure, flow and supply/return temperature are monitored continuously and trends are within limits for the period.
Pressure tests are recorded for all new or modified TCS pipework before fill, at the specified test pressure and hold time.
Make-up volume is metered and any unexplained loss is investigated.
A single-point-of-failure analysis of the TCS path (header, manifold, hoses, valves) exists and identified points are treated.
Rack ΔT and flow anomalies are alarmed before OEM throttle thresholds.
minimumEvidence: TCS telemetry trends (P, ΔP, flow, T)

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent 6 months of telemetry and all pressure tests since last fill
evidenceProfile.independence: Pressure test witnessed by a party other than the installer
acceptableAlternatives: Inventory reconciliation by expansion-tank level where make-up meters are absent
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for loops with unverified integrity

assessmentProcedure: Analyse TCS telemetry for excursions and trends.
Sample pressure-test certificates against modification records.
Reconcile make-up volume log with investigations.
Review the single-point-of-failure analysis.
Inspect a sample of manifolds and hose routes.
controls.applicability: Applies to all liquid TCS loops serving in-scope IT.
failureModes: Slow leak depleting inventory
Air ingress causing pump cavitation
Manifold single point of failure
Over-pressure on valve closure
controls.testingSafety: Pressure testing of filled loops is hazardous; it requires an approved method statement, pressure-equipment competence and isolation from IT equipment. Assessors do not operate valves.
controls.unknownRule: If make-up volume or pressure-test records are missing for modified sections, record U1 UNKNOWN for those loops.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers
Open Compute Project Advanced Cooling Solutions guidance (cold plate, CDU, immersion)
Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU or equivalent national pressure-equipment regulation

controls.title: Quick-Disconnect Management
controls.objective: Ensure quick-disconnect couplings between manifolds and IT are specified, compatible, connected, inspected and replaced under control, because they are the most frequently operated wetted joints and a common leak and flow-restriction source.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a register of quick-disconnect coupling types and compatibility by platform, shall perform connect/disconnect only under a documented procedure by trained staff with drip containment, and shall inspect and replace couplings and seals on a defined interval or cycle count. The AI platform operator shall not install IT with couplings outside the register.
assessmentCriteria: A coupling register lists types, ratings, compatible counterparts and wetted materials per platform.
A connect/disconnect procedure exists with drip containment, purge and post-connection leak check.
Staff performing connections have recorded training.
Sample work orders show the procedure was followed, including post-connection leak checks.
Couplings are inspected or replaced per interval or cycle count, and failures are trended.
minimumEvidence: Sample work orders with leak-check sign-off

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent 6 months of work orders
evidenceProfile.independence: Observation of a live connection by the assessor
acceptableAlternatives: Witnessed demonstration on a non-production rack
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: leak initiation risk unbounded; supports CG-06 and CG-04 evaluation

assessmentProcedure: Review register against deployed platforms.
Sample work orders for procedure adherence.
Observe a connection or disconnection where possible.
Review failure trend and replacement records.
controls.applicability: Applies where IT is connected to TCS manifolds by quick-disconnect couplings. Not applicable to hard-piped cold-plate systems.
failureModes: Incompatible couplings mated
Seal degradation causing drip leak
Partial engagement restricting flow
Coolant spill onto energised equipment
controls.testingSafety: Observation only; connections are made by trained site staff under procedure. Spill onto energised equipment is an electrical hazard: the procedure must require drip containment.
controls.unknownRule: If the coupling register does not cover a deployed platform, record U1 UNKNOWN for that platform.
informativeReferences: Open Compute Project Advanced Cooling Solutions guidance (cold plate, CDU, immersion)
ASHRAE TC 9.9 Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers

controls.title: Chiller Capacity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that chillers (where present) deliver required capacity at design condenser conditions with declared redundancy, restart quickly after power interruption, and that refrigerant hazards are controlled.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall demonstrate chiller capacity at design condenser conditions with the declared redundancy, shall evidence restart-to-capacity time after power interruption, and shall maintain refrigerant inventory, leak detection, machinery-room ventilation and safety classification records in accordance with the applicable refrigeration safety standard.
assessmentCriteria: Chiller capacity at design condenser conditions with N−1 meets design load.
Restart-to-capacity time after power interruption is evidenced by test and is within the ride-through window.
Refrigerant type, charge, safety class and machinery-room requirements are documented.
Refrigerant leak detection and ventilation are installed and functionally tested.
Refrigerant leak and charge records meet applicable regulatory requirements.
Chiller sequencing logic is documented and tested for failure of the lead chiller.
minimumEvidence: Chiller performance test or commissioning data at design conditions

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within 12 months; refrigerant records for 12 months
evidenceProfile.independence: Refrigerant safety inspection by a certified refrigeration engineer
acceptableAlternatives: Manufacturer factory witness test plus site performance verification at partial load
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-06 UNKNOWN for chilled-water-dependent paths; refrigerant safety gaps escalated to CG-04

assessmentProcedure: Review capacity and restart test records.
Compare restart time with ride-through analysis in MCF-THM-003.
Inspect refrigerant detection and machinery-room provisions.
Review sequencing tests and refrigerant records.
controls.applicability: Applies where mechanical refrigeration is in the heat-removal path. Not applicable to chiller-less designs (for example W32+ with dry coolers only), provided MCF-THM-004 shows dry-cooler capacity at design ambient.
failureModes: Chiller fails to restart after transfer
Lead chiller failure without sequencing to standby
Refrigerant leak in occupied space
Capacity loss at high condenser temperature
controls.testingSafety: Restart tests interrupt chilled water; Requires a permit-to-work and method statement approved by the site authorising engineer and thermal-storage or redundancy cover. Refrigerant work requires certified personnel.
controls.unknownRule: If restart-to-capacity has not been tested, record U1 UNKNOWN; this carries into MCF-THM-003 ride-through.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE Standard 15 / ISO 5149 / EN 378 (refrigeration system safety)
EU F-gas Regulation or applicable refrigerant regulation

controls.title: Cooling Tower or Dry Cooler
controls.objective: Ensure final heat-rejection equipment (cooling towers, adiabatic or dry coolers) operates at the required capacity, is protected against fouling, freezing, recirculation and fan or spray failures, and is maintained to preserve capacity.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall operate and maintain heat-rejection units to preserve capacity at design ambient, shall monitor approach temperature and fan/pump status per unit, shall protect against freezing and hot-air recirculation, and shall record fouling and coil-cleaning interventions. Where evaporative or adiabatic systems are used, the facility operator shall implement MCF-THM-018 water treatment.
assessmentCriteria: Approach temperature per unit is trended and units with degraded approach are investigated.
Fan and pump status is monitored per unit with alarms.
Freeze protection (glycol concentration, heat tracing, drain-down) is in place where ambient can fall below freezing.
Layout or wind analysis addresses hot-air recirculation between units and from adjacent sources.
Coil cleaning or tower maintenance follows schedule.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months including summer and winter
evidenceProfile.independence: Thermal imaging or independent recirculation survey
acceptableAlternatives: Seasonal performance test by the manufacturer
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: heat-rejection capacity condition recorded; CG-06 supporting

assessmentProcedure: Analyse approach temperature by unit.
Inspect units for fouling, damage and recirculation paths.
Review freeze protection.
Review maintenance compliance.
controls.applicability: Applies to all final heat-rejection equipment in the boundary.
failureModes: Hot-air recirculation raising entering temperature
Coil fouling
Freeze damage
Fan failure at peak ambient
controls.testingSafety: Roof and plant-yard inspection requires working-at-height controls; evaporative towers require respiratory precautions under the legionella risk assessment.
controls.unknownRule: If per-unit monitoring is absent, record U5 UNKNOWN for unit-level degradation.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE Standard 169 / ASHRAE Handbook Fundamentals (climatic design conditions)
ASHRAE Standard 188 (legionellosis risk management for building water systems)

controls.title: Water Continuity
controls.objective: Ensure evaporative and adiabatic heat rejection, and loop make-up, can continue through loss or restriction of mains water supply for the declared autonomy period.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall determine water consumption at design ambient and peak load, shall provide on-site storage or alternative supply for the declared water autonomy, and shall document the dependency on the water utility, including restriction scenarios and drought orders. The facility operator shall test the switchover to stored or alternative water and shall monitor stored volume.
assessmentCriteria: Peak water consumption at design ambient and load is calculated.
On-site storage or alternative supply provides the declared autonomy at peak consumption.
Switchover to stored water is tested and recorded.
Stored volume is monitored with low-level alarms.
The water utility dependency, including restriction scenarios, is documented and owned.
A fallback mode (for example dry operation with reduced capacity) is defined with its capacity impact on IT load.

parameters.name: Peak water consumption
parameters.basis: Design calculation at design wet-bulb and load

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3

controls.title: Heat-Rejection Dependency
controls.objective: Make explicit every dependency of the heat-removal path on external or shared resources (water, power, controls, district systems, shared plant with other tenants) and the common modes that could remove several redundant trains at once.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall maintain a heat-rejection dependency map from IT heat source to final heat sink, identifying shared headers, common controllers, common power boards, shared water supplies, third-party plant and heat-reuse interfaces, and shall record the treatment and owner of each common mode. The facility owner shall ensure heat-reuse or district-energy interfaces cannot reduce heat-rejection capacity below design load.
assessmentCriteria: A dependency map exists from rack to final heat sink for each redundant train.
Common-mode points (shared header, controller, board, water feed) are listed with treatment and owner.
Third-party or shared plant is identified with contractual service levels.
Heat-reuse or district interfaces have a defined fall-back that preserves heat rejection when the external heat sink is unavailable.
The map is reconciled to the current P&ID.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current version
evidenceProfile.independence: Review by an engineer independent of the designer
acceptableAlternatives: Fault tree for loss of heat rejection covering the same elements
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: hidden common mode possible; referred to CG-03 and CG-09 evaluation

assessmentProcedure: Obtain dependency map and P&ID.
Trace each train for shared elements.
Review treatment of each common mode.
Review heat-reuse fall-back.
controls.applicability: Applies to all heat-rejection paths in scope.
failureModes: Shared header defeating redundancy
District heat sink unavailable
Common controller failure
Tenant plant change
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based review of dependency records and P&IDs; site walk-downs to confirm shared elements are visual only.
controls.unknownRule: Any unmapped shared element discovered during inspection is recorded as a U10 dependency UNKNOWN and escalated to CG-03.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Coolant Compatibility
controls.objective: Ensure every coolant and immersion fluid is compatible with all wetted materials and IT components, is safe to handle, and that its hazards (toxicity, flammability, environmental, pressure) are identified and controlled.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall specify each coolant (for example propylene-glycol solution, treated water, dielectric immersion fluid) with its composition, inhibitor package, approved wetted materials and OEM approval, and shall obtain and act upon the safety data sheet. The facility owner shall ensure fluid handling, storage, spill response and disposal arrangements are in place and accepted by the site safety authority.
assessmentCriteria: Each coolant has a specification with composition, inhibitor package and OEM approval for every platform it contacts.
A wetted-materials list exists for each loop and is checked against the coolant's compatibility data.
Mixing of incompatible fluids is prevented by labelling, dedicated fill equipment and procedure.
Safety data sheets are held and hazards are reflected in handling, PPE, storage and spill procedures.
For immersion fluids, flammability, material compatibility with IT components and long-term fluid degradation are assessed.

assessmentProcedure: Review coolant specifications against OEM requirements.
Cross-check wetted-materials list.
Inspect fluid storage and labelling.
Review handling procedures against the SDS.
controls.applicability: Applies to all liquid and immersion cooling fluids in scope.
failureModes: Galvanic corrosion from mixed metals
Inhibitor package incompatible with wetted materials
Fluid mixing
Dielectric fluid incompatibility with cable jackets
controls.testingSafety: Fluid sampling follows the SDS and site PPE requirements.

controls.title: Water Quality
controls.objective: Maintain the chemistry, cleanliness and microbiological quality of TCS, FWS and condenser water so that cold plates do not foul, corrosion is controlled, and evaporative systems do not present a legionella risk to people.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall implement a water-quality programme with sampling frequencies and limits for each loop (pH, conductivity, inhibitor level, glycol concentration, suspended solids, microbiological counts), shall maintain filtration to the OEM rating, and shall act on out-of-limit results within defined times. Where evaporative cooling towers or adiabatic systems exist, the facility owner shall maintain a legionella risk assessment and written control scheme under the applicable regulation, reviewed by a competent person.
assessmentCriteria: Sampling schedule and limits exist for each loop and are derived from OEM and fluid-supplier requirements.
Sample results for the period are within limits or exceedances were corrected within the defined time.
Filter differential pressure and replacement records show filtration maintained.
A current legionella risk assessment and written scheme exist for evaporative systems, with competent-person review.
Microbiological testing results for evaporative systems are recorded and actioned.
Laboratory analyses use an accredited or OEM-approved laboratory.
minimumEvidence: Legionella risk assessment and written scheme

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months of results
evidenceProfile.independence: Accredited laboratory analysis; legionella scheme reviewed by an independent competent person
mandatoryItems: Legionella risk assessment (where evaporative systems exist)
acceptableAlternatives: Inline monitoring of conductivity/pH with periodic laboratory confirmation
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical where evaporative systems exist (CG-04 life safety); otherwise US3 Material for CG-06

assessmentProcedure: Obtain programme and limits.
Analyse 12 months of results for exceedances and corrective actions.
Review filter records.
Review legionella risk assessment, scheme and results.
Inspect a sample point and dosing equipment.
controls.applicability: Applies to all water and water-glycol loops in scope. Legionella criteria apply only where evaporative or aerosol-generating systems exist.
failureModes: Cold-plate microchannel fouling
Biofilm and microbiologically influenced corrosion
Legionella proliferation in cooling towers
Inhibitor depletion
controls.testingSafety: Sampling of evaporative systems requires respiratory protection per the legionella risk assessment. Chemical dosing equipment is operated only by the water-treatment contractor.
controls.unknownRule: If no microbiological results exist for an evaporative system, record US4 UNKNOWN against CG-04; the control cannot be CONFORMING.

controls.title: Leak Detection
controls.objective: Ensure liquid leaks from TCS, FWS, rear-door heat exchangers and immersion tanks are detected quickly and located precisely enough to isolate the right section before liquid reaches energised equipment or spreads beyond its fault domain.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall install leak detection (rope/cable sensors, spot sensors, CDU and rack-level detection, flow/pressure-based detection) covering every wetted zone above or adjacent to IT and electrical equipment, shall route alarms to a staffed function with locational information, and shall functionally test detection at defined intervals. The thermal engineering authority shall define detection coverage and response time requirements per zone.
assessmentCriteria: A coverage map shows detection for every zone where liquid is present above, within or adjacent to IT or electrical equipment.
Functional tests (wet test or manufacturer test method) are recorded for sampled sensors within the interval.
Alarms carry zone/location and reach a staffed function; response time is measured.
Detection is supplemented by flow/pressure or make-up anomaly detection for slow leaks.
False-alarm rates are tracked and do not lead to disabled sensors.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months of alarm records; tests within interval
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor-witnessed functional test of sampled sensors
acceptableAlternatives: Incident evidence of real leak detection with full alarm timeline
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: leak detection effectiveness uncertain; CG-09 and CG-04 supporting evaluation

assessmentProcedure: Review coverage map against the P&ID and room layout.
Witness or review functional tests on sampled sensors.
Analyse alarm log for response times.
Check disabled-sensor register.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever liquid cooling or water piping is present in or above IT or electrical spaces.
failureModes: Leak in an uncovered zone
Sensor disabled after false alarms
Alarm without location
Slow leak below sensor threshold
controls.testingSafety: Wet tests use small water volumes away from energised equipment, under permit, with the IT operator informed.
controls.unknownRule: Zones with no functional-test record within interval are recorded as U3 stale UNKNOWN.
informativeReferences: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Liquid Cooling Guidelines for Datacom Equipment Centers

controls.title: Isolation and Drainage
controls.objective: Ensure a detected leak can be isolated to the smallest practicable section, the released liquid is contained and drained away from energised equipment, and the remaining cooling capacity is preserved, so that a leak remains within its fault domain.
controls.requirement: The thermal engineering authority shall design isolation valves, drip trays, bunding and drainage so that a leak at any credible point can be isolated to a defined fault domain and drained without reaching electrical equipment outside that domain. The facility operator shall maintain isolation procedures, exercise valves, and demonstrate isolation of a representative section while adjacent sections continue cooling.
assessmentCriteria: Isolation points are defined so that each credible leak location can be isolated within a defined fault domain.
Automatic isolation (where used) is linked to leak detection and tested.
Drip trays, bunding or floor drainage direct liquid away from electrical equipment and are inspected.
Valve exercise records show isolation valves operate and seal.
A representative isolation test showed adjacent fault domains maintained cooling.
Spill volumes per fault domain are bounded by design.

parameters.name: Maximum release volume per isolated section

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within 12 months
evidenceProfile.independence: Isolation test witnessed by a party independent of the maintenance contractor
acceptableAlternatives: Documented real leak incident showing isolation and containment within fault domain
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-09 UNKNOWN for liquid-leak containment

assessmentProcedure: Review isolation design against P&ID.
Inspect drip trays and drainage.
Review valve exercise and automatic isolation tests.
Review representative isolation test results.
Assess release volume bounds.
controls.applicability: Applies wherever liquid cooling is present in IT space.
failureModes: Isolation valve seized
Isolation of a leak removes cooling from a larger domain than intended
Liquid tracks to electrical busway
Automatic isolation fails to close
controls.testingSafety: Isolation tests reduce cooling to the isolated section; Requires a permit-to-work and method statement approved by the site authorising engineer, with the affected IT drained or protected.
controls.unknownRule: If no isolation test exists, record U1 UNKNOWN; design review alone supports DESIGN, not EFFECTIVENESS.

controls.title: Control Stability
controls.objective: Ensure cooling controls (CDU controllers, BMS sequences, chiller plant managers, pump and valve PID loops) remain stable under rapid AI load swings, fail to a safe cooling state on controller or network loss, and cannot be changed without control.
controls.requirement: The controls engineering authority shall document control sequences and fail-safe states for each cooling controller, shall demonstrate stability of temperature and pressure loops under step load changes representative of synchronous training, and shall demonstrate that loss of controller, sensor or controls network leaves pumps running and valves in a safe position. The facility operator shall manage controller configuration under change control with version-controlled backups.
assessmentCriteria: Sequences of operation and fail-safe states are documented per controller.
Step-load test shows TCS supply temperature and pressure settle within the declared band and time without sustained oscillation.
Loss-of-controller and loss-of-network tests show pumps continue and valves fail to the safe state.
Controller configurations are backed up, version-controlled and reconciled to the approved baseline.
Remote write access to cooling controllers is restricted and logged.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within 12 months; 3 months control trends
evidenceProfile.independence: Fail-safe test witnessed by an independent controls engineer
acceptableAlternatives: Recorded production load step with full telemetry analysed against criteria
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-07 UNKNOWN for cooling controls

assessmentProcedure: Review sequences and fail-safe definitions.
Review step-load and fail-safe test traces.
Reconcile running configuration with baseline.
Review access controls and logs.
controls.applicability: Applies to all automated controls in the heat-removal path, including vendor CDU controllers.
failureModes: PID oscillation under synchronous load
Controller failure stopping pumps
Valve fails closed on network loss
Unauthorised setpoint change
controls.testingSafety: Fail-safe tests on live systems are hazardous; Requires a permit-to-work and method statement approved by the site authorising engineer, controls specialist on site and manual override available.
controls.unknownRule: If fail-safe behaviour is undocumented or untested, record US4 UNKNOWN against CG-07.
informativeReferences: IEC 62443 series (industrial automation and control system security)

controls.title: Sensor Trust
controls.objective: Ensure the sensors that drive cooling control and alarming (temperature, pressure, flow, leak, level) are accurate, calibrated, redundant where control-critical, and that implausible or failed readings are detected before they mislead control or operators.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall identify control-critical sensors, shall calibrate them at defined intervals, shall provide redundancy or plausibility checks (cross-sensor comparison, rate-of-change, stuck-value detection) for control-critical points, and shall configure controllers to a safe default on sensor failure.
assessmentCriteria: Control-critical sensors are identified in a register.
Calibration records exist within interval for sampled sensors.
Control-critical points have redundant sensors or plausibility logic.
Controllers default to safe action on sensor failure, verified by documentation or test.
Sensor faults are alarmed and tracked.
minimumEvidence: Calibration certificates for control-critical temperature, pressure and flow sensors

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months of calibration and fault records
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor spot check with reference instrument
acceptableAlternatives: Cross-comparison analysis of redundant sensors over the period
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: telemetry reliability reduced; dependent operating claims capped at CONF-2

assessmentProcedure: Review register.
Sample calibration certificates.
Review plausibility logic.
Analyse sensor-fault log.
Spot-check readings.
controls.applicability: Applies to sensors used for cooling control or alarming of in-scope systems.
failureModes: Drifted sensor causing undercooling
Stuck flow meter masking flow loss
Single sensor failure driving valve closed
controls.testingSafety: Non-intrusive spot checks only.
controls.unknownRule: If a control-critical sensor has no calibration record, treat its data as unverified (U6) and record UNKNOWN against controls relying on it.

controls.title: Maintenance States
controls.objective: Ensure planned maintenance on cooling plant (CDU servicing, filter changes, valve replacement, chiller overhaul, loop drain-down) is carried out without unplanned loss of cooling, with declared residual redundancy and safe isolation of pressurised fluid systems.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall plan cooling maintenance with a documented method statement stating residual capacity and redundancy during the work, required IT load limits, isolation and lock-out points, and back-out steps; shall coordinate with the AI platform operator where IT load must be reduced; and shall record post-maintenance return-to-service checks.
assessmentCriteria: Method statements for sampled cooling work state residual capacity and redundancy.
IT load limits during maintenance are agreed with the AI platform operator where required.
Isolation and lock-out of pressurised and energised systems are recorded.
Post-maintenance return-to-service checks (flow, pressure, temperature, leak check) are recorded.
Maintenance-induced incidents are analysed.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent 6 months of cooling maintenance
evidenceProfile.independence: Observation of a maintenance activity by the assessor
acceptableAlternatives: Computerised maintenance management system records with embedded checklists
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: maintenance-state continuity uncertain; CG-06 and CG-14 supporting

assessmentProcedure: Sample method statements.
Check residual capacity statements against N−1 analysis.

Observe a maintenance activity where possible.
controls.applicability: Applies to all planned work on in-scope cooling systems.

Air trapped after drain-down
Unsafe isolation of pressurised loop
Return to service without leak check
controls.testingSafety: Observation only; assessors do not take part in isolation.
controls.unknownRule: If residual capacity is not stated on method statements, record a Finding; if records are missing, record U1 UNKNOWN.

controls.title: Thermal Recovery
controls.objective: Ensure that after loss of cooling or power, the heat-removal path is restored in the right order (power, controls, pumps, heat rejection, CDUs) and IT load is readmitted in steps that do not exceed recovering capacity or trigger repeated thermal trips.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall maintain a thermal recovery procedure defining restart sequence, prerequisites, hold points, verification criteria (flow, TCS supply temperature, leak checks) and staged IT readmission limits agreed with the AI platform operator, and shall exercise it at a defined interval. The facility owner shall define the thermal recovery time objective for each fault domain.
assessmentCriteria: A recovery procedure defines restart sequence, prerequisites and hold points.
Verification criteria for each step (flow, pressure, temperature, no leak) are defined.
Staged IT readmission limits are defined and agreed with the AI platform operator.
The procedure has been exercised (test or real event) within the interval, achieving the recovery time objective.
Lessons from exercises and incidents are incorporated.
minimumEvidence: Exercise or incident record with timeline

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Exercise within 12 months
evidenceProfile.independence: Exercise observed by a party independent of the operating shift
acceptableAlternatives: Real recovery event with full timeline and analysis
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-10 UNKNOWN for thermal recovery

assessmentProcedure: Review the recovery procedure and its alignment with power restoration.
Review the exercise timeline step by step against the recovery time objective.
Check readmission limits against recovering capacity.
Interview shift staff on hold points and verification criteria.
Record unachieved steps as Findings.
controls.applicability: Applies to all heat-removal paths serving in-scope IT.
failureModes: Pumps restarted before controls, causing pressure surge
IT readmitted too fast, causing repeat trip
Air lock after restart
No agreed readmission plan
controls.testingSafety: Recovery exercises should be tabletop or on isolated sections unless a live exercise is authorised; Requires a permit-to-work and method statement approved by the site authorising engineer and AI platform operator agreement.
controls.unknownRule: If no exercise or real event is recorded, record US4 UNKNOWN against CG-10.

controls.title: Temperature Control
controls.objective: Demonstrate that air inlet temperatures at IT equipment and liquid coolant supply temperatures to cold plates or immersion tanks stay within the declared envelope and rate-of-change limits in all declared operating states, measured where the equipment experiences them.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall declare, for each hall and liquid loop, the environmental class (ASHRAE air-cooling class and liquid-cooling W class, or OEM envelope where more restrictive) and shall measure inlet air temperature at representative rack inlets and coolant supply temperature at the technology cooling system interface. The facility operator shall alarm excursions and rates of change outside the envelope, investigate them, and report excursion time per hall at the declared interval.
assessmentCriteria: Each hall and loop has a declared envelope traceable to ASHRAE classes or OEM specification.
Inlet sensors are at rack inlets (not return air) at the declared density, and coolant supply sensors are at the TCS interface.
Excursion time outside the recommended envelope per hall is reported and within the declared limit.
Rate-of-change alarms exist and events are investigated.
Sensor calibration is current for the sampled sensors.

controls.title: Humidity Control
controls.objective: Ensure moisture conditions avoid condensation on liquid-cooled components and pipework, electrostatic discharge risk at low humidity, and corrosion acceleration at high humidity.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall control and monitor dew point and relative humidity in IT spaces within the declared envelope and shall maintain coolant supply temperatures above room dew point by the declared margin wherever uninsulated liquid-cooling components are exposed to room air. The facility operator shall alarm when the margin is lost and shall define the response.
assessmentCriteria: Dew point and RH are monitored in each hall against the declared envelope.
Coolant supply temperature minus room dew point is monitored continuously for liquid-cooled halls and is at or above the declared margin for the period.
Margin-loss alarms exist with a defined response (raise supply temperature, dehumidify, isolate).
Humidification systems, if any, are maintained and water quality is controlled.

parameters.basis: ASHRAE TC 9.9 thermal guidelines recommended envelope

controls.title: Particulate and Corrosion
controls.objective: Ensure airborne particulate and gaseous contaminants are controlled so that hardware reliability is not degraded, particularly where economisation or high airflow increases outdoor air exposure.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall measure gaseous corrosivity by copper and silver reactivity coupons or real-time monitors and particulate cleanliness at the declared interval, shall maintain filtration to the declared grade, and shall act when the severity level exceeds the declared class, including restricting economiser operation during external pollution events.
assessmentCriteria: Corrosivity measurements at the declared interval meet the declared severity level.
Particulate cleanliness meets the declared ISO 14644-1 class in sampled halls.
Filtration grade and replacement intervals are maintained.
Economiser operation has a contamination-triggered lockout or procedure.

controls.title: Vibration and Acoustic Conditions
controls.objective: Ensure vibration and sound levels do not degrade storage and IT equipment (including acoustic damage to hard disk drives during gaseous suppression discharge), do not exceed occupational noise limits in dense halls, and comply with boundary noise limits in permits.
controls.requirement: The facility owner shall specify suppression discharge nozzles and agent release rates that keep sound pressure at storage equipment below the storage OEM threshold, shall measure occupational noise exposure in halls and plant rooms against regulatory action values and provide hearing protection and signage where exceeded, and shall demonstrate that site boundary noise from generators, heat rejection and transformers complies with planning or permit limits.
assessmentCriteria: Suppression nozzle and discharge design addresses acoustic impact on storage, with OEM threshold.
Occupational noise surveys exist for dense halls and plant rooms, with controls where action values are exceeded.
Boundary noise assessment or monitoring shows compliance with permit limits, including during generator testing.
Vibration-sensitive equipment locations are separated or isolated from vibration sources.

controls.title: PUE Measurement
controls.objective: Ensure power usage effectiveness is measured according to ISO/IEC 30134-2 with a declared measurement category, boundary and period, so that reported values are comparable, traceable and not distorted by metering gaps or boundary choices.
controls.requirement: The energy manager shall calculate PUE as annual total facility energy divided by annual IT equipment energy per ISO/IEC 30134-2, shall declare the measurement category and the metering points used for IT energy, shall include all energy sources (grid, on-site generation, fuel for generators), and shall report the value with category, period and data completeness.
assessmentCriteria: PUE uses annual energy (not instantaneous power) over a 12-month period.
The ISO/IEC 30134-2 measurement category is declared and IT energy meters match it.
All facility energy inputs, including generator fuel energy, are included.
Meter accuracy classes and calibration are documented for the meters used.
Data completeness is reported and gaps are filled by a documented method.

evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve consecutive months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Calculation reperformed by the assessor from meter data.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 (Material) where the control result could change a decision condition, otherwise US2 (Moderate) with a confidence ceiling of CONF-2 for the affected claims.

Check inclusion of all energy inputs.
Review data gaps and fill method.

Generator fuel energy omitted
IT energy measured at wrong point

controls.requirement: The facility owner shall evaluate flood levels under the declared climate scenario and horizon, shall confirm critical plant remains above the adjusted design level plus freeboard or is protected by permanent or demountable defences, and shall maintain a flood response plan with deployment time for demountable defences shorter than the warning lead time.
assessmentCriteria: Climate-adjusted flood levels are evaluated for the declared scenario and horizon.

controls.title: Accelerator Architecture
controls.objective: Establish a documented, approved accelerator architecture that links the Capability Instance's workload (training, fine-tuning, inference) to the accelerator type, memory capacity and bandwidth, scale-up domain size, scale-out fabric, power and cooling envelope, so that compute is sized and constrained by the Service Outcome rather than by procurement availability.
controls.requirement: The compute engineering authority shall maintain an accelerator architecture record per cluster stating accelerator model and generation, accelerator memory capacity and bandwidth, scale-up domain size and interconnect, host CPU and memory ratio, scale-out network attachment per accelerator, per-node and per-rack power and heat, and the cooling method required. The AI platform owner shall approve the record and shall confirm its sufficiency against the performance and integrity outcomes defined for the Capability Instance.
assessmentCriteria: An approved architecture record exists per cluster with the attributes listed in the requirement.
Each attribute traces to a workload requirement (model size, parallelism strategy, sequence length, throughput or latency target).
Power and heat per rack in the record reconcile with the facility heat-load model (MCF-THM-001) and power budget.
Scale-up and scale-out attachment ratios are stated and match the fabric design (NET-01).
Mixed-generation or heterogeneous accelerators, where present, are identified with their scheduling constraints.
Known platform limitations and OEM errata relevant to the outcome are recorded.

controls.title: Node Configuration
controls.objective: Ensure each compute node's hardware and low-level configuration (BIOS/UEFI settings, BMC configuration, PCIe topology, NUMA and accelerator affinity, NIC attachment, power and thermal limits) matches the approved node specification, because silent configuration drift degrades performance and reliability of collective workloads.
controls.requirement: The AI platform operator shall define a node configuration specification per node type and shall verify, at provisioning and at a defined interval, that every node conforms, using automated collection from the BMC (for example via Redfish) and host OS. The AI platform operator shall secure BMC interfaces with unique credentials, management-network isolation and logged access.
assessmentCriteria: A node configuration specification exists per node type covering BIOS/UEFI, BMC, PCIe/NUMA topology, accelerator power limits and NIC mapping.
Automated conformance collection covers ≥ the declared percentage of nodes and runs at the declared interval.

BMCs use unique credentials, are reachable only from the management network, and access is logged.
Accelerator power and clock limits set in configuration match the facility power and thermal envelope.

controls.title: Scale-Up Domain Integrity
controls.objective: Ensure each scale-up domain (the accelerator group joined by the high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnect, from a single node to a rack-scale domain) delivers its rated bandwidth with all links and switches healthy, and that a degraded domain is detected and withdrawn before it slows or corrupts a training job.
controls.requirement: The AI platform operator shall validate every scale-up domain at acceptance and at a defined interval by running an all-to-all or all-reduce bandwidth test against the platform's rated performance, shall monitor interconnect link errors, retrains and lane degradation continuously, and shall automatically drain domains that fall below the declared bandwidth threshold or exceed the link-error threshold.
assessmentCriteria: Acceptance bandwidth tests for each scale-up domain meet the declared fraction of rated bandwidth.
Periodic re-validation runs at the declared interval with results recorded.
Link error, retrain and lane-width telemetry is collected for every domain.
Drain automation triggers on threshold breach and has been observed to work (test or real event).
Domains returned to service after repair pass the bandwidth test.

controls.objective: Ensure logical partitions of the cluster (tenant, project, production versus test, accelerator partitioning such as multi-instance modes) are enforced so that one partition's jobs, faults or administrators cannot consume, disrupt or read another's resources.

The scheduler is configured to spread or co-locate according to the fault-domain policy.

controls.objective: Measure the accelerator capacity actually usable by the Capability Instance (healthy, schedulable, at rated performance, not thermally or power-throttled) and compare it with the capacity the outcome requires, rather than reporting installed accelerator count.

Reported usable capacity reconciles with scheduler state on a sampled day.

controls.title: Node Rebuild
controls.objective: Ensure nodes and scale-up domains can be rebuilt from bare metal to an accepted, schedulable state within the declared time after failure, corruption or mass events (for example after a power or cooling outage), including re-qualification before rejoining production.

controls.objective: Ensure the storage tier holding training and fine-tuning datasets is designed for the read pattern of data loaders at cluster scale, preserves dataset versions and lineage, and keeps data within declared sovereignty and residency boundaries.

controls.title: Checkpoint Tier
controls.objective: Ensure the checkpoint tier is sized so that model and optimiser state can be written within the declared checkpoint window at the declared interval, with the interval chosen against observed failure rates, and that checkpoints are placed in a fault domain independent of the compute they protect.
controls.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall document checkpoint size per job class, required write bandwidth (checkpoint size ÷ checkpoint window), checkpoint interval and its derivation from job-level failure rate and checkpoint cost, retention count, and the fault-domain separation between the checkpoint tier and the protected compute. The AI platform operator shall confirm the parameters per production job class.
assessmentCriteria: Checkpoint size per job class is stated with its basis (parameter count, precision, optimiser state, sharding).
Required write bandwidth is derived from size and window and is within the tier's demonstrated capability (MCF-STO-005).
Checkpoint interval is justified against job-level mean time between interruptions and checkpoint cost.
Retention of N most recent good checkpoints is defined.
Checkpoint storage does not share a power, cooling or fabric fault domain with all of the compute it protects, or the residual risk is accepted.
Asynchronous or tiered (local NVMe then parallel file system) checkpointing, if used, documents when a checkpoint is considered durable.

controls.objective: Ensure the storage system absorbs synchronised write bursts (many ranks checkpointing simultaneously, several jobs checkpointing at once, restart storms after an outage) without timeouts, job failure or degradation of other tenants.
controls.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall characterise peak burst demand (concurrent checkpoints, restart read storm), shall provide burst absorption (client-side or burst-buffer tier, QoS, admission control or staggered checkpoint scheduling), and shall demonstrate by test or production evidence that the declared burst completes within the window without client timeouts or impact beyond tolerance on other workloads.
assessmentCriteria: Peak burst demand is characterised including post-outage restart reads.
Burst absorption mechanisms are configured.
A test or production event shows the declared burst completed within the window.
No client timeouts or job failures attributable to storage occurred during the burst.
Impact on other tenants stayed within tolerance.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within 12 months or event in 90 days
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor analysis of raw telemetry
acceptableAlternatives: Simulation calibrated to measured single-job checkpoint
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: burst resilience uncertain; CG-08 and CG-09 supporting

assessmentProcedure: Review characterisation.
Review configuration.

failureModes: Restart storm after outage overwhelms storage
Concurrent checkpoints time out
Noisy neighbour degrades inference
controls.testingSafety: Burst tests in maintenance windows only.
controls.unknownRule: If restart read-storm behaviour is untested, record U5 UNKNOWN and link to MCF-STO-018.

controls.title: Data Integrity
controls.objective: Ensure data, checkpoints and model artefacts are protected end-to-end against undetected corruption from client to media and back, so that silent corruption cannot enter training or deployment.
controls.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall implement end-to-end integrity protection (application or file-level checksums on checkpoints and artefacts, plus storage-level checksums or protection information) and shall verify checksums on read and on restore. The AI platform operator shall verify checkpoint checksums before resuming training from them and shall treat a verification failure as an integrity incident.
assessmentCriteria: Checksum or protection-information mechanisms cover the path from client to media.
Checkpoints and artefacts carry application-level checksums recorded at write.
Checksums are verified on restore and before resume (sampled).
Verification failures are treated as integrity incidents with impact analysis.
Detection effectiveness was demonstrated by injected corruption on a test copy.

parameters.name: Checksum coverage of checkpoints and artefacts

evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: CG-08 UNKNOWN for integrity outcomes

assessmentProcedure: Review integrity architecture.
Recompute checksums on sample.
Review resume-time verification.
Review injection test.

failureModes: Silent corruption in checkpoint resumed into training
Bit flip in transit undetected
Corrupt model deployed
controls.testingSafety: Corruption injection only on test copies in isolated namespaces. Tests run against test namespaces or copies; no destructive action against production data, snapshots or recovery copies is permitted without the data owner's written authorisation.

controls.title: Metadata Integrity
controls.objective: Ensure file-system or object-store metadata (namespace, layout, allocation, object maps) is protected, consistent and recoverable, because metadata loss can render intact data unreachable for the whole tier.
controls.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall protect metadata with redundancy independent of the data path (replicated metadata servers or volumes), shall run consistency checks at a defined interval, shall back up metadata where the platform supports it, and shall demonstrate metadata service failover and recovery on a test system or in a controlled test.
assessmentCriteria: Metadata redundancy is configured and independent of single server or enclosure.
Consistency checks run at the interval and results are reviewed.
Metadata backups exist where supported and have been restored on test.
Metadata failover has been demonstrated within the declared time.
Metadata service failures in the period were contained.
minimumEvidence: Metadata backup and test restore records

controls.title: Checksum and Scrubbing
controls.objective: Detect latent media and data errors before they are needed by scrubbing stored data and verifying checksums on a schedule that completes within the declared cycle.
controls.requirement: The storage service owner shall schedule scrubbing so that all data on in-scope tiers is verified within the declared cycle, shall monitor scrub completion and error rates, and shall repair detected errors from redundancy promptly.
assessmentCriteria: Scrub schedule covers all in-scope tiers.

controls.objective: Ensure storage configuration (protection schemes, quotas, exports, client mount options, QoS, replication policies, retention locks) matches the approved baseline across all storage systems and clients.
controls.requirement: The storage service owner shall maintain an approved storage configuration baseline, shall detect drift automatically, shall apply changes under change control with post-change verification, and shall verify client mount options and versions across the fleet.
assessmentCriteria: An approved baseline exists.

controls.objective: Ensure snapshots of datasets, artefact registries and checkpoint directories are taken at the declared frequency, retained, protected from deletion by ordinary users, and actually restorable, to recover from accidental deletion or logical corruption.
controls.requirement: The storage service owner shall configure snapshot schedules and retention per protected namespace, shall restrict snapshot deletion to authorised roles, shall monitor snapshot success, and shall restore from snapshot on a sample basis at a defined interval.
assessmentCriteria: Snapshot schedules and retention are configured per protected namespace.
Snapshot success rate is monitored and failures remediated.

controls.title: Replication
controls.objective: Ensure data required for recovery is replicated to a target in an independent fault domain (another hall, site or region) within the declared recovery point objective, within permitted jurisdictions, and that replication lag and failures are detected.
controls.requirement: The storage service owner shall define replication scope, target, mode (synchronous or asynchronous) and RPO per data class, shall place targets outside the source's power, cooling, network and administrative fault domains as declared, shall keep targets within permitted jurisdictions, shall monitor lag, and shall demonstrate failover or restore from the replica.
assessmentCriteria: Replication scope, target, mode and RPO are defined per data class.
Target fault-domain independence is documented.

controls.title: Erasure Coding
controls.objective: Ensure erasure coding or RAID protection is configured so that stripes span independent failure domains (drive, server, enclosure, rack) and tolerate the declared number of concurrent failures, with rebuild completing before a further failure is likely.
controls.requirement: The storage engineering authority shall document the protection scheme per tier (for example k+m), the failure domains across which stripes are placed, the number of concurrent domain failures tolerated, and expected rebuild time at current capacity; shall verify placement against physical topology; and shall demonstrate rebuild of a failed component within the declared time.
assessmentCriteria: Protection scheme and failure-domain placement are documented per tier.
Placement is verified against physical rack and power topology.
