controls.title: Immutable Recovery Copy
controls.objective: Ensure at least one copy of recovery-critical data (latest good checkpoints, model artefacts, key datasets, storage and platform configuration) is immutable for its retention period and held in a separate administrative and fault domain, so that ransomware, privileged-account compromise or operator error cannot destroy every copy.
controls.requirement: The storage service owner shall maintain an immutable recovery copy of declared recovery-critical data with retention locks that cannot be shortened by administrators of the primary system, in a separate administrative domain with separate credentials, and shall demonstrate restore from it within the declared time.
assessmentCriteria: Recovery-critical data scope is declared.
Immutable copy exists with retention locks in compliance (non-shortenable) mode.

controls.title: Checkpoint Durability
controls.objective: Ensure each checkpoint is complete, consistent across all shards and ranks, durably committed and verifiable before it is marked good and before older checkpoints are deleted.
controls.requirement: The AI platform operator shall mark a checkpoint good only after all shards are written, flushed to durable storage, checksummed and manifest-recorded; shall never delete the previous good checkpoint until the new one is verified; and shall retain the declared number of good checkpoints. The storage service owner shall ensure the checkpoint tier honours flush semantics.
assessmentCriteria: Checkpoint completion requires all shards, flush, checksum and manifest.
Previous good checkpoint is retained until the new one is verified.
Retained count meets the declared value for sampled jobs.

controls.title: Fabric Topology
controls.objective: Ensure the scale-up and scale-out fabrics are built to an approved topology whose bisection bandwidth, tiering, rail assignment and endpoint attachment match what the declared training and inference Service Outcomes require.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall maintain an approved topology design for every back-end (scale-out) fabric and scale-up domain in scope, stating the topology class (for example rail-optimised multi-plane, two-tier leaf-spine or three-tier fat-tree/Clos, or rack-scale scale-up domain), switch radix, tier count, rail and plane assignment, endpoint-to-leaf mapping and the design bisection bandwidth per Capability Instance. The fabric operations lead shall reconcile the as-built fabric (LLDP or subnet-manager discovered topology, cabling records and port maps) to the approved design at commissioning and after every material change, and shall record every deviation as either an approved variance or a Finding.
assessmentCriteria: An approved topology design exists for each in-scope fabric and identifies topology class, tiers, radix, planes/rails, endpoint attachment and design bisection bandwidth.

Discovered topology (LLDP neighbour tables, InfiniBand subnet-manager topology dump or controller inventory) reconciles to the design with all mismatched, missing or miswired links listed and dispositioned.
Each accelerator NIC port is attached to the rail/plane and leaf required by the design; rail-mapping errors are zero or individually approved.
Design bisection bandwidth and per-endpoint injection bandwidth are traceable to the Service Outcome performance requirement for the Capability Instance.
Topology changes since the last reconciliation are linked to approved change records.

parameters.name: Rail-mapping conformance
parameters.unit: % of accelerator ports on design rail/leaf
parameters.basis: Rail-optimised designs assume ordinal NIC n connects to rail n; any deviation alters collective paths. Site-specific.

parameters.name: Maximum topology reconciliation age
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; shorten where change rate is high.

minimumEvidence: Approved fabric topology design and high-level design document, with version and approver
Discovered topology export (LLDP tables, subnet-manager topology file or fabric-controller inventory) dated within the reconciliation window
Automated or manual reconciliation report of discovered versus designed links and port maps
Rail/plane mapping table per node type
Change records for topology modifications since the previous reconciliation
