reassessmentTriggers: Change of topology class or tier count
Major NOS or subnet-manager upgrade altering discovery

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the approved topology design and confirm its version applies to the assessed Capability Instance.
Extract discovered topology from switches or the subnet manager using read-only collection.
Run or reperform the reconciliation of discovered links, port speeds and neighbours against design port maps.
Verify rail and plane assignment for a sample of nodes of each type, including recently replaced nodes.
Trace design bisection bandwidth to the Service Outcome performance requirement and to NET-003 oversubscription analysis.
Disposition every mismatch as approved variance or Finding and record residual UNKNOWNs.
controls.applicability: Applies to every back-end scale-out fabric (InfiniBand or Ethernet/RoCEv2) and every scale-up domain supporting an in-scope Capability Instance. Front-end and storage networks are covered by NET-009 and NET-010. Not applicable to single-node inference with no inter-node fabric, subject to approved rationale.
failureModes: Miswired or missing links reducing effective bisection bandwidth
Rail-mapping error forcing cross-rail traffic through spine
Undocumented topology drift after expansion
Mixed link speeds negotiated below design rate
controls.testingSafety: Topology collection shall use read-only interfaces and credentials. Re-cabling or port disablement to verify mapping shall not be performed on a production fabric without an approved change and workload owner consent.
controls.unknownRule: If discovered topology cannot be obtained for a gate-critical fabric, or reconciliation coverage is below the full fabric without a justified sample, record a US4 UNKNOWN against CG-08 and do not infer conformance from design documents.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
InfiniBand Trade Association, RoCEv2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification
IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Path Diversity
controls.objective: Ensure that logical redundancy in fabrics, inter-hall links and WAN/DCI connections is matched by physically diverse paths, so a single cable route, conduit, carrier or building entry cannot defeat redundant connectivity.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define, for each redundant path group (spine uplinks between halls, storage and front-end uplinks, WAN and data-centre interconnect circuits, OOB uplinks), the required diversity attributes: separate cable routes and containment, separate building entries, separate carriers or carrier-neutral dark-fibre routes, and separate optical line systems where DWDM is used. The connectivity manager shall obtain route evidence (carrier KMZ or route maps, cable-route surveys, containment records) for each path and shall record every shared segment, shared conduit, shared meet-me room or shared upstream carrier as a common-mode dependency.
assessmentCriteria: Each redundant path group has documented diversity requirements derived from the outcome criticality.
Route evidence for each external circuit identifies building entry, route and any shared segments to a defined granularity.
Intra-site redundant trunks are routed in separate containment or the shared section is analysed and accepted.
Carrier diversity accounts for wholesale or tail-circuit sharing (diverse brand on a shared underlying route is not treated as diverse).
Shared segments are registered as common-mode dependencies with owners and linked to DEP-007.
Diversity is re-verified after carrier grooming or re-routing notices.

parameters.name: Minimum physical separation between diverse routes
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Site-specific; set by risk analysis (illustrative: separate containment and entry points)
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter; no universal distance applies.

minimumEvidence: Path-group register listing redundant groups and diversity requirements
Carrier route documentation (maps, KMZ or route letters) for WAN/DCI circuits
Internal cable-route and containment drawings for inter-hall trunks
Common-mode analysis of shared segments with dispositions
Carrier notifications of re-routing and the review of each

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current route evidence within the evidence-age parameter; carrier change notices for the prior 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: External route claims corroborated by a second source (site walk-down of entries, independent route survey, or carrier-signed route letter).
mandatoryItems: Route evidence for each external circuit in a redundant group
acceptableAlternatives: Where a carrier will not disclose routes, a contractual diversity guarantee plus an independent survey of building entry and first-kilometre routes, with the remainder recorded as UNKNOWN U2
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 by default; US4 against CG-03 where the undisclosed segment carries the only DCI path for a gate-critical outcome.
reassessmentTriggers: Incident affecting two nominally diverse paths

assessmentProcedure: List all redundant path groups and their stated diversity requirements.
Collect route evidence for each member path and overlay routes to identify shared segments, entries and nodes.
Walk down building entries, risers and inter-hall containment for a sample of paths.
Check whether diverse carriers share wholesale tails, ducts or landing points.
Confirm each shared segment is in the dependency register with an owner and disposition.
Review carrier change notices for unreviewed re-routing.
controls.applicability: Applies to every network path relied upon as redundant for an in-scope outcome, including WAN/DCI used for multi-site training, replication or alternate capacity. Not applicable to paths whose loss is explicitly tolerated by the Service Outcome.
failureModes: Single excavation severing both 'diverse' DCI circuits
Both trunks in one cable tray exposed to one fire
Diverse carriers sharing one wholesale route
Silent carrier re-grooming removing diversity
controls.testingSafety: Route verification is non-intrusive. Failover tests between diverse circuits shall be scheduled under change control with the service owner, and shall not be performed during declared DEGRADED states.
controls.unknownRule: If a route for any member of a redundant path group cannot be evidenced, record UNKNOWN U2 or U10 and treat the group as non-diverse for CG-03 and blast-radius analysis until evidenced.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)
EN 50600 series / ISO/IEC 22237 series (Data centre facilities and infrastructures)

controls.title: Oversubscription
controls.objective: Ensure each fabric tier's oversubscription ratio is a deliberate design decision justified against the expected traffic matrix of the declared workloads, so collective and storage traffic are not throttled by uplink scarcity.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall state the design oversubscription ratio at every tier boundary (leaf-to-spine, spine-to-superspine, pod-to-core, storage and front-end uplinks) and shall justify each ratio against the traffic matrix of the declared workloads, including all-reduce, all-to-all (for example expert-parallel) and checkpoint bursts. The fabric operations lead shall re-derive effective oversubscription after link failures, partial builds and planned maintenance, and shall record the minimum tolerated effective ratio for each Service Outcome.
assessmentCriteria: Design oversubscription ratios are stated per tier and per fabric.
Each ratio is justified by a traffic-matrix or workload analysis covering the collective patterns and checkpoint traffic of declared workloads.
Effective oversubscription under N-1 uplink and N-1 spine conditions is calculated and compared to the tolerated ratio.
Partial-build or phased-expansion states that temporarily increase oversubscription are identified with accepted limitations.
Back-end fabrics designated non-blocking are verified to have uplink capacity equal to downlink capacity at each tier.

parameters.name: Back-end fabric design oversubscription
parameters.basis: Common design choice for large training fabrics; site and workload specific.

parameters.name: Front-end/storage uplink oversubscription
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter justified by traffic analysis.

parameters.name: Minimum tolerated effective ratio under N-1
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Set per Service Outcome (illustrative 1.15:1 for back-end)

minimumEvidence: Fabric design ratio table per tier
Traffic-matrix or workload communication analysis for declared workloads

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C2 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current design baseline; reconfirmed at each fabric expansion phase.
evidenceProfile.independence: Analysis reviewed by a network engineer independent of the design author or by the workload performance team.
acceptableAlternatives: Simulation or emulation results from a vendor or internal fabric model, provided inputs are traceable to declared workloads
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unjustified ratios cap performance assurance; CG-08 SUPPORTING evaluation required.
reassessmentTriggers: Change of workload mix (for example introduction of expert-parallel models)
Change of link speed at one tier only

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the per-tier ratio table and the topology design from NET-001.
Recompute ratios from port counts and speeds.
Review the workload traffic analysis and confirm it covers declared collectives and checkpoint bursts.
Calculate effective ratios under N-1 uplink and N-1 spine and compare to tolerated values.
Record limitations for phased-build states.
controls.applicability: Applies to every multi-tier fabric in scope. Single-tier fabrics need only the endpoint-to-switch capacity check.
failureModes: Uplink scarcity throttling all-to-all traffic
Checkpoint burst saturating storage uplinks
Ratio degrading beyond tolerance after spine loss
Phased build left in temporary state
controls.testingSafety: Analytical; no production traffic injection is required. Synthetic load tests belong to NET-007/NET-008 and require scheduling with workload owners.
controls.unknownRule: If no traffic analysis exists for a declared workload class, record UNKNOWN U1 against the performance outcome and do not accept a ratio solely on vendor reference designs.
informativeReferences: IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)
InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Fabric Fault-Domain Design
controls.objective: Ensure fabric failure domains (switch, rail, plane, pod, spine group, subnet manager, controller, power feed and cooling zone) are designed so that any single credible failure stays within a blast radius the Service Outcome tolerates.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the fault domains of each fabric, including each switch, rail, plane, pod, spine group, subnet manager or fabric controller instance, and the power and cooling zones serving fabric equipment, and shall state for each the maximum affected endpoints and the resulting outcome impact. The fabric operations lead shall demonstrate, by controlled test or by analysed incident, that loss of a leaf, a spine, a rail or plane, a subnet-manager master and one power feed to a switch row each stay within the declared blast radius, and that fabric equipment does not share an undisclosed power or cooling fault domain with its own redundancy.
assessmentCriteria: Fault-domain register for each fabric lists domain, members, maximum affected endpoints and tolerated impact.
Redundant fabric elements (spines, planes, subnet managers, controllers) are not co-located in a single power distribution path, cooling zone or rack without accepted rationale.
Loss of a single leaf, spine, plane or subnet-manager master has been tested or observed, and the measured effect (endpoints lost, job failures, reroute time) is within declared tolerance.
Fabric behaviour that widens a failure (for example PFC pause propagation, routing reconvergence storms or subnet-manager sweep load) is analysed and bounded.
Fault domains reconcile to CMP-008 compute fault domains and RES-005 site fault domains.
Residual multi-element failure scenarios outside tolerance are recorded with accepted limitations.

parameters.name: Maximum endpoints affected by a single switch failure
Maximum reroute/reconvergence time after single spine loss
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Set by job collective timeout margin (illustrative 30)
parameters.basis: Must be below framework collective timeouts; site-specific.

minimumEvidence: Fabric fault-domain register and blast-radius analysis
Power and cooling mapping of fabric switches, subnet managers and controllers
Test records or incident analyses for leaf, spine, plane and subnet-manager failure
Reconciliation to compute and site fault-domain models

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests or incidents within the previous 24 months and after any topology class change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test witnessed by a party independent of the fabric operations team, or independent review of incident analysis.
mandatoryItems: At least one test or analysed incident per fault-domain class
acceptableAlternatives: Pre-production or staging fabric test at representative scale, with a documented representativeness argument
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-09 cannot PASS while a gate-critical fabric's single-failure blast radius is untested and unanalysed.
reassessmentTriggers: Power or cooling re-zoning of network rows
Incident with impact beyond the declared domain

assessmentProcedure: Review the fault-domain register and confirm completeness against NET-001 topology.
Map each fabric element to its power path and cooling zone and identify co-location of redundant elements.
Review test plans and results for single-element failures, checking measured blast radius and reroute time.
Analyse PFC pause propagation and routing reconvergence as failure-widening mechanisms.
Reconcile fabric fault domains with CMP-008 and RES-005.
Record residual scenarios outside tolerance and their acceptance status.
controls.applicability: Applies to all fabrics supporting in-scope Capability Instances. For fabrics where loss of any element is tolerated by job restart from checkpoint, the analysis still applies but tolerance may be expressed as lost work.
failureModes: Both subnet managers on one PDU
Spine group sharing one cooling zone
PFC storm spreading a single NIC fault fabric-wide
Reconvergence exceeding collective timeouts and killing all jobs
controls.testingSafety: Element-failure tests on a production fabric (switch power-off, link shutdown, subnet-manager failover) are disruptive and shall only be performed with written authorisation from the service owner and network change board, a rollback plan, workload drain or owner consent, and monitoring in place. Power-feed removal tests require electrical authorisation under OPS-007 permit-to-work.
controls.unknownRule: Where blast radius has only been asserted by the vendor and not tested or observed locally, record UNKNOWN U8 (method uncertain) at US4 against CG-09.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Latency Baseline
controls.objective: Ensure the fabric has a measured latency baseline (idle and loaded, per path class) against which degradation can be detected and Service Outcome performance claims tested.
controls.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall establish and maintain latency baselines for each path class (intra-leaf, intra-pod, cross-spine, cross-plane, storage path, front-end path) including idle round-trip time, loaded tail latency at defined percentiles and switch-hop count, measured with a repeatable method (for example perftest-class RDMA latency tools or active probing). The fabric operations lead shall alert on deviation from baseline beyond a defined threshold and shall re-baseline after any material NOS, firmware, topology or congestion-control change.
assessmentCriteria: Baselines exist per path class with method, tool, message size and date recorded.
Tail latency percentiles are captured under representative load, not only idle conditions.
Continuous or periodic probing compares current latency to baseline and alerts on deviation.
Re-baselining occurred after each material change in the period.
Deviations exceeding the threshold in the period were investigated and closed.

parameters.name: Latency deviation alert threshold
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter tuned to measurement noise.

parameters.name: Baseline percentile set
parameters.basis: Tail latency drives synchronous collective step time.

minimumEvidence: Baseline report per path class with method details
Probe telemetry for the assessment period
Alert and investigation records for deviations

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Representative operating period of at least 90 days (illustrative) including a maintenance window.
evidenceProfile.independence: Telemetry extracted directly from the probe system by the assessor, not summarised by the operations team.
acceptableAlternatives: Workload-derived step-time telemetry where synthetic probes are not permitted, with mapping to path classes
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2: absent baselines reduce confidence in performance claims; US3 if a performance Service Outcome depends on latency tolerance.

assessmentProcedure: Review baseline reports for method repeatability and coverage of path classes.
Sample probe telemetry across the period and compare against baselines.
Trace deviations to alerts and investigation records.
Verify re-baselining after material changes recorded in NET-022.
controls.applicability: Applies to latency-sensitive fabrics supporting training or low-latency inference outcomes. May be limited to idle baselines for batch-only storage networks with approved rationale.
failureModes: Silent latency regression after firmware update
Degraded optic causing retransmission-driven tail latency
Unnoticed path asymmetry after reroute
controls.testingSafety: Active probes shall be rate-limited and run in a dedicated traffic class; loaded-latency measurements on production fabrics require scheduling with workload owners.
controls.unknownRule: If baselines predate the current NOS/firmware baseline, treat them as stale (U3) and do not use them to support performance claims.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
InfiniBand Trade Association, RoCEv2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Loss and Retransmission
controls.objective: Ensure packet loss, link errors and transport retransmissions are monitored against thresholds so that degrading links, optics and lossless-class failures are detected before they defeat job progress.
controls.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall monitor, per port and per traffic class, pre-FEC and post-FEC bit error indicators, FEC corrected and uncorrectable codeword counts, CRC/symbol errors, link flaps, discards, and RDMA transport retransmission and out-of-sequence counters at NICs, against defined thresholds. The fabric operations lead shall automatically isolate or drain links that exceed uncorrectable-error or flap thresholds, shall track each to closure, and shall verify that the lossless traffic class shows no congestion drops under normal operation.
assessmentCriteria: Thresholds are defined for FEC uncorrectable codewords, symbol/CRC errors, link flaps and NIC retransmission rates.
Collection covers all switch ports and NICs in the fabric with gaps listed.
Links breaching thresholds were isolated or drained and tracked through remediation in the period.
The lossless (RDMA) traffic class shows zero congestion drops in normal operation, or each drop event is explained.
Trend analysis identifies slow-burn degradation (rising corrected-error rates) before uncorrectable thresholds are reached.

parameters.name: Post-FEC uncorrectable codeword threshold
parameters.basis: Post-FEC errors become packet loss; vendor guidance applies.

parameters.name: Pre-FEC BER warning threshold
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Vendor/PHY specific (illustrative: one order of magnitude below FEC limit)
parameters.basis: Set from IEEE 802.3 FEC capability and vendor guidance.

minimumEvidence: Error counter telemetry for all ports for the period
Auto-isolation or drain events and tickets

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 90 days (illustrative) of continuous counter data.
evidenceProfile.independence: Counter data sampled directly from devices or the telemetry store by the assessor.
acceptableAlternatives: Periodic counter snapshots at defined intervals where streaming telemetry is unavailable, with interval justification
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unmonitored error classes may hide job-defeating link faults; CG-08 SUPPORTING evaluation.
reassessmentTriggers: Rise in job failures attributed to network

assessmentProcedure: Review threshold definitions against PHY and vendor guidance.
Confirm telemetry coverage across switch ports and NICs and list gaps.
Sample breaching links and trace isolation, ticket and remediation.
Inspect lossless-class drop counters and explain each event.
Review trend analysis for slow-burn degradation detection.
controls.applicability: Applies to all back-end, storage and front-end fabrics. Lossless-class criteria apply only to fabrics carrying RDMA over Ethernet or InfiniBand.
failureModes: Marginal optic causing intermittent uncorrectable errors and job stalls
Link flapping triggering repeated reroute
Lossless-class drops due to misconfigured PFC headroom
Slow optical degradation unnoticed
controls.testingSafety: Monitoring review only. Deliberate error injection or link disablement requires change approval and workload owner consent.
controls.unknownRule: If NIC-side retransmission counters are not collected, record U5 coverage gap; switch-side counters alone shall not support a claim of transport health.
informativeReferences: IEEE 802.3 (Ethernet, including optical PHY and FEC clauses)
InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
InfiniBand Trade Association, RoCEv2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification

controls.title: Congestion Control
controls.objective: Ensure congestion control and lossless configuration (ECN marking, PFC, DCQCN-style or vendor rate control, adaptive routing, InfiniBand credit-based flow control) keep fabrics stable under incast and many-to-one load, and that lossless-mode hazards such as PFC storms and deadlocks are prevented or contained.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define a congestion-control design per fabric stating traffic-class mapping, ECN marking thresholds, PFC enablement and headroom per priority, PFC watchdog behaviour, end-host rate-control algorithm and parameters, and adaptive routing settings, and shall analyse the design for cyclic buffer dependency (PFC deadlock) and pause-storm propagation. The fabric operations lead shall verify by controlled test that incast and congestion scenarios representative of declared workloads do not cause lossless-class drops, sustained pause propagation beyond the congested port, or deadlock, and that the PFC watchdog detects and breaks a stuck-pause condition within the configured time.
assessmentCriteria: A congestion-control design states class mapping, ECN thresholds, PFC priorities and headroom, watchdog settings, NIC rate-control parameters and routing behaviour.
Device configurations across the fabric match the design for all congestion-related parameters (sampled or fully reconciled).
Deadlock analysis demonstrates absence of cyclic buffer dependency under normal and failure routing, or mitigations (for example limiting lossless classes, routing restrictions) are in place.
Incast/congestion tests representative of declared workloads show no lossless-class drops and bounded pause propagation.
A simulated stuck-pause (pause-storm) condition is detected and isolated by the PFC watchdog or equivalent within the configured time.
ECN marking and congestion notification counters are monitored and show expected behaviour in operation.

parameters.name: PFC watchdog detection time
parameters.basis: Configured per NOS; verified by test.

parameters.name: Maximum tolerated pause propagation
parameters.basis: Design objective to keep pause local.

parameters.name: Lossless traffic classes
parameters.basis: Fewer lossless classes reduce deadlock and headroom exposure.

minimumEvidence: Configuration reconciliation of ECN, PFC, headroom, watchdog and NIC rate-control settings
Incast and pause-storm test plans and results

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within the previous 12 months and after any congestion-control parameter or NOS change; 90 days (illustrative) of counter telemetry.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test designed or witnessed by an engineer independent of the person who tuned the parameters.
acceptableAlternatives: Representative staging-fabric tests with identical NOS, NIC firmware and parameters where production testing is not authorised, with representativeness argument
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS for an RDMA-over-Ethernet fabric while lossless behaviour under congestion is untested.

assessmentProcedure: Review the congestion-control design and its rationale.
Reconcile congestion parameters across all fabric devices and NICs, recording drift.
Review deadlock analysis including failure-routing cases.
Review or witness incast tests and evaluate drops, pause propagation and job-level effect.
Review or witness a controlled pause-storm test and confirm watchdog action.
Sample operational counters for unexplained pause or drop events.
controls.applicability: Applies to every fabric carrying RDMA (RoCEv2, InfiniBand) or other congestion-sensitive collective traffic. For InfiniBand, PFC criteria are replaced by credit-based flow control and adaptive-routing configuration review.
failureModes: PFC storm from a malfunctioning NIC halting a pod
PFC deadlock from cyclic buffer dependency after a routing change
Insufficient headroom causing lossless drops
ECN thresholds too high leading to buffer exhaustion
Parameter drift between switches
controls.testingSafety: Incast and pause-storm tests can stall production fabrics and shall only be run with explicit written authorisation from the service owner and network change board, in a scheduled window, with the workload drained or isolated, the watchdog verified enabled beforehand and an abort criterion defined.
controls.unknownRule: If NIC-side rate-control parameters cannot be extracted, record U2 and treat the end-to-end congestion design as unverified.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, RoCEv2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification
InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)

controls.title: Collective Communication Performance
controls.objective: Ensure collective operations (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all) achieve the bus bandwidth and step-time required by declared training and inference outcomes at full and degraded scale.
controls.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall run a defined collective benchmark suite (for example NCCL- or RCCL-class tests and a representative workload proxy) at commissioning, after every material fabric, NIC or library change and at a defined periodic interval, covering message sizes and scales used by declared workloads, and shall compare achieved bus bandwidth and latency to acceptance targets. The capability owner shall set the acceptance targets from the performance Service Outcome and shall accept or reject results for degraded scale (for example one plane or one spine unavailable).
assessmentCriteria: A collective benchmark suite is defined with operations, message sizes, scales, library versions and environment variables recorded.
Acceptance targets per operation and scale are approved by the capability owner and traceable to the performance Service Outcome.
Current results at full scale meet targets, or shortfalls are recorded as Findings.
Results at defined degraded scale meet the degraded targets.
Benchmarks were rerun after every material change and at the periodic interval.
Per-node or per-rail outliers are identified and remediated.

parameters.name: Collective acceptance target
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter derived from performance outcome.

minimumEvidence: Benchmark results with raw outputs and environment captures

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent periodic run within the interval parameter, and runs after each material change in the previous 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reperforms or witnesses at least one benchmark run, or raw outputs are independently parsed.
acceptableAlternatives: Production job step-time telemetry from instrumented workloads, where synthetic benchmarks are impractical, with mapping to operations and scales
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS while collective performance at required scale is unmeasured.

assessmentProcedure: Review the benchmark suite definition against declared workload communication patterns.
Confirm targets are approved and traceable to Service Outcomes.
Parse raw outputs and verify reported bus bandwidth and latency.
Witness or reperform a benchmark run at representative scale.
Review degraded-scale results and acceptance.
Trace outliers to remediation.
controls.applicability: Applies to multi-node training and distributed inference Capability Instances. Not applicable where outcomes do not depend on inter-node collectives.
failureModes: Collective bandwidth regression after library upgrade
Single bad node or rail throttling a whole job
Degraded-scale performance below outcome tolerance
Environment misconfiguration bypassing RDMA
controls.testingSafety: Full-scale benchmarks consume the cluster and shall be scheduled with the capability owner; degraded-scale tests that disable a plane or spine are disruptive and require change-board authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Benchmarks run with library versions or environment settings different from production are not representative (U5) and shall not support a CONFORMING result.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
InfiniBand Trade Association, RoCEv2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Storage Fabric
controls.objective: Ensure the storage network (dedicated or converged) delivers the throughput, latency and isolation needed for dataset reads and checkpoint write bursts without interfering with collective traffic.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the storage network design: whether storage traffic uses a dedicated fabric, a dedicated plane or a separate traffic class on the compute fabric; the path from compute nodes to storage servers and metadata services; capacity per storage server; and the traffic-class and congestion policy that prevents checkpoint bursts from degrading collective traffic. The storage platform owner and fabric operations lead shall jointly test a synchronised checkpoint write and a dataset-read burst at declared scale and confirm achieved throughput and the effect on concurrent collective performance meet targets.
assessmentCriteria: Storage network design states topology, traffic-class policy, capacity per storage target and metadata service paths.
Configured traffic-class and QoS settings match the design.
A synchronised checkpoint-write test at declared scale achieves the throughput needed to meet the checkpoint-time target.
Concurrent collective performance during the checkpoint burst stays within the tolerated degradation.
Storage metadata services are reachable over redundant paths with no single switch dependency.

parameters.name: Checkpoint write window
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Derived from checkpoint size and goodput target (illustrative 120)

minimumEvidence: Storage network design and traffic-class policy

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within 12 months and after storage or network capacity change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Joint test witnessed by an assessor or a party independent of both storage and network teams.
acceptableAlternatives: Production checkpoint telemetry from large jobs showing achieved write throughput and concurrent step time
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-08 cannot PASS while checkpoint-path throughput at declared scale is unverified (scenario X06).

assessmentProcedure: Review storage network design and confirm path to metadata and data services.
Reconcile traffic-class configuration on switches and NICs.
Review or witness checkpoint-burst and dataset-read tests.
Measure or review collective performance during the burst.
Confirm metadata path redundancy.
controls.applicability: Applies to any Capability Instance that reads training data or writes checkpoints over a network. Local-NVMe-only checkpointing still requires assessment of the path used to drain checkpoints to durable storage.
failureModes: Checkpoint burst saturating shared uplinks (X06)
Storage and collective traffic sharing a lossless class causing head-of-line blocking
Metadata service reachable via a single switch
Dataset-read starvation reducing accelerator utilisation
controls.testingSafety: Checkpoint-burst tests load shared storage and may affect other tenants; schedule with the storage platform owner and notify affected service owners. Do not run destructive storage tests under this control.
controls.unknownRule: If checkpoint throughput is only known from storage vendor specifications, record U8 and limit the claim to DESIGN.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, RoCEv2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Frontend Network
controls.objective: Ensure the front-end network that carries user, API, inference request, orchestration and data-ingest traffic is built to an approved, redundant design and reconciles to it.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall maintain an approved front-end network design covering node attachment (dual-homed or single-homed), routing protocol and ECMP design, uplinks to core and edge, load-balancer and gateway placement, and capacity for inference request and data-ingest peaks. The network operations manager shall reconcile as-built configuration and attachment to the design at commissioning and after material changes, and shall confirm that loss of a single front-end switch or uplink does not disconnect inference endpoints or orchestration control traffic beyond tolerance.
assessmentCriteria: Approved front-end design exists with attachment, routing, capacity and redundancy stated.
As-built attachment and routing configuration reconcile to design.
Inference and orchestration endpoints have redundant attachment or an accepted single-homed rationale.
Capacity for declared inference request and ingest peaks is demonstrated by telemetry or test.
Single-switch or uplink failure has been tested or observed with effect within tolerance.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Reconciliation within 90 days (illustrative); peak telemetry over a representative period.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation reviewed by someone other than the implementer.
acceptableAlternatives: Witnessed sample inspection of attachment where automated inventory is incomplete
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unreconciled front-end attachment may hide single points of failure for inference outcomes.

assessmentProcedure: Review design and capacity basis.
Reconcile attachment and routing configuration.
Check redundancy of inference and orchestration endpoints.
Review peak utilisation telemetry.
Review failover evidence.
controls.applicability: Applies to front-end networks serving in-scope inference, orchestration and data-ingest. Where the front end is provided by a cloud or colocation provider, the provider boundary (DEP-018) governs evidence rights.
failureModes: Single-homed inference gateways
ECMP imbalance saturating one uplink
Orchestration traffic lost on front-end switch failure
controls.testingSafety: Front-end failover tests affect customer-facing inference and require service owner authorisation and customer-impact assessment.
controls.unknownRule: Where provider-operated front-end segments cannot be inspected, record U2 and bound claims to the owned segment.
informativeReferences: IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)
ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)

controls.title: Service Gateways
controls.objective: Ensure gateways, load balancers, NAT, firewalls and edge routers on the service path operate within capacity, with health monitoring and redundancy that sustain inference and data-ingest outcomes.
controls.requirement: The network operations manager shall operate each service gateway cluster (load balancers, inference API gateways, NAT, edge routers and in-path firewalls) as a redundant pair or cluster with health checks, session-state handling and capacity monitoring, and shall define capacity thresholds for connections, throughput and TLS handshakes. The network operations manager shall review gateway capacity and failover events monthly and shall demonstrate that gateway failover occurred, or was tested, within tolerance in the assessment period.
assessmentCriteria: Every in-path gateway is redundant or the single instance is an accepted limitation.
Capacity thresholds for connections, throughput and handshake rate are defined and monitored.
Health checks and failover triggers are configured and their behaviour is understood (state synchronisation, session loss).
Monthly capacity and event reviews occurred in the period with actions tracked.
Failover occurred or was tested in the period with measured disruption within tolerance.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least six months (illustrative) of capacity data and reviews.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor samples telemetry directly.
acceptableAlternatives: Provider service-level reports for managed gateways, with evidence rights per SUP-006
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unknown gateway capacity or failover behaviour conditions the inference availability claim.

assessmentProcedure: Inventory in-path gateways and redundancy modes.
Review thresholds and sample telemetry for breaches.
Review monthly reviews and actions.
Examine failover events or tests and measured disruption.
controls.applicability: Applies to gateways on the path of in-scope inference, API and data-ingest outcomes. Security policy content of firewalls is assessed under SEC-011.
failureModes: Gateway connection-table exhaustion
Failover dropping all sessions
TLS handshake capacity exhausted at peak
Asymmetric routing through stateful gateways
controls.testingSafety: Gateway failover tests disrupt sessions and require service owner authorisation and a customer communication plan where external customers are affected.
controls.unknownRule: If session-state behaviour during failover is undocumented and untested, record U8 and limit availability claims.
informativeReferences: IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Traffic Isolation
controls.objective: Ensure tenant, workload and traffic-class isolation on shared fabrics prevents one tenant or job from degrading, observing or reaching another beyond tolerance.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the isolation model for shared fabrics: InfiniBand partition keys, VRFs, VXLAN/EVPN segments, VLANs, RDMA queue-pair and memory-region protections, traffic-class guarantees and rate limits. The fabric operations lead shall verify by test that endpoints in one isolation domain cannot reach endpoints in another, and that a saturating or misbehaving tenant cannot reduce another tenant's guaranteed bandwidth or trigger fabric-wide pause beyond the defined tolerance.
assessmentCriteria: The isolation model states mechanisms, domains, and which traffic classes are shared.
Configuration of partitions, VRFs or segments reconciles to tenant assignments.
Reachability tests confirm no unintended cross-domain connectivity at layer 2, layer 3 and RDMA.
Performance-isolation tests show a saturating tenant does not reduce another tenant's guaranteed share beyond tolerance.
Tenant onboarding and offboarding updates isolation configuration and is verified.

parameters.name: Guaranteed bandwidth share per tenant class

minimumEvidence: Partition/VRF/segment configuration extracts with tenant mapping

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within 12 months and after isolation model change; onboarding records for the period.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reachability tests executed or witnessed by the security function independent of fabric operations.
acceptableAlternatives: Staging-fabric performance-isolation tests with identical configuration, with representativeness argument
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 for single-tenant estates; US4 against CG-09 for multi-tenant platforms where isolation is a declared outcome.

assessmentProcedure: Review the isolation model and tenant assignments.
Reconcile partition/VRF/segment configuration with tenant records.
Review or witness reachability tests across domains.
Review or witness performance-isolation tests.
Sample onboarding/offboarding changes for verification.
controls.applicability: Applies to fabrics shared by more than one tenant, customer or trust domain. For single-tenant fabrics, only traffic-class isolation between storage, collective and management traffic applies.
failureModes: Partition key misassignment exposing tenant RDMA memory
Noisy-neighbour congestion degrading other tenants
Stale segment after offboarding
Shared lossless class propagating pause across tenants
controls.testingSafety: Cross-tenant reachability tests shall use designated test endpoints and shall not access tenant data. Saturation tests require tenant notification and change approval.
controls.unknownRule: If RDMA-layer isolation has not been tested separately from IP-layer isolation, record U5 and do not infer RDMA isolation from IP results.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Management Separation
controls.objective: Ensure management traffic for switches, servers, BMCs, PDUs, storage and facility gateways traverses a management network separated from data and tenant networks, so data-plane failure or compromise does not remove management reach.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall define the management network architecture, separating in-band management, BMC/out-of-band management and facility OT management, and shall prohibit management interfaces from being reachable from tenant or data networks except through defined conduits. The network operations manager shall reconcile the management network attachment of every switch management port, BMC, PDU, console server and storage controller to the design, and shall record any device whose management is only reachable in-band as a Finding.
assessmentCriteria: Management network architecture defines in-band, out-of-band and OT management segments and permitted conduits.
Every in-scope managed device has its management interface attached to the designated segment.
No management interface is reachable from tenant or data networks except via defined conduits (verified by scan or ACL review).
Devices relying solely on in-band management are listed and dispositioned.
Management network capacity and addressing are independent of the data fabric.
minimumEvidence: Reachability scan or ACL analysis from tenant/data networks

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Reconciliation within 90 days (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Reachability scan run by the security function.
acceptableAlternatives: Firewall and ACL rule analysis where active scanning is not permitted
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; escalates to US4 against CG-15 where BMCs or facility gateways are reachable from tenant networks.

assessmentProcedure: Review the management architecture and conduits.
Reconcile device management attachment against inventory.
Review reachability scans or ACL analysis from tenant/data segments.
Disposition in-band-only devices.
controls.applicability: Applies to all managed network, compute, storage, power-distribution and facility gateway devices supporting in-scope outcomes. Security policy of the conduits is assessed under SEC-010.
failureModes: BMCs on tenant VLAN
Switch management only in-band, lost when the fabric fails
Facility gateways bridged to IT management
controls.testingSafety: Reachability scans shall be non-intrusive, rate-limited and authorised by the security owner; scanning OT segments requires OT owner approval (see SEC-009).
controls.unknownRule: Devices whose management attachment cannot be determined are treated as reachable from data networks (U1) until evidenced.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)
ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)

controls.title: Console Access
controls.objective: Ensure serial console and remote KVM access to network, compute and storage devices exists, is authenticated and is reachable independently of the data plane.
controls.requirement: The network operations manager shall provide serial console access to every switch, router, firewall and storage controller, and BMC/KVM access to every server, through console servers or OOB infrastructure that is independent of the data fabric, and shall require individual authentication, session logging and role-based authorisation for console sessions. The network operations manager shall verify console reachability for every device at a defined interval and after rack moves.
assessmentCriteria: Every in-scope device has a mapped console or BMC path recorded in inventory.
Console servers authenticate individual users against a central identity source with local fallback governed by NET-016.
Console sessions are logged with user, device, time and, where supported, keystroke capture.
Periodic console reachability checks cover all devices and failures are remediated.
Console port mappings are verified after rack moves or re-cabling.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent reachability check within the interval and checks over the prior six months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor samples console reachability live with read-only login.
acceptableAlternatives: Witnessed manual console checks on a sample where automated checks are unavailable
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unknown console reach weakens recovery assurance; SUPPORTING evaluation for CG-10.

assessmentProcedure: Review console mapping completeness against device inventory.
Review console authentication and logging configuration.
Sample devices and confirm live console reach using read-only access.
Review reachability check history and remediation.
controls.applicability: Applies to all network, storage and compute devices that would need recovery action during fabric or control-plane failure.
failureModes: Unmapped console after rack move
Shared console credentials
Console servers dependent on the failed fabric
controls.testingSafety: Live console checks shall use read-only roles and shall not send break signals or keystrokes that could interrupt device boot or operation.
controls.unknownRule: If console mapping completeness cannot be verified, treat unmapped devices as lacking recovery access (U1) in recovery-sequence analysis.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)
ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)

controls.title: OOB Resilience
controls.objective: Ensure the out-of-band management network remains available when the data fabric, site core, primary identity services or primary WAN fail, so restoration can proceed.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall design the OOB network with its own switching, power supply from a protected source with defined autonomy, independent upstream connectivity (for example a separate carrier or cellular path), and locally available authentication and name resolution, and shall document every dependency the OOB network has on the systems it is used to recover. The network operations manager shall test at a defined interval that OOB access to critical devices is achievable with the production fabric, primary WAN and primary identity provider unavailable.
assessmentCriteria: OOB design states switching, power source and autonomy, upstream paths and authentication fallback.
Dependency analysis shows the OOB network does not depend on the production fabric, production DNS/identity or the primary WAN, or each dependency is mitigated.
OOB equipment power is from a protected supply with autonomy meeting the recovery-sequence requirement.
A test in the period demonstrated OOB reach to critical devices with production fabric, primary WAN and primary identity unavailable (or simulated unavailable).
OOB health is monitored and failures alarm to an independent channel.

parameters.name: OOB power autonomy
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Equal to or greater than black-start sequence duration (illustrative 4)

minimumEvidence: Power path and autonomy evidence for OOB equipment
OOB health monitoring configuration and alarms

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Isolation test within the interval parameter; health telemetry for six months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test witnessed by the recovery or resilience function independent of network operations.
acceptableAlternatives: Scenario exercise with simulated isolation (credentials and paths forced to fallback) where full isolation is not authorised, with residual UNKNOWN recorded
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS while OOB independence from the systems it recovers is unverified.

assessmentProcedure: Review the OOB design and list its dependencies.
Trace OOB power to its source and verify autonomy.
Confirm local authentication and name resolution fallback exist and are tested.
Review or witness the isolation test.
Review OOB health monitoring and alarm routing.
controls.applicability: Applies to every site supporting in-scope outcomes. Where OOB is provided by a colocation operator, responsibilities shall be explicit under DEP-018.
failureModes: OOB authentication dependent on the identity provider hosted on the failed cluster
OOB switches powered from non-protected supply
OOB uplink sharing the primary carrier route
Circular dependency on production DNS
controls.testingSafety: Isolation tests shall not disconnect production identity or WAN; they shall simulate isolation by forcing OOB clients to fallback paths, under an approved change with a rollback plan.
controls.unknownRule: Any OOB dependency on a production service that has not been analysed is recorded as U10 at US4 against CG-10.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)
EN 50600 series / ISO/IEC 22237 series (Data centre facilities and infrastructures)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: Break-Glass Access
controls.objective: Ensure emergency access to network devices and controllers works when central authentication is unavailable, and that its use is controlled, logged and reviewed.
controls.requirement: The network operations manager shall provision break-glass local credentials or offline authentication for network devices, fabric controllers, subnet managers and console servers, stored in a sealed or vaulted mechanism with dual control, and shall test break-glass login on a sample of device classes at a defined interval. The infrastructure security owner shall review every break-glass use within a defined time, rotate the credentials afterwards, and confirm that break-glass accounts are disabled for routine use.
assessmentCriteria: Break-glass credentials exist for every device class needed in recovery and are stored under dual control.
Break-glass login works on a sampled device of each class when central authentication is unreachable.
Every break-glass use in the period was logged, reviewed within the defined time and followed by credential rotation.
Break-glass accounts are not used for routine operations (log analysis).
Retrieval of break-glass credentials is possible during loss of the primary vault (offline copy governed by SEC-004).
minimumEvidence: Break-glass account inventory per device class
Use logs, reviews and rotation records

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within the interval; all uses in the previous 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Security function reviews use logs independently of network operations.
acceptableAlternatives: Tabletop plus a single live test on a non-production device of each class where production tests are not authorised
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 if no tested emergency access exists for gate-critical fabric controllers.

assessmentProcedure: Review break-glass inventory against recovery device classes.
Inspect dual-control and offline retrieval arrangements.
Review or witness a break-glass login test with central authentication made unreachable for the test device.
Sample use events and confirm review and rotation.
Analyse logs for routine use of break-glass accounts.
controls.applicability: Applies to network devices, fabric controllers, subnet managers and console servers supporting in-scope outcomes. Governance of break-glass across all infrastructure is SEC-004.
failureModes: Break-glass password unknown or expired at time of need
Vault unreachable during outage
Break-glass account used routinely
No rotation after use
controls.testingSafety: Break-glass tests shall be performed on a non-critical device or in a maintenance window, without disabling central authentication for other devices; rotation shall follow every test.
controls.unknownRule: If no break-glass test has been performed for a device class, record U1 and treat emergency access for that class as unavailable in recovery analysis.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: Cabling Standards
controls.objective: Ensure structured cabling and high-density fibre plant are designed to recognised standards for pathways, bend radius, polarity, labelling, density and serviceability so that the physical layer does not become a latent fabric failure source.
controls.requirement: The cabling plant owner shall maintain a cabling design standard for the site covering pathway and containment fill limits, segregation from power, minimum bend radius by cable type, MPO/MTP polarity method, connector cleanliness acceptance, labelling scheme and test acceptance (insertion loss and, where applicable, reflectance), aligned with recognised data-centre cabling standards. The cabling plant owner shall approve deviations, and installers shall be bound to the standard contractually.
assessmentCriteria: A site cabling standard exists covering pathways, fill, segregation, bend radius, polarity, cleanliness, labelling and test acceptance.
The standard references recognised cabling standards families and is approved by the cabling plant owner.
High-density back-end trunk designs (fibre counts, breakout scheme, patch-panel density) are specified.
Installer contracts reference the standard and its acceptance tests.
Deviations are approved and recorded.
minimumEvidence: Trunk and breakout design for back-end fabrics

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C2 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current approved version.
evidenceProfile.independence: Review by a qualified cabling designer other than the author.
acceptableAlternatives: Adoption of an operator-wide standard with site addendum
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2: absent standard reduces confidence in physical-layer claims; US3 where NET-018 shows optics failures attributable to cabling.

assessmentProcedure: Review the cabling standard against adopted standards families.
Check coverage of high-density back-end trunk design.
Inspect a sample of installed pathways for conformance.
Review installer contracts and deviations.
controls.applicability: Applies to all owned or operated cabling plant supporting in-scope fabrics. Provider-owned cabling is governed by provider contracts.
failureModes: Bend-radius violations causing marginal loss
Polarity errors on MPO trunks
Overfilled trays preventing safe moves
Dirty connectors
controls.testingSafety: Physical inspection shall not disturb live cabling; opening trays or handling live fibre requires an approved method statement.
controls.unknownRule: If no site standard exists, physical-layer claims rely only on test results (NET-018/NET-020) and confidence is capped at CONF-2.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)
ISO/IEC 11801 series (Generic cabling for customer premises, including data centres)
ISO/IEC 14763 series (Implementation and operation of customer premises cabling, including optical fibre testing)
EN 50600 series / ISO/IEC 22237 series (Data centre facilities and infrastructures)
IEC 61300-3-35 (Fibre optic connector endface visual and automated inspection)

controls.title: Optics Compatibility
controls.objective: Ensure transceivers, active and passive cables and NIC/switch firmware are qualified combinations with adequate link budget, so optics do not become a common-mode source of link errors and flaps.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall maintain a qualified-optics matrix listing approved transceiver and cable part numbers, firmware versions, host switch/NIC models and NOS/firmware versions, reach and link-budget class. The fabric operations lead shall reconcile installed optics (from digital diagnostic and CMIS inventory) to the matrix, shall monitor optical diagnostics (Rx/Tx power, temperature, bias, pre-FEC error indicators), and shall quarantine unqualified or degrading optics.
assessmentCriteria: A qualified-optics matrix exists with part numbers, firmware, host combinations and link-budget class.
Installed optics inventory reconciles to the matrix; unqualified parts are listed and dispositioned.
Optical diagnostics are collected for all optics with thresholds for low Rx power and high temperature.
Measured link loss for a sample of links is within the transceiver budget with the defined margin.
Optics firmware is at qualified versions; mixed versions within a fabric are justified.
Failure and RMA data are analysed for batch or lot-level common modes.

parameters.name: Rx power warning margin
parameters.basis: Capability-profile parameter derived from vendor budget.

minimumEvidence: Installed optics inventory with serial, part and firmware

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Inventory within 30 days (illustrative); diagnostics for 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Inventory extracted by assessor from devices.
acceptableAlternatives: Sample-based physical inspection with serial capture where diagnostics are not readable
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unqualified optics at scale are a common-mode exposure; escalate to US4 under CG-08 if failure analysis shows lot-level defects.

assessmentProcedure: Review the qualified-optics matrix for completeness.
Extract installed optics inventory and reconcile.
Review diagnostics thresholds and sample telemetry.
Sample link loss test records against budget.
Review RMA data for lot or firmware common modes.
controls.applicability: Applies to all pluggable optics, AOCs and DACs in in-scope fabrics; for co-packaged or linear-drive optics, the matrix records host and module firmware combinations.
failureModes: Unqualified optic causing intermittent errors
Optic lot defect affecting thousands of links
Firmware mismatch between module and host
Insufficient link margin
controls.testingSafety: Reading diagnostics is non-intrusive; removing optics for inspection requires change approval and link drain.
controls.unknownRule: Optics whose diagnostics cannot be read are treated as unqualified (U1) pending inspection.
informativeReferences: OSFP MSA and QSFP-DD MSA module specifications; CMIS (Common Management Interface Specification)
IEEE 802.3 (Ethernet, including optical PHY and FEC clauses)
IEC 61300-3-35 (Fibre optic connector endface visual and automated inspection)
ISO/IEC 14763 series (Implementation and operation of customer premises cabling, including optical fibre testing)

controls.title: Cross-Connect Control
controls.objective: Ensure physical moves, adds and changes to patching and cross-connects (including in meet-me rooms and carrier demarcations) are authorised, recorded and verified, so that maintenance does not sever redundant paths.
controls.requirement: The network operations manager shall require an approved work order for every physical patch or cross-connect change, specifying both ends, labels, affected path groups and redundancy impact, and shall verify after each change that the link came up on the expected ports and that the cabling records were updated. The network operations manager shall prohibit simultaneous work on members of the same redundant path group unless explicitly approved.
assessmentCriteria: Every physical change in the sampled period has an approved work order identifying both ends and path-group impact.
Post-change verification (link state, neighbour, label) is recorded for each change.
Cabling records are updated within the defined time after change.
No simultaneous work on members of one redundant path group occurred without approval.
Carrier and colocation cross-connect changes are reconciled to provider orders.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least six months (illustrative) of changes.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor selects the sample from device link-event logs rather than from the work-order system.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: link events without matching work orders indicate uncontrolled physical change; CG-14 SUPPORTING.

assessmentProcedure: Extract link up/down events for the period from devices.
Match events to work orders and identify unmatched changes.
Check sampled work orders for path-group impact and post-change verification.
Check for concurrent work on redundant pairs.
Reconcile provider cross-connect orders.
controls.applicability: Applies to all owned patching and to provider cross-connects for in-scope paths.
failureModes: Wrong cable pulled during maintenance severing the surviving path
Unrecorded patch causing rail mis-mapping
Simultaneous work on both diverse trunks
controls.testingSafety: Reconciliation is records-based and non-intrusive.
controls.unknownRule: Unmatched link events are recorded as Findings unless explained; if link-event logs are unavailable, record U2 and limit the claim.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)

controls.title: Path Documentation
controls.objective: Ensure end-to-end physical and logical path records (port to patch panel to trunk to panel to port, and circuit to route) are complete and accurate enough to support fault isolation, diversity analysis and recovery.
controls.requirement: The network operations manager shall maintain a path-documentation system (DCIM or cable-management database) recording every in-scope link from endpoint port through patch panels, trunks and cross-connects to the far-end port, with labels matching the physical plant and links to circuit IDs for external paths. The network operations manager shall audit a sample of paths physically and electronically at a defined interval and shall correct discrepancies, with an accuracy target set as a capability-profile parameter.
assessmentCriteria: Path records exist for all in-scope links including intermediate panels and trunks.
Labels in the field match records for the audited sample.
Electronic reconciliation (LLDP or subnet-manager neighbours) matches end-to-end records.
Audit accuracy meets the target, and discrepancies are corrected.
External circuit records link to provider circuit IDs and routes (NET-002).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Most recent audit within 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Physical audit performed by the assessor or a party independent of the record maintainers.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: inaccurate path records undermine diversity (CG-03) and recovery (CG-10) analysis.

assessmentProcedure: Extract path records for in-scope fabrics.
Select a sample and physically verify labels and routes.
Reconcile electronically against neighbour data.
Compute accuracy and review corrections.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope links and external circuits.
failureModes: Records misidentifying the surviving path during an incident
Untraceable trunks after expansion
Circuit ID not linked to route
controls.testingSafety: Physical audits shall not disturb live cables beyond visual label inspection.
controls.unknownRule: Where records cannot be reconciled for a fabric segment, the segment's paths are treated as undocumented (U1) in diversity and blast-radius analysis.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)
ISO/IEC 14763 series (Implementation and operation of customer premises cabling, including optical fibre testing)

controls.title: Controller Resilience
controls.objective: Ensure fabric control functions (InfiniBand subnet managers, SDN or EVPN controllers, fabric management platforms, route reflectors) survive single failures and that their loss does not disrupt forwarding beyond tolerance.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall deploy fabric control functions with redundancy (master/standby subnet managers, clustered controllers, redundant route reflectors) placed in separate power and rack fault domains, and shall document the data-plane behaviour when the control function is lost (forwarding continues with stale state, or fails). The fabric operations lead shall test controller and subnet-manager failover at a defined interval and after upgrades and shall confirm forwarding continuity and failover time within tolerance.
assessmentCriteria: Each fabric control function has redundancy and placement in separate power/rack domains.
Data-plane behaviour on control-plane loss is documented.
Failover tests in the period show forwarding continuity and failover time within tolerance.
Controller state backups exist and restore has been tested.
Controller health is monitored and alarms on loss of redundancy.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Failover test within the interval and after the last upgrade.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test witnessed by a party independent of fabric operations.
acceptableAlternatives: Staging test at representative scale where production failover is not authorised
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-08 for InfiniBand fabrics where subnet-manager failover is untested.

assessmentProcedure: Review controller architecture and placement against power and rack domains.
Review documented behaviour on control-plane loss.
Review or witness failover test.
Review backup/restore test.
Verify health monitoring.
controls.applicability: Applies to fabrics whose forwarding or configuration depends on a control function. Security of controllers is SEC-007.
failureModes: Subnet-manager split-brain
Standby controller unable to take over at scale
Controllers co-located on one PDU
Controller loss causing data-plane flush
controls.testingSafety: Controller failover tests risk fabric-wide disruption and require change-board authorisation, a rollback plan and workload owner consent.
controls.unknownRule: If data-plane behaviour on controller loss is undocumented and untested, record U8 at US4 against CG-08.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)
OpenConfig gNMI specification and OpenConfig data models

controls.title: Configuration Management
controls.objective: Ensure network operating system, firmware and configuration across switches, NICs, optics and controllers are held to an approved baseline, changed only through staged and verified rollout, and restorable.
controls.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall maintain a version-controlled source of truth for intended network configuration and an approved baseline of NOS, switch firmware, NIC firmware and driver, optics firmware and controller versions; shall detect configuration and version drift at a defined interval; and shall roll out changes in stages (canary, partial, full) with automated pre- and post-change checks and defined rollback. The network operations manager shall ensure that no single change can be applied simultaneously to both members of a redundant pair or to all planes of a fabric.
assessmentCriteria: A version-controlled intended configuration and an approved version baseline exist for each device class.
Drift detection runs at the defined interval and drift is remediated or approved.
Changes in the period followed staged rollout with pre- and post-checks and recorded rollback plans.
No change was applied simultaneously to both members of a redundant pair or all planes without approval.
Configuration backups exist for all devices and a restore from backup has been tested.
Emergency changes were retrospectively reviewed.
minimumEvidence: Source of truth repository and version baseline
Change records with stage plans, checks and rollback
Configuration backup inventory and restore test

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least six months (illustrative) of changes and drift reports.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor runs or reperforms a drift comparison on a sample of devices.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: uncontrolled NOS/firmware change on a gate-critical fabric defeats CG-14; CG-08 SUPPORTING.

assessmentProcedure: Review the source of truth and version baseline.
Reperform drift detection on a sample of devices.
Sample changes and verify staged rollout, checks and rollback plans.
Check for simultaneous change to redundant pairs or all planes.
Review backup coverage and the restore test.
Review emergency change retrospectives.
controls.applicability: Applies to all network devices, NICs, optics and fabric controllers in scope. Site-wide change governance is OPS-018.
failureModes: Firmware rollout common-mode failure across all planes (X08)
Configuration drift breaking congestion control
No backup for recovery
Recovery restoring corrupt configuration (X15)
controls.testingSafety: Drift comparison is read-only. Restore tests shall be on a spare or isolated device unless a maintenance window is authorised.
controls.unknownRule: If NIC or optics firmware versions are not in the baseline, record U5 and treat firmware common-mode exposure as unassessed.
informativeReferences: OpenConfig gNMI specification and OpenConfig data models
IETF RFC 7938 (Use of BGP for routing in large-scale data centres)

controls.title: Flow Telemetry
controls.objective: Ensure network telemetry (counters, streaming telemetry, flow sampling, congestion and buffer metrics) is collected with sufficient coverage, resolution and retention to detect degradation, attribute job slowdowns and support evidence for assurance.
controls.requirement: The fabric operations lead shall collect streaming or polled telemetry from all in-scope switches and NICs covering interface counters, error counters, PFC pause and ECN mark counts, buffer occupancy, and flow sampling, at a resolution sufficient to observe collective-scale events, and shall retain it for the evidence retention period. The fabric operations lead shall monitor telemetry pipeline health and alert on collection gaps.
assessmentCriteria: Telemetry coverage includes all in-scope switches and NICs with gaps listed.
Counters include errors, PFC pause, ECN marks, buffer occupancy and drops per traffic class.
Collection resolution meets the defined parameter for congestion visibility.
Retention meets the evidence retention requirement.
Pipeline gaps are alerted and recorded, and gap rates are within tolerance.

parameters.name: Telemetry collection interval for congestion counters

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 90 days (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor queries the telemetry store directly.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2: gaps reduce confidence of all NET OPERATION claims relying on telemetry.

assessmentProcedure: Compare telemetry source list to device inventory.
Query a sample of counters and check resolution.
Review gap reports and pipeline health.
Verify retention.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope fabrics and networks.
failureModes: Telemetry gaps hiding congestion events
Coarse sampling missing microbursts
Telemetry pipeline sharing failure domain with fabric
controls.testingSafety: Non-intrusive; increasing collection frequency on production switches shall be assessed for control-plane CPU impact first.
controls.unknownRule: Telemetry with unresolved gaps covering the assessed period is marked INCOMPLETE and cannot alone support OPERATION claims.
