controls.title: Time and Core Services
controls.objective: Ensure time (NTP/PTP), DNS, DHCP, IPAM and network AAA services that fabrics and clusters depend on are redundant, independent of the services they support, and resilient to failure and divergence.
controls.requirement: The network architecture owner shall deploy time sources (with at least two independent references such as GNSS and a holdover oscillator or a remote time service), DNS, DHCP, IPAM and network AAA as redundant services placed in separate fault domains, and shall document every circular dependency between these services and the systems they support. The network operations manager shall monitor time offset, stratum and source agreement, and service availability, and shall test failure of a time source and of a DNS/AAA instance at a defined interval.
assessmentCriteria: Each core service has redundancy across separate power and rack fault domains.
Time architecture has independent references with holdover and monitors offset and source divergence (X13).
Circular dependencies (for example DNS needed to reach the time server, or AAA hosted on the cluster it authenticates) are documented and broken or mitigated.
Tests of time-source loss and DNS/AAA instance loss in the period showed service continuity.
Clients are configured with multiple servers and sensible failover.
Time offset across a sample of devices stays within tolerance.

parameters.name: Time offset tolerance
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Workload- and log-correlation-dependent (illustrative 1 for NTP; sub-microsecond for PTP where required)

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within 12 months (illustrative); telemetry for 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor samples device time offset directly.
acceptableAlternatives: Analysed incidents of time-source or DNS loss in the period
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where a circular dependency could prevent cold start (X19).

assessmentProcedure: Review architecture and placement for each core service.
Review circular-dependency analysis against RES-013.
Sample time offsets and source agreement.
Review failure tests.
Sample client configurations.
controls.applicability: Applies to time, DNS, DHCP, IPAM and network AAA services relied upon by in-scope infrastructure.
failureModes: Time-source divergence corrupting log correlation and certificate validity (X13)
AAA hosted on the failed cluster
DNS loss blocking cluster bring-up
GNSS spoofing or loss without holdover
controls.testingSafety: Time-source failure tests shall be performed by withdrawing one source while monitoring offset; never step production clocks. DNS/AAA instance tests require change approval.
controls.unknownRule: If time source independence cannot be established, record U10 and treat time as a single common-mode dependency.
informativeReferences: IETF RFC 8915 (Network Time Security for NTP)

controls.title: 24x7 Coverage
controls.objective: Competent and authorised staff are present or available within response time, every hour of every day, in the numbers and disciplines needed to perform the time-critical tasks of the emergency procedures within the time-to-impact of the failures they address.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall define minimum staffing per shift and per discipline (electrical, mechanical/thermal, controls/BMS, NOC/IT infrastructure, security) derived from an emergency task analysis that lists the time-critical manual actions in each EOP (for example manual generator start or transfer, CDU failover, leak isolation, load shedding) and compares their completion time with the time-to-impact from MCF-DEP-003. The operations manager shall roster to that minimum, record every shift that falls below it and the compensating measures, and shall define on-call response times for specialists not on site.
assessmentCriteria: An emergency task analysis exists linking EOP time-critical actions to time-to-impact and required staff.
Minimum staffing per shift and discipline is derived from that analysis and approved.
Rosters and time-and-attendance records for the period show the minimum was met, or each shortfall is recorded with compensating measures.
On-call specialist response times are defined and met in call-outs during the period.
Fatigue limits (maximum shift length, consecutive shifts) are defined and adhered to.

parameters.name: Minimum on-site staff per shift
parameters.basis: Derived from emergency task analysis; there is no universal staffing ratio.

parameters.name: On-call specialist attendance time
parameters.basis: Illustrative; must be shorter than the time available after on-site staff stabilise the event.

parameters.name: Maximum shift length
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set with reference to HSE HSG256 guidance and local working-time law.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3

evidenceProfile.independence: Attendance records from access-control or time systems, not rosters alone.

reassessmentTriggers: Change in shift pattern or headcount
New system with manual emergency actions

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the emergency task analysis and staffing matrix.
Check the analysis against EOP time-critical steps and DEP-003 time-to-impact.
Reconcile a sample of shifts (including nights and holidays) from access-control records to the minimum.
Sample call-outs and measure response times.
Observe a shift change and staffing on site during an unannounced visit where permitted.
controls.applicability: Applies to all staffed facilities and NOCs supporting the Capability Instance; for provider-operated facilities assessed via MCF-DEP-018 evidence.
failureModes: Night shift below minimum when a generator fails to start
Specialist call-out takes longer than thermal ride-through
Fatigue-related operator error
Concurrent events exceed staff capacity
controls.testingSafety: Unannounced observation shall not interfere with operations; staffing shall not be reduced to test resilience.
controls.unknownRule: Missing attendance evidence for night and weekend shifts is U1, US3; escalate to US4 if a CG-05/06/10 criterion depends on manual action within ride-through.
informativeReferences: Uptime Institute Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability

controls.title: Role Clarity
controls.objective: For every Required Function, dependency and operating state, it is clear who operates, who maintains, who monitors, who may approve change, who responds to alarms and who holds emergency decision authority, including across facilities, IT/NOC, tenant and provider teams.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall maintain a responsibility and authority matrix for every Required Function and material dependency across NORMAL, MAINTENANCE, EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states, naming the role and current holder (and deputy) for operation, maintenance, monitoring, change approval, alarm response and emergency decisions (for example authority to transfer to generator, shed load, power-cap or drain a cluster, isolate a cooling loop, or invoke an EOP). The matrix shall be consistent with GOV-02 accountability and with provider shared-responsibility records (MCF-DEP-018).
assessmentCriteria: A matrix covers every Required Function and material dependency for the four states.
Each role has a named current holder and deputy.
Emergency decision authorities are explicit, including cross-team decisions (facilities ordering IT load reduction and vice versa).
The matrix is consistent with GOV-02 and DEP-018 records.
Interviewed role holders can state their responsibilities and authorities consistently with the matrix.
minimumEvidence: Named role holder list with deputies.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current.
evidenceProfile.independence: Interviews performed by the assessor with role holders selected by the assessor.
mandatoryItems: Responsibility and authority matrix with named holders
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-13 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-14 require gate-level evaluation.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the matrix and holder list.
Check coverage against Required Functions and dependencies.
Reconcile with GOV-02 and DEP-018.
Interview a sample of holders using scenarios (for example cooling loss at sustained AI load).
Record gaps and inconsistencies.
controls.applicability: Applies to all assessments.
failureModes: No one authorised to order cluster power-capping during cooling loss
Facilities and NOC each assume the other responds
Deputy undefined at night
controls.testingSafety: Interviews only.
controls.unknownRule: A Required Function with no identifiable emergency decision authority is US4 (CG-13 criterion).

controls.title: Shift Handover
controls.objective: Situational awareness is transferred completely at every shift change: plant and system state, active alarms, open permits and isolations, temporary configurations, deferred maintenance, degraded redundancy, in-progress work and expected events.
controls.requirement: The shift lead shall conduct and record a structured handover at each shift change using a defined template covering: current operating state per system and redundancy level, active and standing alarms, open permits to work and isolations, temporary configurations and overrides, work in progress and planned work, deferred maintenance with risk, provider or tenant events, and expected events (deliveries, tests, high-load periods). Outgoing and incoming leads shall both sign, and the incoming lead shall verify critical items at the BMS/EPMS/NOC consoles.
assessmentCriteria: A handover template covering the listed elements exists.
Handover records exist for the sampled shifts, signed by both leads.
Open permits and temporary configurations in handover records reconcile with the permit and temporary-configuration registers at that time.
Incoming leads verified critical items at consoles (record or observation).
minimumEvidence: Permit and temporary-configuration registers for the same times.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Sample of at least 20 handovers over 3 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reconciles handover content to registers.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-04, CG-14 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain template and sample records.
Reconcile with permit and temporary-configuration registers.
Observe a live handover.
Record omissions.
controls.applicability: Applies to all shift-based operations, including NOC.
failureModes: Open isolation not handed over and re-energised
Alarm inhibit forgotten
Degraded redundancy unknown to incoming shift
controls.testingSafety: Observation shall not distract operators during the handover.
controls.unknownRule: Missing handover records is U1, US3.

Uptime Institute Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability

controls.title: Competence and Authorisation
controls.objective: Only people assessed as competent, and formally authorised for the task and system, perform hazardous or consequential work, including HV/LV switching, work on battery systems, liquid-cooling and pressurised fluid systems, refrigerants, and control-system changes.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall maintain a competence framework defining required knowledge, skills and assessment for each task class, and an authorisation register recording each person's authorisations (for example authorised person and competent person for HV/LV systems, refrigerant handling certification where legally required, liquid-cooling and CDU work, BMS/EPMS engineering), their scope, expiry and assessor. The operations manager shall verify contractor competence and authorisation before work and shall ensure permits (MCF-OPS-007) are issued only to authorised persons.
assessmentCriteria: Competence framework covers all hazardous and consequential task classes.
Authorisation register records scope, expiry and assessor for each person.
No authorisation in the sample has expired.
Permits in the sample were issued to and received by persons authorised for that task.
Contractor competence was verified before work for sampled jobs.

parameters.name: Authorisation revalidation interval
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set by site safety rules and legal requirements.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months of permits.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor cross-references permits to register independently.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-13 require gate-level evaluation.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain framework and register.
Sample permits and reconcile issuers and receivers to authorisations.
Check expiry and scope.
Sample contractor jobs for pre-work verification.
Interview a sample of authorised persons on scope.
controls.applicability: Applies to all hazardous and consequential work in the boundary, by staff or contractors.
failureModes: Unauthorised person performs HV switching
Contractor without liquid-cooling competence breaks a pressurised loop
Expired authorisation

controls.unknownRule: Inability to verify authorisation of persons receiving hazardous-energy permits is US4 (CG-04 critical).

controls.title: Standard Operating Procedures
controls.objective: Routine, alarm-response and emergency operations on critical infrastructure are performed from controlled, technically reviewed and current procedures (SOPs, alarm response procedures, EOPs) that match the as-built systems and are available at the point of use.
controls.requirement: The operations manager shall maintain a controlled procedure set comprising SOPs for routine operation, alarm response procedures for critical alarms, and EOPs for each credible emergency scenario (including utility loss, generator failure to start, UPS failure, cooling loss at sustained AI load, CDU or secondary-loop failure, liquid leak, fire alarm and suppression interfaces, BMS/EPMS loss, and loss of NOC). Each procedure shall have an owner, technical reviewer, version and review date, shall be validated against the as-built system by walkthrough before issue, and shall be available at the point of use including when the BMS and IT systems are unavailable.
assessmentCriteria: The procedure set includes EOPs for each scenario in the RES-01 scenario list and alarm response procedures for each critical alarm.
Each procedure has owner, reviewer, version and review date within the interval.
A sample of procedures matches as-built equipment identifiers, valve and breaker designations and current setpoints.
Procedures are available in hard copy or offline form at points of use.
Walkthrough validation is recorded for procedures issued or revised in the period.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current.
evidenceProfile.independence: As-built cross-check by assessor during walk-down.
acceptableAlternatives: Electronic procedures on a system with independent power and offline availability.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-13, CG-14 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain register and map EOPs to scenarios.
Sample procedures and check control metadata.
Walk down sampled procedures against equipment.
Inspect point-of-use availability.
Observe an operator walk through an EOP.

controls.title: Method Statements
controls.objective: Non-routine work on critical infrastructure is executed from a task-specific method of procedure (MOP) that states the exact steps, hold points, isolation points, expected readings, redundancy exposure during the work, and back-out steps, so that maintenance and change do not cause outages.
controls.requirement: The maintenance manager shall require an approved MOP for every non-routine task on critical infrastructure, including: scope and affected assets; the operating state and redundancy level during each step (for example N during work on one of N+1 UPS modules); preconditions (for example job checkpoint or workload drain agreed with the platform owner, spare on hand, weather); step-by-step actions with hold points and expected indications; isolation and LOTO points; back-out steps; communications plan; and approvals by engineering, operations and change control (MCF-OPS-018). The MOP shall be executed as written with each step signed off and deviations stopped and escalated.
assessmentCriteria: Every non-routine task in the sample had an approved MOP before work.
MOPs state redundancy exposure per step and preconditions including workload coordination.
Executed MOPs show step sign-off; deviations were stopped and escalated.
MOPs were reviewed by engineering and operations and linked to an approved change.
Back-out steps are present for each irreversible step boundary.
minimumEvidence: Sample of approved and executed MOPs.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months of non-routine work.
evidenceProfile.independence: Sample selected by the assessor from work-order system, not from MOP register.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-14 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned. Supporting gates CG-04 require gate-level evaluation.

assessmentProcedure: Extract non-routine work orders for the period.
Reconcile each to an approved MOP and change.
Check content against required elements.
Review executed sign-off and deviations.
Observe a MOP execution where scheduled.
controls.applicability: Applies to non-routine work on critical infrastructure.
failureModes: Maintenance removes hidden shared dependency (scenario X04)
Wrong breaker opened
Work during training run without checkpoint
No back-out when step fails
controls.testingSafety: Observation of MOP execution only from a safe position as directed by the person in charge; observers shall not operate equipment.
controls.unknownRule: Non-routine work without a traceable MOP is a Finding; missing work-order data for the sample period is US4 (CG-14 critical).
informativeReferences: Uptime Institute Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability
ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety management systems)

controls.title: Permit to Work
controls.objective: Hazardous work is authorised, controlled, coordinated and handed back through a permit-to-work system so that hazardous energy, fluids, confined spaces, hot work and work at height are controlled and conflicting work is prevented.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall operate a permit-to-work system for hazardous work, including electrical (HV and LV), battery and DC systems, hot work, confined spaces (for example tanks, pits, trenches, plenums), work at height, pressurised and liquid-cooling systems, refrigerants and fire-suppression systems. Each permit shall identify the work, hazards, isolations (cross-referenced to LOTO), precautions, issuer and receiver (both authorised under MCF-OPS-004), validity period, and cross-references to other live permits in the same system. Permits shall be suspended at shift change unless re-validated, and closed only after hand-back confirms the system is safe to return to service.
assessmentCriteria: Permit types cover all hazardous work categories present on site.
Sampled permits are complete and issuer and receiver are authorised.
Conflicting permits in the same system were cross-referenced and coordinated.
Permits were suspended or re-validated at shift change.
Hand-back records confirm the system state before return to service.
Periodic audits of live permits at the worksite were performed and findings closed.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months of permits.
evidenceProfile.independence: Worksite verification by assessor or HSE function.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned.

Sample permits across types.
Check completeness, authorisation, cross-reference and hand-back.

Review audit findings.
controls.applicability: Applies to all hazardous work in the boundary including contractors and provider staff in owner spaces.
failureModes: Conflicting work on same electrical system
Confined-space entry without permit
Liquid loop opened while pressurised
System returned to service before hand-back
controls.testingSafety: Worksite inspection only under escort of the permit issuer; assessors shall not enter the permit boundary unless included on the permit.
controls.unknownRule: Missing permit records for hazardous work in the period is US4 (CG-04 critical).
informativeReferences: ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety management systems)

controls.title: Lockout and Tagout
controls.objective: All hazardous energy sources (electrical including back-feeds and DC/battery sources, stored energy in capacitors and UPS, mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic, pressurised coolant, thermal) are isolated, locked, tagged and proven dead or depressurised before work, and restored only under control.
controls.requirement: The facility operator shall define LOTO procedures for each equipment class that identify every energy source (including generator, UPS and battery back-feeds, BESS, capacitors, CDU pumps, pressurised secondary loops and facility water), the isolation points, locking devices, and the method to prove isolation (test-before-touch with a proven tester, pressure and temperature verification). Each worker shall apply a personal lock, group lockboxes shall be used for multi-worker jobs, and restoration shall follow a verified sequence. The facility operator shall audit LOTO practice at the profile interval.
assessmentCriteria: Equipment-specific LOTO procedures identify all energy sources including back-feeds and stored energy.
Sampled jobs have LOTO records with personal locks, proving tests and restoration sign-off.
Testers are proven before and after use (live-dead-live) and are in calibration.
LOTO audits were performed at the interval and findings closed.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Field audit by HSE or a person independent of the work team.
mandatoryItems: LOTO records for sampled hazardous jobs
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-04 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain procedures and verify energy-source identification against SLDs and P&IDs for a sample.
Sample LOTO records.
Check tester calibration.
Observe a LOTO application from a safe position.
Review audits.

Battery DC source not isolated

Isolation removed by another worker

controls.title: Maintenance Strategy
controls.objective: Each critical asset class has a maintenance strategy (preventive, predictive, condition-based or run-to-failure) justified by its failure modes and consequence, aligned with OEM requirements and recognised practice, and executable without exceeding the redundancy available in the MAINTENANCE state.
controls.requirement: The maintenance manager shall define and approve a maintenance strategy for each critical asset class (including MV/LV switchgear and protection, transformers, UPS and batteries, generators and fuel systems, busways and PDUs, chillers, CRAH/fan walls, CDUs and secondary loops, pumps, cooling towers or dry coolers, BMS/EPMS, fire detection and suppression, and IT infrastructure hardware) stating tasks, intervals, basis (OEM, recognised practice, reliability analysis), and the operating state and redundancy level during each task. The capability owner shall confirm that each maintenance configuration leaves capacity sufficient for the declared load, or that maintenance windows are coordinated with workload reduction.
assessmentCriteria: A maintenance strategy exists per critical asset class with stated basis.
Intervals are consistent with OEM requirements or deviations are justified.
Each task states the redundancy level during the task and the capacity check for declared load.
Run-to-failure decisions are limited to items whose failure is tolerable and are approved.
The strategy is approved by a competent engineer.

controls.title: Condition Monitoring
controls.objective: Deterioration of critical assets is detected before functional failure through defined condition-monitoring techniques with thresholds and actions.
controls.requirement: The maintenance manager shall operate condition monitoring for critical assets using techniques appropriate to their failure modes, for example infrared thermography of electrical connections, partial discharge monitoring on MV equipment, dissolved gas and oil analysis on transformers, battery impedance or conductance and temperature monitoring, vibration analysis on pumps, fans and chillers, coolant quality monitoring (conductivity, pH, inhibitor and biocide levels, particulates) on liquid-cooling loops, and filter differential pressure. Each technique shall have defined thresholds and response actions, and exceedances shall generate work orders.
assessmentCriteria: Techniques are defined per critical asset class aligned to failure modes.
Measurements were taken at the defined frequency in the period.
Thresholds and actions are defined; exceedances generated work orders that were completed.

controls.title: Calibration
controls.objective: Instruments whose readings drive control, protection, alarming, billing or assurance decisions (temperature, pressure, flow, leak, power and energy meters, CTs/VTs, protection relays, gas detectors, and the test instruments used by technicians) are calibrated to traceable standards at defined intervals, so that control loops and evidence are trustworthy.

controls.title: Alarm Rationalisation
controls.objective: Alarms from BMS, EPMS, CDU, fire, leak detection, security and NOC systems are rationalised so that every alarm is meaningful, prioritised by consequence and time to respond, has a defined response, and the alarm load on operators remains manageable in normal and upset conditions.
controls.requirement: The control-system owner shall maintain an alarm philosophy and master alarm database for in-scope monitoring systems in which each alarm has a documented cause, consequence, priority (derived from consequence and time-to-impact per MCF-DEP-003), setpoint basis, and response procedure. assessmentCriteria: An approved alarm philosophy exists covering priority definitions and performance targets.

controls.objective: Ensure every in-scope Capability Instance has a defined minimum service outcome and impact tolerance (maximum tolerable disruption, minimum capacity, maximum lost work, maximum data loss) that resilience design, testing and recovery claims can be measured against.

controls.title: Graceful Degradation
controls.objective: Ensure that partial loss of power, cooling, compute, storage or network capacity results in planned, controlled reduction of AI service (load shedding, job preemption, throttling, reduced replicas) rather than uncontrolled failure.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall define graceful-degradation modes for each Capability Instance, stating the trigger condition (for example loss of one cooling string, utility loss on UPS autonomy, loss of a fabric plane), the action (power capping, job preemption by priority, checkpoint-and-drain, inference replica reduction, admission control), the owner of the decision and the expected residual capacity. The platform operations lead shall implement the actions as tested automation or procedures and shall demonstrate by test or analysed event that each mode achieves the expected residual capacity within the time available before the triggering constraint is exceeded.
assessmentCriteria: Degradation modes are defined per Capability Instance with trigger, action, decision owner and residual capacity.

Tests or events in the period demonstrated achieved residual capacity and time-to-act.
