Check for adverse transients created by the action.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Capability Instance whose infrastructure can lose partial capacity. Not applicable where the declared outcome is all-or-nothing and that is explicitly accepted.
failureModes: Load not shed before UPS exhaustion
All jobs killed instead of priority preemption
Power cap causing simultaneous load step
Thermal ride-through exceeded
controls.testingSafety: Degradation tests that cap power or preempt jobs affect workloads and require capability owner authorisation; tests that remove power or cooling capacity require facility authorisation under OPS-007 and engineering safety review.
controls.unknownRule: If time-to-act has not been measured, treat the mode as unavailable (U1) for scenarios where available time is shorter than the estimated time-to-act.

controls.title: Resilience Scenarios
controls.objective: Ensure a maintained library of credible single, compound and common-mode scenarios is used to design and test resilience, including the AIDCF-004 cross-domain scenarios relevant to the site.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain a scenario library for each site and Capability Instance that includes, at minimum, the applicable AIDCF-004 cross-domain scenarios (X01 to X20), site-specific hazards, and maintenance-induced and recovery-induced scenarios; each scenario shall have an initiating event, initial operating state, propagation path, safeguards, residual capability and recovery path. The resilience owner shall prioritise scenarios using the AIDCF-004 prioritisation criteria and shall review the library annually and after major incidents.
assessmentCriteria: A scenario library exists with the minimum record fields from AIDCF-004.
Applicable cross-domain scenarios X01–X20 are included or excluded with rationale.
Maintenance-induced, recovery-induced and compound scenarios are represented.
Scenarios are prioritised and linked to tests (RES-017/RES-018) and exercises (RES-019).
The library was reviewed in the last 12 months and after major incidents.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C2 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current version, reviewed within 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Reviewed by a cross-domain panel including facilities, network, compute, storage and security.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: missing scenarios limit coverage of CG-09/CG-10 evidence; US4 if a prioritised scenario is excluded without rationale.

assessmentProcedure: Review library completeness against AIDCF-004 fields.
Check applicability rationale for each X-scenario.
Confirm maintenance- and recovery-induced scenarios exist.
Trace prioritised scenarios to tests and exercises.
Confirm review history.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope site and Capability Instance; scenario libraries may be shared across sites of identical design if site-specific hazards are added.
failureModes: Compound scenario never considered
Recovery-induced failure not anticipated
Library not updated after incident
controls.testingSafety: Scenario development is analytical. Where scenario parameters are validated against live telemetry, collection shall be read-only.
controls.unknownRule: Scenarios whose propagation path crosses an unanalysed dependency are recorded with U10 and flagged for DEP analysis.

controls.title: Resilience Ownership
controls.objective: Ensure resilience of each Capability Instance has a single accountable owner with authority across facility, IT and provider boundaries and that resilience responsibilities are explicit for every contributing domain.
controls.requirement: The executive sponsor shall appoint an accountable resilience owner for each site or Capability Instance with authority to set resilience requirements, approve accepted limitations and direct cross-domain testing. The resilience owner shall maintain a resilience responsibility matrix naming the responsible owner for power, cooling, network, compute, storage, control-plane and provider elements of each resilience and recovery capability, including colocation and cloud provider responsibilities.
assessmentCriteria: An accountable resilience owner is appointed in writing with defined authority.
A resilience responsibility matrix covers all contributing domains and providers.
Provider responsibilities are reflected in contracts or service descriptions.
Accepted resilience limitations are approved by the resilience owner or higher authority.
Owners named in the matrix confirm awareness (sampled).
minimumEvidence: Provider contract or service description extracts

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C2 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current version.
evidenceProfile.independence: Matrix confirmed by interviews with a sample of named owners.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 against CG-13 where a recovery-critical element has no owner.

assessmentProcedure: Review appointment and authority.
Review matrix coverage against domains and providers.
Check provider contract alignment.
Interview a sample of owners.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope sites and Capability Instances.
failureModes: Colocation responsibility gap (X14)
No one owns cross-domain recovery
Limitations accepted by unauthorised staff
controls.testingSafety: Not applicable (governance control).
controls.unknownRule: Any recovery-critical element with no named owner is recorded as a US4 UNKNOWN for CG-13.

controls.title: Fault-Domain Definition
controls.objective: Ensure the site-level fault-domain model (power, cooling, fire, water, network, compute, storage and control-plane domains) is defined and reconciled to the as-built infrastructure, so that redundancy and independence claims are traceable.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain a site fault-domain model that defines each fault domain (for example electrical distribution paths, UPS systems, cooling strings and CDU groups, fire compartments, water zones, network planes, compute pods, storage failure domains, control-plane clusters) with its members, and records which domains overlap. The resilience owner shall reconcile the model to as-built evidence (single-line diagrams, P&IDs, rack power and cooling mapping, fabric topology, scheduler and storage placement) at commissioning and after material change, and shall flag every redundancy claim whose members share a fault domain.
assessmentCriteria: A fault-domain model exists covering all infrastructure classes.
Domain membership is reconciled to as-built evidence for each class.
Overlaps between domains (for example a network plane inside a single power path) are recorded.
Every redundancy claim is checked for members sharing a fault domain, and such cases are dispositioned.
The model was updated after each material change in the period.
minimumEvidence: As-built references used in reconciliation (SLD, P&ID, rack maps, topology, placement)

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Reconciliation within the age parameter.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciled by a party other than the model author, using primary as-built sources.
acceptableAlternatives: Graph-based dependency model meeting AIDCF-014 with automated reconciliation
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-09 cannot PASS while the site fault-domain model is unreconciled for gate-critical outcomes.
reassessmentTriggers: Incident affecting more than one domain

assessmentProcedure: Review model coverage across infrastructure classes.
Reconcile a sample of domains to primary as-built sources.
Examine overlaps and shared-domain register.
Test a sample of redundancy claims for shared membership.
Confirm update after recent changes.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope site. Domain-specific fault-domain controls (NET-004, CMP-008) feed this model.
failureModes: Redundant spines on one UPS path
Dual-fed racks on PDUs from one switchboard
Storage replicas in one fire compartment
Control-plane quorum in one rack
controls.testingSafety: Reconciliation is non-intrusive; physical verification of power feeds shall use visual inspection or EPMS data only, never live disconnection.
controls.unknownRule: Domain membership that cannot be reconciled is recorded as U1 or U3 and the affected redundancy claims are treated as unproven.
informativeReferences: ANSI/TIA-942 (Telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centres)
EN 50600 series / ISO/IEC 22237 series (Data centre facilities and infrastructures)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Containment Boundaries
controls.objective: Ensure physical, electrical, thermal, network and logical boundaries that are intended to stop propagation are implemented as designed, with their isolating devices identified and maintained.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall identify each containment boundary relied upon (for example fire compartment, electrical protection discrimination point, cooling-loop isolation valves, fabric partition, security zone, scheduler placement constraint, storage failure domain) together with the isolating device or mechanism and its required response. The domain owners shall confirm that each mechanism is installed, configured and maintained as designed and shall record mechanisms in bypass or override as temporary configurations under OPS-019.
assessmentCriteria: A containment-boundary register lists boundaries, isolating mechanisms and intended response.
Mechanisms are installed and configured as designed (sampled inspection or configuration extract).
Maintenance status of isolating devices is current.
Mechanisms in bypass or override are recorded as temporary configurations with expiry.
Scheduler and storage placement constraints that enforce logical containment are configured and verified.
minimumEvidence: Inspection or configuration evidence per mechanism

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current configuration; maintenance within manufacturer interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Inspection by domain specialists independent of the register author.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-09 where the boundary protects a gate-critical outcome.

assessmentProcedure: Review the register for completeness against the scenario library.
Sample mechanisms and verify installation and configuration.
Check maintenance records.
Review bypass/override records.
Verify logical placement constraints in scheduler and storage.
controls.applicability: Applies to every containment boundary relied upon in fault-domain or blast-radius claims.
failureModes: Isolation valve seized
Breaker discrimination lost after setting change
Fire damper not closing
Placement constraint removed from scheduler
controls.testingSafety: Operating isolating devices is not part of this control; functional tests belong to RES-008 and require authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Boundaries whose mechanism status is unknown are treated as absent in blast-radius analysis.
informativeReferences: EN 50600 series / ISO/IEC 22237 series (Data centre facilities and infrastructures)

controls.title: Blast Radius
controls.objective: Ensure the maximum consequence of each credible failure is quantified in capability terms (accelerators, jobs, tenants, inference capacity, data) and compared with the impact tolerance.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall perform and maintain a blast-radius analysis for each prioritised scenario and each fault domain, stating the affected assets, the affected Capability Instances, the capability consequence in outcome units and comparison with impact tolerance, including common-cause and common-mode failures (for example firmware rollout, shared controller, shared identity provider). The resilience owner shall record every blast radius exceeding tolerance as a Finding with a treatment plan or approved limitation.
assessmentCriteria: Blast-radius analysis covers every prioritised scenario and fault domain.
Consequences are stated in outcome units and compared with impact tolerance.
Common-cause and common-mode cases (software, firmware, configuration, identity, automation) are included.
Analysis is reconciled to the current fault-domain model (RES-005).
Exceedances have treatment plans or approved limitations.

parameters.name: Maximum blast radius per single credible failure

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; updated after material change.
evidenceProfile.independence: Reviewed by a cross-domain panel independent of the analyst.
acceptableAlternatives: Graph-query outputs from a conformant AIDCF-014 model with human review
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-09 cannot PASS while blast radius for gate-critical scenarios is unquantified.

assessmentProcedure: Review coverage against scenarios and domains.
Recompute blast radius for a sample of scenarios from the fault-domain model.
Check common-mode inclusion.
Compare with tolerances and review exceedances.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope Capability Instances, including multi-tenant platforms where blast radius is expressed per tenant.
failureModes: Firmware update bricking all nodes
Shared identity provider outage blocking all operations
Single cooling loop serving whole cluster
Concentration of tenant capacity in one hall
controls.testingSafety: Analytical.
controls.unknownRule: If a scenario's blast radius depends on an unresolved dependency, record U10 and use the worst credible case.

controls.title: Isolation Validation
controls.objective: Ensure containment boundaries actually stop propagation when demanded, verified by representative tests, analysed incidents or safe simulations.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain an isolation validation plan that assigns a validation method from the AIDCF-004 safe validation hierarchy (V0–V7) to each containment boundary, with the highest safe level for gate-critical boundaries, and shall execute the plan over a defined cycle. The domain owners shall record results, including failed or partial isolation, and shall retest after remediation.
assessmentCriteria: Each boundary has an assigned validation method and level.
Gate-critical boundaries are validated at V5 (component functional test) or above, or the shortfall is justified and recorded.
Validation in the cycle demonstrated isolation within the expected response.
Failed or partial isolation results led to remediation and retest.
Network and logical isolation (fabric partitions, security zones, scheduler placement) are included alongside physical boundaries.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Within the validation cycle.
evidenceProfile.independence: Tests witnessed by an independent party (E5) for gate-critical boundaries.
acceptableAlternatives: Analysed real incident demonstrating isolation, with event evidence
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: untested gate-critical boundaries leave CG-09 UNKNOWN.

assessmentProcedure: Review the plan and assigned levels.
Sample gate-critical boundaries and review results.
Check failed/partial results for remediation and retest.
Confirm logical boundaries are included.
controls.applicability: Applies to all containment boundaries in the RES-006 register.
failureModes: Boundary passes design review but fails on demand
Fire damper fails to close
Fabric partition leaks traffic
Protection fails to discriminate
controls.testingSafety: Isolation tests involving electrical protection, fire systems, fluid isolation or production fabrics are hazardous or disruptive; they require written authorisation from the facility owner and the relevant engineering authority, permit-to-work, method statements, and a safety and rollback plan. Tests at V6/V7 require additional executive authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Boundaries validated only at V0–V2 are recorded with U8 for effectiveness claims.
informativeReferences: EN 50600 series / ISO/IEC 22237 series (Data centre facilities and infrastructures)

controls.title: Continuity Strategy
controls.objective: Ensure an approved continuity strategy states how each Capability Instance's minimum outcome will be sustained or resumed across site loss, provider loss and major infrastructure loss.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain an approved continuity strategy for each Capability Instance that selects and justifies the continuity approach (for example in-site redundancy, active-active multi-site inference, warm standby training capacity, checkpoint replication to an alternate site, contracted cloud burst, or accepted suspension), states the dependencies of the chosen approach, and is consistent with the impact tolerances in RES-001.
assessmentCriteria: An approved strategy exists per Capability Instance with the selected approach and justification.
The strategy meets or explicitly accepts shortfall against impact tolerances.
Dependencies of the strategy (alternate site, provider, data replication, staff) are listed.
The strategy addresses site loss, major provider loss and loss of the AI control plane.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C2 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current approved version, reviewed within 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Approved by the capability owner and reviewed by the resilience owner.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where no strategy exists for a gate-critical outcome.

assessmentProcedure: Review strategy and approval.
Compare with tolerances.
Review dependencies and coverage of site, provider and control-plane loss.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope Capability Instances, including those whose approved strategy is accepted suspension (the acceptance itself is assessed).
failureModes: No plan for site loss
Strategy relies on unavailable alternate capacity
Control-plane loss not considered
controls.testingSafety: Strategy review is analytical; feasibility of the selected approach is tested under RES-010 and RES-018 with their own authorisation requirements.
controls.unknownRule: Strategies that rely on an unverified dependency are recorded with U10.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (Contingency planning guide for federal information systems)

controls.title: Alternative Capacity
controls.objective: Ensure alternate compute, storage and network capacity relied upon by the continuity strategy exists, is compatible and can be brought into service within tolerance.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall identify the alternate capacity relied upon (alternate cluster, partitioned reserve, alternate site, cloud contract) with its size, compatibility (accelerator generation, software stack, fabric, storage access) and activation time, and shall secure it by reservation or contract. The platform operations lead shall demonstrate by test at a defined interval that a representative workload can be relocated to alternate capacity and resumed from checkpoint or served within the activation time.
assessmentCriteria: Alternate capacity is identified with size, compatibility and activation time.
Capacity is reserved or contracted, with terms that hold during regional demand surges.
Software stack, images and data access on alternate capacity are kept compatible.
A relocation test in the interval demonstrated resumption within activation time.
Data transfer or replication capacity for relocation is sufficient (checkpoint size over link capacity).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within the interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Test witnessed by the resilience owner's function.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where the continuity strategy depends solely on alternate capacity.

assessmentProcedure: Review register and contract terms.
Check compatibility of stack, images and data access.
Review or witness a relocation test.
Recompute data transfer time for relocation.
controls.applicability: Applies where the continuity strategy relies on alternate capacity. Not applicable where accepted suspension is the approved strategy.
failureModes: Alternate cloud capacity unavailable during regional surge
Incompatible accelerator generation
Checkpoint transfer exceeds tolerance
Images outdated on standby cluster
controls.testingSafety: Relocation tests consume alternate capacity and may incur cost; production workloads shall not be moved without capability owner authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Alternate capacity with no test is recorded as U1 for activation-time claims.

controls.title: Site and Provider Continuity
controls.objective: Ensure the continuity arrangements of sites, colocation operators, utilities, carriers and critical service providers are known, evidenced and compatible with the Capability Instance's tolerances.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall obtain, for each site operator and critical provider (colocation, utility, carrier, cloud, OEM support), evidence of their continuity arrangements relevant to the outcome (for example operator emergency response, fuel contracts, carrier restoration commitments, provider recovery objectives), and shall reconcile provider objectives with the Capability Instance's tolerances. The resilience owner shall record every mismatch as a dependency limitation.
assessmentCriteria: Each critical site operator and provider has continuity evidence on file.
Provider recovery objectives are compared with tolerances.
Mismatches are recorded as limitations or treated.
Evidence rights and incident notification are contractually defined (SUP-006, SUP-007).
Provider evidence is current within the evidence-age parameter.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Within evidence age.
evidenceProfile.independence: Third-party evidence (E5) where available; otherwise contractual attestation corroborated by inquiry.
acceptableAlternatives: Independent audit reports covering continuity scope
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-03 where a sole provider's continuity is unknown.

assessmentProcedure: List critical providers.
Review continuity evidence and currency.
Reconcile objectives with tolerances.
Review limitations and contractual rights.
controls.applicability: Applies to all critical providers and site operators.
failureModes: Carrier restoration time beyond tolerance
Colocation fuel contract shared with neighbours
OEM support unavailable in crisis (X18)
controls.testingSafety: Provider evidence is reviewed as documents; any joint failover exercise with a provider requires a jointly approved test plan and provider authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Providers refusing evidence are recorded with U2 and treated as single points of failure in strategy analysis.

controls.title: Crisis Priorities
controls.objective: Ensure pre-agreed restoration and allocation priorities exist for when capacity is scarce, so that crisis decisions on which workloads, tenants and services are protected or restored first are not improvised.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall approve a priority scheme stating, for scarce power, cooling, compute and network capacity during DEGRADED, EMERGENCY and RECOVERY states, which workloads, tenants and services are protected, preempted and restored first, consistent with contractual commitments and life-safety precedence. The platform operations lead shall implement the scheme in scheduler priority classes and runbooks.
assessmentCriteria: An approved priority scheme exists covering protection, preemption and restoration order.
The scheme is consistent with contractual commitments and life-safety precedence.
Scheduler priority classes and runbooks implement the scheme.
Crisis command (RES-021) uses the scheme in exercises.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C2 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current approved version.
evidenceProfile.independence: Approval by the capability owner, review by commercial/contract owner.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: absent priorities condition recovery decisions.

assessmentProcedure: Review scheme and approval.
Check consistency with commitments.
Reconcile to scheduler configuration.
Review exercise use.
controls.applicability: Applies to all shared or multi-workload Capability Instances.
failureModes: Low-priority jobs restored before critical inference
Contractual breach during shedding
Improvised priorities under pressure
controls.testingSafety: Priority review is document-based; testing preemption against live workloads is governed by RES-002 and requires capability owner authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: If the scheme is not reflected in scheduler configuration, record a Finding; claims of priority-based shedding are limited to DESIGN.
informativeReferences: ISO 22320 (Emergency management: guidelines for incident management)

controls.title: Recovery Dependencies
controls.objective: Ensure every prerequisite for recovering each Capability Instance (power, cooling, network, time, identity, DNS, storage metadata, controllers, images, licences, people and providers) is identified, including circular and cold-start dependencies.
controls.requirement: The recovery manager shall maintain a recovery dependency map for each Capability Instance, derived from DEP-004, listing every prerequisite system, service, credential, artefact, person and provider required to restore the outcome from a cold or failed state, and shall identify circular dependencies (for example identity provider hosted on the cluster it unlocks, DNS required to reach the time source, BMC firmware repository on the failed storage) and the means by which each is broken. The recovery manager shall verify the map against the last integrated recovery test.
assessmentCriteria: A recovery dependency map exists per Capability Instance covering infrastructure, services, credentials, artefacts, people and providers.
Circular and cold-start dependencies are identified with a documented break (for example offline copy, local fallback, out-of-band path).
Each dependency has an owner and a recovery path.
The map was verified against the most recent integrated recovery test and updated with discovered dependencies.
Offline artefacts (images, configuration backups, credentials) are stored outside the failure domain they recover.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Verified against a test within 24 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Verified by a party independent of the map author, preferably through test observation.
acceptableAlternatives: Graph-based dependency model with automated cycle detection and human review
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS while circular recovery dependencies are unanalysed.

assessmentProcedure: Review the recovery dependency map for completeness against DEP-004.
Run or review cycle detection for circular dependencies.
Verify breaks for each cycle (offline copies, local auth, OOB).
Check offline artefact locations against fault domains.
Compare the map with the last integrated test discrepancies.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Capability Instance.
failureModes: Identity provider on the failed cluster (X19)
Images only on failed storage
Licence server unreachable
Key personnel unavailable
controls.testingSafety: Analytical; verification draws on RES-018 tests.
controls.unknownRule: Any recovery prerequisite whose location or availability in a failure state is unknown is recorded as U10 at US4 against CG-10.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (Contingency planning guide for federal information systems)

controls.title: Recovery Sequencing
controls.objective: Ensure a tested, ordered restoration sequence exists from total or partial loss through power, cooling, network, storage, compute and control plane to validated service, with hold points and safety checks between stages.
controls.requirement: The recovery manager shall maintain a black-start and restoration sequence for each site and Capability Instance that orders restoration through power (utility or generation, distribution, UPS), cooling (heat rejection, facility water, CDUs and liquid loops before IT load), out-of-band and core network, time and identity services, storage (metadata and quorum before data services), compute (BMC, firmware validation, health checks, burn-in) and AI control plane (cluster manager, scheduler), with entry criteria, hold points, load-step limits and safety checks at each stage. The recovery manager shall demonstrate the sequence by integrated test or exercise at a defined interval and shall record achieved stage durations against the recovery time objective.
assessmentCriteria: A restoration sequence exists covering power, cooling, network, storage, compute and control plane with entry criteria and hold points.
Cooling capacity is confirmed before IT load is restored at each step, and load-step limits respect generator and UPS capability.
The sequence references POW-024, THM-024, STO-019, CMP-023 and NET restoration runbooks consistently.
An integrated test or exercise in the interval executed the sequence (fully or in representative segments) and recorded stage durations.
Total achieved duration is within the recovery time objective, or the shortfall is a Finding.
Validation at the end of the sequence confirms Service Outcome restoration, not only system availability.

parameters.name: Maximum IT load step during restoration

minimumEvidence: Integrated test or exercise records with stage timings

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Integrated test within the interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Witnessed by an independent party (E5) for gate-critical outcomes.
mandatoryItems: Integrated test record with stage timings
acceptableAlternatives: Segmented tests (for example power-to-cooling at site level; network-to-control-plane at cluster level) with interface hand-offs explicitly tested, plus a full tabletop walk-through
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS while the restoration sequence is untested end-to-end or by segments with tested hand-offs.

assessmentProcedure: Review the sequence for order, entry criteria, hold points and safety checks.
Cross-check against domain restoration runbooks for consistency.
Check load-step and cooling-before-load constraints.
Review or observe an integrated test and extract stage durations.
Compare total duration with RTO.
Confirm service-outcome validation at completion.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope site and Capability Instance. Single-system recovery runbooks remain under their domain controls.
failureModes: IT load restored before cooling, causing thermal trip
Simultaneous node power-on exceeding generator load-step
Control plane restored before identity and time
Storage data services started before metadata quorum
controls.testingSafety: Black-start tests involve hazardous energy and site-wide disruption and require written authorisation from the facility owner, the electrical and mechanical engineering authorities and the capability owner, permit-to-work, a safety case and a rollback plan. Segmented and simulation-based tests are preferred where full tests are not authorised.
controls.unknownRule: Stages never executed in test are recorded with U5 and the sequence is assessed only to DESIGN for those stages.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (Contingency planning guide for federal information systems)
AIDCF-013 (AI Data Centre Assurance Reference Architecture)

controls.title: Configuration Restoration
controls.objective: Ensure the configuration of infrastructure and control-plane systems can be restored from a known-good, integrity-verified baseline, avoiding reintroduction of corrupt or malicious configuration.
controls.requirement: The recovery manager shall ensure that configuration backups of network devices, controllers, BMS/EPMS, CDU controllers, storage controllers, cluster managers and identity systems are taken at a defined interval, are integrity-protected (hashed or signed), are stored outside the failure and compromise domain they protect, and are tagged with the approved baseline they correspond to. The recovery manager shall test restoration of a sample of each system class at a defined interval, including verification that the restored configuration matches the approved baseline and not a compromised or drifted state.
assessmentCriteria: Backups exist for every system class with defined interval.
Backups are integrity-protected and stored outside the protected failure/compromise domain.
Backups are tagged to an approved baseline and integrity is verified before restore.
Restore tests per system class in the interval succeeded and were verified against baseline.
A procedure exists for selecting a pre-compromise baseline when compromise is suspected (X15).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Restore tests within interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Restore test observed by a party independent of the system administrators.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where BMS/EPMS or fabric controller configuration has no tested restore.

assessmentProcedure: Review backup inventory coverage.
Verify integrity protection and storage location.
Review or reperform a restore and compare to baseline.
Review pre-compromise baseline procedure.
controls.applicability: Applies to all configuration-bearing infrastructure and control-plane systems in scope.
failureModes: Restoring compromised configuration (X15)
Backups on the same failed storage
BMS controller backup never restored
Restored config drifted from baseline
controls.testingSafety: Restores to OT controllers (BMS, EPMS, CDU, PLC) shall be performed only on test benches or spare controllers unless a maintenance window is authorised by the facility owner with plant in a safe state.
controls.unknownRule: Systems with backups but no restore test are recorded as U1 for restore claims.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (Contingency planning guide for federal information systems)
ISA/IEC 62443-2-1 (Security programme requirements for IACS asset owners)

controls.title: Data and Checkpoint Recovery
controls.objective: Ensure training state (checkpoints, optimiser state, data-loader position), model artefacts and essential datasets can be recovered within the recovery point and time objectives and that restarted jobs resume correctly.
controls.requirement: The capability owner shall set a checkpoint policy per training Capability Instance stating checkpoint interval (justified against failure rate, checkpoint cost and maximum lost work, for example using a Young/Daly-style optimisation), checkpoint retention, and the number and placement of durable copies outside the training cluster's failure domain. The platform operations lead shall verify checkpoint integrity at write and before restore, and shall test at a defined interval that a representative job can be restarted from checkpoint (including on a different set of nodes) and reaches equivalent training state within RTO and lost-work tolerance.
assessmentCriteria: Checkpoint interval, retention and copy placement are defined and justified against lost-work tolerance.
Durable copies are stored outside the training cluster's power, storage and compromise domain.
Checkpoint integrity is verified at write and before restore.
Restart tests in the interval achieved resumption within RTO and lost-work tolerance, including on alternate nodes.
Model artefacts and essential datasets have recovery copies meeting RPO.
Inference model artefacts can be redeployed within the inference RTO.

parameters.name: Checkpoint interval
parameters.illustrativeDefault: Optimised from failure rate and checkpoint cost (illustrative 60)

parameters.name: Durable checkpoint copies outside cluster failure domain

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Restart test within 6 months (illustrative); integrity logs for 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Restart test witnessed independently of the training team.
acceptableAlternatives: Production restart events with recorded resumption times and training-state checks
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS while checkpoint restart is untested for gate-critical training outcomes.

assessmentProcedure: Review the checkpoint policy and interval justification.
Verify copy placement against fault domains.
Sample integrity logs.
Review or witness a restart test including alternate nodes.
Review artefact and dataset recovery copies.
controls.applicability: Applies to training and fine-tuning Capability Instances, and to inference for model artefact recovery.
failureModes: Corrupt checkpoint discovered only at restore
All checkpoints on the failed storage
Restart fails on different topology
Lost-work exceeds tolerance due to long interval
controls.testingSafety: Restart tests consume capacity and shall be scheduled with the capability owner; do not delete or overwrite production checkpoints during tests.
controls.unknownRule: Checkpoints without integrity verification are recorded as U7 and do not support recovery claims.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (Contingency planning guide for federal information systems)

controls.title: Component Tests
controls.objective: Ensure resilience-relevant components (generators, UPS, transfer switches, CDU pumps, valves, fabric failover, controller failover, storage failover) are functionally tested on a defined programme and results tracked.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain a component test programme listing each resilience-relevant component class, the test method, frequency and acceptance criteria, coordinated with domain maintenance programmes. Domain owners shall execute tests per programme, record results, and raise and close defects; the resilience owner shall review programme adherence quarterly.
assessmentCriteria: A component test programme exists with class, method, frequency and acceptance criteria.
Tests were executed per schedule in the period (adherence rate meets target).
Failed tests raised defects that were closed or have approved deferral.
Quarterly adherence reviews occurred.

parameters.name: Programme adherence target
parameters.unit: % of scheduled tests completed on time

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor samples from asset registers rather than from completed-test lists.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: programme gaps reduce support for CG-05/06/08/10 claims.

assessmentProcedure: Review programme coverage.
Sample components from asset registers and trace tests.
Review defects and closure.
Review adherence reviews.
controls.applicability: Applies to all resilience-relevant components across domains.
failureModes: Latent failure of untested component (generator no-start)
Test failures not remediated
Programme drift
controls.testingSafety: Component tests involving hazardous energy require permit-to-work and authorised persons under OPS-007; disruptive IT failover tests require change approval.
controls.unknownRule: Components with no test record in the period are recorded as U1 for operational claims.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-84 (Guide to test, training and exercise programs for IT plans and capabilities)

controls.title: Integrated Scenario Tests
controls.objective: Ensure prioritised cross-domain scenarios are exercised as integrated tests across power, cooling, network, compute, storage and control plane, demonstrating that the Capability Instance stays within or recovers within tolerance.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall plan and execute integrated scenario tests for prioritised scenarios from RES-003 (for example utility loss with generator start and UPS transfer under AI load, cooling string loss at sustained load, fabric plane loss during checkpoint, control-plane loss), measuring capability-level outcomes (job survival, lost work, inference availability, restoration time) as well as system behaviour. The resilience owner shall define test objectives, safety case, abort criteria and success criteria tied to impact tolerances before each test and shall record results and defects.
assessmentCriteria: Integrated tests cover the highest-priority scenarios on a defined cycle.
Each test has objectives, safety case, abort criteria and success criteria tied to tolerances.
Tests measure capability-level outcomes, not only component behaviour.
Results demonstrated outcomes within tolerance, or Findings were raised.
Defects discovered are tracked to closure and retest (RES-020).
Tests are conducted at representative load or the load difference is analysed.

parameters.name: Representative load during test
parameters.basis: Load banks or real workload; site-specific.

minimumEvidence: Integrated test plans with safety cases

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Within the cycle for each prioritised scenario.
evidenceProfile.independence: Witnessed by an independent party (E5).
acceptableAlternatives: Analysed real events with equivalent capability-level measurements
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-10 cannot PASS for an outcome whose prioritised scenarios have never been integrated-tested or analysed from real events.

assessmentProcedure: Review test plans, safety cases and success criteria.
Observe or review test execution records.
Verify capability-level measurements.
Assess load representativeness.
Review defect closure and retest.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope Capability Instance with gate-critical outcomes.
failureModes: Cross-domain interaction not revealed by component tests
Generator stable on load bank but unstable on AI load steps
Jobs fail on UPS transfer despite systems passing
Hidden shared dependency (X04)
controls.testingSafety: Integrated tests are disruptive and may be hazardous; they require written authorisation from the facility owner, engineering authorities and capability owner, a safety case, permit-to-work for energised work, a defined abort authority, and communication to affected tenants. Live capability exercises (AIDCF-004 V7) require executive authorisation.
controls.unknownRule: Scenarios tested only at reduced load without representativeness analysis are recorded with U5.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-84 (Guide to test, training and exercise programs for IT plans and capabilities)

controls.title: Tabletop Exercises
controls.objective: Ensure decision-makers, operators and providers rehearse response to scenarios that cannot safely be tested live, including cyber-physical, compound and site-loss events.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall run tabletop exercises on a defined cycle covering scenarios not testable live, including at least one cyber-physical scenario (for example BMS/EPMS compromise, X05) and one compound event (X20) per cycle, with participation of crisis command, facility, IT, security and key providers. The resilience owner shall record decisions, timings, gaps and actions and shall track actions to closure.
assessmentCriteria: Exercises occurred on the defined cycle with documented scenarios and objectives.
Each cycle includes a cyber-physical and a compound scenario.
Participants include crisis command, facility, IT, security and key providers.
Gaps and actions are recorded and tracked to closure.
minimumEvidence: Exercise reports with gaps and actions

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Facilitated or observed by a party independent of the plan authors.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2 for confidence; US3 if no cyber-physical scenario was ever exercised.

assessmentProcedure: Review exercise schedule and scenarios.
Check scenario mix and participation.
Review reports and action closure.
Interview participants.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope site and Capability Instance; exercises may be combined across sites where crisis command is shared.
failureModes: Decision paralysis in cyber-physical event
Provider roles unclear
Actions from exercises never closed
controls.testingSafety: Tabletop exercises are non-intrusive; do not issue live commands to systems during exercises.
controls.unknownRule: Tabletop results support OPERATION claims for decision processes only, not technical recovery effectiveness.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-84 (Guide to test, training and exercise programs for IT plans and capabilities)
ISO 22320 (Emergency management: guidelines for incident management)

controls.title: Lessons and Retest
controls.objective: Ensure that defects and lessons from tests, exercises and real incidents are tracked to closure, reflected in plans and designs, and verified by retest.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall maintain a lessons register capturing every defect and lesson from tests, exercises and incidents with owner, due date, and the plan, runbook, design or control affected. The resilience owner shall require retest or equivalent verification before closure of any lesson affecting a gate-critical safeguard and shall report overdue items to governance monthly.
assessmentCriteria: All defects and lessons from the period are in the register with owner and due date.
Affected plans, runbooks and designs were updated.
Gate-critical items were closed only after retest or equivalent verification.
Overdue items were reported to governance.

parameters.name: Maximum age of open gate-critical lesson

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor traces from source test/incident reports to the register.
mandatoryItems: Retest evidence for closed gate-critical items
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unclosed gate-critical lessons condition the decision.

assessmentProcedure: Trace defects from test, exercise and incident reports into the register.
Sample closed items for plan updates and retest.
Review overdue items and governance reporting.
controls.applicability: Applies to all resilience tests, exercises and incidents in scope.
failureModes: Same defect recurring in successive tests
Lessons closed without verification
controls.testingSafety: Retests follow the safety requirements of the original test control.
controls.unknownRule: Items closed without verification evidence are reopened as UNKNOWN U1.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-84 (Guide to test, training and exercise programs for IT plans and capabilities)

controls.title: Crisis Command
controls.objective: Ensure a crisis command structure with defined levels, authority, activation criteria and facilities can take timely decisions during major infrastructure and cyber-physical events.
controls.requirement: The executive sponsor shall establish a crisis command structure with strategic, tactical and operational levels, named primary and alternate role holders, activation criteria, decision authority (including authority to shed load, suspend tenants, invoke alternate capacity and order controlled shutdown), and command facilities and communication channels that remain available when site systems, corporate identity or primary communications fail. The crisis management lead shall demonstrate activation and decision timings in exercises or real events.
assessmentCriteria: The command structure defines levels, roles, alternates and decision authority.
Activation criteria are defined and linked to monitoring and incident triggers.
Command facilities and communications are available independently of site systems and corporate identity.
Exercises or events in the period demonstrated activation within the target time and decisions within authority.
Decision logs were maintained.
minimumEvidence: Exercise/event records with timings and decision logs

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Exercises within 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Exercises observed by a party independent of the crisis team.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; escalates to US4 against CG-13 if no decision authority exists for controlled shutdown.

assessmentProcedure: Review plan, roles and authority.
Check communication independence.
Review exercise or event timings and decision logs.
Interview role holders on authority.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope organisation and site.
failureModes: No one authorised to order controlled shutdown
Crisis bridge relies on failed identity provider
Alternate role holders untrained
controls.testingSafety: Exercises shall be clearly labelled to prevent confusion with real events; live notifications to customers or authorities during exercises require prior approval.
controls.unknownRule: If command communications depend on an unanalysed service, record U10 against crisis command availability.
informativeReferences: ISO 22320 (Emergency management: guidelines for incident management)

controls.title: Stakeholder Communications
controls.objective: Ensure timely, accurate communication to customers, tenants, regulators, providers and staff during disruption, consistent with contractual and regulatory notification obligations.
controls.requirement: The crisis management lead shall maintain a communications plan listing stakeholders, notification obligations and deadlines (contractual and regulatory), approved message templates, approval authority and channels that remain available during site and identity failures. The crisis management lead shall record each notification issued during events and exercises with timestamp and approver and shall review timeliness against obligations.
assessmentCriteria: A communications plan lists stakeholders, obligations, deadlines and channels.
Templates and approval authorities are defined.
Notifications in events and exercises in the period met deadlines.
Channels are available independently of site and corporate identity systems.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reconciles logs with obligation deadlines.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US2; US3 where regulatory notification timeliness cannot be established.

assessmentProcedure: Review the plan and obligation register.
Reconcile notification logs with deadlines.
Check channel independence.
controls.applicability: Applies to every in-scope organisation.
failureModes: Missed regulatory notification
Inconsistent customer messaging
Communication channel lost with site
controls.testingSafety: Exercise messages shall be marked as exercise and not sent externally without approval.
controls.unknownRule: Obligations without a known deadline are recorded as U9 pending legal interpretation.
informativeReferences: ISO 22320 (Emergency management: guidelines for incident management)

controls.title: Emergency Change
controls.objective: Ensure changes made under emergency conditions are authorised by defined emergency authority, minimal, recorded, and reconciled back to baseline after the event.
controls.requirement: The change authority shall define an emergency change procedure stating who may authorise emergency changes to infrastructure, OT and control-plane systems, the minimum record to be captured at the time, and the deadline for retrospective review. The recovery manager shall ensure every emergency change is retrospectively reviewed, either reverted or formalised, and that baselines and evidence are updated, and shall report unreconciled emergency changes.
assessmentCriteria: An emergency change procedure defines authority, minimum records and retrospective review deadline.
Emergency changes in the period were authorised by defined authority.
Each emergency change was reviewed within the deadline and reverted or formalised.
Baselines (NET-022, OPS-017) were updated after formalised emergency changes.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor identifies emergency changes from configuration drift and logs, not only from the change system.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; affects CG-14 SUPPORTING evaluation.

assessmentProcedure: Review procedure.
Identify emergency changes from logs and drift.
Check authorisation and retrospective review.
Verify baseline updates.
controls.applicability: Applies to all infrastructure, OT and control-plane systems in scope.
failureModes: Emergency bypass left in place
Unrecorded emergency configuration becoming latent fault
Emergency authority exceeded
controls.testingSafety: Records-based.
controls.unknownRule: Emergency changes identified from drift with no record are Findings; if logs are unavailable, record U2.

controls.title: Post-Event Adaptation
controls.objective: Ensure that after material events the organisation analyses root causes and systemic contributors, adapts design, operations and assurance, and triggers reassessment of affected claims.
controls.requirement: The resilience owner shall require a post-event review within a defined time after every material event, covering timeline, root and contributing causes, safeguard performance against expectation, recovery performance against tolerance, and required adaptations to design, operations, controls and evidence. The resilience owner shall raise reassessment triggers for affected controls and gate results and shall track adaptations to completion.
assessmentCriteria: Post-event reviews were completed for every material event within the defined time.
Reviews compare safeguard and recovery performance with expectation and tolerance.
Adaptations are tracked to completion.
Reassessment triggers were raised for affected controls and gates.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 24 months (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Reviews facilitated by a party independent of the teams involved.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unreviewed events may invalidate existing evidence.

assessmentProcedure: List material events from incident systems.
Check review completion and content.
Trace adaptations and reassessment triggers.
controls.applicability: Applies to all material events affecting in-scope outcomes.
failureModes: Repeat incidents from unaddressed systemic causes
Evidence relied on despite invalidating event
controls.testingSafety: Post-event reviews are non-intrusive; any reproduction of the event to confirm causes is a test governed by RES-018 authorisation requirements.
controls.unknownRule: Events without a completed review mark the evidence of affected controls as STALE until reviewed.

controls.title: Supplier Capability
controls.objective: Suppliers of critical equipment and services are shown, before award and at renewal, to have the technical, manufacturing, integration, installation and field-support capability required by the Capability Instance at the site and scale proposed.
controls.requirement: The procurement lead shall perform and record a capability assessment for each supplier of a critical asset class or service before award and at renewal, covering engineering competence, manufacturing and test capacity (including factory acceptance testing), rack-scale or skid integration capability where applicable, installation and commissioning resources, field-service coverage and response at the site, and references for comparable deployments. A competent engineer shall approve the technical part of the assessment.
assessmentCriteria: A capability assessment exists for each critical supplier, dated before award or last renewal.
The assessment addresses manufacturing/test capacity, integration, installation/commissioning and field-service coverage for the specific site.
Factory acceptance test (FAT) capability and witness arrangements are confirmed for equipment where FAT is specified (for example switchgear, UPS, CDUs, rack-scale systems).
Technical approval by a competent engineer is recorded.
Identified capability gaps have conditions in the contract or an accepted risk.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessment valid for the current contract term.
evidenceProfile.independence: Technical approval by an engineer not in the procurement line.
acceptableAlternatives: Prior successful delivery of the same product at a comparable site by the same supplier, documented by acceptance records, may replace part of the reference check.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: List critical suppliers from DEP-011/DEP-014.
Obtain capability assessments and approvals.
Check coverage of manufacturing, integration, installation and field service.
Verify gaps have contractual conditions or acceptance.
controls.applicability: Applies to suppliers of critical asset classes and services; non-critical suppliers follow standard procurement.
failureModes: Integrator lacks capacity to test rack-scale systems before delivery
No field engineer within response time of the site
Supplier cannot perform specified FAT
controls.testingSafety: Not applicable (documentary assessment).
controls.unknownRule: Missing capability assessment for a critical supplier is U1, US3.

controls.title: Financial and Operational Resilience
controls.objective: The financial health, manufacturing footprint, allocation exposure and business-continuity capability of critical suppliers are monitored so that supplier distress or disruption is detected early enough to act.
controls.requirement: The supplier manager shall monitor each critical supplier at the profile interval for financial distress indicators, manufacturing and logistics concentration (single plant or region), allocation or quota exposure (for example accelerator allocations), sanctions and export-control exposure, and business-continuity arrangements, and shall escalate adverse changes to the capability owner with a proposed treatment.
assessmentCriteria: Each critical supplier has monitoring records at the interval for the period.
Manufacturing and logistics concentration is recorded per supplier.
Allocation, sanctions and export-control exposure is assessed for supply-constrained classes.
Supplier business-continuity evidence has been obtained for the most critical suppliers.
Adverse changes in the period were escalated with treatment.
minimumEvidence: Financial risk reports (credit agency or equivalent).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: At least one external information source (credit agency, public filings) per supplier.
acceptableAlternatives: Group-level monitoring by a parent organisation is acceptable if it covers the specific suppliers.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain monitoring records.
Check interval adherence and coverage.
Review export and allocation exposure analyses.
Trace adverse changes to escalation.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical suppliers.
failureModes: Supplier insolvency halts spares
Single plant outage stops supply
Export restriction blocks accelerator deliveries
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based monitoring; no site testing is involved.
controls.unknownRule: No monitoring of a sole-source supplier is US3.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-161r1 (cyber supply chain risk management)

controls.title: Security and Quality Posture
controls.objective: Critical suppliers operate quality management and secure development practices adequate for products that will run, control or protect AI infrastructure, including product security incident response for firmware and control software.
controls.requirement: The procurement lead shall obtain and evaluate evidence of each critical supplier's quality management system, product security development lifecycle for firmware and control software, product security incident response (PSIRT) and vulnerability disclosure process, and factory test and outgoing quality controls. The procurement lead shall record identified gaps with contract conditions and shall track incoming quality (defects on receipt, early-life failures) for each supplier.
assessmentCriteria: Quality management evidence (certificate or audit) is current for each critical supplier.
Secure development lifecycle evidence exists for suppliers of firmware or control software.
A PSIRT or equivalent contact and disclosure process exists for each firmware or software supplier.
Incoming quality data is tracked and reviewed.
Gaps have contractual conditions.
minimumEvidence: Secure development evidence (for example IEC 62443-4-1 assessment or equivalent attestation).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Certificates current; incoming quality for 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Third-party certificates or audit reports preferred (E5).
acceptableAlternatives: Owner-performed supplier audit may replace third-party certificate.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-08, CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain supplier posture evidence.
Check currency and scope.
Review incoming quality data.
Check gap conditions.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical hardware, firmware and control-software suppliers.
failureModes: Supplier without vulnerability disclosure process
Batch quality escape in optics or memory
Uncontrolled firmware build process
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based evaluation; any supplier site audit follows the supplier's site safety rules.
controls.unknownRule: Missing PSIRT evidence for a firmware supplier is US3.

controls.title: Sub-Tier Visibility
controls.objective: Critical sub-tier dependencies behind first-tier suppliers (for example high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging for accelerators, laser and optical components, transformer core steel and bushings, switchgear breaker mechanisms, CDU pumps and heat exchangers, battery cells, controller chipsets, and contract manufacturers) are known well enough to reveal shared sub-tier sources across nominally diverse suppliers.
controls.requirement: The procurement lead shall obtain, for each critical asset class, disclosure of material sub-tier suppliers and manufacturing locations from first-tier suppliers, record them in the dependency graph, and identify sub-tier sources shared across nominally diverse first-tier suppliers. Where a supplier declines disclosure, the procurement lead shall record an UNKNOWN Record and the capability owner shall decide on treatment.
assessmentCriteria: Sub-tier disclosure has been requested and recorded for each critical asset class.
Shared sub-tier sources across diverse first-tier suppliers are identified.
Sub-tier information is in the dependency graph and used in DEP-014 concentration analysis.
Declined or partial disclosures are UNKNOWN Records with treatment decisions.

parameters.name: Sub-tier depth for critical classes
parameters.basis: Illustrative; deeper where single-source components are known.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current; refreshed at renewal.
evidenceProfile.independence: Corroboration from a second source (market intelligence, teardown, certification records) for a sample.
mandatoryItems: Sub-tier disclosure records for critical classes
acceptableAlternatives: Industry consortium sub-tier mapping may substitute where suppliers participate.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: an UNKNOWN result on this control sets CG-03 to UNKNOWN (CG-12 trigger); the decision is capped at LIMITED or INCONCLUSIVE per the gate ceiling until the UNKNOWN Record is dispositioned.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain disclosures.
Map into dependency graph.
Search for shared sub-tier nodes.
Corroborate a sample.
Review UNKNOWN treatment.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical asset classes with constrained supply or long lead times.
failureModes: Two UPS brands share one battery-cell maker
All accelerator suppliers depend on one packaging capacity
Transformer suppliers share one bushing source
controls.testingSafety: Desk-based analysis; sub-tier disclosures may be commercially sensitive and shall be handled under the classification rules of AIDCF-008.
controls.unknownRule: Declined sub-tier disclosure for a critical class whose failure would defeat recovery or expansion is U2/U10, US4 (CG-03 critical).
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-161r1 (cyber supply chain risk management)

controls.title: Service Levels
controls.objective: Contracts for maintenance, support and supply of critical systems contain measurable service levels (response, on-site attendance, restore, parts availability, RMA turnaround) that are consistent with the Service Outcome and recovery tolerances.
controls.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure each critical support or maintenance contract states measurable service levels with units, measurement points, exclusions and escalation, and shall document that each service level is consistent with the time-to-impact and recovery tolerances in DEP-003 and CAP-02. Where contracted levels are inconsistent, the capability owner shall record the gap and its treatment (on-site spares, resident engineers, alternative supplier).
assessmentCriteria: Each critical contract has measurable service levels with units and measurement points.
Service levels are compared with tolerances and the comparison is recorded.
Inconsistencies have treatments.
Escalation contacts and paths are current.

parameters.name: Maximum on-site attendance time for critical electrical/mechanical faults
parameters.basis: Illustrative; set from DEP-003 time-to-impact and spares held.

minimumEvidence: Contracts or schedules with service levels.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current contracts.
evidenceProfile.independence: Comparison checked by engineering, not only procurement.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10, CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: List critical contracts.
Extract service levels.
Compare with tolerances.
Review treatments and escalation lists.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical support and maintenance contracts.
failureModes: Next-business-day support for asset with minutes time-to-impact
Exclusions void service level during regional event
controls.testingSafety: Contract review only; no response-time test shall be performed by raising false faults with suppliers.
controls.unknownRule: Service level absent for a critical contract is US3.

controls.title: Evidence Rights
controls.objective: The owner has contractual rights to obtain the evidence needed to assess supplier-provided and provider-operated functions: test and commissioning records, maintenance records, firmware SBOMs and release notes, telemetry access, incident RCAs, audit reports and access for witness testing and audit.
controls.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure that each critical supplier and provider contract grants rights to the evidence listed in the AIDCF-008 control evidence profiles relevant to the supplied function, within stated timescales and formats, including rights to witness tests and to audit or receive independent assurance reports, and shall record any evidence the supplier will not provide as an UNKNOWN Record against the affected controls.
assessmentCriteria: Each critical contract has an evidence-rights clause or schedule.
The listed evidence covers mandatory items of the affected controls.
Rights to witness FAT/SAT and audit exist where needed.
Refused evidence is recorded as UNKNOWN against controls.
minimumEvidence: Mapping of rights to control evidence profiles.
Records of evidence requests and responses.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current contracts; request log for 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Not applicable beyond document review.
acceptableAlternatives: Independent assurance reports (for example SOC 2 or ISO certification audit reports) with access to underlying evidence on request.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain clauses.
Map to control evidence profiles.
Sample evidence requests and responses.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical supplier and provider contracts.
failureModes: Colocation provider refuses generator test records
OEM declines firmware SBOM
No right to witness CDU FAT
controls.testingSafety: Contract review only; evidence requests are made through the contract channel, not by direct access to supplier systems.
controls.unknownRule: Absent evidence rights for a provider-operated critical function is US3 for this control; the consequential UNKNOWN on dependent controls takes those controls' severity.

controls.title: Incident Notification
controls.objective: Suppliers and providers notify the owner promptly of incidents, vulnerabilities, field notices, recalls, allocation changes and planned changes that could affect supplied functions, and the notifications reach the people who must act.
controls.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure critical supplier and provider contracts define notification obligations and timescales for incidents, security vulnerabilities, field notices and recalls, planned maintenance and changes, and allocation or end-of-life changes, and shall operate a monitored intake (shared mailbox, portal subscription, ticket integration) that routes notifications to the responsible owner. The supplier manager shall test the intake path at the profile interval.
assessmentCriteria: Notification obligations and timescales exist in critical contracts.
Notification intake is monitored and routed to responsible owners.
Notifications in the period were received, routed and acted on within timescales.
The intake path was tested within the interval.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: At least 6 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor cross-checks a sample of public supplier advisories against the intake log.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-03, CG-15 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain clauses and intake design.
Compare public advisories to intake log.
Trace sample to action.
Review intake tests.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical suppliers and providers that can affect a supplied function through incidents, vulnerabilities, recalls or planned changes.
failureModes: Field notice for breaker trip units missed
Carrier planned works not received
Vulnerability advisory for BMC firmware unnoticed

controls.unknownRule: No notification log is U1, US3.

controls.title: Exit and Transition Rights
controls.objective: The owner can exit or replace a critical supplier or provider without losing the ability to operate, maintain or recover critical systems, including access to configuration, control logic, data, documentation, licences, spares and transition assistance.
controls.requirement: The supplier manager shall ensure each critical contract provides exit and transition rights proportionate to the dependency, including export of configuration and operational data in usable formats, ownership or escrow of control logic and configuration for programmable controllers, perpetual or transition licences for software required to operate installed equipment, option to purchase spares and tools, documentation hand-over, and transition assistance for a stated period. The capability owner shall maintain an exit plan for each sole-source or high-concentration supplier.
assessmentCriteria: Exit and transition clauses exist in critical contracts.
Control logic and configuration ownership or escrow is established for programmable controllers.
Licences needed to operate installed equipment survive termination or transition.
Exit plans exist for sole-source and high-concentration suppliers.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T2 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Current contracts.
evidenceProfile.independence: Legal and engineering review recorded.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-10 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain clauses and plans.
Check control-logic and licence provisions.
Review exit plans for feasibility.
controls.applicability: Applies to critical suppliers and providers; mandatory exit plans apply to sole-source and high-concentration suppliers identified under MCF-DEP-014.
failureModes: Supplier exit leaves BMS without editable logic
Licence revocation disables installed equipment
Provider holds operational data hostage
controls.testingSafety: Contract and plan review only; escrow release or licence-transfer trials are performed only under agreement with the supplier.
controls.unknownRule: No exit plan for a sole-source supplier is US3.

controls.title: Approved Sourcing
controls.objective: Critical components (protection devices, circuit breakers and trip units, relays, UPS modules and batteries, accelerators and boards, memory, optics, NICs/DPUs, storage media, controllers and sensors) are purchased only from the OEM or OEM-authorised channels, so that counterfeit, grey-market, refurbished-as-new and tampered parts are excluded at source.
controls.requirement: The procurement lead shall maintain an approved source list for each critical component class naming the OEM and authorised distributors, shall configure purchasing controls so that orders for critical classes can be placed only with approved sources, and shall require documented engineering approval and enhanced inspection (MCF-SUP-010) for any exception, such as broker purchase of obsolete parts.
assessmentCriteria: An approved source list exists per critical component class.
Purchasing system controls restrict critical-class orders to approved sources.
