evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: an UNKNOWN result requires gate-level evaluation for CG-15, CG-13 and caps the decision at CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED with a recorded condition until resolved.

assessmentProcedure: Obtain revocation and recertification records.
Sample accounts and badges.
Reconcile to active contracts and personnel.
controls.applicability: Applies to all third-party access.
failureModes: Departed contractor badge active
Expired contract vendor account active
controls.testingSafety: Account and badge reconciliation only; no access shall be revoked or tested by the assessor.
controls.unknownRule: No recertification evidence is US3.
informativeReferences: IEC 62443-2-4 (security requirements for IACS service providers)

controls.title: Human Identity
controls.objective: Ensure every person who can observe, configure or command facility OT, infrastructure management planes or AI control planes is uniquely identified, strongly authenticated and lifecycle-managed, with no shared or orphaned accounts.
controls.requirement: The identity and access manager shall ensure that every human identity with access to BMS, EPMS, CDU and PLC engineering workstations and HMIs, BMC/Redfish interfaces, network devices, hypervisor and Kubernetes control planes, cluster managers and storage controllers is individually attributable, uses phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication where the system supports it (with compensating controls recorded where it does not, for example legacy HMIs), and is joined, moved and removed through an authoritative identity source within defined deadlines. The OT security owner shall maintain an inventory of OT systems that cannot integrate with central identity and the compensating controls applied.
assessmentCriteria: All human accounts on in-scope systems map to a named individual in the authoritative identity source; shared accounts are absent or individually approved with session attribution.
Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for remote and privileged access to in-scope systems, with exceptions listed and compensated.
Leaver access is removed within the defined deadline (sampled against HR leaver records).
Periodic access recertification of in-scope systems occurred at the defined interval.
OT systems lacking central identity integration are inventoried with compensating controls (for example jump-host attribution, local account review).
Identity services relied upon for infrastructure access have documented fallback for outage (linked to SEC-004).
minimumEvidence: Account extracts from in-scope systems reconciled to the identity source
MFA enforcement configuration and exception list

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Account extracts within 30 days (illustrative); leaver sample over 6 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Account extracts taken by the assessor directly from target systems, not from the identity system alone.
acceptableAlternatives: Witnessed screen extraction from legacy OT systems that cannot export accounts
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-15 where accounts on BMS/EPMS or BMC planes cannot be enumerated.

assessmentProcedure: Enumerate in-scope systems including OT HMIs and engineering workstations.
Extract local and directory-linked accounts from a sample of each class.
Reconcile to the identity source and HR records.
Verify MFA enforcement and review exceptions.
Review recertification and OT exception inventory.
controls.applicability: Applies to all human access to in-scope OT, infrastructure management and AI control-plane systems, including contractors and provider staff (with SUP-021 for provider identities).
failureModes: Shared HMI login preventing attribution
Leaver retaining BMC access
MFA absent on remote engineering access
Orphaned local admin on switches
controls.testingSafety: Account extraction shall use read-only methods; no password testing or credential guessing is permitted without written authorisation from the security owner and, for OT, the facility owner.
controls.unknownRule: Systems whose accounts cannot be enumerated are recorded with U2 and their access treated as uncontrolled in authority-path analysis.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: Machine Identity
controls.objective: Ensure machine identities (service accounts, API tokens, certificates, workload identities, node and device identities) used by automation, controllers and agents are inventoried, scoped, rotated and, for hardware, anchored in a root of trust with attestation.
controls.requirement: The platform security lead shall maintain an inventory of machine identities with access to in-scope infrastructure, including owner, purpose, scope, credential type, rotation interval and expiry, and shall prohibit long-lived static credentials for consequential authority where short-lived or certificate-based credentials are supported. The platform security lead shall require hardware-rooted identity (for example TPM or device identity certificates) and boot or firmware attestation (for example via SPDM or TPM quotes) for accelerator nodes, BMCs and fabric devices that support it, and shall gate cluster admission on successful attestation.
assessmentCriteria: A machine-identity inventory covers service accounts, tokens, certificates and workload identities with owner and scope.
Long-lived static credentials with write or command authority are absent or individually approved with rotation.
Certificates and tokens are rotated within defined intervals and expiry is monitored.
Nodes and devices supporting hardware root of trust present device identity and attestation, and cluster admission rejects failed attestation.
Machine identities are scoped to least privilege (sampled).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Inventory within 30 days (illustrative); admission logs for 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Inventory reconciled by the assessor to secrets stores and target-system configurations.
acceptableAlternatives: Secrets-manager reports combined with target-side token listings
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-15 where unscoped machine credentials with OT or control-plane write authority exist.

assessmentProcedure: Review the inventory and reconcile with secrets stores and target systems.
Identify static credentials with consequential authority.
Review rotation and expiry monitoring.
Review attestation configuration and sample admission logs including rejections.
Sample scopes for least privilege.
controls.applicability: Applies to machine identities with access to in-scope infrastructure. Hardware attestation criteria apply only where devices support it; unsupported classes are listed.
failureModes: Hard-coded API token in automation with BMS write access
Expired certificate halting control plane
Tampered node joining cluster without attestation
Over-scoped service account
controls.testingSafety: Attestation rejection tests shall use a designated test node; do not alter firmware on production nodes to test rejection.
controls.unknownRule: Credentials discovered on target systems but absent from inventory are Findings; if discovery is not possible, record U5.
informativeReferences: Trusted Computing Group TPM 2.0 Library Specification
DMTF DSP0274 (Security Protocol and Data Model, SPDM)

controls.title: Privileged Access
controls.objective: Ensure privileged and consequential authority over facility OT, BMC/Redfish, network, hypervisor/Kubernetes, cluster manager and storage control planes is least-privilege, brokered, time-bound and monitored, so no single compromised identity can command cross-domain infrastructure.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall define privileged roles by authority action (observe, configure, command, bypass, update, revoke, recover, per AIDCF-005) and by domain, shall prohibit standing cross-domain privileged roles (for example a single role with write access to both BMS/EPMS and cluster control planes) except as approved break-glass, and shall broker privileged sessions through a privileged access management (PAM) system or jump hosts providing just-in-time elevation, session recording and approval for command and bypass actions. The infrastructure security owner shall test at a defined interval that privilege boundaries hold, including that elevation requires approval and that sessions are recorded.
assessmentCriteria: Privileged roles are defined by authority action and domain, with an effective-permission analysis for each.
No standing identity holds command or bypass authority across more than one infrastructure domain without approved break-glass status.
Privileged access to in-scope systems is brokered with just-in-time elevation and session recording.
Command and bypass actions on OT systems require approval or are restricted to authorised operators on site.
Tests in the interval confirmed that direct (non-brokered) privileged access is blocked and elevation requires approval.
Privileged session logs are reviewed at a defined frequency.
minimumEvidence: Privileged role catalogue by authority action and domain
PAM configuration and session recordings sample

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within interval; 90 days (illustrative) of session logs.
evidenceProfile.independence: Bypass-path testing by the security function or an independent tester.
acceptableAlternatives: Configuration analysis of network and host controls proving non-brokered paths are blocked, where active testing is not authorised
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while consequential cross-domain authority is unanalysed or untested.

assessmentProcedure: Review role catalogue and effective permissions, including group and federation inheritance.
Identify identities with cross-domain command or bypass authority.
Review PAM configuration and sample session recordings.
Review or perform tests of non-brokered access paths.
Review session review records.
controls.applicability: Applies to all privileged access to in-scope OT, infrastructure management and AI control-plane systems.
failureModes: Domain admin inheriting BMS write rights (control-plane inheritance)
Direct SSH to BMCs bypassing PAM
Standing cluster-admin token
Shared management identity across power and cooling
controls.testingSafety: Bypass-path tests shall be non-destructive (attempt authentication or connection only, no commands) and require written authorisation from the security owner; tests touching OT systems also require facility owner authorisation and must not issue any write or command.
controls.unknownRule: If effective permissions cannot be computed because of opaque federation or local roles, record U9 at US4 against CG-15.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (Security and privacy controls)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: Break-Glass Governance
controls.objective: Ensure emergency accounts and procedures across OT, infrastructure and control planes work when central identity fails, are protected against misuse, and every use is reviewed.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall govern break-glass arrangements for all in-scope domains: inventory of emergency accounts, storage under dual control with an offline copy outside the failure domains they recover, use triggers, notification on use, maximum duration, mandatory post-use review and credential rotation. The infrastructure security owner shall verify at a defined interval that break-glass retrieval and login work with the primary identity provider and vault unavailable, and shall review all uses.
assessmentCriteria: Break-glass inventory covers OT, BMC, network, hypervisor/Kubernetes, cluster manager and storage domains.
Credentials are under dual control with an offline copy located outside recovered failure domains.
Use triggers alerts to the security function in real time.
Every use in the period was reviewed and followed by rotation within the deadline.
Retrieval and login tests with primary identity and vault unavailable succeeded in the interval.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative) of uses; test within 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Use reviews by security function independent of the user.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 if no tested emergency access exists for recovery-critical control planes.

assessmentProcedure: Review inventory coverage across domains.
Inspect storage and offline copy location against fault domains.
Verify alerting on use.
Sample uses for review and rotation.
Review retrieval test.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope domains. Network-specific break-glass implementation is NET-016.
failureModes: Offline copy stored in the data centre it recovers
Silent break-glass use
Emergency account used as routine admin
controls.testingSafety: Retrieval tests shall not disable production identity; simulate unavailability for the test client only, and rotate credentials afterwards.
controls.unknownRule: Domains without a tested break-glass path are recorded with U1 for recovery claims.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (Security and privacy controls)
ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: BMS and EPMS Security
controls.objective: Ensure building management, electrical power monitoring, CDU and PLC/SCADA systems that monitor and command power and cooling are secured to a target security level appropriate to their consequence, so compromise or misuse cannot defeat electrical or thermal continuity.
controls.requirement: The OT security owner shall perform a security risk assessment for BMS, EPMS, CDU controllers, PLCs, SCADA servers, historians and engineering workstations using a zone-and-conduit approach consistent with ISA/IEC 62443, assign a target security level (SL-T) to each zone, and implement countermeasures across the foundational requirement areas (identification and authentication, use control, system integrity, data confidentiality, restricted data flow, timely response to events, resource availability). The facility owner shall ensure that safety-instrumented and protection functions (electrical protection relays, emergency shutdown, hardwired interlocks) are independent of BMS/EPMS networks, and the OT security owner shall verify by test that unauthorised write or command attempts against controllers are blocked or detected and that controllers fail to a defined safe state on loss of supervisory communication.
assessmentCriteria: A security risk assessment exists for BMS/EPMS/CDU/PLC assets with zones, conduits and assigned SL-T.
Achieved countermeasures are assessed against SL-T for each foundational requirement area, with gaps recorded.
Protection relays, emergency shutdown and hardwired interlocks do not depend on BMS/EPMS network availability or integrity.
Default credentials are absent and engineering protocols (for example BACnet, Modbus/TCP) are restricted to defined conduits.
Tests confirmed that unauthorised write/command attempts from outside permitted conduits are blocked or alarmed.
Controllers fail to the defined safe state (for example last good setpoint, mechanical fail-safe position) on loss of supervisory communication, verified by test or vendor-witnessed evidence.
Controller logic and firmware changes are detected (checksum or version monitoring).

parameters.name: Target security level for power and cooling control zones
parameters.illustrativeDefault: SL-T 2 minimum; SL-T 3 for zones whose compromise defeats CG-05/CG-06 (illustrative)
parameters.basis: Assigned by risk assessment per ISA/IEC 62443-3-2.

minimumEvidence: OT security risk assessment with zone/conduit model and SL-T
SL gap assessment against foundational requirements
Independence analysis for protection and safety functions
Fail-safe behaviour test or witnessed vendor evidence

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Tests within 12 months (illustrative); integrity monitoring for 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Testing by an OT security specialist independent of the BMS/EPMS integrator.
acceptableAlternatives: Test on a representative OT test bench with identical firmware and configuration, plus production configuration review
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-07 cannot PASS while BMS/EPMS write/command exposure or fail-safe behaviour is unverified (scenario X05).
reassessmentTriggers: New integration (for example IT/OT data export)

assessmentProcedure: Review the risk assessment, zone/conduit model and SL-T assignments.
Review SL gap assessment by foundational requirement area.
Trace protection and safety functions to confirm independence from BMS/EPMS networks.
Inspect credential and protocol restrictions on a sample of controllers.
Review or witness write/command blocking tests from non-permitted zones.
Review fail-safe evidence and logic integrity monitoring.
controls.applicability: Applies to all BMS, EPMS, CDU, PLC, SCADA, historian and OT engineering systems supporting in-scope power and cooling. Where operated by a colocation provider, evidence rights are required (DEP-018, SUP-006).
failureModes: Malicious setpoint change causing cooling loss at load
EPMS compromise masking electrical alarms
Protection logic dependent on BMS network
Default credentials on CDU controller
Controller failing to unsafe state on comms loss
controls.testingSafety: No active scanning, fuzzing, write or command test shall be performed against production BMS/EPMS/CDU/PLC systems without written authorisation from the facility owner and OT security owner, plant in a safe state, operator presence, and vendor consultation; passive monitoring and test-bench testing are preferred. Fail-safe tests that remove supervisory communication require engineering authorisation and a defined restoration plan.
controls.unknownRule: If controller logic integrity or fail-safe state cannot be established, record U8 at US4 against CG-07; do not infer from vendor marketing material.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 (Security risk assessment, zones and conduits)
ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
ISA/IEC 62443-4-2 (Technical security requirements for IACS components)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: Cluster Manager Security
controls.objective: Ensure the AI control plane (Kubernetes or HPC scheduler, cluster manager, provisioning and image services, hypervisor managers) cannot be used to gain unbounded authority over compute, data and connected infrastructure.
controls.requirement: The platform security lead shall harden each cluster manager and control plane to a documented benchmark (for example CIS Kubernetes Benchmark where applicable), restrict API server and scheduler administrative access to brokered privileged paths, enforce admission control that blocks privileged containers, host-namespace access and unapproved images on accelerator nodes, protect control-plane state stores (for example etcd) with encryption and access restriction, and separate tenant-facing from infrastructure-administrative interfaces. The platform security lead shall test at a defined interval that a tenant or workload identity cannot escalate to node, cluster-admin or BMC authority.
assessmentCriteria: Control-plane hardening against a documented benchmark is assessed with deviations recorded.
Administrative API access is restricted to brokered privileged paths.
Admission control blocks privileged pods, host mounts and unapproved images on accelerator nodes (verified by test).
Control-plane state stores are encrypted and access-restricted.
Tenant-facing and administrative interfaces are separated.
Escalation tests in the interval found no path from tenant workload to node, cluster-admin or BMC authority, or Findings were raised.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within interval; admission logs 90 days.
evidenceProfile.independence: Escalation tests by an independent tester.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while tenant-to-infrastructure escalation paths are untested.

assessmentProcedure: Review hardening assessment and deviations.
Inspect administrative access paths.
Test admission control with prohibited workload specifications in a test namespace.
Review state store protection.
Review escalation test reports.
controls.applicability: Applies to all cluster managers, schedulers and hypervisor managers controlling in-scope compute.
failureModes: Privileged container giving node root and BMC reach
Exposed etcd
Cluster-admin token leaked
Unapproved image with tampered drivers
controls.testingSafety: Escalation tests shall run in designated test namespaces or clusters under written authorisation; no tests shall modify production workloads or node firmware.
controls.unknownRule: Where the control plane is provider-managed and escalation testing is not permitted, record U2 and require provider assurance (E5).

controls.title: Fabric Controller Security
controls.objective: Ensure fabric controllers, subnet managers, SDN controllers and network automation platforms are protected so that their compromise cannot reconfigure, partition or blackhole fabrics.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall ensure fabric controllers, subnet managers and network automation platforms are reachable only from the management zone, use individually attributable and brokered administrative access, authenticate southbound connections to devices (for example certificate-based gNMI/NETCONF), protect fabric security keys (for example InfiniBand management and partition keys), and log all configuration actions to the security telemetry platform. The fabric operations lead shall reconcile controller access configuration to this requirement at a defined interval.
assessmentCriteria: Controllers and automation platforms are reachable only from the management zone (verified).
Administrative access is individually attributable and brokered.
Southbound device connections are authenticated and encrypted where supported.
Fabric security keys are managed and not left at defaults.
All configuration actions are logged to security telemetry.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Reconciliation within 90 days (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation by security function.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unknown controller exposure conditions CG-15 and CG-08 claims.

assessmentProcedure: Inspect network reachability of controllers.
Review administrative access and logging.
Review southbound authentication and keys.
controls.applicability: Applies to fabric controllers, subnet managers and network automation affecting in-scope fabrics. Resilience of controllers is NET-021.
failureModes: Default management key enabling rogue subnet manager
Automation platform compromised to push malicious config
Unauthenticated southbound sessions
controls.testingSafety: Non-intrusive configuration review; do not attempt rogue subnet-manager tests on production fabrics.
controls.unknownRule: If default fabric keys cannot be ruled out, record U7 against fabric integrity.
informativeReferences: InfiniBand Trade Association, InfiniBand Architecture Specification (Volumes 1 and 2)
OpenConfig gNMI specification and OpenConfig data models
ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)

controls.title: Storage Controller Security
controls.objective: Ensure storage management planes cannot be used to destroy, encrypt or exfiltrate training data, checkpoints and model artefacts, and that destructive operations require additional protection.
controls.requirement: The storage platform owner shall restrict storage controller and management interfaces to the management zone with brokered privileged access, shall require multi-person approval or delayed execution for destructive operations (volume or bucket deletion, snapshot or retention policy reduction, replication break), shall protect immutable recovery copies with retention locks that administrators cannot shorten, and shall log management actions to security telemetry.
assessmentCriteria: Storage management interfaces are reachable only from the management zone.
Privileged storage access is brokered and attributable.
Destructive operations require multi-person approval or delayed execution.
Immutable recovery copies have retention locks not reducible by administrators (verified configuration).
Management actions are logged to security telemetry.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Configuration within 90 days (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Configuration extracted by assessor.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3; US4 against CG-10 where checkpoint recovery copies lack immutability.

assessmentProcedure: Inspect management reachability.
Review privileged access.
Verify destructive-operation protection.
Verify retention locks.
Review logging.
controls.applicability: Applies to storage platforms holding in-scope training data, checkpoints and model artefacts.
failureModes: Compromised admin deleting all snapshots
Ransomware encrypting checkpoint tier
Retention lock shortened by admin
controls.testingSafety: Do not execute destructive operations to test protections; use a test volume in a non-production namespace.
controls.unknownRule: If immutability cannot be verified, treat recovery copies as mutable (U7) in recovery analysis.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (Security and privacy controls)

controls.title: Security Zoning
controls.objective: Ensure the facility OT, infrastructure management, AI control-plane, tenant and corporate environments are partitioned into security zones with defined conduits, so that compromise in one zone cannot reach consequential authority in another.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall maintain a zone-and-conduit model covering facility OT (BMS, EPMS, CDU, PLC, fire and physical security integrations), infrastructure management (BMC, PDU, switch management, OOB), AI control planes, storage management, tenant and corporate networks and external connections, with each conduit's permitted flows, protocols and direction, and the security level target per zone. The OT security owner shall reconcile the as-built network (firewall rules, VLAN/VRF configuration, physical links, wireless and cellular devices) to the model at a defined interval and after change, and shall record every undocumented path (including dual-homed hosts and vendor-installed modems) as a Finding.
assessmentCriteria: A zone-and-conduit model covers all listed environments with permitted flows and SL-T.
Firewall, VLAN/VRF and routing configuration reconcile to the model.
Dual-homed hosts, unmanaged switches, wireless and cellular devices bridging zones are discovered and dispositioned.
Conduits between OT and IT pass through defined boundary devices (for example an industrial DMZ) with no direct routed path.
Reconciliation was performed in the interval and after material change.
minimumEvidence: Passive discovery results (for example network traffic analysis) for undocumented paths

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I2
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Reconciliation within interval; passive discovery covering at least 30 days (illustrative).
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation and discovery by a party independent of the network implementers.
acceptableAlternatives: Physical inspection of OT network cabinets for undocumented links where passive monitoring is not deployed
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-07 cannot PASS while an undocumented path into a power or cooling control zone cannot be ruled out.

assessmentProcedure: Review the zone-and-conduit model against the environment inventory.
Reconcile firewall, VLAN/VRF and routing configuration to permitted conduits.
Review passive discovery for undocumented flows and bridging devices.
Inspect a sample of OT cabinets for unmanaged switches and modems.
Confirm dispositions of discovered paths.
controls.applicability: Applies to all in-scope sites and environments. Physical zoning is PHY-009; this control covers network and logical zones.
failureModes: Vendor cellular modem bridging BMS to internet
Dual-homed historian linking corporate IT and OT
Flat management network spanning BMC and BMS
Unreviewed any-any rule in conduit
controls.testingSafety: Discovery in OT zones shall be passive (traffic mirroring) unless active scanning is authorised in writing by the facility owner and OT security owner after vendor consultation; active scans of controllers can disrupt them.
controls.unknownRule: Zones without discovery coverage are recorded with U5 and treated as potentially bridged in authority-path analysis.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 (Security risk assessment, zones and conduits)
ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)

controls.title: Management-Plane Segmentation
controls.objective: Ensure management planes (BMC/IPMI/Redfish, switch management, PDU, hypervisor and Kubernetes administrative APIs, storage management) are segmented so that tenant, workload and corporate networks cannot reach them, and so that one management plane cannot be used to pivot to another.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall segment each management plane into its own zone, shall disable insecure management protocols (for example IPMI over LAN where Redfish is available, unauthenticated SNMP versions, Telnet), shall restrict BMC access to brokered administrative paths, and shall prevent host operating systems from reaching their own or other BMCs over the network except where required and approved. The infrastructure security owner shall test at a defined interval from representative tenant, workload and corporate vantage points that management interfaces are unreachable and that pivoting between management planes is blocked.
assessmentCriteria: Each management plane is a distinct zone with permitted conduits only.
Insecure management protocols are disabled on BMCs, switches and PDUs (sampled configuration).
Host-to-BMC network access and in-band BMC interfaces are disabled or approved.
Reachability tests from tenant, workload and corporate vantage points found no management interface reachable.
Pivot tests between management planes (for example BMC zone to OT zone) found paths blocked.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Test within interval.
evidenceProfile.independence: Tests by security function or independent tester.
acceptableAlternatives: Rule-base analysis with path computation tooling where active tests are not authorised
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while BMC or control-plane reachability from tenant workloads is untested.

assessmentProcedure: Review management zone design.
Sample protocol configuration on BMCs, switches and PDUs.
Run or review reachability tests from tenant, workload and corporate vantage points.
Run or review pivot tests between management planes.
controls.applicability: Applies to all management planes of in-scope infrastructure.
failureModes: Tenant workload reaching BMCs and reflashing firmware
IPMI cipher weaknesses exploited
Pivot from BMC zone to BMS
PDU web interface reachable from corporate network
controls.testingSafety: Reachability and pivot tests shall attempt connection only and shall not authenticate or issue commands; they require written authorisation from the security owner, and from the facility owner for any test touching OT zones.
controls.unknownRule: Vantage points not tested are recorded with U5; untested pairs of management planes are treated as connected.
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (Security and privacy controls)

controls.title: Filtering and Gateways
controls.objective: Ensure conduits between zones are enforced by managed boundary devices whose rule sets are minimal, reviewed and monitored, including industrial DMZs, unidirectional gateways and API gateways for automation.
controls.requirement: The security operations manager shall operate boundary devices on every conduit in the zone model with deny-by-default rule sets, documented business justification and owner for each rule, review of rules at a defined interval, removal of unused rules, and logging of denied and permitted consequential flows to security telemetry. The OT security owner shall use unidirectional or protocol-break gateways where the zone model requires one-way data export from power and cooling control zones.
assessmentCriteria: Every conduit is enforced by a managed boundary device with deny-by-default.
Each rule has justification and owner; any-any or overly broad rules are absent or approved.
Rule reviews occurred in the interval with unused rules removed.
Required unidirectional or protocol-break gateways are deployed for OT data export.
Boundary logs are forwarded to security telemetry.
minimumEvidence: Boundary device inventory mapped to conduits

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: 12 months (illustrative) of reviews.
evidenceProfile.independence: Rule analysis by assessor using exported rule sets.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3: unreviewed rules condition CG-07/CG-15 evaluation.

assessmentProcedure: Map boundary devices to conduits.
Analyse rule sets for breadth and justification.
Review rule review records.
Verify gateways for OT export.
Check log forwarding.
controls.applicability: Applies to every conduit in the SEC-009 model.
failureModes: Temporary vendor rule left open
Bidirectional path where one-way export intended
Rule sprawl hiding consequential paths
controls.testingSafety: Rule analysis is offline; any active validation follows SEC-010 testing restrictions.
controls.unknownRule: Conduits without an identified enforcing device are treated as open (U1).
informativeReferences: ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 (System security requirements and security levels)
NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (Guide to operational technology security)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (Security and privacy controls)

controls.title: Remote Access
controls.objective: Ensure all remote access to OT, infrastructure management and AI control planes, especially by vendors and OEMs, is brokered, approved per session, time-bound, monitored and revocable.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall permit remote access to in-scope systems only through a managed remote-access gateway that enforces individual identity, MFA, per-session approval by the system owner for vendor and OEM access, time limits, session recording and the ability to terminate sessions in real time, and shall prohibit persistent vendor connections, vendor-installed remote-access tools and modems. The OT security owner shall require that remote sessions to power and cooling control systems with write or command capability are supervised by an on-site or on-shift authorised operator.
assessmentCriteria: All remote access paths to in-scope systems traverse the managed gateway (no alternative paths found in discovery).
Vendor/OEM sessions require per-session approval and are time-limited.
Sessions are recorded and can be terminated in real time (demonstrated).
Persistent vendor connections and unmanaged remote tools are absent.
Remote write/command sessions to OT systems were supervised (sampled).
Revocation of a vendor's access takes effect within the defined time (tested).

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Six months (illustrative) of sessions; revocation test within 12 months.
evidenceProfile.independence: Discovery and revocation tests by security function.
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4: CG-15 cannot PASS while an unmanaged remote path into OT or control planes cannot be ruled out.

assessmentProcedure: Review remote access architecture.
Review discovery results for alternative paths and vendor tools.
Sample sessions for approval, recording and supervision.
Witness real-time termination and revocation test.

controls.title: Secure Baseline
controls.objective: Ensure OT controllers, BMCs, accelerator nodes, NICs, switches and control-plane hosts run hardened configurations and integrity-verified firmware with secure boot, so that tampered or insecure states are prevented or detected.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall define secure configuration baselines for each in-scope device class, including disabled unused services, credential policy, logging, and for firmware-bearing devices the approved signed firmware versions, secure boot enablement, firmware rollback protection and measured boot where supported. The platform security lead shall verify compliance with the baseline at a defined interval using automated assessment or attestation and shall record non-compliant devices as Findings.

controls.title: Vulnerability Management
controls.objective: Ensure vulnerabilities in OT, infrastructure management, firmware and AI control-plane components are identified, prioritised by exploitability and infrastructure consequence, and remediated or mitigated within defined times.

The security operations manager shall report overdue items to governance.

controls.title: Patch Governance
controls.objective: Ensure security patches and firmware updates to OT and infrastructure are tested for compatibility and operational impact, staged to avoid common-mode failure, and applied within defined times.
controls.requirement: The change authority shall require that patches and firmware updates to OT controllers, BMCs, NICs, switches, accelerator nodes and control planes are tested on representative test systems, approved by the system owner and, for OT, the vendor where required, applied in stages that never update all redundant members or all fault domains simultaneously, and verified after application with rollback available. The security operations manager shall measure patch latency against defined targets.

controls.title: Exception and Compensating Control
controls.objective: Ensure security exceptions (unpatchable OT, legacy protocols, missing MFA) are approved by appropriate authority, time-bound and backed by verified compensating controls.
controls.requirement: The infrastructure security owner shall maintain a security exception register for in-scope systems recording the deviation, risk assessment including infrastructure consequence, compensating controls, approver at the authority level required by consequence, and expiry. The infrastructure security owner shall verify compensating controls are in place before approval and at renewal.

controls.title: Security Telemetry
controls.objective: Ensure security-relevant logs and events from OT, management planes, control planes, remote access and identity systems are collected centrally with integrity, time synchronisation and retention sufficient for detection and investigation.
controls.requirement: The security operations manager shall collect security telemetry from identity providers, PAM, remote-access gateways, boundary devices, BMCs, network devices, fabric controllers, cluster managers, storage controllers and OT passive monitoring (including controller write and program-change events), with time synchronised to NET-024 sources, integrity protection, and retention per the evidence retention class, and shall monitor source health and alert on silent sources.
assessmentCriteria: Telemetry sources cover all listed classes with gaps recorded.
OT passive monitoring captures controller write and program-change events.

controls.title: Behaviour Detection
controls.objective: Ensure detection of anomalous or malicious behaviour against infrastructure authority, including unexpected OT writes, BMC firmware operations, mass configuration changes, privilege escalation and anomalous automation actions.
controls.requirement: The security operations manager shall maintain detection use cases mapped to infrastructure threat scenarios (for example ATT&CK for ICS techniques and AIDCF-004 scenarios X05, X08, X15), covering unexpected controller writes or program changes, BMC firmware update or power commands outside change windows, mass configuration pushes, privilege escalation, anomalous remote sessions and automation acting outside its scope, and shall validate detection effectiveness by safe simulation at a defined interval.
assessmentCriteria: Detection use cases map to listed infrastructure scenarios.
Use cases cover OT writes, BMC operations, mass config, privilege escalation, remote sessions and automation scope violations.
Simulations in the interval demonstrated detection and alert triage within target time.
Missed detections were remediated.

controls.title: Incident Containment
controls.objective: Ensure cyber and cyber-physical incidents affecting infrastructure can be contained without causing unsafe states or unnecessary loss of AI service, with pre-approved containment actions and safety-coordinated decision-making.
controls.requirement: The security operations manager shall maintain incident playbooks for infrastructure scenarios (BMS/EPMS compromise, BMC compromise, control-plane compromise, malicious automation, vendor account compromise) that define pre-approved containment actions (credential revocation, conduit closure, session termination, controller isolation to local or manual control), the safety checks required before each action, and the decision authority. The facility owner shall ensure that OT containment actions are coordinated with facility operations so that isolating supervisory control does not remove cooling or power continuity, and the security operations manager shall exercise the playbooks at a defined interval.
assessmentCriteria: Playbooks exist for each listed scenario with containment actions, safety checks and authority.
OT containment actions specify the safe fallback (local/manual control, last-good setpoints) and facility operations role.
Containment actions are technically available (for example conduit closure capability verified).
Exercises in the interval executed containment decisions and actions (or simulations) within target time.
Containment does not depend on systems likely to be compromised in the scenario.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3

evidenceProfile.independence: Exercises observed by an independent party.
acceptableAlternatives: Analysed real incidents demonstrating containment

Verify containment capability.

Check dependencies of containment actions.

No authority to sever vendor access
Delayed decision allows spread

controls.title: Forensic Readiness
controls.objective: Ensure that evidence needed to investigate infrastructure incidents (logs, controller programs, firmware images, session recordings) is preserved with chain of custody and that collection does not endanger operations.
controls.requirement: The security operations manager shall define forensic collection procedures for each in-scope system class, including OT controllers and BMCs, specifying what to collect, how to collect safely, and chain-of-custody requirements, and shall ensure retention and legal hold capability for telemetry and session recordings. The OT security owner shall ensure baseline copies of controller programs and firmware hashes are available for comparison.

controls.title: Agent or Automation Authority
controls.objective: Ensure every AI agent, automation pipeline and closed-loop controller that can act on infrastructure has an explicit, bounded and inventoried authority scope, so that tool-mediated actions cannot exceed what the owner approved.
controls.requirement: The automation owner shall register every agent, automation and closed-loop control that can observe, configure, command, bypass, update or recover infrastructure (including AIOps remediation, cooling optimisation loops, power capping, network automation and AI agents with tool access), stating its effective identity, tools and APIs, target systems, permitted actions, rate and magnitude limits, operating states in which it may act, and its human owner. The infrastructure security owner shall reconcile registered scope with effective permissions at a defined interval and shall prohibit any automation from holding cross-domain command or bypass authority without approval under SEC-003.
assessmentCriteria: All automations and agents with infrastructure authority are registered with identity, tools, targets, actions, limits, states and owner.

No automation holds unapproved cross-domain command or bypass authority.
Telemetry-to-command coupling is analysed for sensor-trust dependency (AIDCF-005 pattern).

The infrastructure security owner shall verify by test that approval cannot be bypassed by the automation's own identity.

controls.title: Command Allowlisting
controls.objective: Ensure that only explicitly allowlisted commands, write operations and parameter ranges can be issued to power, cooling and critical infrastructure controllers by any automated or remote actor, enforced at a point the actor cannot modify.

The OT security owner shall test at a defined interval that out-of-list writes and out-of-range values are blocked and alarmed.

controls.title: Evidence Taxonomy
controls.objective: Ensure that every in-scope control has an Evidence Requirement profile expressed in the AIDCF-008 vocabulary (classes E1-E7, quality floor, sufficiency floor, state and period coverage, independence), and that any local evidence subtypes map unambiguously to those classes.
