evidenceProfile.independence: Hash verification run by the assessor with an independent tool
mandatoryItems: EvidenceManifests for decisions in the period
acceptableAlternatives: Write-once storage with an external manifest generated per decision
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: reproducibility of decisions uncertain; affected decisions treated as integrity-uncertain for CG-11

assessmentProcedure: Export repository configuration and verify identifier immutability and overwrite protection.
Sample Evidence Objects and check mandatory and conditional metadata.
Retrieve manifests for decisions in the period.
Recompute hashes with an independent tool and compare.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme issuing Assurance Decisions.
failureModes: Evidence overwritten with a newer version under the same ID
Decision cannot be reproduced because its evidence set is unknown
Telemetry evidence without source clock or query
Missing collector identity
controls.testingSafety: Hash recomputation uses read-only access to stored objects; no object is modified.
controls.unknownRule: If a decision's manifest cannot be retrieved, record a U1 UNKNOWN against that decision's evidence basis and refer it to MCF-EVA-024 for suspension review.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-014 End-to-End Traceability and Machine-Executable Data Standard
ISO 14721 (open archival information system reference model)

controls.title: Retention and Protection
controls.objective: Ensure that assurance evidence is retained according to its retention class, protected according to its classification, preserved under legal hold, and recoverable after loss of the repository, so that decisions remain reviewable and challengeable throughout their validity.
controls.requirement: The evidence lead shall assign each Evidence Object a retention class (R0-R5) and a classification level, define retention periods by legal, contractual and decision-validity requirements, apply legal holds when instructed, and record authorised destruction. The tool owner shall back up the repository, including manifests and custody logs, to a separate fault domain and shall test restoration at the restoration test interval, verifying hashes and custody logs after restore.
assessmentCriteria: Every Evidence Object in the sample has a retention class and classification.
Retention periods are defined and no Evidence Object supporting a decision still within its validity or challenge period was destroyed.
Legal holds in the period were applied to all relevant objects and destruction was blocked.
Backups of objects, manifests and custody logs are held in a fault domain separate from the primary repository.
A restoration test within the interval restored a representative sample and hashes and custody logs verified after restore.
Access controls enforce classification, and restricted evidence access is logged.
minimumEvidence: Sample of object retention and classification attributes
Backup configuration showing separate fault domain
Restoration test record with hash verification

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Retention events over twelve months and the latest restoration test
evidenceProfile.independence: Restoration test observed or verified by the assessor; hash comparison performed independently
mandatoryItems: Backup configuration showing separate fault domain
Restoration test record with hash verification
acceptableAlternatives: Restoration from an actual repository incident, with verification records, in place of a test
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: future challenge and reassessment of decisions may be impossible; decision condition recorded
reassessmentTriggers: Change of retention law or contract

assessmentProcedure: Review retention schedule and classification policy.
Sample objects and verify attributes and that none supporting a valid decision was destroyed.
Review legal hold application.
Inspect backup configuration for fault-domain separation.
Examine or observe a restoration test and recompute hashes on restored objects.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme retaining evidence beyond a single engagement.
failureModes: Evidence destroyed before challenge period ends
Backups in the same storage system as the primary
Restored evidence fails hash verification unnoticed
Classified evidence accessible to all assessors
controls.testingSafety: Restoration tests use an isolated restore target; production repository content is never overwritten by a restore test.
controls.unknownRule: If restoration has never been tested, the RESILIENCE claim is UNKNOWN (U1); backup existence alone supports only IMPLEMENTATION.

controls.title: Source Provenance
controls.objective: Ensure that every accepted Evidence Object has an established origin, authority and collection lineage, including derived and AI-assisted evidence whose sources, transformation and human review are recorded, so that no conclusion rests on evidence of unknown origin.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall ensure that, before an Evidence Object is accepted, its source, collector, collection activity and authority are recorded and verified; that derived evidence records source Evidence IDs, query or script and version, assumptions and reviewer; and that AI-assisted extraction, summarisation or classification is recorded with model and version, process record and the accountable human review, and is treated as candidate evidence that does not corroborate its own sources.
assessmentCriteria: Every accepted Evidence Object in the sample has recorded source, collector, collection activity and authority.
Provenance was verified (for example extraction witnessed, issuer confirmed) for evidence supporting gate-CRITICAL controls.
Derived evidence records source IDs, transformation method and version, assumptions and reviewer.
AI-assisted evidence records model and version, process record and human reviewer, and is not used as independent corroboration of its sources.
No Evidence Object with P rating below the profile floor supports a CONFORMING result.
minimumEvidence: Sample of accepted Evidence Object provenance records
Collection activity records for gate-supporting evidence

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F3 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Evidence accepted for assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reperforms provenance verification for a sub-sample at source
mandatoryItems: Sample of accepted Evidence Object provenance records
acceptableAlternatives: W3C PROV-compatible provenance graph export in place of per-object records
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results may become UNKNOWN (U6); CG-11 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Sample accepted Evidence Objects, weighted to those supporting CRITICAL controls.
Check provenance fields and verification records.
Trace derived evidence to sources and re-run one transformation.
Inspect AI-assisted processing records and confirm human review and non-use as corroboration.
Reperform provenance verification at source for a sub-sample.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme accepting evidence; AI-assisted criteria apply only where AI-assisted processing is used.
failureModes: Screenshot of a configuration accepted with no record of who captured it or from where
Derived capacity analysis whose source telemetry cannot be identified
AI summary of commissioning reports treated as corroboration
Provider attestation with unverified issuer
controls.testingSafety: Reperformance of extraction at source is read-only and performed by the system owner under observation.
controls.unknownRule: Evidence whose origin cannot be established is recorded as U6 and is excluded from support of any CONFORMING result.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 27037 (identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence)

controls.title: Integrity and Custody
controls.objective: Ensure that alteration of evidence or loss of custody is detected, so that evidence supporting gates and decisions can be shown to be the evidence originally collected.
controls.requirement: The evidence lead shall ensure that every Evidence Object supporting a gate result or Assurance Decision has an integrity value computed at collection, an integrity level (I0-I5) assigned, and a custody log; that integrity values are re-verified before decision issue and on retrieval for challenge or reassessment; and that integrity failures are recorded, investigated and the affected evidence withdrawn from support. The evidence lead shall test detection at least once per integrity test interval by a controlled tamper exercise on test objects.
assessmentCriteria: Every gate-supporting Evidence Object in the sample has an integrity value from collection, an integrity level and a custody log.
Integrity values were re-verified before each decision issue in the period.
Integrity failures in the period were recorded, investigated and the affected evidence withdrawn from support.
A controlled tamper exercise within the interval was detected by the integrity mechanism.
Redactions preserved a controlled unredacted source and recorded basis and method.
minimumEvidence: Integrity values and custody logs for sampled evidence

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C3 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Decisions issued in the last twelve months and the latest tamper exercise
evidenceProfile.independence: Tamper exercise designed by a party other than the repository administrators
mandatoryItems: Integrity values and custody logs for sampled evidence
acceptableAlternatives: Detection of a real integrity event, with investigation record, in place of a tamper exercise
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected evidence treated as U7; dependent gate results may become UNKNOWN under CG-11

assessmentProcedure: Sample gate-supporting evidence and check integrity values, levels and custody logs.
Verify pre-decision re-verification records.
Review integrity failure handling.
Examine the tamper exercise design and result; reperform verification on a sub-sample.
Review redaction records.
controls.applicability: Applies to all evidence supporting gate results or Assurance Decisions.
failureModes: Test report edited after collection to remove an anomaly
Custody gap during provider transfer
Integrity values computed only after editing
Redaction removes content without a controlled original
controls.testingSafety: Tamper exercises use dedicated test objects in a non-production area of the repository, with the evidence lead's written approval; real evidence is never altered.
controls.unknownRule: Any Evidence Object whose integrity cannot be re-verified is recorded as U7 and withdrawn from support until re-collected or independently corroborated.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 27037 (identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence)
ISO/IEC 27042 (analysis and interpretation of digital evidence)

controls.title: Relevance and Reliability
controls.objective: Ensure that each Evidence Object is rated for fitness to the precise assertion and for reliability of its method and source, with rationale, so that reliable but irrelevant evidence (for example a design document cited for an operation claim) does not support a result.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall ensure that every Evidence Object used to support a Control Assessment is rated on all six AIDCF-008 quality dimensions with rationale, that the fitness (F) rating considers subject, criterion, claim type, configuration and operating state, that the reliability (R) rating considers method repeatability and corroboration, and that a second assessor independently re-rates a sample with differences resolved and recorded.
assessmentCriteria: Every supporting Evidence Object in the sample has P, F, C, R, T and I ratings with rationale.
F ratings reflect claim type and operating state; no E1 design evidence alone supports an OPERATION, EFFECTIVENESS or RESILIENCE claim.
Independent re-rating of a sample agrees within one point on each dimension, or differences were resolved and recorded.
No Evidence Object below the profile quality floor supports a CONFORMING result.
Quality vectors are retained and not collapsed to a single averaged number.

parameters.name: Independent re-rating sample
parameters.basis: Programme parameter; illustrative, minimum of 10 objects

minimumEvidence: Quality ratings with rationale for sampled evidence
Control Assessments with supporting evidence lists

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Re-rating by an assessor who did not perform the original rating
mandatoryItems: Quality ratings with rationale for sampled evidence
acceptableAlternatives: Assessor re-rates a sample during this assessment if no re-rating records exist, with a Finding raised
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: result support uncertain; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Sample Control Assessments and their supporting evidence.
Check quality ratings and rationale.
Test claim-type fitness, especially E1-only support for higher claims.
Reperform ratings for a sub-sample and compare.
Compare ratings with profile floors for CONFORMING results.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Control Assessment that relies on evidence, which is every Control Assessment other than NOT_APPLICABLE dispositions.
failureModes: Design drawing accepted as proof of operation
Vendor datasheet accepted as proof of installed configuration
Ratings inflated to meet floors
Single averaged quality score hides a weak integrity rating
controls.testingSafety: Desk re-rating of evidence records only; source systems are not accessed for this control.
controls.unknownRule: Where reviewers cannot agree on a rating after discussion, record a U9 UNKNOWN on the evidence and apply the lower rating until resolved.
informativeReferences: ISO 19011 (guidelines for auditing management systems) - audit evidence
ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information)

controls.title: Currency and Coverage
controls.objective: Ensure that evidence is current for the state asserted and covers the required population, locations, period, operating states and scenarios, so that a result is not extrapolated beyond what the evidence represents.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall ensure that each Evidence Object used to support a result is checked against the AIDCF-008 freshness basis for its category and against any material change since collection, and that each Control Assessment records coverage across entity, population, location, time, operating state, scenario, tenant or workload, and dependency dimensions, with gaps recorded as U3 or U5 UNKNOWN Records.
assessmentCriteria: Every supporting Evidence Object in the sample was checked for currency against its category basis and for intervening material change.
Each sampled Control Assessment records coverage across the AIDCF-008 coverage dimensions relevant to its claim type.
Evidence predating a material change to its subject is not used without re-validation.
Coverage gaps (for example no evidence from DEGRADED or MAINTENANCE states) are recorded as U5 UNKNOWN Records.
No result is stated for a population, state or period broader than the evidence covers.
minimumEvidence: Coverage records in sampled Control Assessments
Change log for subjects of sampled evidence
UNKNOWN Records for currency and coverage gaps

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor compares evidence dates with the change log independently
mandatoryItems: Coverage records in sampled Control Assessments
Change log for subjects of sampled evidence
acceptableAlternatives: Machine-generated freshness flags from the assessment tool, if the rules are verified
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results may be STALE; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Sample Control Assessments and their evidence.
Compare evidence dates with the freshness basis and change log.
Check coverage records against the relevant dimensions.
Confirm coverage gaps are recorded as UNKNOWN Records.
Compare stated result scope with evidence coverage.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Control Assessment at OPERATION claim type or above, and to DESIGN and IMPLEMENTATION assessments where evidence predates a material change.
failureModes: Commissioning test from before a cooling conversion used for current effectiveness
UPS test on one of four modules extrapolated to all
No maintenance-state evidence yet maintenance-state claim made
Telemetry from one hall used for a multi-hall instance
controls.testingSafety: Desk analysis only.
controls.unknownRule: Evidence that predates a material change is recorded as U3 for the changed subject; coverage gaps are recorded as U5 with the missing dimension named.
informativeReferences: ISO 2859-1 (sampling procedures for inspection by attributes)

controls.title: Decision Question
controls.objective: Ensure that each assessment answers a precisely stated decision question (for example 'Can Capability Instance X sustain training goodput within tolerance through loss of one CDU per pod, as of date D?') that names the Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, tolerances, operating states, intended users and prohibited interpretations.
controls.requirement: The decision authority shall approve, before fieldwork begins, a decision question for each assessment that states the Capability Instance, the Service Outcomes and tolerances in question, the operating states, the as-of date or period, the intended users and use, and the interpretations the conclusion shall not support. The lead assessor shall frame the assurance case top claim from the approved decision question and shall obtain re-approval if the question changes during the assessment.
assessmentCriteria: An approved decision question exists for each assessment, dated before fieldwork.
The question names Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, tolerances, operating states, as-of date or period, intended users and use, and prohibited interpretations.
The assurance case top claim is derived from the decision question without broadening it.
Changes to the question during the assessment were re-approved by the decision authority.
The report and Assurance Statement restate the same decision question.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C3 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: The assessment under review
evidenceProfile.independence: Approval by the decision authority, separate from the lead assessor
acceptableAlternatives: Engagement letter containing all required elements, approved by the decision authority
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: decision question undefined; CG-01 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE
reassessmentTriggers: Change in intended users or use
Change of Capability Instance or Service Outcome in scope

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the approved decision question and check required elements and approval date.
Compare the top claim with the question.
Review change records for the question.
Compare the question restated in the report and statement.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that produces an Assurance Decision.
failureModes: Assessment asks 'is the data centre resilient?' with no instance, outcome or state
Conclusion used for a purchase decision it was not designed for
Top claim broader than the approved question
Question changed mid-assessment without approval
controls.testingSafety: Desk review of engagement records only; draft decision questions are treated as confidential to the commissioning party.
controls.unknownRule: If no approved decision question exists, record a US5 UNKNOWN Record; no Assurance Decision above INCONCLUSIVE may be issued.
informativeReferences: ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information) - engagement acceptance

controls.title: Scope and Criteria
controls.objective: Ensure that each assessment has an approved boundary (physical, logical, organisational, provider and temporal), applicable criteria (AIDCF artifact and capability-profile versions, applicable controls, claim types, gates), and visible exclusions with their residual effect.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall prepare, and the decision authority shall approve before fieldwork, a scope record for each assessment stating the boundary across physical, logical, organisational, provider and temporal dimensions; the operating states assessed; the applicable AIDCF artifact and capability-profile versions; the applicable controls with claim types; the applicable gates; and every exclusion with rationale and residual effect on the decision. The lead assessor shall reconcile the boundary to the ArchitectureSnapshot (MCF-CAP-004) and record any element of the snapshot that is neither in scope nor excluded.
assessmentCriteria: An approved scope record exists, dated before fieldwork, covering all five boundary dimensions and the operating states.
Applicable criteria are identified by version, including the control set with claim types and the gate set.
Every exclusion has rationale and residual effect on the decision.
Reconciliation to the ArchitectureSnapshot leaves no element neither in scope nor excluded.
Shared and external dependencies crossing the boundary are listed with how they are assessed (directly, by provider evidence, or as UNKNOWN).
minimumEvidence: Applicable control and gate list with claim types

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: The assessment under review
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation reperformed by the independent reviewer for a sample of snapshot elements
acceptableAlternatives: Machine-readable scope object in the assessment tool, exported with approval history
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US5 Systemic: assessment boundary unresolved; CG-02 Gate Result UNKNOWN and decision capped at INCONCLUSIVE

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the approved scope record and check dimensions, states and approval date.
Check criteria versions, control set and gate set.
Review exclusions for rationale and residual effect.
Reperform boundary reconciliation for a sample of snapshot elements.
Check treatment of cross-boundary dependencies.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment, including delta assessments after material change, which require their own scope record.
failureModes: Utility supply excluded with no residual effect stated
Provider-operated cooling plant neither in scope nor excluded
Criteria version not stated, so results are unreproducible
Maintenance state silently omitted from scope
controls.testingSafety: Desk review and graph reconciliation using read-only queries; no site access is required.
controls.unknownRule: Any ArchitectureSnapshot element that is neither in scope nor excluded is recorded as a US5 UNKNOWN Record against the boundary.
informativeReferences: ISO 19011 (guidelines for auditing management systems) - audit scope and criteria

controls.title: Sampling and Testing
controls.objective: Ensure that sampling is risk-based, reproducible and not over-extrapolated, and that tests are authorised, safe, defined in advance (initial state, method, expected result, abort criteria, restoration) and recorded with anomalies.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall document, for each sample, the population and its frame, strata, selection method, sample size rationale, exclusions and expansion rule, and shall record failed samples and their effect. For each test, the lead assessor shall obtain written authorisation from the system owner and, for hazardous or service-affecting tests, the safety authority, and shall record the initial state, method, expected result, abort criteria, instrumentation, restoration steps, result and anomalies. Tests shall be performed by authorised operators; assessors shall observe.
assessmentCriteria: Each sample in the assessment has documented population frame, strata, method, size rationale, exclusions and expansion rule.
Judgemental samples are not represented as statistical coverage, and sampled results are not extrapolated beyond the represented population and conditions.
Failed samples triggered expansion or were reflected in the result.
Every test has prior written authorisation from the system owner and, where hazardous or service-affecting, the safety authority.
Every test record contains initial state, method, expected result, abort criteria, instrumentation, restoration, result and anomalies.
Tests were performed by authorised operators, with assessors observing.
minimumEvidence: Test records with required conditional metadata

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: The assessment under review
evidenceProfile.independence: Independent reviewer reperforms selection from the population frame for one sample
mandatoryItems: Test records with required conditional metadata
acceptableAlternatives: Use of the operator's own test records as evidence, if they contain the required metadata and authorisation
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected results may be over-extrapolated or unsafe to rely on; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Review sampling plans for required elements.
Reperform selection for one sample from the population frame.
Check expansion after failed samples and absence of over-extrapolation.
Check test authorisations and safety authority sign-off for hazardous tests.
Check test records for required metadata and operator/observer roles.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that samples or tests.
failureModes: Assessor operates switchgear during a test
Test performed without abort criteria and fails to restore
Three good samples extrapolated to an entire fleet
Failed sample discarded
controls.testingSafety: This control governs safety of all assessment testing: hazardous-energy, pressurised-fluid, refrigerant, battery and service-affecting tests require written authorisation from the system owner and the safety authority, a method statement, initial-state verification, abort criteria, permits under the site safe system of work and restoration steps. The safety authority may stop any test at any time; a stopped test is recorded with its partial result and does not count as passed.
controls.unknownRule: If a test lacks authorisation records, its result is excluded from support and recorded as U8 (method uncertain); it is not re-run without authorisation.
informativeReferences: ISO 2859-1 (sampling procedures for inspection by attributes)
ISO 19011 (guidelines for auditing management systems) - audit sampling

controls.title: Specialist Involvement
controls.objective: Ensure that domain specialists (electrical, mechanical, compute, storage and network, OT security, resilience, evidence and data) approve the technical methods and conclusions in their domains, and that reliance on specialists is recorded with scope, competence and responsibility.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall identify, for each assessment, the domains requiring specialist judgement, appoint a competent specialist for each (MCF-GOV-023), and record the specialist's scope, competence evidence and responsibility. Each specialist shall approve the methods and the Control Assessment results in their domain. Where a specialist is external, the lead assessor shall evaluate their independence and the transferability of their conclusions.
assessmentCriteria: Domains requiring specialist judgement are identified for the assessment.
Each identified domain has an appointed specialist with recorded scope, competence evidence and responsibility.
Methods and Control Assessment results in each specialist domain carry the specialist's approval.
External specialists' independence and transferability of conclusions were evaluated.
No technical conclusion in a specialist domain was issued without specialist approval.
minimumEvidence: Specialist approvals on methods and results

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F3 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: The assessment under review
evidenceProfile.independence: Independent reviewer confirms coverage of specialist domains
mandatoryItems: Specialist approvals on methods and results
acceptableAlternatives: Specialist report with explicit scope and sign-off, incorporated by reference
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: affected domain results carry CONF-2 ceiling and a decision condition

assessmentProcedure: Review domain identification against scope.
Check appointments and reliance records.
Reconcile results in each domain to specialist approvals.
Review external specialist evaluations.
Interview one specialist on scope and approval.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that includes technical infrastructure domains.
failureModes: Generalist assessor concludes on protection coordination
OEM engineer acts as independent specialist for their own product
Specialist reviews methods but not results
Liquid-cooling domain not identified as needing a specialist
controls.testingSafety: Record review and interview only.
controls.unknownRule: If specialist approval is missing for a domain result, that result is UNKNOWN (U9 interpretation unresolved) until approved.
informativeReferences: ISO 19011 (guidelines for auditing management systems) - technical experts
ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information) - use of experts

controls.title: Finding Traceability
controls.objective: Ensure that every Finding is traceable to the criterion, the evidenced condition, the supporting and challenging evidence, the affected Service Outcomes, controls and gates, and to its action and closure evidence.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall record every Finding with a stable identifier, criterion (control and assessment criterion), condition, supporting and challenging Evidence Object references, cause where evidenced or labelled as analysis, consequence for Service Outcomes, dependencies and states, classification, and gate and score effect. The action owner shall record closure evidence, and the lead assessor shall close a Finding only after re-assessing that evidence.
assessmentCriteria: Every Finding in the sample has identifier, criterion, condition, evidence references, consequence, classification and gate/score effect.
Cause is either evidenced or explicitly labelled as analysis.
Each Finding is linked in the graph to its control, Service Outcomes and gates.
Closed Findings have closure evidence re-assessed by an assessor, not closed on management assertion.
Findings are not deleted; superseded Findings retain history.
minimumEvidence: Sampled Finding records with evidence links
Graph links from Findings to controls, outcomes and gates

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Findings raised or closed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor selects Findings from the full register including closed and superseded items
mandatoryItems: Sampled Finding records with evidence links
acceptableAlternatives: Findings exported from the assessment tool in AIDCF-014 format with history
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: residual deficiency status uncertain; decision condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: Extract the full Findings register including closed and superseded items.
Sample Findings and check required fields and evidence references.
Check graph links to controls, outcomes and gates.
Verify closure evidence and re-assessment for closed Findings.
Compare register history for deletions.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that raises Findings.
failureModes: Finding closed on an email saying 'fixed'
Finding with no link to the gate it affects
Cause speculated without evidence
Embarrassing Finding deleted
controls.testingSafety: Review of Findings records only; closure evidence involving site changes is verified under the relevant domain control.
controls.unknownRule: If a Finding's evidence references cannot be resolved to Evidence Objects, record a U1 UNKNOWN on the Finding and keep it open.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard
ISO 19011 (guidelines for auditing management systems) - audit findings

controls.title: UNKNOWN Preservation
controls.objective: Ensure that missing, inaccessible, stale, conflicting or unverifiable knowledge is recorded as an UNKNOWN Record with type, severity and decision effect, carried unchanged into gates, scores, decisions and reports, and never silently resolved favourably.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall record every UNKNOWN as an UNKNOWN Record with subject, missing attribute, type (U1-U10), severity (US1-US5) with the test that determined it, reason, potential consequence, evidence needed, owner, status and gate and decision effect. The decision authority shall ensure that every US3, US4 and US5 UNKNOWN Record is reflected in the Gate Results, decision ceiling and report, and that UNKNOWN Records are closed only by new evidence or approved re-scoping, never by assumption.
assessmentCriteria: Every UNKNOWN Record in the sample has all required fields including type and severity with the test applied.
Severity was assigned top-down by the US5-to-US1 tests; reperformance yields the same severity.
Every US4 UNKNOWN Record is reflected as a gate UNKNOWN and every US5 caps the decision at INCONCLUSIVE.
Every US3 and above UNKNOWN Record appears in the report with decision effect.
A seeded or traced set of UNKNOWNs survived unchanged from workpaper to report.
Closed UNKNOWN Records cite new evidence or approved re-scoping.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Traceability test designed and scored by the independent reviewer
acceptableAlternatives: Reperformance by the assessor tracing every US3+ UNKNOWN Record of one completed assessment from workpaper to report
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: the reliability of every Gate Result is in doubt; CG-12 evaluation cannot conclude and decisions are capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: Assessment tool change affecting UNKNOWN handling

assessmentProcedure: Extract the UNKNOWN register and sample records.
Check required fields and reperform severity assignment.
Reconcile US4 and US5 records to Gate Results and decision ceiling.
Trace US3+ records into the report.
Examine or perform the traceability test from workpaper to report.
Review closure basis for closed records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment; an assessment with no UNKNOWN Records shall record that the UNKNOWN search was performed.
failureModes: UNKNOWN downgraded to an 'improvement opportunity' in the executive report
Missing evidence treated as conforming
US4 UNKNOWN not reflected in its gate
UNKNOWN closed because the deadline passed
controls.testingSafety: Seeded-UNKNOWN tests use copies of completed assessments labelled as test material; they are never introduced into live workpapers.
controls.unknownRule: If the register cannot be shown to be complete (for example UNKNOWNs held in personal notes), record a US4 UNKNOWN Record against UNKNOWN completeness for the assessment.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard

controls.title: Conflict Handling
controls.objective: Ensure that when material evidence supports incompatible propositions (for example design shows 2N power, EPMS shows a shared upstream breaker), both lineages are preserved, the conflict is analysed and resolved, bounded or escalated, and the result reflects it.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall register each material evidence conflict as an EvidenceConflict with both assertions and their evidence lineages, analyse scope, time and state differences, seek corroboration, obtain competent review and record whether the conflict is resolved, bounded or escalated. Unresolved conflicts shall be recorded as U4 UNKNOWN Records; observed or tested evidence shall take precedence over design intent unless shown to be unrepresentative.
assessmentCriteria: Every material conflict identified in the sample is registered with both assertions and lineages.
Each conflict record shows analysis of scope, time and state differences and corroboration sought.
Resolution, bounding or escalation is recorded with competent reviewer.
Unresolved conflicts are U4 UNKNOWN Records with severity assigned.
Where design intent conflicts with observed or tested evidence, the observed or tested evidence prevailed or the reason it was unrepresentative is recorded.
Neither lineage was deleted.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor searches workpapers for contradictory evidence not registered as conflicts
acceptableAlternatives: Graph CHALLENGES relationships with linked EvidenceConflict nodes exported from the assessment tool
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: results may rest on contested evidence; CG-11 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the conflict register.
Search workpapers for unregistered contradictions.
Review analysis, corroboration and review for each sampled conflict.
Confirm unresolved conflicts are U4 UNKNOWN Records.
Check precedence of observed evidence over design intent.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment in which two or more evidence sources address the same assertion.
failureModes: Inconvenient telemetry ignored in favour of design documents
Conflicting provider attestation discarded
Conflict resolved by majority of documents rather than by evidence quality
Conflict unresolved but result CONFORMING
controls.testingSafety: Desk analysis only; corroborating extraction, if needed, is read-only.
controls.unknownRule: Unresolved material conflicts are U4 UNKNOWN Records and the affected result is UNKNOWN until resolved or bounded.

controls.title: Limitation Disclosure
controls.objective: Ensure that every limitation on the conclusion (exclusions, restricted or inaccessible evidence, untested states, assumptions, sampling limits, provider reliance) is disclosed in every report and statement at a prominence matching its effect.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall compile a limitations register for each assessment covering exclusions, restricted or inaccessible evidence, unassessed operating states, assumptions, sampling and test limits and reliance on providers or specialists, each with its effect on the decision. The reporting owner shall ensure every report and Assurance Statement for the assessment discloses each limitation with an effect on the decision, and that redaction for security does not remove a limitation.
assessmentCriteria: A limitations register exists covering the six limitation categories, each with decision effect.
Every limitation with a decision effect appears in each report and statement for the assessment.
Limitations affecting gates appear in the executive report alongside the Gate Results.
Redacted reports still state each limitation, even where its technical detail is withheld.
No report broadens scope beyond what the limitations allow.
minimumEvidence: All reports and statements for the assessment

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation by the independent reviewer
mandatoryItems: All reports and statements for the assessment
acceptableAlternatives: Limitations section in the technical report, if it is the single source for other reports
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: intended users may over-rely; decision condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the limitations register.
Reconcile each limitation to every report and statement.
Check executive-report prominence for gate-affecting limitations.
Compare redacted and unredacted versions for limitation removal.
Check report scope against limitations.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that issues a report or statement.
failureModes: Public summary omits that utility dependency was excluded
Redaction removes the statement that cooling failover was untested
Provider reliance not disclosed
Executive summary implies all states were assessed
controls.testingSafety: Desk review; restricted report versions viewed under distribution controls.
controls.unknownRule: If a report version cannot be obtained for reconciliation, record a U2 UNKNOWN for that report and treat its disclosure as unverified.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard
ISAE 3000 (assurance engagements other than audits or reviews of historical financial information) - inherent limitations

controls.title: Gate Applicability
controls.objective: Ensure that, for each assessment, every critical gate CG-01 to CG-15 is determined as applicable or APPROVED_NA with boundary rationale, and that the CRITICAL and SUPPORTING control set for each applicable gate is identified from the registry for the scope.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall determine, for each assessment, the applicability of each gate CG-01 to CG-15 to the decision question and boundary, shall identify for each applicable gate the in-scope CRITICAL and SUPPORTING controls from the AIDCF-007A registry gate mappings and the gate criteria from AIDCF-010, and shall submit any proposed APPROVED_NA with boundary rationale to the decision authority. Meta-gates CG-11 and CG-12 shall always be applicable.
assessmentCriteria: Each of the fifteen gates has an applicability determination for the assessment.
Every APPROVED_NA has boundary rationale and decision-authority approval.
CG-11 and CG-12 are applicable in every assessment.
For each applicable gate, the in-scope CRITICAL and SUPPORTING controls match the registry gate mappings filtered by scope.
Gate criteria and evidence floors applied are those of the declared AIDCF-010 version.
minimumEvidence: Registry gate mapping extract for the declared version

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: The assessment under review
evidenceProfile.independence: Reconciliation to registry mappings reperformed by the assessor using the published registry
mandatoryItems: Registry gate mapping extract for the declared version
acceptableAlternatives: Machine-generated gate-control lists from the assessment tool, if the tool configuration is verified under MCF-GOV-004
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: affected Gate Results cannot be relied upon; decision capped at LIMITED

assessmentProcedure: Obtain the applicability record and check all fifteen gates.
Review APPROVED_NA rationale and approvals.
Reconcile gate-control lists to registry mappings filtered by scope.
Confirm gate criteria and floors match the declared AIDCF-010 version.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that issues Gate Results, including delta and incident-triggered assessments.
failureModes: CG-04 marked not applicable for a site with battery rooms
CRITICAL control omitted from a gate's control list
Superseded gate criteria applied
APPROVED_NA granted by the lead assessor
controls.testingSafety: Desk review against the published registry release; no system access is required.
controls.unknownRule: If the registry version used for gate mappings cannot be identified, record a U8 UNKNOWN against every Gate Result of the assessment.

controls.title: Gate Evidence
controls.objective: Ensure that evidence for each applicable gate meets the gate's mandatory evidence classes and sufficiency floor from AIDCF-008, without substitution below the floor to complete a scorecard, and that Gate Results are computed by the AIDCF-010 roll-up rule.
controls.requirement: The lead assessor shall assemble, for each applicable gate, a gate Evidence Package containing the mandatory evidence classes for that gate, shall assess its sufficiency against the gate floor, and shall compute the Gate Result by the AIDCF-010 roll-up rule from CRITICAL control results, gate criteria and evidence sufficiency. The independent reviewer shall confirm, for each gate, that no evidence below the mandatory type or quality floor was substituted.
assessmentCriteria: Each applicable gate has an Evidence Package containing its mandatory evidence classes.
Sufficiency of each gate package is assessed and recorded against the gate floor.
No gate PASS is supported by a package below its floor; such gates are UNKNOWN.
Each Gate Result reproduces when the roll-up rule is reapplied.
The independent reviewer confirmed absence of below-floor substitution for each gate.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Assessments completed in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Reperformance by a party other than the lead assessor
acceptableAlternatives: Machine-readable gate packages and results in AIDCF-014 format
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US4 Critical: Gate Results unverified; decision capped at LIMITED
reassessmentTriggers: Evidence withdrawn from a gate package

assessmentProcedure: Obtain gate packages and check mandatory classes per gate.
Review sufficiency assessments against floors.
Reapply the roll-up rule to recorded results.
Check independent reviewer confirmations.
controls.applicability: Applies to every assessment that issues Gate Results.
failureModes: CG-05 passed on design documents and an old UPS test
Interview substituted for missing E4 recovery test under CG-10
Gate PASS with a CRITICAL control PARTIAL
Gate result computed by averaging
controls.testingSafety: Desk reperformance of gate roll-up from recorded results; no evidence is re-collected under this control.
controls.unknownRule: Any gate whose package is below floor is UNKNOWN; this shall be recorded as a US4 UNKNOWN Record against the gate.

controls.title: Independent Decision
controls.objective: Ensure that the Assurance Decision is issued by the accountable decision authority, separate from those who prepared and performed the assessment, on the basis of a recorded Decision Recommendation and review, and that automation only proposes.
controls.requirement: The decision authority shall issue each Assurance Decision personally or through documented delegation, on the basis of a Decision Recommendation from the lead assessor and the independent review record, and shall record the decision state, controlling reasons (including Gate Results and UNKNOWN ceilings), conditions with owners and dates, and validity. The tool owner shall ensure that no tool can transition a decision to APPROVED without the decision authority's authenticated action.
assessmentCriteria: Every Assurance Decision in the period was issued by the decision authority or a documented delegate.
The decision authority was not the preparer or performer of the assessment.
Each decision references a Decision Recommendation and independent review record.
Each decision records state, controlling reasons, conditions with owners and dates, and validity.
Tool configuration requires an authenticated decision-authority action for APPROVED status; no automated approval occurred.
minimumEvidence: Decision workflow configuration and audit log

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Decisions issued in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Workflow configuration and audit log extracted by the assessor
mandatoryItems: Decision workflow configuration and audit log
acceptableAlternatives: Signed paper decision records with a decision register, where no workflow tool is used
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: decisions' authority uncertain; intended reliance restricted and condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: List decisions in the period and verify issuer authority.
Compare issuer with preparer and performer records.
Check references to recommendation and review.
Check required decision content.
Inspect workflow configuration and audit log for automated approvals.
controls.applicability: Applies to every Assurance Decision.
failureModes: Lead assessor issues the decision
Tool auto-approves when score exceeds a threshold
Decision issued without review
Conditions without owners or dates
controls.testingSafety: Read-only inspection of workflow configuration and logs.
controls.unknownRule: If the workflow audit log cannot show who approved a decision, record a U7 UNKNOWN against that decision's authority.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 17020 (requirements for bodies performing inspection) - impartiality

controls.title: Claim Language
controls.objective: Ensure that reports and statements use only the controlled decision, gate and result vocabulary, bound every conclusion by Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, scope, states and date, and contain no prohibited claims.
controls.requirement: The reporting owner shall ensure that every report and Assurance Statement uses the controlled decision states (REASONABLY_ASSURED, CONDITIONALLY_ASSURED, LIMITED, NOT_ASSURED, INCONCLUSIVE), Gate Results (PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN, APPROVED_NA, NOT_ASSESSED) and control results of AIDCF-010 with the controlled wording of AIDCF-012; bounds each conclusion by Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, boundary, operating states and as-of date; and contains no prohibited claim (certified, accredited, universally safe, secure or resilient, compliant with all laws). The independent reviewer shall check claim language before issue.
assessmentCriteria: Every report and statement in the sample uses only the controlled decision, gate and result vocabulary.
Each conclusion is bounded by Capability Instance, Service Outcomes, boundary, operating states and as-of date.
No prohibited claim appears.
No visual device (colour, badge, score) presents a stronger conclusion than the decision state.
Independent review of claim language is recorded before issue.
minimumEvidence: Independent review records for claim language

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R3 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Reports and statements issued in the last twelve months
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor screens all issued documents, not a management-selected subset
mandatoryItems: Independent review records for claim language
acceptableAlternatives: Automated vocabulary screening output, verified by manual review of a sample
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: external reliance may exceed decision; condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: Collect all issued reports and statements in the period.
Screen vocabulary and bounding elements.
Screen for prohibited claims and misleading visual devices.
Check independent review records.
controls.applicability: Applies to every report or statement conveying an AIDCF conclusion.
failureModes: Statement says 'fully resilient AI data centre'
Legacy term 'Adverse' or 'Conditional' used
Green badge shown for a LIMITED decision
Conclusion stated without as-of date
controls.testingSafety: Desk review of issued documents only.
controls.unknownRule: If an issued document cannot be retrieved, record a U2 UNKNOWN for that document's claim language.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard
ISO/IEC 17000 (conformity assessment vocabulary and general principles)

controls.title: Evidence Expiry
controls.objective: Ensure that each Evidence Object relied on by a current decision has a currency basis and review date, that expiry is detected, and that expired mandatory evidence triggers review of the claims it supports.
controls.requirement: The evidence lead shall record, for each Evidence Object supporting a current Assurance Decision, its currency basis and review date per AIDCF-008, shall monitor for expiry, and on expiry of mandatory evidence shall notify the lead assessor and capability owner, mark the evidence STALE and initiate review of the dependent claims and Gate Results within the expiry response time.
assessmentCriteria: Every Evidence Object supporting a current decision has a currency basis and review date.
Expiry monitoring operated throughout the period (for example scheduled reports or alerts).
Every expiry of mandatory evidence in the period was notified and the evidence marked STALE.
Dependent claims and Gate Results were reviewed within the expiry response time.
No current decision relies on expired mandatory evidence without a recorded review outcome.
minimumEvidence: Evidence currency records for current decisions

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor runs an independent expiry query against currency records
mandatoryItems: Evidence currency records for current decisions
acceptableAlternatives: Manual quarterly expiry review records, if complete for the period
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: current decisions may rely on stale evidence; condition recorded

assessmentProcedure: Obtain currency records for evidence supporting current decisions.
Run an independent expiry query and compare with monitoring outputs.
Trace expiries to notifications, STALE markings and reviews.
Check current decisions for reliance on expired mandatory evidence.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme with decisions that remain valid over time.
failureModes: Annual UPS test expired but CG-05 PASS still reported
Provider certificate lapsed unnoticed
Evidence with no review date
Expiry alerts sent to a departed staff member
controls.testingSafety: Read-only queries against currency records.
controls.unknownRule: Evidence with no currency basis is treated as STALE (U3) for any OPERATION, EFFECTIVENESS or RESILIENCE claim.

controls.title: Change Triggers
controls.objective: Ensure that material change, incidents, gate changes and evidence invalidation automatically or reliably trigger reassessment of the affected claims, gates and decisions, and that the trigger mechanism is shown to work.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall define reassessment triggers for each current Assurance Decision (material architecture, capacity, configuration, provider or ownership change; incidents affecting Service Outcomes; gate FAIL or critical UNKNOWN; evidence invalidation), shall connect the change, incident and evidence systems so that trigger events are routed to the lead assessor and capability owner, and shall verify at least once per trigger test interval, by injecting a test event, that triggers reach the responsible roles and initiate reassessment.
assessmentCriteria: Each current decision has defined reassessment triggers covering change, incident, gate and evidence events.
Change, incident and evidence systems route trigger events to the lead assessor and capability owner.
Every material change and Service Outcome incident in the period was matched to a trigger response.
An injected test event within the interval reached the responsible roles and initiated the reassessment workflow.
Trigger responses record the affected claims, gates and decisions and the outcome.
minimumEvidence: Integration configuration between change, incident and evidence systems and the assurance workflow

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P3 F4 C4 R4 T3 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months preceding the assessment and the latest trigger test
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reconciles the full change and incident logs to trigger responses
acceptableAlternatives: A genuine trigger event fully traced from source system to reassessment, in place of an injected test
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: current decisions may persist after invalidating change; CG-14 evaluation records the gap

assessmentProcedure: Review trigger definitions per current decision.
Inspect integration configuration.
Reconcile material changes and incidents to trigger responses.
Examine or perform an injected test event with the tool owner.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme with decisions remaining valid after issue.
failureModes: Cooling conversion completed but prior CG-06 PASS still relied upon
Incident ticket never reaches the assurance team
Trigger fires to a mailbox nobody monitors
Provider change outside the owner's change system
controls.testingSafety: Injected test events are clearly marked as tests in non-production change or incident queues, or use a test category agreed with the tool owner; they shall not page operational on-call staff or alter real change records.
controls.unknownRule: If provider-originated changes are not routed, record a U10 UNKNOWN for provider-dependent claims.
informativeReferences: ISO/IEC 20000-1 (service management system) - change and incident management
AIDCF-014 End-to-End Traceability and Machine-Executable Data Standard

controls.title: Monitoring Coverage
controls.objective: Ensure that where continuing assurance is claimed, the specific claims monitored, the telemetry and evidence feeds used, their coverage and their blind spots are defined, and that feed health is itself monitored.
controls.requirement: The assurance programme lead shall, for each claim under continuing assurance, define the monitored indicators, their source feeds, coverage across assets, locations and operating states, thresholds that trigger review, and known blind spots. The tool owner shall monitor feed health (gaps, latency, clock integrity, dropped data) and alert the evidence lead on degradation; the programme lead shall state blind spots in each continuing-assurance report.
assessmentCriteria: Each claim under continuing assurance has defined indicators, feeds, coverage, thresholds and blind spots.
Feed coverage reconciles to the in-scope asset and location population.
Feed health is monitored, and degradations in the period were alerted and actioned.
Threshold breaches in the period triggered review.
Continuing-assurance reports state blind spots and feed-health limitations.

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T4 I3
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months preceding the assessment
evidenceProfile.independence: Assessor reconciles feed coverage to asset registers independently
acceptableAlternatives: Observability platform coverage reports, if they map to assurance claims
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: continuing-assurance claims unsupported; continuing claims reverted to point-in-time with condition
reassessmentTriggers: New assets not onboarded to monitoring

assessmentProcedure: Review continuing-assurance claim definitions.
Reconcile feed coverage to asset and location registers.
Analyse feed-health records for gaps and actions.
Trace threshold breaches to reviews.
Check blind-spot disclosure in reports.
controls.applicability: Applies only where continuing assurance (AL6) is claimed; otherwise NOT_APPLICABLE.
failureModes: Continuous assurance claimed while half the CDUs report no telemetry
Clock drift corrupts event ordering
New hall never onboarded to monitoring
Blind spots omitted from report
controls.testingSafety: Read-only access to observability and monitoring systems.
controls.unknownRule: If feed coverage cannot be reconciled, record a U5 UNKNOWN and do not describe the claim as continuously assured.
informativeReferences: NIST SP 800-92 (guide to computer security log management)

controls.title: Decision Suspension and Supersession
controls.objective: Ensure that when a decision can no longer be relied upon (material change, incident, gate FAIL, evidence invalidation, expiry), it is suspended, withdrawn or superseded promptly, intended users are notified, and history is preserved, so that failure of a prior conclusion is contained.
controls.requirement: The decision authority shall define criteria for suspension, withdrawal and supersession of Assurance Decisions, shall act on each trigger response that meets the criteria within the suspension time, shall notify all intended users and recipients of external communications, and shall preserve the prior decision, its evidence manifest and the reason for change. The programme lead shall rehearse the suspension and notification process at least once per rehearsal interval.
assessmentCriteria: Suspension, withdrawal and supersession criteria are defined.
Each trigger response meeting the criteria in the period resulted in suspension, withdrawal or supersession within the suspension time.
All intended users and external recipients were notified.
Prior decisions, manifests and reasons are preserved and linked by SUPERSEDES relationships.
A rehearsal within the interval exercised suspension and notification end to end, or a real suspension did so.
minimumEvidence: Trigger response and decision lifecycle records

evidenceProfile.qualityFloor: P4 F4 C4 R4 T3 I4
evidenceProfile.periodCoverage: Twelve months preceding the assessment and the latest rehearsal
evidenceProfile.independence: Rehearsal observed by the independent reviewer
mandatoryItems: Trigger response and decision lifecycle records
acceptableAlternatives: Real suspension event fully traced, in place of a rehearsal
evidenceProfile.unknownEffect: US3 Material: reliance on invalid decisions may continue; condition recorded and current decisions reviewed

assessmentProcedure: Review criteria.
Reconcile qualifying trigger responses to lifecycle actions and timing.
Check notifications to intended users and external recipients.
Inspect history preservation and SUPERSEDES links.
Examine or observe a rehearsal.
controls.applicability: Applies to every programme with decisions relied upon after issue.
failureModes: Customer still relying on a decision invalidated by a cooling incident
Superseded decision deleted
Suspension notice not sent to external recipients
Gate FAIL after incident not acted on
controls.testingSafety: Rehearsals use test decision records and test distribution lists; no notice is sent to real external recipients during a rehearsal.
controls.unknownRule: If decision history cannot be shown to be preserved, record a U7 UNKNOWN against prior decisions' traceability.
informativeReferences: AIDCF-012 Reporting and Assurance Statement Standard
